On more than five million proprietary order records, CVAP raises exact-day accuracy from 49.5% for the rule-based estimate to 64.1%. Paired with a decision rule that selects a quantile weighting late errors more heavily, the split CPS (SCPS) gives a point estimate that raises late-delivery detection from 3.8% to 79.4%. Residual-based CPS distributions also meet or slightly exceed nominal interval-coverage targets. In decision experiments with a JD.com simulator over six test dates, C-SAA with CVAP lowers mean total cost by 7.1% and C-SAA with the Mondrian CPS (MCPS) lowers it by 6.7%, relative to C-SAA with the original nonconformal forecast. Both cut the late-delivery rate from 5.7% to below 4.0%.

papers.title: A Kohnen-Zagier Formula in Level 1
papers.abstract: In 1985 Kohnen used the Shimura correspondence to prove a general formula relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms of level $ 4N $ transforming with respect to the theta multiplier to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ N $. This generalized previous work with Zagier. In this paper, we prove a Kohnen-Zagier type formula using Yang's Shimura correspondence for powers of the eta multiplier in level $ 1 $, relating the coefficients of half-integral weight modular forms to central values of $ L $-functions for twists of newforms of level $ 6 $. To do so we develop some of the theory of modular forms transforming with respect to powers of the eta multiplier and introduce Shintani lifts of level $ 6 $, with Fourier coefficients given in terms of cycle integrals.

papers.title: On the Hodge Extension of Local K\"ahler Forms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Stein manifold, and let $K=\{h\le0\}$ be a compact sublevel set of a strictly plurisubharmonic function $h$ defined near $K$. It is known that $K$ is meromorphically convex in $X$ if and only if $dd^ch$ extends to a Hodge form on $X$. We show that if $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)$ is the direct sum of a free abelian group and a torsion group, for example if it is finitely generated, then any extension of $dd^ch$ to a K\"ahler form on $X$ can be modified, after replacing $h$ by a positive multiple, into a Hodge form. Thus meromorphic convexity of $K$ is equivalent to the extendability of $dd^ch$ as a K\"ahler form. We also show that the topological assumption cannot be dropped: we construct a Stein manifold $X$ of dimension $6$ with $H_2(X,\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Q$, a sublevel set $K$ as above that is not meromorphically convex although $dd^ch$ extends to a K\"ahler form, and a totally real torus in $K$ that is isotropic for a K\"ahler form but is not meromorphically convex. This shows that the Hodge condition in Guedj's characterization of meromorphically convex totally real submanifolds cannot be weakened to a K\"ahler condition, and gives counterexamples to two criteria stated by Cieliebak and Eliashberg.

papers.title: An Energy-based discontinuous Galerkin method for the Westervelt equation with absorbing boundary conditions
papers.abstract: This paper develops and analyzes an energy-based discontinuous Galerkin method for the Westervelt equation in the acoustic-velocity-potential formulation with spatially varying material parameters and nonlinear absorbing boundary conditions. The semi-discrete scheme is constructed from the underlying energy balance and incorporates an additional consistent term to accommodate the strong damping operator within the discrete energy framework. Numerical fluxes are designed at both interelement and physical boundaries to provide a unified treatment of interior and boundary dissipation. For the nonlinear analysis, we study an auxiliary variable-coefficient linearized problem and establish stability and a priori error estimates, including the additional terms induced by the solution-dependent absorbing boundary flux. These estimates are combined with a fixed-point argument to prove existence, uniqueness, and convergence of the nonlinear semi-discrete approximation under suitable regularity, smallness, and nondegeneracy assumptions. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical convergence results and illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

papers.title: Neural Stream Function Method for Electrical Impedance Tomography with Lipschitz Conductivities
papers.abstract: Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) reconstructs the conductivity inside an object from voltage and current measurements on its boundary. The resulting inverse problem is nonlinear and severely ill-posed. Neural networks offer a flexible computational approach, but training physics informed neural networks for EIT and relating their training loss to reconstruction accuracy remain challenging. We develop a novel constrained neural stream function method for planar EIT with Lipschitz conductivities. The method builds the conductivity constraints and prescribed boundary voltages into the neural trial functions and replaces the second order conductivity equation with a first order system in strong form. The measured current is also used to construct a fixed baseline for the stream function. For this formulation, we derive error estimates that relate the sampled neural objective to errors in the physical boundary currents and the reconstructed conductivity. The error estimates separate the contributions from neural approximation, measurement noise, and sampling. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high reconstruction accuracy with both exact and noisy boundary data.

papers.title: Loop Space Models and Integral Homology of Connected Quandles
papers.abstract: We construct a marked integral delooping of a connected quandle's covering monoid, realizing its rack space as a homotopy fiber. For finite connected quandles at primes $p$ not dividing a point-stabilizer order, we determine the local $A_\infty$ type and the ordinary rack cohomology shuffle algebra over fields of characteristic $p$. We compute integral quandle homology in all positive degrees for finite connected regular cyclic Alexander quandles and the tetrahedral quandle. At such primes dividing the quandle order, rack-space homotopy groups have exponentially many cyclic direct summands of fixed $p$-power order in each sufficiently large degree.

papers.title: A curve of genus $2$ over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ and hexads of bitangents to a smooth quartic
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the Abel-Jacobi map of a genus 2 curve over $\mathbb{C}(t)$ arising from a double cover of $\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C})$ branched along six lines. We utilize the so-called Mumford representations to conduct the calculations. As an application, we give an alternative proof of classical results on quartics and bitangents. Furthermore, we obtain a method to give explicit defining equations of quartic curves that have the six lines as bitangents and apply it to determine the number of connected components of the realization space.

papers.title: Determining norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields
papers.authors: Gustav Kj{\ae}rbye Bagger, Andrew R. Booker, Tim Trudgian
papers.abstract: We prove that Cavallar and Lemmermeyer's list of $58$ norm-Euclidean complex cubic fields is complete. The proof combines a classical discriminant bound with exact certificates of non-Euclideanity. The unit action reduces their verification to finite lattice enumeration with rigorous interval arithmetic. An independent covering computation confirms norm-Euclideanity for the $58$ fields.

papers.title: Sharp Adams inequality for Critical Biharmonic Equations with Hardy--H\'enon Weights in $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.authors: J. C. de Albuquerque, J. Carvalho, L. M. Silva
papers.abstract: We study a class of weighted fourth-order elliptic problems in \(\mathbb{R}^4\) driven by the biharmonic operator and involving Hardy--H\'enon type potentials. The nonlinear term has critical exponential growth in the sense of an Adams-type inequality. The weights \(|x|^a\) and \(|x|^b\) allow us to incorporate singular, vanishing, and unbounded effects in a unified variational framework. We introduce a suitable weighted function space, establish Sobolev-type embeddings, and prove an Adams-type inequality adapted to this setting. Under appropriate structural assumptions on the nonlinearity, we prove the existence of nontrivial weak solutions. We also obtain regularity properties and derive a Pohozaev identity, which leads to a nonexistence result.

papers.title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program
papers.authors: Liang Wu, Honghui Zheng, Bo Yang, Xu Yang, Yilin Mo, J\'an Drgo\v{n}a
papers.abstract: Solving large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs (mpQPs) in real time often requires thousands of iterative optimization updates, creating a major computational bottleneck in model predictive control and learning-enabled systems. This paper proposes TQPNet, a self-supervised neural compression framework that learns to compress long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. We derive a low-dimensional ADMM scheme operating on the primal-dual variables $(x,\beta)$ and show that its iteration admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, termed ADMM(ReLU). Building on this insight, TQPNet combines a multilayer perceptron with ReLU activations (MLP(ReLU)) and a small number of unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers. The network is trained offline using an optimality-condition-informed residual loss, eliminating the need for solver-generated labels. The proposed residual-based framework enables both self-supervised training and online solution certification through adaptive ADMM(ReLU) refinement. Experiments on large-scale mpQPs and real-time MPC applications demonstrate that TQPNet achieves high accuracy, strong generalization, and substantially faster inference than conventional optimization-based methods.

papers.title: Boxing Problem
papers.authors: April Niu, Santanu Dey, Oktay G\"unl\"uk, Jisun Lee
papers.abstract: We study the \textit{Boxing Problem}, which seeks a subset of points in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) maximizing the total reward of a selection of points minus the width of its axis-aligned bounding box. We also investigate the associated \textit{Boxing Set}, defined by the epigraph of the width function over binary selection variables. Although the width function is not submodular in general, we restore submodularity by fixing an anchor point. After anchoring, we establish a connection to the intersection of mixing sets with a linking constraint, which yields a polynomial-time optimization algorithm and a polynomial-size extended formulation. We then study the polyhedral structure of the Boxing Set and show that its facets admit laminar families of tight sets and can be obtained by sequential lifting. For the one-dimensional case, we provide a complete description of facet-defining inequalities together with a strongly polynomial-time separation algorithm.

papers.title: TensorSpectra: Bridging the Spectral and Tensor Worlds for High-Dimensional PDEs
papers.authors: Bingcheng Hu, Tianchi Yu, Zhaoxiang Li, Ivan Oseledets
papers.abstract: High-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) remain challenging for spectral methods due to the exponential growth of multidimensional coefficient spaces. We propose TensorSpectra, a low-rank spectral framework that directly parameterizes spectral coefficient tensors in canonical polyadic (CP) form, reducing representation complexity from $\mathcal{O}(N^d)$ to $\mathcal{O}(dNr)$. TensorSpectra combines structure-preserving spectral calculus, de-aliased nonlinear interactions, operator-aware residual weighting, and progressive low-rank corrections to enable efficient PDEs solving in compressed coefficient space. We further establish a theoretical framework connecting spectral truncation, low-rank approximation, and optimization errors. Extensive experiments across five PDE families and 24 benchmark configurations demonstrate State-Of-The-Art accuracy among five representative baselines, with TensorSpectra consistently achieving the lowest relative $L^2$ errors. More broadly, our findings offer a new perspective on high-dimensional PDEs solving, suggesting that exploiting intrinsic low-rank structure in spectral coefficient space provides a viable alternative to conventional physical-space approaches.

papers.title: Strong stable sets and asymptotic fineness
papers.abstract: We investigate the strong stable sets of the geodesic flow on hyperbolic surfaces and their relation to the injectivity radius. We prove that the strong stable set of a vector does not coincide with its stable horocycle if and only if the injectivity radius along the associated geodesic ray is not bounded away from zero and the ray does not diverge through a cusp. In that case, the strong stable set is an uncountable union of stable horocycles. In previous works, we considered the particular cases where the ray meets arbitrarily short closed geodesics or closed horocycles. Here we complete the study by treating the third possible case, where the ray meets closed hypercycles of arbitrarily small length.

papers.title: Safety of layered control systems via control barrier morphisms
papers.authors: Aaron D. Ames, Joe Moeller, Massimiliano de Sa, Paulo Tabuada
papers.abstract: Layered control architectures provide a powerful paradigm for synthesizing controllers for complex systems. Yet, translating guarantees at each layer to system-level guarantees is challenging due to the interactions between layers. To address this problem, this paper presents a categorical perspective on layered control architectures. Individual systems are represented as control coalgebras, their interactions are specified as morphisms to mediators, and system-level behaviors are obtained via composition defined categorically as a pullback. To analyze the safety of these systems, we formulate control barrier morphisms (CBMs), the categorical generalization of control barrier functions. We prove that feedback controllers satisfying a CBM condition render the associated safe subobject forward invariant. It is through CBMs that we can establish the safety of layered systems: given a CBM at each layer subject to compatibility conditions, the universal property of the pullback implies the existence of a CBM for the composed system. Safety of a full-order model being safety filtered by a reduced-order model is recovered as a specialization of the categorical framework.

papers.title: New Explicit Examples of Mannheim Pairs in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.authors: Jos\'e Alan, Renato Teixeira, Thiago Mendon\c{c}a
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct new explicit parametrizations of Mannheim pairs in Euclidean 3-space. Unlike the known examples in the literature, which are essentially slant helices or general helices, the curve presented here is neither a helix nor a slant helix. We provide the full Frenet apparatus, the explicit Cartesian coordinates expressed in terms of elementary functions, and the corresponding Mannheim partner curve. The construction is based on a specific choice of the angular function that governs the curve's tangent indicatrix, leading to integrable expressions.

papers.title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
papers.abstract: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack formulated by Emerton, Gee, and Hellmann.

papers.title: The Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over higher dimensional Riemannian manifolds
papers.authors: Jared Casey, Chak Hoi Chan, Min-Chun Hong
papers.abstract: We develop a parabolic formulation of the Uhlenbeck gauge fixing theorem and use it to prove the maximal existence of the Yang-Mills flow in vector bundles over compact $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds for $n \geq 4$. We apply Moser's iteration technique \cite{Mo1} to give a new proof of the bound of the curvature. Using an idea of Hamilton on the Ricci flow \cite{Ha}, we also provide a new proof on uniform estimates of higher order derivatives. Furthermore, we investigate the blow-up of the Yang-Mills flow at the maximal existence time and improve an asymptotical result of Hong-Tian \cite{HT1}.

papers.title: From gauge-covariant Noether invariants to electromagnetic velocity-dependent mechanics
papers.abstract: For a charged particle, a spacetime symmetry need preserve the electromagnetic potential only up to a gauge transformation. Starting from the standard Noether--Bessel-Hagen construction, we make explicit the reduction from the relativistic gauge-invariant worldline charge to the generalized constants of nonrelativistic velocity-dependent mechanics, retaining the quasi-invariance boundary term throughout. With the convention $S_p=-mc\int ds+q\int A$, the canonical worldline one-form is $P=-m u^\flat+qA$, and a Killing vector satisfying $\mathcal L_XA=d\chi_X$ generates $C_X=P(X)-q\chi_X$. Its low-velocity limit is the Noether--Bessel-Hagen charge of the coordinate-time Lagrangian, from which generalized linear momentum, angular momentum and energy follow generator by generator. A uniform magnetic field gives an elementary gauge-dependent representative but gauge-invariant translational charge. The Darwin interaction then supplies the conservative $O(c^{-2})$ many-particle realization after field elimination, while a closed particle--field system is governed by the total stress-energy Killing charge. The result is an explicit reduction map linking three established descriptions without identifying their distinct conserved quantities.

papers.title: Graph-diameter criteria and sharp dissipation in discrete Wasserstein-Fisher geometry
papers.abstract: We study the probability simplex of a finite connected weighted graph with an Onsager operator combining logarithmic-mean transport and mass-conserving Fisher reaction. For every fixed positive reaction parameter, we prove that the entropy Hessian has a finite global lower bound if and only if the original transport graph has diameter at most two. Near a boundary probability, the corresponding criterion is that its positive support reaches every vertex in at most two steps. The proof controls all potential directions under arbitrary multiscale boundary degeneration. For graphs of diameter at most two, the optimal lower bound is Lipschitz on bounded parameter intervals, including the pure-transport endpoint. We also determine the largest instantaneous logarithmic-amplitude dissipation function depending only on the graph and the current amplitude, and construct two-level probabilities attaining it. Its positivity has the same two-step criterion. As consequences, we obtain graph-dependent entropy-decay estimates and exact projective contraction bounds without assuming nonnegative entropic curvature.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We improve a parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem for the Yang-Mills flow. This allows us to prove new existence of weak solutions of the Yang-Mills flow having with better properties than Struwe's weak solution on four manifolds in \cite {St2}. Finally, we apply the new parabolic version of Uhlenbeck's gauge fixing theorem to solve the Struwe problem in \cite {St2} and prove uniqueness of weak solutions to the Yang-Mills flow on compact four-manifolds with initial value $A_0 \in W^{1, 2}(M)$.

papers.title: Exponential decay of threshold correlations for symmetric periodic functions
papers.abstract:
We study how often $n$ distinct integer dilates of a periodic function can all lie above a fixed threshold or all lie below its negative. We consider continuous functions $f:\mathbb R\to[-1,1]$ that are $1$-periodic, even, strictly decreasing on $[0,1/2]$, and satisfy $f(0)=1$ and $f(t+1/2)=-f(t)$. This class includes the cosine and the triangle wave. For $0\leq\alpha<1$, let $\rho_\alpha\in(0,1/4]$ be determined by $f(\rho_\alpha)=\alpha$, and let $F_\alpha(n)$ denote the infimum of these proportions over all sets of $n$ distinct positive integer frequencies.
  We prove that $F_\alpha(n)\geq 4\rho_\alpha^n$ and that the limit $\lim_{n\to\infty}F_\alpha(n)^{1/n}$ exists for every threshold. When $\rho_\alpha^{-1}$ is an integer, we obtain \begin{align} F_\alpha(n) &\leq C_\alpha n^{\log_2((1-\rho_\alpha)/(1-2\rho_\alpha))}\rho_\alpha^n, \end{align} and hence the limit equals $\rho_\alpha$. Otherwise, the limit belongs to the interval $[\rho_\alpha,\lfloor\rho_\alpha^{-1}\rfloor^{-1}]$.
  The upper bound in the reciprocal case uses a cyclic covering construction previously studied in the context of circular graphs. We give a self-contained proof of the corresponding optimal modulus.

papers.title: The Miyaoka-Yau inequality and the delta invariant for Fano varieties II -soliton case-
papers.abstract: Inspired by recent work of Inoue and Hallam-Lahdili, we prove an equivariant Miyaoka-Yau inequality with a correction term for smooth Fano manifolds admitting K\"ahler-Ricci solitons. It recovers the usual Miyaoka-Yau inequality in the K\"ahler-Einstein case. Our proof uses weighted equivariant Bogomolov-Gieseker and Langer inequalities for torsion-free sheaves, together with a weighted slope estimate for the canonical extension sheaf. We also construct toric examples showing that the existence of a soliton implies neither weighted semistability of the canonical extension sheaf nor nonnegativity of the equivariant Miyaoka-Yau number.

papers.title: Non-associative Hopf Algebra on Dyck Paths Arising from the Shuffle-insertion Product
papers.authors: Nantel Bergeron, Yuchen Guo, Huilan Li
papers.abstract: In this paper, we define a shuffle-insertion product and a cut-box coproduct on the vector space spanned by Dyck paths, where the product is commutative but non-associative. We prove that the product and coproduct are compatible, making the space a non-associative bialgebra. This bialgebra is connected and bigraded by path degree and peak number, and hence is a non-associative Hopf algebra. Its primitive subspace is spanned by atoms, and associators of primitive elements are primitive. Furthermore, we provide closed-form formulas for its left and right antipodes. We also define the convolution product on the space of linear transformations of the non-associative Hopf algebra, which equips this space with a non-associative algebra structure. Finally, we construct a one-parameter deformation preserving the cut-box coproduct. Its zero specialization is the ordinary shuffle Hopf algebra, which is also the associated graded algebra for the atom filtration, while every nonzero specialization is isomorphic to the shuffle-insertion algebra.

papers.title: New structure for Villadsen algebras of the first type
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish two main results concerning the comparison theory of positive elements in approximately homogeneous $C^{*}$-algebras with diagonal maps. The first is an existence theorem which interfaces with the rank problem; given a Villadsen algebra $A$, we construct a convex cone that induces an embedding of a semigroup into $Cu(A)$. This semigroup is identified with the set of strictly positive, lower-semicontinuous affine maps on the trace simplex of $A$. The second is a construction of an AH algebra that produces an obstacle to classifying the approximate unitary orbits of positive elements in terms of their spectral data. Our counterexample sheds light on a critical topological obstruction when attempting to understand equivalence classes of $*$-homomorphisms from $C_{0}((0,1])$ to an arbitrary $C^{*}$-algebra of stable rank one.

papers.title: Comparison categories: the normal form and the regularity of comparison data
papers.abstract: There are many types of equivalence relations in mathematics, each one enjoying its own defnition, but many of them can also be defined by transformations of morphisms: Green's relations, orbit relations, conjugacy, equality of orbit closures, equivalence of Cauchy sequences, stable isomorphism. We unify them through the comparison category of a comparison datum, read at levels $-1,0,1,2,\dots$ (comparisons in both directions, connected components, homotopy groups). Its normal form is a full subcategory of a Grothendieck construction $\int_VH$ cut out by a map $s$; the classical relations are traced back to it by restriction along $s$, enrichment by a cost (limit relations) and filtered colimits (stabilization). If the map $\sigma$ transporting morphisms into a $2$-category is arbitrary, every relation occurs, so the constraint is the regularity of $\sigma$. We grade data along seven regularity classes. The rigid and diagonal classes are classified completely (on finite groups, by the double coset relations); completely functorial data contain conjugacy and obey a dichotomy on nil monoids. Whether every relation on a monoid is level $0$ of a completely functorial datum is open.

papers.title: Homogenization theory of topological Anderson insulators: genuine gaps and pseudo-gaps
papers.abstract: A topological Anderson insulator is an insulator whose non-trivial topological phase is induced by disorder. We develop a homogenization theory of this phenomenon for constant-coefficient elliptic systems perturbed by fluctuations oscillating at scale $\varepsilon$. Periodic fluctuations of every order below that of the operator, with appropriate amplitudes, do not average out: they produce an order-one correction $M$ given by a second-order (Born) formula, and the operator converges in the norm-resolvent sense to its homogenized limit. In particular, electric potentials and magnetic fields of zero mean, usually regarded as topologically trivial perturbations, generate corrections $M$ that change the topological phase. Fluctuations confined to a half-plane create an interface that carries the bulk-difference invariant of the homogenized operator for all $\varepsilon$ sufficiently small, a property that is stable under local defects. For random fluctuations, rare regions typically fill the homogenized gap, which becomes a pseudo-gap, and the standard interface index need no longer be defined. We define an index along cuts deformed so as to avoid the rare regions, and prove that it equals almost surely the bulk-difference invariant of the operator homogenized in the Born approximation, for first-order alloys with vanishing low moments and for a class of second-order systems with scalar disorder at criticality that includes the BHZ model.

papers.title: Randomized algorithms in numerical linear algebra for scientific computing
papers.authors: Ethan N. W. Epperly, Daniel Kressner, Yuji Nakatsukasa
papers.abstract: Randomized numerical linear algebra (RNLA) has fundamentally changed the landscape of scientific computing over the last twenty to thirty years. While early breakthroughs focused primarily on low-rank approximation and least-squares problems, randomized techniques are now used to solve a broad range of linear algebra problems, supporting applications spanning data science, optimization, and computational engineering. This paper surveys some of the main ideas of RNLA, focusing on methods that are effective in practice and on simple theoretical bounds that can be used to understand them. We highlight the core benefits of randomization: improved scalability, algorithmic simplicity, and---contrary to what the name may suggest---remarkable reliability and numerical stability. Topics include sketching, low-rank approximation, least squares, orthogonalization and approximate orthogonalization, randomized Krylov subspace methods, preconditioning, trace and spectral density estimation, row and column selection algorithms, posterior error estimation, randomized regularization, and tensor-structured randomness.

papers.title: Asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distributions of the Betti and Hodge numbers of the moduli spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ of stable pointed curves and the all-light Hassett spaces $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0|n}$, for fixed genus $g\ge1$ as the number of markings tends to infinity. We prove central limit theorems for the full Betti distributions, whose variances grow linearly in $n$ with leading coefficients independent of the genus. For the normalized even Betti numbers, we establish refined local limit theorems with estimates uniform in degree. These local estimates yield asymptotic formulas for individual even Betti numbers and determine the sharp central ultra-log-concavity thresholds $\frac{3(e-2)}{2(3-e)}$ and $3$, respectively. For $g\ge2$, the off-diagonal Hodge components form proportions of exact orders $n^{-1/2}$ and $n^{-1}$ of the total cohomology of the two spaces, respectively. The conditional distributions of the Hodge difference $p-q$ given $p\ne q$ converge, for both spaces, to a single discrete law independent of the genus. We also prove that tautological classes account for all but a proportion of exact order $n^{-1}$ of the even cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$. The tautological degree distribution converges to the standard Gaussian under the centering and scaling of the ambient even Betti distribution. An explicit asymptotic formula for the ratio of the ordinary Euler characteristics of the light and heavy spaces answers a question of Kannan, Serpente and Yun. The proofs combine the heavy/light substitution with a stratification of the light spaces by stable cores, singularity analysis of Hodge generating functions, and refined Fourier estimates exploiting Poincar\'e duality.

papers.title: Test ideals can be computed by boundaries
papers.authors: Rahul Ajit, with Appendix joint with Daniel Apsley
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be a normal $F$-finite ring of characteristic $p>0$. We show that one effective $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor $\Delta$, with $K_R+\Delta$ $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$, computes the big test ideal. This answers a question of Schwede and Smith. More generally, we prove their conjecture that test module of a Cartier algebra acting on an ideal is the test module of a single map $\psi$ in the algebra and even the image of $\psi$. We prove a global version for schemes quasi-projective over an $F$-finite local ring as well. In particular, every such normal, locally strongly $F$-regular scheme admits an effective boundary $\Delta$ for which $(X,\Delta)$ is locally strongly $F$-regular and $K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier of index prime to $p$.

papers.title: Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Semilinear Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a rigorous mathematical framework for the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of semilinear stochastic partial differential equations. The invariant Gaussian measure of the associated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which need not be time-reversible, serves as the reference measure. We define thermodynamic quantities in terms of probability densities and derive the entropy balance equation. We obtain explicit expressions for the entropy production rate and prove that its vanishing in the stationary state is equivalent to time reversibility. Sample-path entropy production is identified with the logarithm of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the forward path measure with respect to the time-reversed path measure and is shown to satisfy fluctuation theorems. For nonstationary systems, sample-path entropy production decomposes into housekeeping heat and free-energy dissipation, each satisfying an integral fluctuation theorem. Both have nonnegative expectations, and the mean free-energy dissipation equals the decrease in relative entropy with respect to the stationary distribution. The theory is applied to semilinear stochastic heat equations with spatially correlated noise, a random polymer model, a nonlinear model with a divergence-free drift, and two coupled stochastic heat equations in contact with heat baths at different temperatures.

papers.title: Endpoint estimates for spherical maximal operators acting on radial functions in hyperbolic spaces
In-Context Learning for Multi-Fidelity Multiscale Model Closure and Cross-Operator Out-Of-Distribution Generalization
papers.authors: Xinyuan Li, Matthew Zahr, Panos Stinis, Zecheng Zhang
papers.abstract: Multi-fidelity learning uses low-fidelity information (coarse-scale PDE models) together with limited high-fidelity data (fine-scale solutions) to obtain high-accuracy PDE solutions. It is a data-driven approach to downscale reduced-order models to solve PDEs efficiently and accurately. Standard multi-fidelity learning focuses on one operator or PDE; given a new PDE, retraining using additional coarse-fine solution pairs may be required, which is costly. In this work, we propose an in-context multi-fidelity learning framework for learning multiple multi-fidelity operators with one shared model. The model is trained using paired low- and high-fidelity examples as demonstrations from multiple operators, together with a new coarse-scale solution query, to predict the corresponding fine-scale solution. Once trained, given a new PDE operator, a few (fewer than five) coarse-fine demonstration pairs, and a low-cost coarse query, the model predicts the corresponding fine-scale solution without fine-tuning. When the target operator appears in the training dataset but has a different prediction goal, such as predicting beyond the training time interval, no additional demonstrations are needed. Instead, the model uses training coarse-fine pairs from that PDE and information from other training operators. Testing then only requires generating a low-cost coarse-scale solution query, without fine-tuning. Notably, our smallest model contains only 255,364 trainable parameters, corresponding to approximately 456 parameters per training operator for 560 operators.

papers.title: Geometry of $m$-direct-sum morphisms
papers.authors: Duo Li, Yanjie Li, Francesco Russo
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a complex vector space of dimension $mk$ ($m\ge2$). A morphism from a positive-dimensional projective variety $f\colon X\to\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$ is $m$-direct-sum if $V=U_{x_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus U_{x_m}$ for every $m$ pairwise distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_m$ on $X$, where $U_x\subset V$ is the subspace represented by $f(x)$. We show that $X$ is necessarily a smooth rational curve. When the so-called drill $d(f)$ of $f$ is $1$ or when the rank $k$ is at most $2$, we give complete classifications of $f$ up to the automorphisms of $\mathrm{Gr}(k,V)$. As applications, we classify all so-called skew scrolls in $\mathbb{P}^3$, which completely answers a question of Day. Then we show that if $X\subset \mathbb{P}(V)$ is a smooth, projective, nondegenerate subvariety whose higher-order Terracini locus is empty, then $X$ is the rational normal curve, which strengthens the critical Terracini rigidity discovered by Ballico and Chiantini. By using the same machinery, we also prove a dual version of Terracini rigidity. Finally, we show that $m$-unisolvent systems form an abelian category of finite length and that $7$ is the least diagonal exponent of a simple rank-three $2$-unisolvent system.

papers.title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}. Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily--Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.

papers.title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
papers.abstract: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

papers.title: Soliton resolution conjecture and soliton gases for the Benjamin-Ono equation with infinite-order multisolitons in the sharp well-posedness space
papers.abstract:
We prove the soliton resolution conjecture for infinite-order multisoliton solutions in the sharp well-posedness space $H^s(\mathbb R)$, $s>-\frac12$, and construct soliton gases in $H^{s}(\mathbb R)$ with arbitrary $s\in\mathbb R$, for the Benjamin--Ono equation. In particular, our work addresses two important open problems about inverse spectral for Lax operator, including the problem of spectral characterization of infinite-order multisolitons and that of determining the range of their asymptotic parameters.
  A central ingredient of our work is a spectral decomposition adapted to rough initial data. This extends the global soliton--radiation description to weakly weighted $H^s$ data while allowing infinite negative eigenvalues. Another important ingredient is a continuous norming action that extends finite inverse spectral shifts to gas limits while retaining a full continuous norming weight. Our framework provides a basis for studying infinite-order soliton resolution and the construction and asymptotics of soliton gases for nonlocal equations.

papers.title: Two-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions
papers.authors: Jing Liu, Kainan Xiang, Lang Zou
papers.abstract: It is trivial that $1$-dimensional $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates. Coupier, Henry, Jahnel and K\"oppl proved the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in dimension 2; and then for sufficiently large dimensions, B\"aumler, Jahnel, K\"oppl, Lodewijks, Reeves and T\'obi\'as showed this is still true. In this paper, we verify that the $2$-neighbor lattice percolation percolates in all dimensions $d\ge 3.$

papers.title: Strong approximations for dependent random fields
papers.abstract: We establish strong Gaussian approximations for centered stationary random fields on $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge2$, represented as measurable functions of i.i.d.\ innovations. Under finite $p$th moments, $p>2$, and sufficiently fast decay of spatial dependence, we construct a single coupling of the field with an i.i.d.\ Gaussian field. Its partial sums, scaled by the long-run standard deviation, approximate those of the original field almost surely, uniformly over all rectangular prefixes and all observation scales. Over a cube of side length $n$, the approximation error is $O_{\mathrm{a.s.}}(n^{\max\{d/p,(d-1)/2\}})$ up to logarithmic factors. While $d/p$ is the familiar moment term, the surface term $(d-1)/2$, absent for independent planar arrays, emerges as a cost of dependence, and cannot be removed even for finite-range Gaussian fields. The assumptions accommodate nonlinear and noncausal fields without imposing mixing. The proof combines a permanent dyadic blocking, a local Gaussian coupling in tensor Haar coordinates driven by a Doob martingale with vanishing conditional third moments, and a comparison of the resulting dependent Gaussian blocks with white noise.

papers.title: Scalable Bayesian Quadrature via Operator-Adapted Features
papers.abstract: Kernel methods face two recurrent bottlenecks: the cubic cost of inverting an $n\times n$ kernel matrix, as in kernel ridge regression, and the evaluation of kernel integrals, as required in kernel quadrature. Existing low-rank kernel and Gaussian process approximations primarily address the former bottleneck, but do not control the downstream quadrature error when both the kernel matrix and kernel mean are approximated, particularly when the integrand lies outside the kernel reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We address both challenges through an operator-adapted finite-feature approximation. Specifically, we construct a finite-dimensional working kernel from the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of a second-order differential operator. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting finite-feature estimators in kernel quadrature, with extension to other related kernel methods. Our results show that, with $m \lesssim n$ basis functions, the truncated estimator attains the corresponding benchmark statistical rates. The theory covers fixed/random designs, noisy/noiseless observations, oversmoothing/undersmoothing regimes, and Mat\'ern/Gaussian-type weights. We provide explicit error bounds that quantify the roles of the spectral cutoff, regularization parameter, lengthscale, sampling geometry, and operator boundary condition. We verify the convergence results in numerical experiments.

papers.title: Bound-preserving and mass-conserving projection BCFD methods for incompressible miscible displacement in porous media
papers.authors: Xiaoying Wang, Shusen Xie, Hongfei Fu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze two novel structure-preserving projection schemes for the incompressible miscible displacement problem in porous media. These schemes are specifically designed to preserve two essential physical properties--concentration bounds and the mass balance identity, and are accompanied by a rigorous error analysis for the projection approach. Both schemes are second-order accurate in space but differ in temporal accuracy: one is first-order and the other is second-order. Methodologically, both schemes comprise a prediction step for the concentration variable, based on a second-order modified upwind discretization together with an implicit-explicit finite difference approximation, followed by a projection (or correction) step that enforces the desired physical constraints, namely bounds and mass conservation. For the first-order temporal scheme, the velocity and pressure are solved at the first step on staggered spatial grids with explicit treatment of concentration. In contrast, for the second-order scheme, to ensure well-posedness and to suppress non-physical oscillations in the simulation, the velocity and pressure are solved at the final step with the concentration treated implicitly. A rigorous numerical theoretical framework is established for the first-order scheme, encompassing optimal-order error estimates, stability, and proofs of the existence and uniqueness of the numerical solutions. The numerical analysis framework is further extended to the more involved second-order scheme, and the corresponding theoretical results are briefly outlined. Finally, numerical examples, including some 'real' simulations, are presented to verify the theoretical findings and demonstrate the strong performance of the proposed schemes. In particular, the occurrence of viscous fingering is successfully captured and confirmed by the numerical results.

papers.title: A finiteness result for split exceptional dual pairs
papers.abstract: We prove that big theta lifts have finite length for thirteen split exceptional dual pairs arising from the minimal representations of the split real groups of types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$.

papers.title: Introduction to Separable Simplicial Algebras
papers.authors: Xuan Huang, Garcia Sun, Eric Zhang, James J. Zhang
papers.abstract: We study separable simplicial algebras and Azumaya simplicial algebras.

papers.title: Langevin Dynamics of Non-reciprocally Coupled Spherical Spin Glasses
papers.abstract: We analyze the limiting dynamics of two copies of a disordered mean-field spherical $p$-spin system coupled non-reciprocally to one another and initialized independently of the disorder. We prove that, on every finite time interval, as the system size tends to infinity, the empirical correlation and integrated response functions converge almost surely and in $L^q$ for $q \geq 1$, uniformly in time, to the unique non-random solution of a system of coupled integro-differential equations. For even $p$-spin models, we establish stationarity and exponential decay of the correlation and response functions in the high-temperature regime. In the special case of the spherical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, we derive explicit representations of the limiting correlation and integrated response functions. These representations allow us to characterize the long-time dynamics throughout the full range of temperatures. In particular, we prove the occurrence of aging in the low-temperature regime and fluctuation-dissipation behavior in the high-temperature regime, and provide a separate characterization of the dynamics at the critical temperature.

papers.title: Inflection sets of permutations
papers.authors: Gordon Rojas Kirby, Mariana Smit Vega Garcia
papers.abstract: In 2020, Brualdi and Dahl introduced the discrete derivative $\sigma'(i)=\sigma(i+1)-\sigma(i)$ of a permutation $\sigma\in\Sym_n$. In this paper, we focus on the second derivative of a permutation, $\sigma''(i)=\sigma(i+1)+\sigma(i-1)-2\sigma(i)$, and the inflections it determines. We show that for even $n$, the only distinct permutations with the same second derivative are the identity and its reverse, while for odd $n$, the second derivative is not injective even after excluding them. We then study which sets of pairs of integers $(i,j)$ are the inflection set of some permutation and whether a given set is witnessed in $\Sym_n$ for infinitely many $n$. We show that exactly $14$ permutations of $[n]$ have no inflections when $n\ge5$. For a single inflection $\{(k,m)\}$, we determine all $n$ for which it is witnessed in $\Sym_n$: we prove it is always witnessed, and it is witnessed for only finitely many $n$ if and only if $m\ge 2k+1$. In that case, all such $n$ satisfy $2m-2k+1\le n\le 2m-k+2$ (apart from $k=2$, $n=m+1$), and, perhaps surprisingly, this range has gaps once $k\ge 10$, the smallest occurring at $(k,m,n)=(10,21,30)$. Finally, we characterize maximally inflected permutations, whose second derivative alternates in sign, and show that their number $|\mathcal M_n|$ satisfies $2E_n\le|\mathcal M_n|\le(2/3)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1}\,n!$, where $E_n$ is the Euler zigzag number.

papers.title: Meromorphic solutions of a nonlinear differential-difference equation with two exponential terms
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ and $k\geq 1$ be integers. We study finite order meromorphic solutions of the nonlinear differential-difference equation \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+P_{d}(z,f)=p_{1}(z){\rm e}^{\alpha_{1}z^{k}}+p_{2}(z){\rm e}^{\alpha_{2}z^{k}}, \end{equation*} where $P_{d}(z,f)\not\equiv 0$ is a difference polynomial in $f$ of degree $d\leq n-1$ whose coefficients are small meromorphic functions with respect to $f$, $p_{1},~p_{2}$ are nonzero meromorphic functions with $T(r,p_{j})=o(r^{k})$, $j=1,2$, and $\alpha_{1}\neq\alpha_{2}$ are nonzero constants. We prove that every such solution has order exactly $k$, and obtain sufficient conditions on $n,~d,~k$ for the equation to admit no finite order meromorphic solution with $N(r,\frac{1}{f})=S(r,f)$. Our results extend the known ones from linear exponents $z$ to polynomial exponents $z^{k}$, and replace the linear difference polynomials with the degree restriction $d\leq n-2$ assumed in the literature by general ones of degree $d\leq n-1$. Examples show that the restrictions on $n$ and $d$ are sharp.

papers.title: On the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue Problem
papers.abstract: The classical Blaschke-Lebesgue problem seeks the convex body of minimal volume among all convex bodies of prescribed constant width. In this paper, we investigate the necessary conditions for volume minimizers of the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem via the inverse Gauss map and the inverse Weingarten transformation. We first introduce a generalized support function for hypersurfaces induced by the inverse Gauss map, characterize the Wigner caustic of constant width bodies, and accordingly construct convex bodies of constant width from prescribed functions. Building upon there results and applying the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, we establish a high-dimensional necessary condition: for almost every antipodal pair of a volume minimizer, one point is non-regular; at the other point, the minimum principal curvatures equals the reciprocal of the constant width. As an application, we provide a new proof for the two-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue theorem. Furthermore, we study the dimension-raising construction of Lachand-Robert and Oudet, and prove that every convex body produced by this construction satisfies our necessary condition. Finally, we put forward a conjecture stating that the sequence obtained by iterating this construction starting from a line segment yields minimizers for the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem for all dimensions.

papers.title: Damped stochastic mirror descent for non-smooth ill-posed problems in Banach space
papers.authors: Harshit Bajpai, Gaurav Mittal, Ankik Kumar Giri
papers.abstract: We introduce a damped variant of the stochastic mirror descent method for systems of non-smooth nonlinear ill-posed operator equations in Banach spaces. At each iteration, the method samples a random subset of the equations, performs a mirror-descent step in the dual space with an adaptive step size derived from the discrepancy principle, and applies a damping term that prevents the iterates from drifting away from the initial guess. The scheme accommodates non-smooth forward operators through a family of bounded linear surrogates, admits general $p$-convex penalty functionals which also includes trained convex penalty, allows the noise level to differ from equation to equation, and dispenses with two classical requirements, namely reflexivity of the image space and G\^ateaux differentiability of the forward operator. We study its regularization properties under an \textit{a posteriori} stopping rule by proving first that the iteration terminates after finitely many steps almost surely, and then that the mean-square error of the iterates tends to zero as the noise level vanishes. Numerical experiments on a system of non-smooth semilinear inverse source problems and the identification of a diffusion coefficient confirm the theoretical analysis and shows improved convergence results.

papers.title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Geodesic Computation and Visualization of Geodesic Spheres on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract:
Visualizing geodesic structures associated with general Riemannian metrics is a challenging problem in computational differential geometry. In this work, we present a computational framework for visualizing geodesics and geodesic spheres on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold equipped with the metric $g=\text{diag}(1,x^2,1), x>0$. The associated Christoffel symbols and curvature tensors are computed symbolically, and the resulting geodesic equations are solved using both \texttt{SciPy}'s numerical integration method and a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN). The two solutions are compared to assess the accuracy of the neural network approximation. We further develop geodesic spike diagrams and surface visualizations to illustrate the deformation of geodesic spheres relative to their Euclidean counterparts. Intrinsic Riemannian surface area and volume are estimated numerically using the induced metric and the Riemannian volume density, respectively. For the chosen metric and a geodesic ball of radius one, the computed area and volume are approximately
  $0.362\%$ and $0.364\%$ smaller than the corresponding Euclidean values at the base grid resolution. A grid-refinement study is also performed to examine the sensitivity of these estimates to numerical resolution. The proposed framework demonstrates how symbolic differential geometry, numerical integration, and PINNs can be combined to investigate and visualize geometric structures associated with Riemannian metrics.

papers.title: Hybrid CutFEM-IFEM model for embedded and immersed interfaces with triply-cut cells for the 2D Poisson problem
papers.abstract: We present a hybrid CutFEM--IFEM method for 2D Poisson problems with an immersed fluid--fluid interface and an embedded fluid--solid interface on a single unfitted mesh. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both unfitted finite element methods and immersed interface techniques to handle complex interface geometries and strong discontinuities efficiently. A composite equivalent polynomial representation of the Heaviside and Dirac delta functions is used to integrate on triply-cut cells. Moreover, the IFEM basis functions are enriched with the lift functions exactly representing solution and flux jumps. Numerical examples show optimal convergence for linear and quadratic elements, with accuracy comparable to that of a mesh fitted to both interfaces.

papers.title: A time-map description of the one-dimensional (p,q)-Laplacian Fu\v{c}ik spectrum
papers.abstract:
We study a one-dimensional Fu\v{c}ik-type boundary value problem (BVP) driven by the nonhomogeneous, one-dimensional $(p,q)$-Laplacian, \[
  -\left(|u'|^{p-2}u' + |u'|^{q-2}u'\right)'
  =
  \lambda (u^+)^{p-1}
  -
  \mu (u^-)^{q-1},
  \qquad
  u(0)=u(L)=0,
  \qquad L>0, \] where $1<q<p$ and $\lambda,\mu\in\mathbb{R}$. The problem is asymmetric: the positive component is paired with the $p$-power and the negative component with the $q$-power. This asymmetry prevents the standard homogeneous $p$-Laplacian scaling argument from producing explicit Fu\v{c}ik curves.
  We first prove a quadrant reduction theorem. Any positive nodal interval for a solution forces $\lambda>0$, and any negative nodal interval forces $\mu>0$. Hence, all sign-changing solutions occur for values of $(\lambda,\mu)$ in the positive quadrant. Outside the positive quadrant, only one-sign solutions can occur.
  We also formulate the equation as an autonomous planar system and establish existence and uniqueness for its initial value problem in the positive quadrant. We then impose the second Dirichlet condition through a shooting formulation and show that every zero of a nontrivial Dirichlet solution is simple and isolated. This provides the dynamical foundation for the subsequent construction and gluing of nodal humps of solutions.
  Inside the positive quadrant, we use a classical one-dimensional time-map method to obtain a projected-geometry description of the spectrum, or the set of values of $(\lambda, \mu)$ for which there exist nontrivial solutions. Every nodal solution has a common energy $E>0$ shared by all positive and negative humps.

papers.title: Moments propagation in the Vlasov equation and application to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
papers.authors: Yanqing Wang, Wei Wei, Yulin Ye, Huan Yu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study how the propagation of particle moments depends on the fluid velocity in the Vlasov equation. We present some new moment estimates involving the velocity in this equation. As an application, we establish Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin-type regularity criteria involving only the velocity field for weak solutions of the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov system.

papers.title: Data-driven stochastic asymptotic regularization for ill-posed inverse problems with a posteriori and heuristic stopping
papers.authors: Simran Soni, Harshit Bajpai, Ankik Kumar Giri
papers.abstract: A novel Data-driven STochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{D-STAR}) method is proposed for solving linear and nonlinear ill-posed inverse problems, which incorporates a data-driven drift and a stochastic diffusion mechanism. Both known and unknown noise level cases are accommodated by the method, thereby making the framework applicable to a broader range of practical inverse problems. For known noise level, a modified discrepancy principle is employed, whereas for unknown noise level, a heuristic stopping rule based solely on noisy data is developed. For each stopping rule, an appropriate diffusion term is defined and the well-posedness of the associated stochastic differential equation is demonstrated. The finite termination of \texttt{D-STAR} method under both stopping rules is established and its convergence to the exact solution in the noise-free setting is proved. For the noisy data, stability and the regularization property in the mean-square sense are further established. In addition, the uncertainty quantification of the proposed method and its comparison with the Stochastic Asymptotic Regularization (\texttt{SAR}) method under both rules are provided. Furthermore, it is shown that local minima arising in the Data-Driven Iteratively Regularized Landweber (\texttt{DDIRLI}) method may be escaped. Finally, detailed numerical experiments, including comparisons with existing \texttt{DDIRLI} and \texttt{SAR} methods, are presented on X-ray computed tomography and nonlinear schlieren tomography for both stopping rules, thereby demonstrating the performance of \texttt{D-STAR}.

papers.title: Classification of threshold dynamics for the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous NLS
papers.abstract: We study the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation $i\partial_{t}u+\Delta u+|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{4-2b}{d}}u=0$ in dimensions $d\ge3$. For $\frac12<b<\min\{2,d/2\}$, we prove that every forward-global $H^1$ solution with mass equal to that of the ground state $Q$ either scatters forward or coincides with $e^{it}Q$, up to phase rotation and scaling. As a consequence, every solution with nonradial $H^1$ initial data at the ground-state mass must be global and scatter in both time directions. For $0<b\le\frac12$, analogous rigidity and scattering results hold under an additional finite-variance assumption. The key new ingredients in our proof are a nonradial incoming/outgoing decomposition and exterior frequency-decay estimates, which yield the kinetic-energy localization needed for a localized virial argument.

papers.title: On $q$-middle convolution and generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation
papers.abstract: We investigate higher-order $q$-difference equations obtained by successive applications of a $q$-analogue of addition and the $q$-middle convolution. We construct an $n$-dimensional system of linear $q$-difference equations and derive a single $q$-difference equation whose coefficients are polynomials of degree at most $1$ in the independent variable. Under certain conditions on the parameters, the resulting equation is a generalized $q$-hypergeometric equation of order $n$. We also obtain a multiple Jackson integral representation of solutions and give sufficient conditions for its convergence. By suitably choosing the functions appearing in the integrand and specializing the parameters, we obtain $q$-hypergeometric series solutions of type ${}_n \phi_{n-1}$.

papers.title: A Characterization of Functions on the Integer Lattice That Are L-Extendable through Local Convex Extensions
papers.authors: Ken Yokoyama, Yuni Iwamasa, Kei Kimura
papers.abstract:
L-extendable functions on the integer lattice are functions that admit a $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation; that is, values can be assigned to the additional half-integral points, while keeping the original values at integer points, so that the resulting function is $\frac12$UJ-convex. Various examples of L-extendable functions and their applications are known. A general characterization of L-extendability for functions on the integer lattice, however, remains open.
  In this paper, we study the L-extendability of functions on the integer lattice. We first obtain a necessary condition: L-extendable functions are integrally convex. We then consider a special subclass of L-extendable functions, namely, those whose local convex extensions give L-convex relaxations. This subclass has a useful optimization property: the optimal value of the original function coincides with that of the $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation given by its local convex extension, a property not guaranteed for general $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxations. We characterize this subclass by showing that a function is L-extendable through its local convex extension if and only if it is integrally convex and its restriction to every unit hypercube is D-convex, where D-convexity is a discrete convexity associated with reflected Freudenthal simplicial divisions. This subclass strictly contains the class of D-convex functions. We also give a combinatorial characterization of D-convex subsets of the vertices of a unit hypercube: a set $X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ is D-convex if and only if it is majority-closed and contains a relative opposite pair.

papers.title: A note on a problem of Ma and Chen
papers.abstract: Let $S=(s_1,s_2,\cdots)$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers. For any real number $\alpha>0$, let $S_\alpha=(\lfloor\alpha s_1\rfloor,\lfloor\alpha s_2\rfloor,\cdots)$. We prove that if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for every positive integer $n$, then there exists $0<\alpha<1$ such that $S_\alpha$ is strongly complete. In addition, this gives a negative answer to a problem of Ma and Chen in [Acta Arith. 203 (2022), 307--318]. We also prove that the same result is true if $s_{n+1}\le 2s_n$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: Stability conditions on Calabi-Yau threefolds of type K
papers.abstract: A Calabi-Yau threefold of type K is a free quotient $X=(S\times E)/G$ of the product of a K3 surface and an elliptic curve. We construct a family of geometric Bridgeland stability conditions on $X$ by using Liu's product construction on $S\times E$ and then inducing along the Galois covering. The family has dimension $2h^{1,1}(X)$, and is disjoint from the $\widetilde{\GL}_2^+(\R)$-orbit of Li's stability conditions. These threefolds carry a K3 fibration, and the pushforward of an object from a smooth K3 fiber is (semi)stable if and only if it is (semi)stable on the K3 surface.

papers.title: A lattice order on the complex field
papers.abstract: Birkhoff and Pierce asked in 1956 whether the field $\mathbb{C}$ of complex numbers admits a lattice order compatible with addition and multiplication. We answer the question affirmatively. Using a valuation with value group $\mathbb{Q}$, we construct a positive cone $P$ by a transfinite recursion of countable ordinal length. At each stage we extend a lattice order on a subspace while preserving its lattice operations in the whole field and maintaining multiplicative closure of the ambient positive cone. These subspaces eventually exhaust $\mathbb{C}$. The construction depends on choices of a valuation extension, compatible rational powers and vector-space bases. The cone $P$ contains $1$ and satisfies $\{x\in P\setminus\{0\}:x^{-1}\in P\}=\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$. The induced order is not total: $i$ is incomparable with $0$. For a chosen transcendental element $t$ and $i^2=-1$, one may prescribe $0\vee i=(t+i)/2$ and $0\vee(-i)=(t-i)/2$. Varying the first extension yields exactly $2^{\mathbf c}$ distinct lattice positive cones on $\mathbb{C}$, where $\mathbf c=|\mathbb{C}|$. The count concerns cones as subsets of $\mathbb{C}$.

papers.title: Exact Second-Order Asymptotics for the Gaussian Gray--Wyner Problem
papers.abstract: We revisit the Gray-Wyner problem of lossy compression of bivariate Gaussian sources under the quadratic distortion measure and derive the exact second-order asymptotics. Specifically, we first identify the boundary rate tuples using the explicit first-order asymptotics by Yu (TIT 2023) and then characterize the tradeoff among three second-order coding rates subject to a constraint on the joint excess-distortion probability. Our main contribution is the achievability proof, where we derive a covariance shell covering lemma that is analogous to the type covering lemma for the discrete case. In particular, our covering lemma classifies the source sequences into power shell types via their empirical covariance matrix. For each such power shell type, we derive sufficient conditions on the compression rates so that covering within distortion levels are achievable. Finally, asymptotical analysis via the Berry-Esseen theorem yields the desired result.

papers.title: Tight Stationarity Transfer and Repeatability for Inexact Proximal-Gradient Methods
papers.abstract: Proximal-gradient methods are widely used for composite optimization, but inexact proximal updates introduce a residual in the proximal optimality condition, complicating the analysis of how stationarity changes across a step. We study this question for composite objectives consisting of a smooth convex term and a possibly nonsmooth weakly convex term, focusing on the relationship between the directional-stationarity measures at the input and output points of an inexact proximal-gradient step. We first establish separate input and output bounds, but their combination can yield a conservative estimate because their worst-case residual directions may differ. By exploiting the magnitude and orientation of this shared residual, we establish tight joint bounds and derive an exact one-step stationarity-transfer factor that strictly improves the estimate from separate bounds in the short-step regime. We also identify the precise residual-tolerance threshold for finite uniform stationarity transfer. A further distinction emerges over multiple steps: endpoint worst cases can repeat over arbitrarily many iterations, whereas interior worst cases cannot persist across two consecutive steps, yielding strict two-step submultiplicativity. These results also provide principled tolerance-selection rules, descent estimates, and stationarity-complexity guarantees for inexact proximal-gradient methods.

papers.title: Determination of weight enumerators of binary extremal self-dual codes of length 60
papers.abstract: We construct three binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ with weight enumerators for which no binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$ were previously known to exist. This completes the determination of the weight enumerators that occur for binary extremal self-dual codes of length $60$.

papers.title: Sizes of cross-intersecting families
papers.abstract:
The size of cross-intersecting families ${\cal F}_1, \dots, {\cal F}_d$ is usually measured by the sum or the product of the sizes $|{\cal F}_i|$. These two natural size functions have different extremal structures, and different techniques have been developed for them.
  We introduce the cross-degree of a size function and show that the potential extremal structures of maximum cross-intersecting families are the same for all size functions of finite cross-degree, including the sum and the product. Our main tool is a strengthened form of the generating family method of Ahlswede--Khachatrian, based on standard generating families and on local modifications of cross-intersecting families, which we call mutations. It treats two completely different types of extremal structures in a unified way and, unlike the original method, needs shifting in only one step.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on Torsional Rigidity of Metric Graphs with Signed Delta-Vertex Strengths
papers.abstract: We study torsional rigidity on finite compact connected metric graphs with real \(\delta\)-vertex strengths in the regime of strictly positive torsion. For a fixed total length \(L>0\), let \(I_+\) be the sum of the positive strengths and \(I_-\) the sum of the magnitudes of the negative strengths, with \(I_+>I_-\). We determine the sharp infimum and the exact threshold for a finite universal supremum. The supremum is finite precisely when \(I_-<I_+/(1+LI_+)\). In this regime, an interval with strengths \(I_+\) and \(-I_-\) at opposite endpoints attains the sharp Saint--Venant bound. At and beyond the threshold, torsional rigidity is unbounded even among three-vertex paths with the same data and strictly positive torsion. The sharp infimum is \(L^2/(I_+-I_-)\) throughout the range \(I_+>I_-\ge0\). It is not attained by any finite graph and is approached by graphs with two vertices joined by increasingly many parallel edges of equal length, preserving both strength totals separately. A vertex-matrix formulation and explicit path examples clarify the relation between strength placement, spectral positivity, and solvability.

papers.title: The Characteristics of Finite Projections of Certain Stochastic Processes and Queues
papers.abstract: This thesis studies finite projections of transient regenerative processes, constructed by conditioning regeneration cycles to be finite. It develops comparisons between the original and projected laws, including finite-time bounds and best-approximation properties for specified metrics and comparison classes. Applications concern birth-and-death processes, Markov chains and semi-Markov processes, with explicit queueing examples. Structural results describe projections associated with different regeneration states, invariant measures and connections with Martin boundary kernels. The thesis also studies reconstruction of birth-and-death rates from passage-time laws and continued-fraction representations of Laplace-Stieltjes transforms for skip-free semi-Markov processes, together with truncation-error bounds. This is a corrected English edition of a Romanian doctoral thesis completed in 1998 and defended in 1999. The preface distinguishes the historical work from corrections and later additions made for this edition.

papers.title: Maximal regular subsemigroups containing the group of units of transformation semigroups that preserve a uniform equivalence relation with two classes
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a nonempty set and $E$ an equivalence relation on $X$. The semigroup $T_E(X)$ consists of all transformations on $X$ that preserve $E$. Although the collection of all regular elements of $T_E(X)$ is not, in general, a subsemigroup, we investigate maximal regular subsemigroups of $T_E(X)$ containing the group of units $G_E(X)$. We construct two such maximal regular subsemigroups, denoted by $\mathcal{M}_1$ and $\mathcal{M}_2$, and show that their maximality holds in full generality for an arbitrary set $X$ and an arbitrary equivalence relation $E$ that is neither the identity relation nor the universal relation on $X$ (whether finite or infinite, uniform or non-uniform). Furthermore, when $X$ is finite and $E$ is a uniform equivalence relation with exactly two classes of cardinality at least $2$, we provide a complete classification by proving that they are the only maximal regular subsemigroups containing $G_E(X)$.

papers.title: Uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of nodal states for a mixed-power scalar field equation
papers.abstract:
We consider the scalar field equation $$\begin{cases} -\Delta u+u+\lambda |u|^{q-1}u =\mu |u|^{p-1}u, & x\in\mathbb R^n,\\[2mm] u(x)\to 0, & |x|\to\infty, \end{cases}$$
  where $n\geq3$, $1<q<p<(n+2)/(n-2)$, and $\lambda,\mu>0$. We study uniqueness and radial nondegeneracy of its sign-changing radial bound states. The proof combines a comparison argument for the shooting variation across nodal intervals with uniform compactness estimates for families of bounded nodal number and continuation in a normalized parameter. We show that, for every integer $k\geq1$, fixing the centre and requiring $u(0)>0$ leaves exactly one radial bound state with $k$ nodes. Its radial linearized operator has trivial kernel in the radial space. For each fixed $k$, the corresponding normalized solutions form a global $C^1$ branch.

papers.title: Asymptotic Formula of the Lifespan of Classical Solutions to 1D Quasilinear Wave Equations
papers.abstract:
We study the lifespan \(T^*(\varepsilon)\) of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem
  for the one-dimensional quasilinear wave equation
  $u_{tt}-(c(u)^2u_x)_x=0$,
  with initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$.
  We assume that $c'(\theta)\sim a|\theta|^{p-2}$ as $\theta \to 0$,
  where \(a>0\) and \(p>3\) or $p=2$.
  We obtain explicit asymptotic formulas for
  $T^*(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.
  We treat both the case $\psi \in L^1(\mathbb R)$
  and the case
  $\psi=\psi_1+\Braket{x}^{-\alpha}$,
  where \(\psi_1\in L^1(\mathbb R)\) and \(0<\alpha\le1\).
  Our results identify the dependence of the lifespan scale on the decay exponent,
  including the borderline case $\alpha=1$.
  The proof combines Riccati equations along characteristics
  with a scaling argument inspired by Lindblad.

papers.title: The Minimax Complexity of Federated Optimization under Interpolation: The Role of Oracle Models
papers.authors: Kirill Novoselov, Yuriy Dorn, Darina Dvinskikh, Alexander Gasnikov

papers.title: Crescent configurations in three dimensions
papers.abstract: A crescent configuration of $n$ points in $\mathbb R^d$ is a set in general position whose distinct pairwise distances have multiplicities $1,\ldots,n-1$. We construct such a configuration in $\mathbb R^3$ for every $n\geq3$, giving a uniform bound of three for the minimum dimension. The proof uses equally spaced parameters on a short circular helix and Rolle's theorem. We also give explicit integer-coordinate configurations with $O(n\log n)$ bits per coordinate, and prove that every finite initial segment of the sequence $(\cos j,\sin j,2j)_{j\geq0}$ of length at least three is a crescent configuration.

papers.title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
papers.authors: Miguel E. P\'erez Ibarra, Jaziel Flores Rodr\'iguez
papers.abstract: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.

papers.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
papers.abstract: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.

papers.title: An analogue of $\Gamma$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $\Gamma$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.

papers.title: A logarithmic error term for subset sums of zero-sum-free sets
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the minimum number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free $k$-element set, where the minimum is taken over all finite abelian groups. We prove $f(k)\ge \frac{k^2}{2}-13k\log(k+1)-116k$. Together with the classical upper bound, this gives $f(k)=k^2/2+O(k\log k)$, with the optimal leading coefficient. As a consequence, the Olson constant of every finite abelian group $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ol}(G)\le\sqrt{2|G|}+O(\log|G|)$. The argument combines a triangular lower bound for repeated supports, a count using blocks of two and three copies, and a greedy expansion argument. No restriction is imposed on the order of the group or on the stabilizer of the set of subset sums.

papers.title: A five-species counterexample to the Hofbauer--Kon--Saito conjecture on qualitative permanence
papers.abstract: Hofbauer, Kon and Saito (J. Math. Biol. 2008) showed that a Lotka-Volterra interaction matrix $A$ with negative diagonal can be qualitatively permanent only if (C1) every cycle of length $\ge 2$ of $A$ is nonpositive and (C2) every negative cycle contains exactly one negative entry. They conjectured that these conditions are also sufficient, and proved this for $n\le 3$. We give a $5\times 5$ integer matrix with seven nonzero off-diagonal entries that satisfies (C1) and (C2) but is not qualitatively permanent.
