For an explicit integer growth vector the system has an interior equilibrium, and an asymptotically stable heteroclinic cycle on the boundary of the orthant attracts an open set of interior orbits. Adding non-interacting species gives counterexamples for every $n\ge 5$. The interactions form a one-way feedback loop (two one-sided benefits and one one-sided harm) together with a predator of two prey. The verification is elementary except for one heteroclinic connection, which lies in a face that is not Volterra-Lyapunov stable. For it we prove a connection lemma based on invasion graphs.

papers.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

papers.title: Is Dual Polarization Always Optimal? Unlocking New Spatial Degrees of Freedom
papers.authors: Adrian Agustin, Xavier Mestre, Carlos Su\'arez Garc\'ia, Alberto Pellon Sancho
papers.abstract: Current wireless communication systems are designed based on channel models obtained under the assumption of far-field operation, where electromagnetic waves can be approximated by a planar wave. In those circumstances, dualpolarized antennas seem to be the optimal solution for maximizing the spectral efficiency. However, the recent research on XLMIMO systems represents a paradigm shift, since communication may take place in the near-field and an additional degree of freedom can be achieved. This work presents a modular, lowcost tripolarized antenna at 2.4 GHz band, that is used to experimentally validate theoretical findings about tripolarized antennas, which are commonly based on orthogonal infinitesimal dipoles. The evaluation is carried out in two indoor scenarios and one outdoor scenario, with transmitter comprising multiple tripolarized antennas and a receiver equipped with a single tripolarized antenna. We show that this type of antenna can increase the number of spatial streams up to three or extend the region where terminals are able to achieve two spatial streams

papers.title: Phase-Space Realization of Stochastic Multivalued Dynamics with Gyroscopic Subdifferential Coupling
papers.authors: Ioana Ciotir, Andreea Negrut-Grajdeanu, Dan Goreac, Eduard Rotenstein
papers.abstract: We introduce a new framework for stochastic variational inequalities with oblique reflections generated by non-symmetric matrix coefficients. The loss of symmetry fundamentally changes the structure of the reflected dynamics: besides the dissipative component, it produces a genuinely gyroscopic component describing rotational effects that are invisible to the associated energy forms. To capture this hidden component, we consider planar obstacle problems and we lift the dynamics to an extended phase-space system, where the dissipative and gyroscopic mechanisms are naturally separated. This leads to a new notion of solution, for which we establish existence and uniqueness. The resulting framework allows for genuinely rotated reflections, which can lead to angle-controlled rotations.

papers.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
papers.abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.

papers.title: The residue field as an infinite syzygy
papers.abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m},k)$ be a commutative Noetherian ring which is either local or positively graded over the field $k$. We provide a method based on liftings for constructing free coresolutions of $k$ over $R$. We apply this method to twisted trivial extensions of the node $k[u,v]/(uv)$ to build a family of positively graded $k$-algebras of dimension $1$ over which $k$ is an infinite graded syzygy, resolving an open question of Iyengar in the negative. We also prove a formula for alternating sums of lengths of Ext modules when $R$ is positively graded, and use it to show that a graded free coresolution of $k$ cannot dualize to a resolution unless $R$ is Artinian Gorenstein.

papers.title: Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of Perelman's pseudolocality theorem for Ricci flow, which does not rely on Perelman's Harnack-type inequality. The key step is an estimate relating initial local $\mu$-entropy to pointed Nash entropy at later spacetime points. The argument also works for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian flow, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature lower bound. As a consequence, we can also prove the quantitative rigidity results concerning pointed Nash entropy due to Hein-Naber and Bamler for such geometric flows. In the appendix, we also show that the other results in Bamler's work (arXiv:2008.07093), when suitably modified, remain valid for Laplacian flow with bounded torsion. These include log-Sobolev/Poincar\'{e} inequality for conjugate heat kernel measure, heat kernel estimates, and dependence of the pointed Nash entropy on its basepoint.

papers.title: Stability of a Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation
papers.authors: Sun-Sook Jin, Soon-Mo Jung, Yang-Hi Lee
papers.abstract: We establish the generalized Hyers-Ulam stability of the Fr\'{e}chet-type functional equation \begin{align*} \sum_{\emptyset \neq I \subset \{ 1, 2, \ldots, n+1 \}} (-1)^{|I|-n+1} f \Bigg( \sum_{i \in I} x_i \Bigg) = 0 \end{align*} in the sense of G\u{a}vru\c{t}a.

papers.title: Nice Partitions of Signed-Graphic Arrangements Are Inductive Factorizations
papers.authors: Weikang Liang, Suijie Wang, Yue Zhou
papers.abstract: Nice partitions of hyperplane arrangements give tensor factorizations of Orlik-Solomon algebras as graded vector spaces. In general, a hyperplane arrangement admitting a nice partition need not be free. In this paper, we consider signed-graphic arrangements, the subarrangements of type-$B$ Weyl arrangements, over fields of characteristic different from $2$. We prove that every nice partition of a signed-graphic arrangement is an inductive factorization and hence that the arrangement is free, with nonzero exponents given by the part sizes. In particular, Terao's conjecture holds for the intersection lattices of signed-graphic arrangements admitting a nice partition.

papers.title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.

papers.title: Using delays for prescribed-time static output feedback stabilization of LTI controllable and observable systems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a stabilization problem: can every controllable and observable LTI system be stabilized by static output feedback? To the best of our knowledge, we provide, for the first time, a solution to this problem. Furthermore, the proposed design achieves prescribed-time convergence to the origin, with the convergence time arbitrarily assigned a priori and independently of the initial condition. Two static output-feedback methods are developed. The first employs multiple artificial output delays with smooth time-varying gains and provides an explicit gain construction for every controllable and observable LTI system, based on a generalized controllability--observability Gramian introduced in this paper. The second combines constant-gain feedback of the current output with time-varying-gain feedback of a single artificially delayed output and also applies to every controllable and observable LTI system. Its simpler structure requires auxiliary parameters whose existence is guaranteed but whose explicit construction is not provided for general MIMO systems; for SISO systems, the constant current-output gain can be readily selected. The multiple-delay design is further extended to known bounded and fast-varying (without any constraints on the delay derivative) measurement delays, yielding fixed-time stabilization under a corresponding rank condition, with an assignable settling-time bound greater than three times the delay bound. For unknown constant measurement delays, fixed-time stabilization is established for systems with nilpotent state matrices. A numerical implementation is also presented. Numerical examples involving nonminimum-phase, flexible-structure, and cart--pole systems illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Backward Pseudolocality of $G_2$-Laplacian Flow
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a new estimate on the time-derivative of pointed Nash entropy and use it to give a new proof of backward pseudolocality for Ricci flow. The proof does not rely on Bamler's compactness theorem and structure theory concerning limits of Ricci flows. Our methods also work for other reasonable geometric flows, like the $G_2$-Laplacian, at a scale depending on its deviation from Ricci flow and its scalar curvature.

papers.title: Logarithmic fractional Hardy inequalities
papers.abstract:
We establish sharp fractional Hardy inequalities in the critical regimes $sp=d$ and $sp=1$, with explicit logarithmic weight functions. In the whole-space setting, for $p>d\ge 1$, $sp=d$, we prove that \begin{equation*}
  \int_{\mathbb R^d} \int_{\mathbb R^d} \frac{|u(x)-u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{2d}}\,dx\,dy \geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}\right)^p \int_{B_R}|u(x)|^p W_{p,d,R}(x)\,dx, \end{equation*} for $u\in C_c(B_R)$, where $W_{p,d,R}$ is a logarithmic-type weight and the constant is sharp. We also show that the corresponding inequality with the simpler weight $|x|^{-d}(\log(R/|x|))^{-p}$ cannot hold with any positive constant. Furthermore, we derive two-sided estimates and asymptotic formulae for $W_{p,d,R}$, including its limiting connection with the classical Hardy inequality. In the half-space $\mathbb{R}^{d}_{+}$, we establish an analogous sharp fractional Hardy inequality in the critical case $sp=1$, with an explicit logarithmic weight depending on the distance to the boundary. We also investigate the asymptotic behaviour of this weight, obtaining estimates that describe its behaviour near the boundary. These results elucidate the role of logarithmic weights in critical fractional Hardy inequalities in both whole-space and half-space settings.

papers.title: Inverse Scattering of Periodic Surfaces with Multilayer Superlenses: Perturbation Analysis and Resolution Enhancement
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous mathematical analysis of inverse scattering for periodic surfaces through a multilayer superlens. Using the transformed field expansion, we derive a highly explicit reconstruction formula. We theoretically prove that under perfect matching, the reconstruction factor is independent of the number of layers and depends solely on the total material thicknesses, achieving uniform boundedness when the slab thickness dominates. By establishing first-order perturbation formulas and high-frequency asymptotics, we quantify how small material losses induce exponential amplification of high-frequency errors. Crucially, we show that increasing the number of layers substantially reduces this amplification coefficient. Consequently, for fixed total thicknesses, multilayer structures offer significantly improved stability and extended resolution limits for subwavelength reconstruction.

papers.title: On the Witt liftability of quasi-F-split Calabi--Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that a quasi-$F$-split strict Calabi--Yau variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$ admits a smooth projective lifting over $W(k)$ if $p\geq d-1$, or if $p=d-2$ and $H^0(X,T_X)=0$. We also prove $W_3(k)$-liftability in odd characteristic.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Constructions of Asymptotically Good Random Access Codes from Linear Codes
papers.abstract: Random access codes (RACs) encode a $q$-ary input string into fewer $q$-ary symbols while allowing any requested input symbol to be recovered with probability above the random-guessing value $1/q$. However, it remains unclear what asymptotic guarantees on compression and recovery probability should be required of RACs. We address this question by introducing the notion of asymptotically good RACs and give two polynomial-time constructions. First, an $[n,k,d]_q$ linear code with $d\ge2$, together with an encoder based on its orthogonal-array property, yields an $(n,n-k)_q$-RAC with worst-case decoding success probability \[ p_{\rm wc}=\frac{1}{q}+\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)\frac{d-2}{n}. \] These OA-RACs are asymptotically good whenever the underlying linear codes are, and Garcia--Stichtenoth algebraic-geometry codes give a concrete polynomial-time realization. Second, a direct-sum strategy using OA-RACs derived from $q$-ary Hamming codes and the trivial $(1,1)_q$-RAC yields asymptotically good RAC families at every prescribed RAC rate $R_{\rm RAC}=(n-k)/n\in(0,1)$. Numerical results demonstrate favorable finite-length performance of both constructions.

papers.title: Tur\'an number of three disjoint cliques of arbitrary sizes
papers.authors: Alexandr Kostochka, Dadong Peng, Zimu Xiang, Liang Zhang
papers.abstract: The Tur\'an number $\rm ex(n,H)$ of a given graph $H$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph. In this paper, for all $p\ge q\ge r\ge 2$ and $n\geq p+q+r$, we determine the exact value of $\rm ex(n,K_p\cup K_q\cup K_r)$ and describe all extremal graphs.

papers.title: Optimal approximation error approach in Bayesian inverse problems
papers.abstract: In many inverse problems, evaluating the forward operator is computationally expensive, making it common practice to accelerate inference with a less costly approximate model. However, such approximations introduce unwanted bias and must be carefully accounted for to ensure the reliability of the solution. This phenomenon is particularly pronounced in Bayesian inference, where accurate posterior characterisation typically requires a large number of forward model evaluations. In this paper, we focus on the approximation error model (AEM), which compensates for the modelling error by adjusting the likelihood density. More precisely, AEM incorporates the model error into the additive Gaussian noise distribution. A central challenge in this approach is how to choose the modified noise mean and covariance in a principled way. To address this, we propose a new framework, optimal approximation error (OAE) which determines the noise model by minimising the expected information loss, measured via the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the true and approximate posterior distributions. We show that the standard enhanced error approach (EEA) is recovered as the minimiser of the expected divergence between likelihoods rather than posteriors and develop OAE as a direct alternative targeting posterior accuracy. We establish bi-convexity of the OAE objective, introduce a regularised, provably convergent proximal alternating minimisation scheme, and derive closed-form expressions in the Gaussian linear setting. We further show that OAE estimates computed from empirical training data are statistically consistent. Numerical experiments on a linear CT problem and a nonlinear Darcy-flow problem show that OAE improves posterior accuracy relative to both the uncorrected and EEA-corrected likelihoods.

papers.title: Nevanlinna Theory on Berkovich Curves
papers.abstract: We develop a value distribution theory for finite analytic morphisms between proper connected quasi-smooth Berkovich curves over a complete algebraically closed non-Archimedean field. The central tool is a multi-tail Dirichlet Green function on finite truncations of a generalized skeleton, which makes non-Archimedean potential theory on skeleta compatible with global Nevanlinna asymptotics. Using it, we prove the first main theorem as an exact identity relating the characteristic, counting, and proximity functions. For logarithmic targets we establish a second main theorem in both ramified and level-one truncated forms. The defect relation is also given. The theory provides a Berkovich-analytic framework for non-Archimedean value distribution, bridging classical Nevanlinna theory and its $p$-adic counterpart.

papers.title: MacKay-Neal Codes for DNA Channels under Block-MAP Decoding
papers.abstract: We prove achievability below the symmetric information rate (SIR) under block maximum a posteriori (MAP) decoding for a fixed-degree MacKay-Neal (MN) socket ensemble on the quaternary insertion-deletion-substitution channel used to model DNA reads. For every integer $\ell\ge4$, the $(\ell,3,3)$ socket ensemble, with one transmitted bit fixed and an independent uniform known offset, has limiting rate $r_\star=6/\ell$ bits per stored nucleotide. If the joint SIR $J_t$ of a fixed number $t$ of reads under independent, uniformly distributed input nucleotides exceeds $r_\star$, the ensemble-average full extended-word block error is $O(1/n)$, and deterministic graph-offset sequences attain the same limiting rate and message-average error bound. This result concerns the discrete rate family $6/\ell$, not arbitrary rates approaching a given SIR. The channel permits arbitrarily many insertions and unbounded drift, with no alignment supplied to the receiver. The proof combines established MN parity and distance estimates with a strict arbitrary-candidate-list bound and a list construction that accounts for hidden output boundaries.

papers.title: A $\pi / 4$ lower bound for random access in symmetric linear ensembles under optimal decoding
papers.authors: Daniella Bar-Lev, Ohad Elishco, Ryan Gabrys
papers.abstract: We study the expected number of random linear observations required to recover a prescribed information symbol. For ensembles with uniformly random supports, independently sampled nonzero coefficients, and uniformly bounded column weights, we prove that the asymptotic normalized expected recovery time is at least $\pi/4$ under optimal decoding. The result holds over finite or infinite fields and extends the lower bound previously established for binary fully symmetric codes under peeling decoding. For singleton - pair observations, we determine the exact limiting expectation and show that optimal and peeling decoding have the same limit, independently of the field and coefficient distribution. The minimum within this family is approximately $0.793933445$, which explicit constructions attain asymptotically over every fixed finite field.

papers.title: Davenport constants with growing binary rank
papers.abstract: We study the correction to the standard lower bound $D^*$ for Davenport constants of finite abelian groups with a growing elementary two-component. For every fixed nontrivial abelian $p$-group $H$ of odd order, we prove $D(H\oplus C_2^r)=D^*(H\oplus C_2^r)+(D(H)-1)\log_2 r+O_H(1)$, with a uniform version for varying $H$. For $C_3\oplus C_2^r$, we determine exact values on explicit infinite intervals of ranks. More generally, the correction is logarithmic or smaller precisely when the fixed group has at most one odd prime divisor. We show that the two-primary part affects the logarithmic coefficient: for $C_{24}\oplus C_2^r$, the ratio $(D-D^*)/\log_2 r$ has limsup at least $2.4933231\ldots>2$, whereas for $C_3\oplus C_2^r$ the limit is $2$. These upper limiting coefficients are unbounded even with the odd prime fixed. The proofs use binary codes and finite-field Fourier analysis.

papers.title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver Empowered Hybrid Non-orthogonal Multiple Access
papers.authors: Xinya Shen, Zheng Chu, David Chieng, Chiew Foong Kwong, Qihao Peng, Pei Xiao, Theodoros Tsiftsis, Jianyue Zhu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel uplink Hybrid Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) architecture assisted by Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers (RAQRs) to improve energy efficiency by addressing the physical constraints of atomic sensing. We formulate a joint optimization problem encompassing phase measurements and multi-user power allocation to minimize the total transmit power. This problem is particularly challenging due to the non-linear amplitude-only observations of atomic vapor cells. To decomposes the resulting non-convexity, we develop a hierarchical three-layer decomposition optimization framework that systematically decouples the global problem. The inner layer employs a customized Expectation Maximization-Gerchberg-Saxton (EM-GS) algorithm to resolve phase ambiguity and estimate equivalent channel gains. The middle layer derives closed-form optimal power allocation solutions via Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions. The outer layer utilizes linear Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) detection for high-reliability signal recovery. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over conventional RF-based Hybrid NOMA. Notably, the atomic architecture achieves approximately a 93% reduction in total power consumption compared to Orthogonal Multiple Access (OMA) baselines while maintaining strict backward compatibility, thereby laying a solid foundation for practical deployment in next-generation green communication networks.

papers.title: Notes on Orlicz Spaces and Interpolation
papers.abstract: Orlicz spaces are a natural generalization of classical Lebesgue spaces. They are built upon convex growth functions and provide a flexible framework for studying integrability conditions beyond power-type behavior. In this survey paper, we present the basic definitions, main properties, and fundamental results concerning Orlicz spaces, and also discuss the Marcinkiewicz interpolation result for Orlicz spaces.

papers.title: Sheaves on quoric manifolds
papers.abstract: Quoric manifolds are quaternionic analogues of quasitoric manifolds introduced by Hopkinson. Given a quoric manifold over a simple polytope, we study the stratification induced by the faces of the polytope. We then show that the equivariant derived category of constructible sheaves with respect to the face stratification is equivalent to the derived category of constructible DG-modules over a DG-algebra defined on the orbit space. Finally, we prove that the associated DG-algebra is formal.

papers.title: Class groups of polynomial Krull domains
papers.abstract: A polynomial Krull domain is a Krull domain contained between $\mathbb Z[X]$ and $\mathbb Q[X]$. The domains of this class are precisely the Noetherian integrally closed domains between these polynomial rings by a result of Heinzer, and they have been recently classified by Chang and the second author of this paper as rings of polynomials which are integer-valued over a finite set of ultrametric balls in $\mathbb C_p$, as $p$ ranges through the set of primes in $\mathbb Z$. We show here that every ideal class of a polynomial Krull domain contains a prime ideal. Furthermore, given such a Krull domain $R$, we prove that there exists a polynomial Krull domain $R'$ that is Dedekind, contains $R$ and has the same class group as $R$.

papers.title: Tensor products of 2-representations
papers.abstract: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.

papers.title: Finite-volume and thermodynamic-limit lower bounds for the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model via the Lieb--Yamazaki method
papers.authors: Maciej Janowicz, Joanna Kaleta, Filip Krzy\.zewski, Andrzej Zembrzuski
papers.abstract: We derive rigorous lower bounds on the ground-state energy of the coherently driven Bose--Hubbard model using a Lieb--Yamazaki positive-operator decomposition. The resulting quadratic bounding Hamiltonian is diagonalized by displacement and Bogoliubov transformations, yielding explicit stability conditions and finite-volume bounds in arbitrary dimension. We establish the thermodynamic-limit energy density and characterize the excitation spectrum of the bounding Hamiltonian. We also derive its Gaussian-state observables, including filling, number fluctuations, and second-order correlations, and identify regimes of antibunching and sub-Poissonian statistics. Numerical calculations assess the tightness of the bounds across representative parameter regimes.

papers.title: Stable Dynamical Mass Transportation via port-Hamiltonian Structure
papers.authors: Dongjun Wu, Yankai Lin, Gang Feng
papers.abstract: Dynamical optimal mass transportation over nonlinear systems is often hindered by the curse of dimensionality and open-loop implementation. We propose an alternative framework that sacrifices exact optimality in favor of stability, robustness, and scalability. We use a stochastic port-Hamiltonian system as a reference model. Under suitable structural assumptions, we show that its density converges asymptotically to a prescribed steady-state distribution. We then shape a deterministic nonlinear system into a compatible port-Hamiltonian form and add a local density-feedback term so that its closed-loop continuity equation matches the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation of the reference model. The resulting feedback drives a broad class of initial distributions to the target distribution. Because the density term is local at the particle level, the controller admits decentralized implementation and avoids solving a global finite-horizon transport problem online. Nonlinear examples and simulations illustrate the method. For linear systems with Gaussian targets, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for stabilizing density feedback and give explicit controller constructions.

papers.title: Hilbert functions of filtered graphical zonotopal algebras
papers.authors: Boris Shapiro, Ilya Smirnov, Arkady Vaintrob
papers.abstract:
The external zonotopal algebra of a graph is generated by nilpotent vertex elements $X_v$ and determines the graphical matroid after deleting loops. Replacing these generators by $f(X_v)$, for a power series $f(u)$, and filtering by word length gives a family of filtered algebras. We extend filtered graph reconstruction from simple graphs to loopless multigraphs without isolated vertices when the linear and quadratic coefficients of $f$ are nonzero. Nevertheless, even the family of Hilbert functions indexed by all polynomials does not determine the graph: two nonisomorphic ten-vertex trees have the same Hilbert function for every $f$, answering a question of Nenashev and the first author. For forests and series whose first nonconstant term has degree $k\ge 2$, we give a monomial presentation indexed by partial score vectors whose entries are divisible by $k$.
  For normalized nondegenerate functions, a boundary-state calculus gives a common finite parameter partition for all trees of a fixed maximum degree. In maximum degrees three and four, exact symbolic calculations identify these partitions by the vanishing of specified coefficients of $f^{-1}$. For functions with nonzero quadratic coefficient, the same calculus gives explicit recurrences for attached or connecting paths. Symmetry reductions, including commuting actions of $sl_2$ and the symmetric group on the leaves of a star, determine the generic Hilbert series of stars and two-vertex multigraphs and also apply to parallel edges and leaves in larger graphs. For cycles, we determine the highest-degree term and the first three nonconstant coefficients in the stable range. A weighted independent-set formula describes the trace sequence in the remaining conjecture.

papers.title: On isomorphisms of tetravalent Cayley graphs over generalized quaternion groups
papers.authors: Lele Jin, Li Ma, Wei Meng
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and $S$ be a subset of $G$ with $1\not\in S$. $S$ is called a $CI$-subset of $G$ if for any $T\subset G$, whenever $Cay (G,S)\cong Cay (G,T)$, there is an element $\sigma\in Aut(G)$ such that $S^{\sigma}=T$. For a positive integer $m$, $G$ is called an $m$-$CI$-group if all subsets $S$ of $G \setminus \{1\}$ with $|S|\leq m$ and $S^{-1}=S$ are $CI$-subsets. In this paper, we show that the generalized quaternion group of order $4n$ is a $4$-$CI$-group if and only if $n$ is odd.

papers.title: Arithmetic classification of the Dirichlet eigenvalues for a one-dimensional nonlocal $p$-Laplacian problem
papers.abstract: We classify the arithmetic nature of the Dirichlet eigenvalues of a homogeneous nonlocal one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian problem with power-type nonlinearity $|u|^{q-2}u$. For rational $p,q>1$, either all eigenvalues are algebraic or all are transcendental. Algebraicity holds exactly when the interval length is an algebraic multiple of a distinguished scale determined by a beta value. This scale is transcendental. When $p=q$, the criterion reduces to algebraicity of the interval length divided by $\pi$,independently of the rational exponent.

papers.title: EKR Results for Cuspidal Representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_\chi$ be a cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_2(q)$ is \emph{$t$-intersecting} if $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\{v \in \mathcal{S}_\chi: g_1v = g_2v\} \geqslant t$ for any $g_1, g_2 \in S$. In this paper, we determine $\max{|S|}$ where $S$ is $t$-intersecting.

papers.title: On the motivic approach to the Abhyankar rectifiability problem and concrete rectifications
papers.authors: A. S. Frolov, I. S. Dorofeev
papers.abstract: We study closed embeddings of the complex affine line into affine three-space. We prove that, for every such embedding, the complete-intersection normal map identifies the $\mathbb{A}^1$-fundamental sheaf of its complement with $\mathbf{K}_2^{\mathrm{MW}}$. The proof compares torsors under arbitrary strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant group sheaves. A nodal projection expresses a torsor by a normal parameter and finitely many node parameters. Extension across the node axes gives equations for the latter. Their correction terms increase a nilpotent filtration generated by the Milnor-Witt symbols of the branch-height differences. We deduce the vanishing of the first Alexander sheaf of every complex embedded line. We also construct polynomial rectifications using finite inverses and affine modifications, including rectifications of the Shastri trefoil and a harmonic figure-eight over $\mathbb{Z}[a]/(a^2-a+1)$, with arbitrary base change. The companion repository (https://github.com/qft98romanov-hash/abhyankar-moh-trefoil) contains explicit rectifiers, their inverses, proofs, and symbolic checks. We prove that a normal map with a polynomial section and geometric generic affine-line fiber is a coordinate projection. We formulate the remaining rectifiability and descent questions; the general complex rectifiability problem is not settled here. An appendix treats other fields, normal orientations, and arithmetic descent.

papers.title: Lyubeznik numbers of the face rings of simplicial posets
papers.abstract: For a simplicial poset $P$, Stanley assigned the face ring $A_P$, which is the quotient of the polynomial ring $S:=K[t_x \mid x \in P \setminus \{\widehat{0} \}]$ by the ideal $I_P$. This is a generalization of Stanley-Reisner rings, but the grading of $S$ is more involved. Building on our previous paper, we further develop and complete the study of the local cohomology modules $H_{I_P}^i(S)$. In our categorical framework, $\mathrm{Ext}_S(A_P, S)$ ``encodes" all the information of $H_{I_P}^i(S)$. We treat $H_{I_P}^i(S)$ in a reasonably explicit way. In particular, Lyubeznik numbers $\lambda_{i,j}(A_P)$ can be simply expressed in terms of $[\mathrm{Ext}_S^*(\mathrm{Ext}_S^*(A_P,S), S)]_\bf{0}$, and depend only on the homeomorphism class of the underlying space of the CW complex associated with $P$ and $\mathrm{char}(K)$.

papers.title: A fully nonlinear parabolic segregation problem
papers.authors: Emily Casey, Cornelia Mihaila, Mar\'ia Soria-Carro, Clara Torres-Latorre
papers.abstract: We study a two-phase parabolic free boundary problem arising as the segregation limit of a competition-diffusion system with strong interactions and fully nonlinear diffusion. The positive and negative phases are governed by different equations and are coupled through global viscosity inequalities. We construct viscosity solutions that are Lipschitz in space and $1/2$-H\"older in time, and establish differentiability in space across the free boundary, including at singular points. At regular points, we prove that the solution has a parabolic $C^{1,\alpha}$ asymptotic expansion, and deduce that the free boundary is locally a $C^{1,\alpha}$ hypersurface. The proof relies on a parabolic Alt-Caffarelli-Friedman monotonicity formula to classify blow-up limits, followed by an improvement of flatness argument.

papers.title: Carnot geodesics with H\"older controls
papers.authors: Nicola Cavallucci, Enrico Le Donne, Sebastiano Nicolussi Golo
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit length-minimizing curve in a polynomial rank-two sub-Riemannian structure on $\R^4$. Its arclength parametrization is $C^{1,1/2}$ and is not $C^{1,\alpha}$ near an interior point for any $\alpha>1/2$. Minimality is proved by an approximate calibration chosen separately for each competitor. The example admits a minimizing lift to a rank-two Carnot group of step five. Generalizations are announced.

papers.title: Beyond Reachability: When Edit Order Preserves Couplings in Graph Flow Matching
papers.abstract: Shortest-path optimality does not guarantee that a memoryless graph generator preserves a prescribed source-target correspondence. We study whether reordering legal shortest edits can retain this correspondence without changing the pairing, mandatory edits, or sampling budget. Under a common Poisson clock, we establish an exact criterion for endpoint coupling recoverability: the source-blind Markov projection attains the unavoidable clock-error floor if and only if routes to distinct targets do not share graph states. Routes to the same target may merge without sacrificing endpoint fidelity. This characterization leads to an exact finite-state routing formulation and a legality-preserving scheduling procedure with recovery certificates. A marker-free construction demonstrates how shared edge structure can retain source distinctions, while a capacity-constrained family exhibits a sharp separation in paired error between edit orders with identical marginal error. Finally, a target-conditioned aliasing bound connects structural route design to the terminal fidelity of a learned graph-only generator. These results characterize when legal edit ordering can preserve a prescribed coupling under fixed operational costs.

papers.title: Low-regularity global well-posedness for the defocusing cubic wave equation outside a ball with radial initial data
papers.abstract: We study the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear wave equation with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary condition in the exterior of the unit ball, $\Omega=\R^3\backslash\overline{B(0,1)}$, for radial initial data. For every $\frac12\leq s\leq\frac34$, we establish global well-posedness in $\dot H^s_{D,rad}(\Omega)\times\dot H^{s-1}_{D,rad}(\Omega)$, including the critical endpoint $s=\frac12$, without an additional $L^4$ assumption on the initial displacement. The proof uses the distorted Fourier transform associated with the Dirichlet Laplacian to establish radial Sobolev embeddings, including the quantitative estimate $\|f\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\leq C\sqrt p\,\|f\|_{\dot H_D^{1/2}(\Omega)}$ for $4\leq p<\infty$, with $C$ independent of $p$. We combine a nonlinear Fourier truncation argument with the critical Strichartz estimate to construct a global nonlinear component with high-frequency-truncated initial data. For the remainder, we construct a local energy solution in an affine energy space and derive a logarithmic energy inequality that prevents finite-time energy blow-up. Persistence of the original Sobolev regularity, uniqueness, and local Lipschitz dependence on each finite time interval complete the proof.

papers.title: On the Supersingular reduction of Cubic fourfolds with Complex Multiplication
papers.abstract: If $X$ is a K3 surface with complex multiplication by a CM field $E$, Kazuhiro Ito proved that the height of the reduction of $X$ in characteristic $p>0$, and its Artin invariant if it is supersingular, can be computed from the decomposition of $p$ in $E$. We present analogous results for cubic fourfolds by using the main theorem of complex multiplication for cubic fourfold, proved by Rikuto Ito.

papers.title: Electromagnetic Potentials via the Extended Maxwell System
papers.authors: Rainer Picard, Sascha Trostorff, Marcus Waurick
papers.abstract: We construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. The main idea is to invoke the extended Maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.

papers.title: On loop-soup clusters in three dimensions and higher
papers.abstract:
We study clusters of the Brownian loop soup on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and of random walk and metric-graph loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ within a unified framework. For the continuum model, when the one-arm exponent $\xi(\alpha)$ is positive, we prove that almost surely every cluster has Hausdorff dimension $3-\xi(\alpha)$. A key step is to show that, conditioned on the one-arm event, a crossing cluster has capacity comparable to the crossing scale with uniformly positive probability. This gives one-arm estimates of order $\alpha r^{-\xi(\alpha)}$, uniformly down to zero intensity, and shows that $\xi(\alpha)$ is strictly decreasing and left-continuous. Moreover, $1-\xi(\alpha)\asymp\alpha$ as $\alpha\downarrow0$. As another application of the one-arm estimates, we prove that several critical values coincide, resolving a conjecture of Jego and Lupu in arXiv:2601.04840.
  The proof combines a decoupling technique with a multiscale recursive argument to control the combined effects of large and small loops. These methods also extend to loop soups on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ for $d=3,4,5$, yielding capacity lower bounds of order $r$, $r^2/\log r$, and $r^2$ for the cluster of the origin, conditioned on the one-arm event, throughout the small-loop decay regime. In particular, these bounds imply strict polynomial comparisons between one-arm probabilities at different intensities in dimension three. We also show that the small-loop decay regime on $\widetilde{\mathbb{Z}}^d$ has upper endpoint $\frac{1}{2}$ by adapting the OSSS sharpness framework to the truncated loop soup.

papers.title: Nonlinear coercivity and orbital stability of smooth solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation
papers.authors: Xijun Deng, Ji Li, Zhisu Liu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish orbital stability of smooth zero-background solitary waves for the modified Camassa--Holm equation in $H^1(\R)\cap W^{1,4}(\R)$ for the full range $\gamma<c<2\gamma$. The main difficulty is that spectral coercivity of the Hessian does not by itself yield nonlinear coercivity in this topology, because normalized perturbations may develop derivative concentration. In order to overcome this obstruction, we apply a penalized Lyapunov functional and introduce a derivative factorization. The key ingredient is a concentration-coercivity principle for the normalized Lyapunov energy, which yields local nonlinear Lyapunov coercivity. Our result extends the $H^1(\mathbb R)\cap W^{1,4}(\mathbb R)$ orbital-stability results of Li and Liu [Ann. PDE, 2021] and Zhang and Zhu [JDE, 2025] to the entire parameter range $\gamma<c<2\gamma$.

papers.title: The asymptotics of off-diagonal book Ramsey numbers
papers.authors: Lulu Dai, Chunchao Fan, Qizhong Lin
papers.abstract:
Let $B_n$ be the book graph consisting of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge. We prove upper bounds for $r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)$ that asymptotically match the known lower bounds in the remaining range $1/6<\alpha<1/4$. Combined with the known results for the other ranges of $\alpha$, this completely determines the asymptotics of the Ramsey number $r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)$ for every fixed $0<\alpha\le1$: \[
  r(B_{\lceil\alpha n\rceil},B_n)=(c(\alpha)+o(1))n,
  \qquad
  c(\alpha)=
  \begin{cases}
  2, & 0<\alpha\le1/6,\\[1mm]
  \displaystyle\frac{3}{1+2p_\alpha^2},
  & 1/6<\alpha\le\alpha_0,\\[3mm]
  (1+\sqrt\alpha)^2, & \alpha_0<\alpha\le1,
  \end{cases} \] where \(\alpha_0:=\frac{52-16\sqrt3}{121}, \;\;
  p_\alpha:=\frac{1-\sqrt{\alpha(3-2\alpha)}}{1-2\alpha}
  \;\; (1/6<\alpha\le\alpha_0).\) Consequently, the random lower bound is asymptotically tight if and only if $\alpha\ge\alpha_0$, thereby determining exactly the range of $\alpha$ for which the conjecture of Conlon, Fox and Wigderson holds. The proof develops a defect-compensation framework around a $K_4$-free auxiliary graph.

papers.title: High-dimensional two-sample testing: From optimal transport to optimal derangements
papers.authors: Abhradipta Ghosh, Vaibhav Sherkar, Bilol Banerjee, Anil K. Ghosh
papers.abstract: In recent years, optimal transport has emerged as a useful framework for constructing distribution-free multivariate two-sample tests by transporting observations to a reference distribution under a suitable transportation cost. However, existing optimal transport-based tests can perform poorly in high dimension, low sample size (HDLSS) settings, and their performance depends critically on the choice of the reference distribution and transportation cost. We investigate this phenomenon and show that suitable choices can substantially improve their performance. Motivated by this analysis, we introduce a class of two-sample tests based on optimal derangements that do not require an external reference distribution. The minimum distance pairing test of Rosenbaum arises as a special case when the optimization is restricted to a subclass of derangements, thereby revealing a connection between this method and optimal transport. We propose the optimal derangement (ODER) test and its distribution-free variant, the ODER-SHC test, obtained by restricting the minimization to derangements consisting of a single Hamiltonian cycle. We establish their consistency under both HDLSS and classical large-sample asymptotic regimes. We also develop corresponding procedures based on the $L1$ distance and establish their high-dimensional consistency under conditions involving coordinate-wise energy distances. These $L1$ distance based tests can also discriminate between two high-dimensional distributions with identical first two moments but different marginal distributions. Analyses of benchmark datasets and extensive simulation studies demonstrate the performance of the proposed methods across a variety of alternatives and data settings.

papers.title: Dimension-free exponential entropy quotients over $\mathbb{F}_2$
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a random vector in $\mathbb{F}_2^m$, and let $X'$ be an independent copy. We prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a subspace $G$ with $\dim G\le 2^{320(1+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon}H(X)$ such that $H(q_GX)\le(1+\varepsilon)(H(q_GX+q_GX')-H(q_GX))$. In particular, the quotient entropy is at most $(1+\varepsilon)(H(X+X')-H(X))$. The coefficient is independent of the ambient dimension, and its exponential order in $1/\varepsilon$ is necessary. The structural result is a logarithmic rigidity estimate for finite weighted families of laws with averaged subspace entropy sparsity. A common variational quotient controls both a family and its convolution family without decreasing the original family's normalized mean entropy defect. Posterior families preserve averaged sparsity, and a fresh-index argument combines a local-to-global estimate with the entropic Marton theorem to increase the defect ratio at a fixed multiplicative sparsity cost. We also obtain two-input almost-additivity and concentration of moderate-doubling sets on subspace cosets at the same exponential scale. The constants are not optimized.

papers.title: Reduced and Mixed-Precision Block Householder QR Factorization
papers.authors: Peter Benner, Martin K\"ohler, Xiaobo Liu, Eda Oktay
papers.abstract: Recent advances in hardware architecture have highlighted the importance of reduced-precision arithmetic for improving performance and reducing energy consumption in large-scale scientific applications. However, uniformly low-precision methods can suffer from numerical instability, especially in fundamental linear algebra routines. Mixed-precision strategies therefore play an important role in balancing efficiency, stability, and accuracy. In this paper, we focus on the block Householder QR decomposition using the WY representation and study its behavior in reduced- and mixed-precision settings. Starting from a uniform half-precision variant, we show that performing norm computations with fp32 accumulation is necessary to avoid overflow and underflow on large matrices. Based on this observation, we introduce mpWYQR, a mixed-precision algorithm that increases the precision of only selected computations and avoids most of the precision conversions required by the existing mixed-precision blocked QR algorithm (mpBQR3) introduced in [L. M. Yang, A. Fox, and G. Sanders, SIAM J. Sci. Comp., 43.3 (2021), pp. A1723--A1753]. Our analysis shows that mpWYQR accuracy is governed by low-precision unit roundoff, and that its error bound exceeds that of mpBQR3 by only a constant factor, with identical heuristic bounds. In experiments across a range of matrix sizes and condition numbers, we show that mpWYQR retains mpBQR3 accuracy while running up to $18\times$ faster and using less memory. We also discuss the performance cost of computing inner products in higher precision, and the library support needed for an efficient GPU implementation.

papers.title: Curvature-Dimension Conditions Along Discrete Refinement Sequences
papers.abstract: We introduce the sequence curvature--dimension condition $SCD(K,N)$ for complete refinement systems of finite metric probability spaces. The condition couples a transport action bound with entropy comparisons along a single probability section through the prescribed refinement layers. Within a bounded comparison range, we prove that midpoint comparisons on three consecutive layers characterize the condition on every fixed finite segment. If, in addition, the refinement sequence converges in the measured sense in its intrinsic bridge realization, then $SCD(K,N)$ is equivalent both to the vanishing of single-layer midpoint defects and to the entropic curvature--dimension condition $CD^{e}(K,N)$ of the limit. In the reverse direction, a $CD^{e}(K,N)$ bound on the limit yields quantitative recovery estimates that identify shrinking transport scales on which finite layers retain its second-order curvature comparison. These estimates are uniform over endpoint measures and include Dirac masses. Examples illustrate the effects of the refinement rule, the layer metrics and the reference measures.

papers.title: Minimizing the spectral radius of unicyclic graphs with fixed order and dissociation number
papers.authors: Yu Zhou, Yuanyuan Chen, Dan Li, Dandan Fan
papers.abstract: A dissociation set of a graph G is a vertex subset S contained in V(G) such that the induced subgraph G[S] has maximum degree at most 1, and the dissociation number of G is the cardinality of a maximum dissociation set denoted by {\Phi}(G). In this paper, we first derive a sharp lower bound on the dissociation number for all unicyclic graphs. Furthermore, we also study the graphs with minimum spectral radius among all unicyclic graphs with given order and dissociation number and explicitly identify all extremal graphs for \(n-4 \le \Phi(G) \le n-1\).

papers.title: New explicit examples of Mannheim pair in $\mathbb{L}^3$
papers.authors: Jos\'e Alan, Renato Teixeira, Thiago Mendon\c{c}a
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct explicit examples of Mannheim pairs, in the classical sense, in Minkowski 3-space $\mathbb{L}^3$, one for each of the five types of such pairs. In our main examples the Mannheim curve is neither a helix nor a slant helix. For each example we give the complete Frenet apparatus of both curves of the pair and their Cartesian coordinates in terms of elementary functions. The construction writes the tangent indicatrix in angular coordinates and uses a suitable auxiliary angle function, which reduces all the relevant integrals to elementary form; it is carried out both starting from the Mannheim curve and starting from its partner. In these coordinates, we also characterize the helices and the slant helices with timelike axis. We also prove, for the five types, that a Mannheim curve is a slant helix if and only if its partner is a helix, and we give an explicit example of such a pair.

papers.title: Equal diffusions and zero Dirichlet boundary conditions can induce blow-up
papers.abstract: For a class of systems of two parabolic equations with equal diffusion and homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, we show the existence of finite time blow-up solutions, although the corresponding system of ODE's has only global, exponentially decaying solutions. Such a phenomenon of blow-up induced by equal diffusions, which originates in the works of Bebernes-Lacey [SIAM J. Math. Anal. 21 (1990), 1415--1425, and J. Differential Equations 95 (1992), 105--129] and Weinberger [J. Differ. Equations 154 (1999), 225--237], was previously known, for instance, in the case of homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, but it had remained an open question whether it can happen in the homogeneous Dirichlet case. The latter, which corresponds to an absorption or cooling of the system at the boundary, that is a priori more stabilizing, requires nontrivial new ideas. As another new feature, we show that this can happen even if the nonlinearity acts only on a compact sub-region, and our proof actually covers the Neumann and Cauchy, as well as Dirichlet problems in a unified way.

papers.title: Equivalence of freeness and higher order freeness of hyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: Using vector bundle theory, we prove that an essential hyperplane arrangement in an $\ell$-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero is free if and only if its module of logarithmic derivations of order $p$ is free for some $1\le p\le\ell-1$. The same statement holds for multiarrangements.

papers.title: Directed isoperimetry and infinitely fast robbers
papers.abstract: We study the fast version of the cops and robber game on finite digraphs with unit-speed cops and an unbounded-speed robber. We prove a lower bound for the cop number of every strongly connected digraph in terms of its order, maximum out-degree, and out-vertex expansion, extending Mehrabian's isoperimetric lower bound to digraphs, where connected components are replaced by forward reachable sets. For strongly connected abelian Cayley digraphs of fixed out-degree, we show that the ratio of the cop number to the number of vertices is comparable to each of out-vertex expansion, vertex expansion of the underlying undirected graph, minimum nontrivial character displacement, the square root of the unnormalized Laplacian spectral gap of the underlying undirected graph, and the reciprocal of its diameter. The comparison constants depend polynomially on the out-degree. In the undirected case, we also compare pathwidth with these parameters, complementing the bounded-degree treewidth comparison of Alon and Mehrabian. Combining the directed lower bound with recent cyclic sweep techniques for abelian Cayley graphs, we determine the order of the cop number of positively oriented tori and directed Heisenberg graphs.

papers.title: Optimality Conditions and Solution Set Characterisations of Convex Minimal Time Optimisation Problems
papers.authors: Doan Huu Hieu, Nguyen Duy Cuong
papers.abstract: The paper studies convex minimisation problems involving a composition of a coordinatewise nondecreasing convex function with a finite family of nonnegative, locally Lipschitz continuous and convex functions. We establish complete dual optimality conditions and characterise the entire solution set using multipliers and subgradients associated with a given solution. The results are applied to norm optimisation problems involving minimal time functions with different convex dynamics sets and convex target sets. The sum, maximum and p-norms yield minimal time versions of the Fermat--Torricelli, Chebyshev centre and p-Fermat--Torricelli problems, respectively. Examples in finite and infinite dimensional spaces are provided to illustrate the solution set characterisations.

papers.title: A conditional no-splash criterion for two-fluid Euler--MHD interface
papers.abstract: We study a two-dimensional incompressible two-fluid system: an inviscid, irrotational Euler phase and a viscous, conducting MHD phase, separated by a free interface. We prove a conditional quantitative no-splash criterion for smooth solutions in a specified admissible class. In addition to a bound on the trace of the Euler velocity, an initial bound on the magnetic trace and bounds on the bulk vorticity, this class imposes bounds on the interface Biot--Savart potential and its tangential derivative, fixed exponential vertical localization, and the normal derivative of the bulk vorticity at the interface together with one tangential derivative of it. It also requires a Biot--Savart representation of the Euler velocity up to a bounded-gradient harmonic part and a positive initial chord-arc bound. Under these assumptions the chord-arc functional has a uniform positive lower bound on $[0,T]$, depending only on the interval length, the decay width and the a priori bound, after an enlargement that absorbs the surface tension and the densities. The proof combines a maximum-principle analysis of the interface-vorticity equation, in which the magnetic field enters through the Lorentz term and the pressure jump, with a geometric reduction in the style of Fefferman--Ionescu--Lie.

papers.title: Large tight components and Dirac thresholds for tight Hamilton cycles
papers.authors: Hao Lin, Guanghui Wang, Jiande Zhang, Wenling Zhou
papers.abstract: For every odd integer $r\ge1$, let $q_r=1-2^{-r}\binom r{(r-1)/2}$. We show that, for every odd $r\ge3$ and sufficiently large $n$, every $n$-vertex $r$-uniform hypergraph with at least $q_r\binom nr$ edges contains a tight component with at least $(1/2-o(1))\binom nr$ edges. This confirms a conjecture posed by Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2024. As an application, for every odd $r\ge1$ and every integer $k\ge\lceil r(3-2q_r)\rceil$, we prove that the asymptotic minimum $(k-r)$-degree threshold for a tight Hamilton cycle in a $k$-uniform hypergraph is $q_r$, which settles, in this range, another conjecture of Lang and Sanhueza-Matamala in 2022 stating that the lower-bound construction due to Han and Zhao is asymptotically optimal. Our proof combines an isoperimetric inequality for Johnson graphs with a Kruskal-Katona-type theorem, which is of independent interest.

papers.title: Local Hardy and bmo Spaces on Filtered Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of local Hardy and $bmo$ spaces on a connected Lie group with polynomial growth whose Lie algebra is endowed with a filtration. Under suitable assumptions, we prove that the local Hardy spaces enjoy an appropriate atomic decomposition, are compatible with Calder\'on--Zygmund operators, and can be identified with certain Triebel--Lizorkin spaces, as it happens in the classical settings.

papers.title: Prescribed mean curvature surfaces of Riemann minimal type
papers.abstract: We construct analogues of Riemann minimal examples among surfaces in the Euclidean 3-space whose mean curvature is given by a prescribed function on the unit sphere in terms of their Gauss map. Specifically, we obtain a 2-parameter family of complete, properly embedded surfaces foliated by circles and straight lines and invariant under a nontrivial translation.

papers.title: The exact digirth and out-degree bounds for $C(k,k)$-subdivision and out-forest in digraphs
papers.authors: Bin Chen, Jianfeng Hou, Xinmin Hou, Siyue Liu, Xinjie Wang, Xinyu Zhou
papers.abstract:
For each integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud ({\small European J. Combin., 2024}) asked for the smallest integer $g_k$ such that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two and digirth at least $g_k$ contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$. We completely resolve this problem by proving that $g_k=k+1$. Our proof relies on a refinement of Thomassen's theorem ({\small Discrete Math., 1985}) on two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one vertex: we prove that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least two contains two directed cycles intersecting in exactly one arc.
  We also establish an embedding theorem for out-forests with prescribed images of their roots, under minimum out-degree and digirth conditions determined by the number of leaves and the heights of vertices in antichains. As an application, for integers $k,\ell\ge2$, we show that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least \(k\) and digirth at least \(k(\ell-1)+1\) contains \(k\) directed paths of length \(\ell\) sharing only their initial vertex, which can be prescribed arbitrarily. This improves the previous digirth bound \((k^\ell-1)/(k-1)+1\) of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud to a sharp bound.

papers.title: Lifting mod $p$ Galois representations over local fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a local field with absolute Galois group $G_{K}$ and let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. We prove that every continuous representation $G_K\to \operatorname{GL}_{n}(k)$ lifts to a continuous representation $G_K\to\operatorname{GL}_{n}(W(k))$ where $W(k)$ is the ring of infinite Witt vectors over $k$.

papers.title: The smallest singular value of products of random combinatorial and deterministic matrices
papers.authors: Yuxiao Shi, Kexin Yu, Tingzhou Yu
papers.abstract: Let $p\in(0,1/2]$ be fixed, and let $d,n$ be positive integers satisfying $d=pn$. Let $Q_n$ be an $n\times n$ random combinatorial matrix whose rows are independent and uniformly distributed over the vectors in $\{0,1\}^n$ having exactly $d$ ones. For an arbitrary deterministic invertible $n\times n$ matrix $M$, we establish two-sided bounds for the smallest singular value of $Q_nM$. More precisely, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, \[ \mathbb P\!\left( \varepsilon\le s_n(Q_nM)\cdot \|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}} \le \varepsilon^{-2} \right) \ge 1-C\left( \varepsilon+d^{-1/2}+e^{-c\,\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})} \right)-2e^{-cn}, \] where positive constants $C, c$ depend only on $p$ and $\operatorname{sr}$ denotes the stable rank. Consequently, for any sequence of deterministic invertible matrices $M$ satisfying $\operatorname{sr}(M^{-1})\to\infty$, $s_n(Q_nM)$ is typically of order $\|M^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^{-1}$. In particular, taking $M=\mathbf I_n$ recovers the known $n^{-1/2}$ scale for $s_n(Q_n)$.

papers.title: Finite-State Time-Inhomogeneous Markov Chains Conditioned to Survive
papers.abstract: We study conditioning on long survival for time-inhomogeneous Markov chains on finite state spaces. We assume that a sequence of substochastic transition kernels converges to an irreducible substochastic kernel and that the transition probabilities admit asymptotic expansions up to order $n^{-2}$. Under these assumptions, we construct a positive space-time harmonic function and prove that the limiting path distributions under conditioning on long survival are given by the corresponding Doob h-transform. We also investigate the long-time behavior of the resulting conditioned process. Finally, we apply our general theory to an elephant random walk, a generalized P\'{o}lya urn model, time-inhomogeneous Wright--Fisher and Moran models, and noncolliding random walks.

papers.title: The Polynomially Self-repelling Motion
papers.abstract: [Kosygina et al. 2023] showed that the rescaled polynomially self-repelling walk does not converge to any Brownian motion perturbed at extrema (BMPE). Motivated by this result, we introduce an explicit candidate for the scaling limit, the polynomially self-repelling motion (PSRM), and study its properties. The construction relies on a new family of continuous stochastic flows, called polynomially self-repelling flows, introduced in [Yu 2026]. A key ingredient in relating the limiting process of the rescaled walk to the PSRM is a joint Ray-Knight theorem for rescaled local time processes, extending the classical Ray-Knight theorems of [T\'oth 1996].

papers.title: Unique Positive Extremals and Sharp Stability Constants for Singular Moser-Trudinger Inequalities
papers.abstract:
We combine spectral perturbation with orthogonal transformations in $H_0^1(\Omega)$ to study singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities under the energy constraint $\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^2\,dx\le1$, where $\Omega$ is a smooth bounded planar domain containing the origin. For the weight $|x|^{-2\beta}$, $0\le\beta<1$, the positive maximizer is unique for small $\alpha>0$, and the sharp global stability constant satisfies \[
  C_\alpha=\frac{\alpha}{2}
  \left(\frac1{\mu_1}-\frac1{\mu_2}\right)+O(\alpha^2),
  \qquad \alpha\downarrow0, \] where $\mu_1<\mu_2$ are the first two weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues. We compute the second asymptotic coefficient by a weighted quartic maximization on the second eigenspace, even when the second eigenvalue is multiple. An exact reduction to the sphere orthogonal to the maximizer identifies the attaining functions and yields a limiting global-to-local ratio of $1/2$. On the disk, the energy derivative with respect to the central value characterizes radial constrained degeneracy and yields finitely many exceptional normalized parameters. Combined with known critical uniqueness and nondegeneracy, this gives uniform quadratic stability near criticality, while compactness and analytic reduction yield finite-power stability throughout the admissible range.

papers.title: A $p$-Laplacian Problem with Slightly Subcritical Regularly Varying Nonlinearity
papers.abstract: We study a quasilinear elliptic problem involving the $p$-laplacian operator and a slightly subcritical nonlinearity with a sign-changing weight. We assume that the slightly subcritical nonlinearity is a regularly varying function at zero and at infinity, which are not necessarily asymptotic to a power at infinity. We state sufficient conditions which guarantee a Palais-Smale condition. We also provide a bifurcation theorem for these nonlinearities, which allow us to state the existence of a bifurcated branch of positive solutions, containing a turning point, and multiplicity of solutions.

papers.title: Graphon Colourings and Limits of Graph Partitions
papers.authors: Svante Janson, Tiffany Y. Y. Lo, Colin McDiarmid, Anda Skeja, Fiona Skerman
papers.abstract:
We develop a framework for pure and mixed graphon colourings and use it to study the limiting behaviour of graph partition parameters under cut convergence. Pure colourings correspond to measurable partitions, while mixed colourings assign a probability distribution on the colour set to each point. We develop the representation, equivalence and convergence theory, and show that every mixed graphon colouring has an equivalent pure representative, possibly on a different probability space. For each fixed finite colour set, we establish compactness and describe the topology of coloured graph limits using the cut norm on graphons and the weak-$*$ topology on colourings. The usual coloured cut distance characterises convergence for pure colourings, but not for general mixed colourings.
  As applications, we prove that the Cheeger constant and modularity converge to their mixed graphon counterparts along cut-convergent graph sequences whose orders tend to infinity, assuming uniformly linear minimum degree and positive limiting edge density, respectively. Both mixed functionals are invariant under graphon equivalence. We also establish their continuity in cut distance on the corresponding classes of graphons, with a stability bound for the Cheeger constant. For modularity, we further characterise coloured graphons attaining extremal modularity values and prove attainment of the mixed optimum for each fixed number of colours. We also exhibit a graphon whose modularity supremum is not attained by any finite colouring.

papers.title: Matrix orthogonal polynomials related to diffference operators for $L$-orthogonal polynomials
papers.authors: Erik Koelink, Ana Loureiro, Pablo Rom\'an
papers.abstract: The difference operator $J$ arising from the higher order occurrence for the $L$-orthogonal polynomials is studied using various families of matrix orthogonal polynomials. The matrix orthogonal polynomials determine the polar decomposition of $J$ and its adjoint $J^\ast$ considered as operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$. The special case of symmetric $J$ leads to the case where the matrix polynomials reduce to diagonal matrix polynomials. The example of the symmetric case with constant coefficients for $L=2$ is discussed in detail.

papers.title: Approximating the poles of a Painlev\'e V transcendent for the Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel
papers.abstract: The Fredholm determinant of the sine kernel has an expression as an integral containing a Painlev\'e transcendent $r$ satisfying Painlev\'e V, in the same way that the Fredholm determinant of the Airy kernel has an expression involving the Hastings-McLeod solution of Painlev\'e II. In this paper we use Pad\'e approximation to approximate the poles of this Painlev\'e transcendent $r$ in the complex plane. We use Pad\'e approximation near $0$, Hermite-Pad\'e approximation near $0$ and two-point Pad\'e approximation near $0$ and infinity.

papers.title: Transfer kernels and the Schur multiplier
papers.abstract: In this article we prove that if $H$ is a normal subgroup of a finite group $G$ with $G/H$ cyclic, then the kernel of the transfer map $G/G' \longrightarrow H/H'$ equals $(G:H)$ times the order of the cokernel of the natural map $M(H) \longrightarrow M(G)$.

papers.title: Well-Posedness and Regularity for a Modified Liquid Crystal Model with Transport Noise
papers.authors: Gianmarco Del Sarto, Antoine Moneyron, Esm\'ee Theewis, Tarek Z\"{o}chling
papers.abstract: We prove well-posedness for a stochastic Lin-Liu model of modified liquid crystals, coupling an incompressible fluid to a director field under transport and multiplicative noise. On smooth bounded domains in two dimensions, we prove global well-posedness for energy-class initial data, provided the leading coefficient of the polynomial director potential is positive. On the torus, we establish local well-posedness in time-weighted $L^p$-$L^q$ frameworks with Besov initial data, including regimes of low and negative regularity.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous Geometric Last Passage Percolation and the $q$-deformed Jacobi Unitary Ensemble
papers.authors: Sung-Soo Byun, Yeong-Gwang Jung, Nick Simm
papers.abstract: We study directed last passage percolation with geometric weights in a spatially inhomogeneous environment. We derive an explicit limit shape and establish fluctuation limits for the passage time, showing that, depending on the strength of the inhomogeneity, the limiting fluctuations are governed by Fredholm determinants associated with either the Airy or Bessel kernel. Our approach is based on an exact relation between the passage time and the smallest particle of the $q$-deformed Jacobi unitary ensemble ($q$-JUE). As part of our analysis, we derive the macroscopic limiting density of the $q$-JUE, which provides a natural $q$-deformation of the classical Wachter distribution, as well as of the limiting distribution of the Meixner ensemble. We further establish Airy and Bessel scaling limits for the smallest particle, which are of independent interest.

papers.title: Multiplicity of normalized solutions for the $L^2$-supercritical Kirchhoff equation with partial confinement
papers.abstract: We study the existence of positive normalized solutions for the nonlocal Kirchhoff equation with partial harmonic confinement \[-\left(a+b\int_{\mathbb{R}^{3}}|\nabla u|^{2}\,dx\right)\Delta u +(x_1^2+x_2^2)u+\lambda u=|u|^{p-2}u,\] subject to the mass constraint $\int_{\mathbb{R}^{3}}|u|^2\,dx=\mu$, where $a,b>0$ are constants, $\frac{14}{3}<p<6$, $\mu>0$ is a prescribed mass, and $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ is a Lagrange multiplier associated with the mass constraint. For every sufficiently small $\mu>0$, we prove the existence of two positive normalized solutions. One of these solutions is a local minimizer, while the other is obtained at a mountain-pass level. The construction of the local minimizer relies on a combination of profile decomposition and a new nonlocal merging technique, yielding compactness up to translations in the unconfined $x_3$-direction. The mountain-pass solution is obtained by considering positive solutions defined on expanding balls. A uniform bound on the Morse index allows us to obtain a spectral estimate for the limiting Lagrange multiplier. Together with an energy comparison, this spectral estimate yields strong convergence in the energy space and recovers both the prescribed mass and the Kirchhoff coefficient.

papers.title: Regularity of Symbolic Powers of Polymatroidal Ideals and Supermodular Prime Intersections
papers.abstract: Let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $\mathbb{K}$. For a polymatroidal ideal $I\subseteq S$ generated in degree $d$, we prove $$\omega(I^{(s)})=\operatorname{reg} I^{(s)}=\operatorname{reg} I^s=sd\qquad(s\ge1),$$ where symbolic powers use all associated primes and $\omega$ denotes the largest degree of a minimal generator. Thus every symbolic power has a degree resolution. The argument uses a regularity bound for supermodular prime intersections, obtained from Takayama's formula and a homological estimate for noncover complexes. For every nonzero proper squarefree monomial ideal $L$, we also show $\operatorname{reg} L^{(s)}\le s\min\{m,\lambda(L)-\operatorname{ht}L+1\}$, where $m$ counts the minimal primes and $\lambda(L)$ is the support size, and obtain equality for skeleton and pure skeleton ideals. Finally, for every $d\ge3$, we construct a simple graphic matroid whose basis ideal is generated in degree $d$ and has a second symbolic power that is not componentwise linear.

papers.title: Larger Crossing Families
papers.abstract: We give the first explicit constant for crossing families of linear size by showing that every set of $n$ points in general position in the plane contains a crossing family of size approximately $\frac{n}{79}$. We further identify some conditions where there are even larger crossing families. The first such condition forbids the existence of a large different pattern, namely non-convex 4-clusters: We show that every point set contains either a large non-convex 4-cluster or a large crossing family. The second condition is the existence of many crossings: We give a bound for the size of a crossing family in terms of the number of crossings of the complete geometric graph drawn on the point set.

papers.title: The equal norm Grassmannian: topology and applications to frame fields
papers.authors: Samuel A. Ballas, Ferhat Karabatman, Tom Needham, Clayton Shonkwiler
papers.abstract: Given an orientable rank-$d$ vector bundle over a $d$-manifold, the Euler class is the unique obstruction to finding a nowhere-zero section. An equal norm Parseval frame is a certain collection of sections, one of whose properties is that the lengths of each vector at each point are equal. This makes the Euler class an obvious obstruction to finding such a frame. In this work we show that this is the only obstruction so long as the number of sections is at least $2d+2$. We also identify precise obstructions when the number of sections is $2d$ and produce examples showing that for smaller numbers of sections it is sometimes impossible to find Parseval frame fields.

papers.title: Simple Cuts, Simple Landscapes: Global Synchronization and Rank-Width-One Matrices
papers.abstract: We study how the structure of the coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ shapes the energy landscape $E_{\boldsymbol A}(\boldsymbol\theta)=-\frac12\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)$ of the Kuramoto model. We prove that, for an entrywise nonnegative coupling matrix $\boldsymbol A$ with connected support, if $\boldsymbol A$ has rank-width one over $\mathbb R$, then the landscape is "simple", i.e., every local minimum is synchronized. The rank-width bound is sharp, and the result has many interesting implications for global synchronization. The key contribution of this work is to uncover a structural synchronization mechanism beyond the rank-one regime, which has served as a starting point for earlier analyses of global synchronization.

papers.title: Projected Brion's theorem
papers.abstract: We present an analogue of Brion's theorem for the projected integer-point transform. Brion's theorem writes the integer-point transform of a rational polyhedron $P$ as the sum of the rational functions associated to its vertex cones. The pushforward $\pi_*$ along a lattice projection $\pi$ turns the transform of $P$ into the generating function of the numbers of lattice points in the fibres of $\pi$. We group the vertices of $P$ into contracted classes, generated by the edges whose direction $\pi$ kills, and show that the sum of the rational functions associated to the vertex cones in a contracted class can be pushed forward along $\pi$, yielding a rational function decomposition of the projected integer-point transform. For a lattice polytope, the classes correspond to the connected components of the fixed locus of the associated toric variety under the action of a subtorus, and our formula resembles the localization formula for this subtorus. We use this decomposition to provide an explicit formula for the projected integer-point transform of a linear family of polytopes. We illustrate this result with families of Gelfand--Zetlin and string polytopes.

papers.title: Modified Scattering for Infinite-Rank Hartree--Fock Equations
papers.authors: Masaki Kawamoto, Jinyeop Lee, Changhun Yang, Chanjin You
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of the Hartree--Fock equation with Coulomb interaction in dimensions $d\geq2$ for small initial density matrices of possibly infinite rank. We prove global well-posedness and modified scattering governed by a resonant Hartree-Fock equation. Our approach is based on the half-density formulation and a final-state construction for the resonant dynamics. We also characterize the stationary states of the resonant Hartree--Fock equation and prove that ordinary linear scattering fails when the initial density matrix has rank at least two. These results extend long-range modified scattering to genuinely operator-valued infinite-rank Hartree-Fock evolution. Despite cancellation between the direct and exchange terms, the long-range effect persists, with resonant dynamics evolving on the same logarithmic time scale as in the Hartree equation.

papers.title: On a family of domains associated with $\mu$-synthesis in $M_2(\mathbb C)$
papers.authors: Indranil Biswas, Sourav Pal, Nitin Tomar
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that the domain $\mathbb H$ serves as a unifying domain for $\mathbb G_2, \mathbb E$ and $\mathbb P$ by proving that each of these domains is an analytic retract of $\mathbb H$. Further, we prove that the bidisc $\mathbb D^2$ and the Euclidean unit ball $\mathbb B_2$ are also analytic retracts of $\mathbb H$. Then the rational $\overline{\mathbb H}$-inner functions, i.e., the rational maps from $\mathbb D$ into $\overline{\mathbb H}$ whose boundary values lie in the distinguished boundary of $\mathbb H$, are characterized. Two different versions of Schwarz type lemma for $\mathbb H$ are established of which one provides a necessary and sufficient condition. Finally, capitalizing on the theory of $\mathbb H$, we present alternative proofs to a few known results on $\mathbb P$ from the literature.

papers.title: Equivariant Morita equivalence for finite cyclic group actions on noncommutative tori
papers.abstract: Li proved that the noncommutative tori $A_\theta$ and $A_{g\theta}$ are strongly Morita equivalent whenever $g\in\mathrm{SO}(n,n|\mathbb{Z})$ and $g\theta$ is defined. We study equivariant extensions of these equivalences for canonical finite cyclic group actions.
