Let $W\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$ satisfy $W^t\theta W=\theta$, $W^k=I_n$ and $1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)$, and write $\rho(R)=\operatorname{diag}(R,(R^t)^{-1})$. If $g\rho(W^t)g^{-1}=\rho(P)$ for some $P\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$, we equip Li's $A_{g\theta}$--$A_\theta$ Heisenberg equivalence bimodule with a compatible $\mathbb{Z}_k$-action. Consequently, the crossed products $A_{g\theta}\rtimes_{\alpha_{P^t}}\mathbb{Z}_k$ and $A_\theta\rtimes_{\alpha_W}\mathbb{Z}_k$ are strongly Morita equivalent. For the canonical flip action by $\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that Morita equivalence of crossed products implies Morita equivalence of the underlying tori in every dimension, and prove the converse in dimensions two through four. For each fixed dimension $2\leq n\leq 4$, the complete invariants are the central rank and canonical $K_0$-trace range of the underlying torus, with the latter taken up to positive scaling. For the standard cyclic group actions of orders $2$, $3$, $4$ and $6$ on rotation algebras, we prove that the crossed products are Morita equivalent exactly when the action orders agree and the parameters lie in the same fractional-linear $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-orbit, generalizing the result of B\"onicke et al.\ from irrational to arbitrary real parameters. We also construct infinite families of distinct parameters giving Morita-equivalent crossed products for each fixed $W$ satisfying the stated hypotheses.

papers.title: Models of n-dimensional categories as $n\to\infty$
papers.authors: Viktoriya Ozornova, Martina Rovelli, Tashi Walde
papers.abstract: We verify that saturated complicial sets model the right limit of the $\infty$-categories of $(\infty,n)$-categories, whereas the canonical comparison with the left limit is not an equivalence. By contrast the category of strict $\omega$-categories is equivalent to both the right and left limits of the categories of strict $n$-categories.

papers.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
papers.authors: Riley Decker, Matthew C. B. Zaremsky
papers.abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ there exists a finite generating set $A$ such that $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;A)$ is contractible for all $t\ge 1$. We prove this as a special case of a more general result about certain groups. Let $G$ be a group and $H$ a subgroup. A subgroup $F\le G$ is a supplement of $H$ in $G$ if $G=HF$. We prove that for $H\le G$ with $F$ a supplement of $H$ in $G$, for generating sets $A_H$ and $A_G$ of $H$ and $G$ satisfying certain conditions involving $F$, the Vietoris-Rips complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;A_G)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A_H)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$. In particular this applies to affine Coxeter groups, since free abelian groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. Beyond these general results, we also investigate affine Coxeter groups $W_a$ specifically using the standard generating set $S$, and prove contractibility of $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ for large enough $t$.

papers.title: cuPDQPx: A GPU-Accelerated Restarted Halpern PDHG for Large-Scale Convex Quadratic Programming
papers.authors: Haihao Lu, Zedong Peng, Jinwen Yang
papers.abstract: We present cuPDQPx, a GPU-accelerated, factorization-free first-order solver for large-scale convex quadratic programming (QP). Building on the restarted reflected Halpern primal-dual framework of cuPDLPx, we introduce an auxiliary-variable splitting that yields explicit updates without linearizing the quadratic objective or solving inner quadratic subproblems. A preconditioned proximal point interpretation yields both sublinear and linear fixed-point residual convergence guarantees. For practical efficiency, cuPDQPx integrates diagonal preconditioning, step-size selection, adaptive restart, and adaptive primal and quadratic weight updates. cuPDQPx is implemented in C and CUDA with optimized sparse matrix-vector products, kernel fusion, and CUDA Graphs. Numerical experiments on the Maros-M\'esz\'aros collection, a convex subset of QPLIB, and synthetic large-scale QPs demonstrate that cuPDQPx has strong numerical performance at both $10^{-4}$ and $10^{-8}$ tolerances.

papers.title: Sparse domination for $q$-variation associated with functional calculus
papers.abstract: We establish sparse domination for the $q$-variation of functional calculus families $\{\varphi(tL)\}_{t>0}$ on spaces of homogeneous type. Under generalized Gaussian estimates, we consider holomorphic multipliers of injective accretive operators, and Sobolev-type spectral multipliers of non-negative self-adjoint operators. For the Sobolev-type multipliers, we show that our regularity assumption is sharp in general except the endpoint. As corollaries, we obtain weighted $q$-variational estimates for Bochner-Riesz means and regularized Schr\"{o}dinger groups. Finally, we give several examples of operators to which our results apply.

papers.title: The Mean First-Reaction Time on a Thin Filament in a 3-D Domain
papers.authors: Denis S. Grebenkov, Theodore Kolokolnikov, Alan E. Lindsay, Michael J. Ward
papers.abstract: We study the mean first-reaction time (MFRT) of a Brownian particle in a bounded three-dimensional domain $\Omega$ with a reflecting boundary $\partial\Omega$, that contains a thin reactive filament. The filament is a tube of cross-sectional diameter $\varepsilon\ll 1$ around a smooth closed curve $\Gamma$, and its surface is partially reactive with reactivity $b$. As $\varepsilon\to 0$ the filament reduces to a line source in the outer problem. Its cross-section enters only through a logarithmic reactive capacitance $d_c(b)$, so that the MFRT is $\mathcal{O}(-\log[\varepsilon d_c])$. This contrasts with the $\mathcal{O}(\eps^{-1})$ scaling for spatially localized traps of radius $\eps$. Using matched asymptotic expansions, we derive a Fredholm integral equation on $\Gamma$ for the line density of the reactive flux. It sums all powers of $\nu\equiv -1/\log[\varepsilon d_c]$ and involves two geometric quantities: the regular part $R$ of the Neumann Green's function, which encodes the interaction of $\Gamma$ with $\partial\Omega$, and an intrinsic self-energy of $\Gamma$ that depends only on its shape. The framework extends to multiple filaments, splitting probabilities, a spatially heterogeneous diffusivity, and the principal eigenvalue of the Laplacian. For the unit sphere we solve the integral equation with a simple trapezoidal Nystr\"om scheme, and we validate the predictions for rings, linked rings and torus knots against full 3-D finite-element solutions.

papers.title: A Primer on Instanton Physics - A Short Course
papers.abstract: These six lectures, delivered at the University of New Brunswick 6-21 October 2026, are an introduction to instantons in quantum mechanics and quantum field theory for senior undergraduate and beginning graduate students. The first four lectures deal solely with particle mechanics, building the necessary background for the last two that cover applications in semi-classical field theory.

papers.title: The convolution product is generally not an open map
papers.abstract: We show that the convolution product $\ell^1(G)\times \ell^1(G)\to \ell^1(G)$ is not an open map if $G$ is either non-abelian or contains an element of infinite order. The case $G=\mathbb Z$ solves a problem posed by Kania and Ma\'slany.

papers.title: Solitons on Statistical Manifolds and Their Submanifolds
papers.abstract:
Statistical manifolds, introduced by Amari in information geometry, carry a pair of dual torsion-free connections $(
abla,
abla^{*})$ together with a Riemannian metric. In this chapter we survey the theory of \emph{statistical solitons}, that is, vector fields and constants that solve the Ricci-soliton equation simultaneously for $
abla$ and $
abla^{*}$, together with the statistical analogue of almost quasi-Yamabe solitons. We discuss two principal settings: (i) statistical warped products $\R	imes_f N_2$ and $N_1	imes_f\R$ for (pseudo) Riemannian manifolds $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$, where the soliton equation constrains the warping function; and (ii) statistical submanifolds of Kenmotsu statistical manifolds, where the position of the Reeb field $\xi$ relative to the submanifold and the presence of concircular or concurrent vector fields determine the Einstein, $\eta$-Einstein or quasi-Einstein character of the submanifold. We further review the results of Blaga and Chen on gradient solitons and statistical structures, in particular the connections $
abla^{	heta}$ defined by a $1$-form, volume formulas and bounds for the Ricci tensor. We also describe Chen-type inequalities for statistical warped product submanifolds, which give the extrinsic context in which such solitons live. Key steps of the proofs, remarks on the sharpness of hypotheses, worked examples, and open problems are included.

papers.title: Existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for weighted complete intersections
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth well formed Fano or Calabi-Yau weighted complete intersection admits a nef-partition. As an application, we establish the existence of weak Landau-Ginzburg models for all such Fano weighted complete intersections.

papers.title: Transverse rational curves and the homogeneity of contact Fano manifolds
papers.authors: Zhengyu Hu, Kefeng Liu, Xueyuan Wan
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth complex projective contact Fano manifold is homogeneous under its connected contact automorphism group. The argument extends and simplifies the incidence method of our earlier proof of the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture. After the classical reductions, balanced transverse rational maps through every point yield tangent sections extending across the nodal boundary. These establish irreducibility and nonlinearity of the general variety of minimal rational tangents associated with contact lines, enabling Hwang's descent theorem to produce global vector fields generating the tangent bundle. Consequences include very ampleness of the contact line bundle, embeddedness of every balanced rational map, K\"ahler--Einstein existence, K-polystability, and the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture.

papers.title: The Birthday Problem and the Birthday Person Problem: Intuition, Probability and Cryptographic Applications
papers.authors: Alisson Garcia da Silva, Iarythssa Duarte de Ara\'ujo, Francisco M\'arcio Barboza
papers.abstract: The present work discusses the birthday problem and the birthday person problem, two classical problems in probability theory widely used to illustrate situations in which human intuition diverges from mathematical results. Taking the work of [1] as its main reference, the study analyzes the probability of birthday coincidences within groups of people, considering a year with 365 days and assuming that all birth dates are equally likely. The birthday problem seeks to determine the probability that at least two people in a group share the same birthday, showing that, even in relatively small groups, the probability of a coincidence increases rapidly due to the large number of possible pairwise comparisons among individuals. In contrast, the birthday person problem investigates the probability that a previously selected person shares the same birthday as another member of the group. This probability increases more slowly, since the number of relevant comparisons is restricted to the pairs formed by the selected person and the remaining members of the group. Despite the interpretative differences, both problems share a similar mathematical foundation based on combinatorial analysis and probability theory. In addition to the theoretical development, numerical results and graphical representations are presented to illustrate the behavior of the probabilities involved and to visualize how the likelihood of coincidences increases as the number of people grows. Finally, applications related to computing and cryptography are discussed, particularly the study of collisions in hash functions and the so-called birthday attack. The discussion highlights the importance of probabilistic reasoning in understanding apparently unlikely phenomena, while also emphasizing how the growth in the number of possible combinations directly influences the results obtained.

papers.title: Examples of rigid Twistor D-modules
papers.abstract: The well-established theory of D-modules gives a framework to study linear differential equations from the perspective of algebraic geometry. A significant advancement in this theory has been the introduction of Twistor D-modules by Claude Sabbah and Takuro Mochizuki: These objects expose inherent, but hidden information of the underlying differential equations in an elegant way. We explain the foundational concepts of Twistor D-modules and give concrete examples of these objects. We introduce a notion of rigidity for Twistor D-modules, which these examples fulfill. We conclude with a certain algebraicity conjecture about rigid Twistor D-modules, which we prove in a special case.

papers.title: Eternal Total Positivity and Matrix-Dependent Hadamard Thresholds
papers.authors: Shaun M. Fallat, Seyed Mahmoud Manjegani, Mohammadrahim Saeidi Dahaki
papers.abstract: We study entrywise powers of totally positive matrices. Our first question is which matrices remain totally positive under every positive Hadamard power. We call them eternally totally positive. Our second question concerns a fixed totally positive matrix: what is the smallest exponent after which all of its entrywise powers are totally positive? We call this number the Hadamard threshold of the matrix. Unlike the usual critical exponent, this threshold depends on the individual matrix. We give a complete characterization in order three, obtain explicit bounds for the transition exponent, and construct symmetric matrices that realize every threshold in $[0,1)$. We also prove the basic transformation rules and continuity of the threshold on the normalized $3\times3$ totally positive cone. For higher orders, we introduce the logarithmic core and use it to expand each minor near the zero exponent. This reduces the $4\times4$ problem to the full determinant and the $3\times3$ submatrices. For symmetric $4\times4$ matrices, we show that a positive-definite logarithmic core makes the full determinant positive for every positive exponent. A two-parameter Hankel family then realizes every threshold in $(1,2)$. Hence the exact range of thresholds in the symmetric order-four case is $[0,1)\cup(1,2)$; neither $1$ nor $2$ is attained. We also give a recursive symmetric ETP criterion in every order and an explicit classification for symmetric Toeplitz matrices of order four. In order five, a certified example exhibits an intermediate-power obstruction in a nonprincipal minor. An explicit order-three condition and a finite critical-point test give a complete order-five test.

papers.title: Sharp global stability for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near equilibrium
papers.authors: Xuwen Chen, Shunlin Shen, Zhifei Zhang
papers.abstract: We study the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation near a global Maxwellian and have found the bifurcation between the stability and instability in $H_{x}^{s}$ Sobolev space. We prove a strong-weak type instability result in the $s<1$ regularity regime, and establish the global stability under the regularity $s>1$ via the interplay between the dissipation and dispersive effects. In this intricate competition of dispersion, dissipation, large-velocity growth, and the asymmetric nature of the gain and loss terms, we prove that the instability is jointly generated by the dispersive effect and the loss term structure. To reach the sharp regularity for the global stability, we incorporate the dispersive effect into the dissipative energy framework for the analysis near equilibrium. This hence concludes sharp threshold and provides a complete characterization of global well-posedness near equilibrium.

papers.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
papers.abstract: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.

papers.title: Localization of generators of Markov processes via the Dynkin operator
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider a Feller process whose resolvent has the strong Feller property. Using the Dynkin operator of this process, we define local realizations of the generator on an open subset $U$ of its state space. In particular, this allows us to describe the generator of the process killed upon leaving a regular, open subset $U$ as a realization of a maximal operator subject to Dirichlet boundary conditions. Besides the definition via the Dynkin operator, we also consider other possible definitions of such a local realization: a definition in terms of the unkilled semigroup, a definition based on approximation with elements of the generator and a probabilistic definition using martingales. Under mild additional assumptions, we prove that all these definitions are equivalent.

papers.title: Central limit theorems for high-dimensional ridge regression under uniform subsampling
papers.authors: Thomas Lam, Nina D\"ornemann, Holger Dette
papers.abstract: We study ridge regression based on uniformly subsampled observations in high-dimensional linear models, where the number of predictors and the sample size grow proportionally. Subsampling is implemented through independent Bernoulli indicators with a common selection probability. We establish central limit theorems for linear contrasts of the ridge estimator, allowing for non-Gaussian predictors and general population covariance matrices. Under a vanishing-signal assumption, we obtain an explicit bias correction in the isotropic case and develop consistent estimators of the asymptotic variances. These results enable asymptotically valid tests for linear contrasts of the regression parameter in the isotropic setting. Our proofs exploit the resolvent representation of the ridge estimator and combine leave-one-out arguments with deterministic equivalents from random matrix theory.

papers.title: Small-time Wasserstein action for KPZ and $\Phi^4_3$
papers.abstract: We determine the leading small-time Wasserstein action of the full spatial laws of centered KPZ and dynamical $\Phi^4_3$, both started from zero. The leading term is Gaussian, with an explicit heat-trace constant. A common comparison also determines the ratio of length to displacement. For KPZ, a first-chaos cancellation yields a quadratic coupling error. For $\Phi^4_3$, two weighted entropies and an adjoint estimate give comparison bounds uniform in the spectral cutoff. Integrating a Gaussian rotation gives a differentiable realization of the full law; the comparison holds at every positive time.

papers.title: Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for Nonlinear Optimization
papers.authors: Youngkyu Lee, George Em Karniadakis, Alena Kopani\v{c}\'akov\'a
papers.abstract: We introduce the Safeguarded Neurally-Accelerated Preconditioning (SNAP) framework for hybridizing nonlinear optimization methods with pre-trained neural operators (NOs). SNAP targets parametric optimization problems arising from variational formulations of nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), where many parameter instances require repeated solves. Inspired by multilevel line-search methods, SNAP operates in cycles, combining classical optimization steps with a search direction generated by a pre-trained NO. Since NO-generated search directions carry no a priori descent guarantee, SNAP employs an a posteriori safeguard by accepting only corrections that satisfy prescribed descent and acceptance conditions. We prove global convergence of the SNAP algorithm and show that it preserves the convergence rate of the underlying optimization method independently of the employed NO architecture. Moreover, we also show that when the NO corrections are sufficiently accurate, SNAP converges faster, with the improvement directly related to the NO training error. To demonstrate SNAP's efficiency in practice, we run numerical experiments on a diverse set of nonlinear parametric optimization problems, including parametric minimal surface, Allen--Cahn, and nonlinear Helmholtz problems. The efficiency of SNAP is demonstrated by comparing two NO architectures, Fourier neural operator (FNO) and Transolver, and by using SNAP as a standalone solver and as a nonlinear preconditioner. Our numerical results show a substantial reduction in the number of required iterations, while demonstrating robustness and generalization across a wide range of problem parameters and mesh resolutions.

papers.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
papers.abstract: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper \'etale correspondence $\Omega:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(\Omega)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.

papers.title: Random Non-Commutative Error-Correcting Codes
papers.abstract: Chapman, Dinur, and Lubotzky recently introduced the theory of non-commutative error-correcting codes, generalizing classical coding theory to arbitrary groups via $\delta$-robust subsets used to detect proper subgroups. Building on this foundation, this paper systematically studies an analogue of random codes for arbitrary groups, exploring the extent to which the classical Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound holds in this non-commutative setting. While random universal codes of linear size in free groups are shown to be asymptotically bad, we establish a complete characterization for general families of finite groups. Specifically, a family of finite groups admits good random codes (forming a GV family) if and only if it exhibits uniform polynomial maximal-subgroup growth. Furthermore, we provide explicit quantitative bounds on the rate and optimal distance range based on intrinsic parameters, proving that families of finite solvable groups always form GV families and determining the exact probabilistic rate for direct powers of a fixed finite simple group.

papers.title: Dimensions of Fano schemes of lines on hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^n_\mathbb{C}$ be a smooth hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$, with $n\ge3$. We prove that an $m$-dimensional integral projective family of lines sweeping a variety of dimension $y$ satisfies $m\le\max\{2y-d-1,n-3\}$. This proves the de Jong-Debarre conjecture for $d\le n$ and the Beheshti-Starr bound for lines on smooth hypersurfaces for $d\ge n+1$.

papers.title: Composition factors and finite representation type
papers.authors: Liang Chen, Zhenxian Chen, Yongyi Wen, Weiheng Xia
papers.abstract: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.

papers.title: Order invariance of the generalized Rosenblatt transform on standard Borel spaces
papers.authors: Christian T. Covington, Jeffrey W. Miller
papers.abstract: The Rosenblatt transform maps a random vector to independent uniform variables through successive conditional distribution functions; for laws on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with atomless conditional distributions and a fixed order of the coordinates, it is the almost surely unique monotone triangular map with this property. For a fixed reference law, transform-based tests remain valid under every fixed admissible order, but that choice can still affect their statistical power. We extend the generalized Rosenblatt transform to laws on countable products of standard Borel spaces, which requires, in addition to an order on the index set, a total order on each component space. For fixed orders, we establish identification and uniqueness results for this extended generalized Rosenblatt transform (EGRT) that parallel those for the classical transform. We then characterize order dependence in two senses: first demonstrating conditions under which the EGRT is invariant under linear extensions of prescribed partial orders, and second showing that under every admissible order the output of the EGRT retains all the statistical information from the input observations over reference-dominated families. We close with a brief discussion of what these results mean for the relationship between order choice and goodness-of-fit testing.

papers.title: Primitive flag-transitive generalized quadrangles
papers.authors: Timothy C. Burness, Tao Feng, Jianbing Lu
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{Q}$ be a finite thick generalized quadrangle of order $(s,t)$ with a flag-transitive automorphism group $G$. A well-known conjecture of Kantor from the early 1990s asserts that up to duality, $\mathcal{Q}$ is either of classical type, or it is one of two sporadic examples of order $(3,5)$ or $(15,17)$. Although this fundamental problem in finite geometry remains open, it has been resolved in some special cases. For example, a theorem of Buekenhout and Van Maldeghem from 1994 proves Kantor's conjecture under the stronger assumption that $G$ acts distance-transitively on the set of points of $\mathcal{Q}$.
  In this paper, we study Kantor's conjecture in the setting where $G$ acts primitively on both the points and lines of $\mathcal{Q}$. Here a theorem of Bamberg et al. implies that $G$ is almost simple with socle $X$ a finite simple group of Lie type, and several special cases where the Lie rank of $X$ is at most $2$ have recently been settled in a sequence of papers. Our main theorem resolves the problem for all almost simple groups of Lie type, thereby completing the proof of Kantor's conjecture for generalized quadrangles with a flag-transitive automorphism group acting primitively on points and lines.

papers.title: From Entanglement Bootstrap to DHR Theory
papers.abstract: We establish a direct connection between the entanglement bootstrap and the Doplicher--Haag--Roberts theory of superselection sectors for two-dimensional quantum spin systems. Under the entanglement-bootstrap assumptions, we prove Haag duality and establish a one-to-one correspondence between simple entanglement-bootstrap anyon types and irreducible superselection sectors. For each fusion channel, we further construct an affine bijection from density matrices on the entanglement-bootstrap fusion space to normalized positive intertwiners in the corresponding operator-algebraic fusion channel. These results connect the entropic and operator-algebraic descriptions of anyons directly, without passing through exactly solvable lattice models.

papers.title: Representations and $n$-universality of hermitian lattices over local and number fields
papers.abstract: Let $E/F$ be a quadratic field extension. For any positive integer $n$ an integral hermitian form over $E/F$ is called $n$-universal if it represents all integral hermitian forms of rank $n$ over $E/F$. We study $n$-universal hermitian forms when $F$ is a local field of characteristic $\neq 2$ or a number field. In the local case, we characterize $n$-universal integral hermitian forms and provide finite criterion sets for $n$-universality. In the number field case, we show that an indefinite integral hermitian form is $n$-universal if and only if it is $n$-universal everywhere locally.

papers.title: Solution of Laczkovich's Lipschitz mapping problem
papers.abstract: In 1991, Laczkovich asked whether every measurable set of positive measure in $\mathbb R^d$ can be mapped onto a cube with a Lipschitz map. We show that the answer is positive for every $d$. Our results also give a positive answer for Kolmogorov's problem on contractions onto polygons with small measure loss in the case of Jordan measurable sets.

papers.title: Intrinsic Non-Reductive Geometric Invariant Theory and Moduli Spaces of Principal Bundles with Non-Reductive Structure Groups
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of moduli spaces for algebraic stacks with a weak action of $\Theta = [\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$ (including stacks of filtered objects and unstable $\Theta$-strata) for which the center admits a good moduli space and the retraction to the center has flat, finitely presented relative inertia, providing a stack-intrinsic generalization of the existence of non-reductive Geometric Invariant Theory quotients. As an application, we construct quasi-projective coarse moduli spaces of principal bundles over a smooth projective curve with non-reductive structure groups, including moduli spaces of Ramanathan unstable principal bundles of fixed Harder--Narasimhan type.

papers.title: Number of ends of conjugacy diagrams
papers.authors: Alexey V. Naianzin, Andronick A. Arutyunov
papers.abstract: For each $n\geq 2$, we construct a finitely generated group $W_n$ with a conjugacy class such that the conjugacy diagram of this class has exactly $n$ ends. For this class, we compute the quotient spaces of the space of derivations of the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[W_n]$ modulo quasi-inner and inner derivations, as well as the corresponding component of the first Hochschild cohomology.

papers.title: A Feasible-Direction-Type Method for Nonconvex Optimization with Infeasible Starts
papers.abstract: We develop an infeasible-start extension of the Topkis--Veinott feasible-direction method for nonconvex composite optimization. At each main iteration, a strongly convex local model is used to obtain objective descent while limiting increases in constraint violation. A separate feasibility-reduction step is invoked when feasibility improvement is needed. Under a feasibility-reduction condition, we establish the standard first-order rate for reducing the Fritz John residual and constraint violation. We then verify that both proximal-gradient and regularized Gauss--Newton methods applied to minimizing the squared constraint-violation function satisfy the required feasibility-reduction property under a Polyak--{\L}ojasiewicz condition. Numerical experiments compare the reduction methods, including an experimental prox-linear variant, and compare the scalar-regularized and curvature-enhanced subproblem formulations.

papers.title: The geometry of Floquet states
papers.authors: Vladimir Y. Cherynak, John R. Klein
papers.abstract:
This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians.
  The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.

papers.title: Gradient Estimates for Hessian Equations with Measure Data
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the interior gradient estimates for $k$-Hessian equations with measure data. We use the ideas from the potential theories for the $p$-Laplacian type equations and pointwise estimates of $k$-subharmonic functions by Labutin. The interior gradient regularity is optimal for $k\geqslant3$, while for $k=2$, we prove the interior $W^{2,1+\varepsilon}$ and $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimates for $2$-subharmonic solutions.

papers.title: Extended weak order in all rank three Coxeter groups
papers.authors: Grant Barkley, Colin Defant, Patricia Hersh, Jon McCammond, Thomas McConville, David E Speyer
papers.abstract: We prove that extended weak order is a lattice for all rank 3 Coxeter groups. This was previously known in finite and affine types, and in the universal Coxeter group of rank 3. All other cases are new to this paper. As in earlier work, the proof proceeds by showing that all rank 3 Coxeter arrangements are clean arrangements, meaning that every biclosed set is weakly separated from its complement by a hyperplane. As a consequence, we also deduce Dyer's Conjecture A for all rank 3 Coxeter groups, which asserts that cover relations in extended weak order are given by toggling a single root.

papers.title: Selection spectra and sharp perturbations of normal sequences
papers.abstract:
For a bounded sequence $y=(y_n)\subset E^*$ and $0<p<\infty$, let $$ G_p(y)=\{x\in E:(y_n(x))\in\ell_p\}, $$ and call $y$ $p$-strongly normal when $G_p(y)$ is dense in $E$. We study the spectra obtained by passing to subsequences and, for Schauder basic sequences, to normalized successive blocks. Their possible values are exactly $$ \varnothing,\quad (0,\infty),\quad (1,\infty),\quad [r,\infty),\quad (r,\infty)\qquad (r>1), $$ and the possible pairs are precisely the nested pairs. Every admissible pair has a normalized weakly null $1$-unconditional basic realization, even in the fixed dual $\ell_\infty(\mathfrak c)=\ell_1(\mathfrak c)^*$, and may be realized with empty spectrum for the original sequence.
  We also determine sharp universal perturbation classes: $\ell_p$ for $p$-strong normality at a fixed exponent, $c_0$ for the whole subsequence spectrum, and $\ell_1$ for the block spectrum. More generally, for every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal $A\subsetneq c_0$, membership of the error sequence in $A$ is exactly the universal condition preserving density of the $A$-summability domain.
  Finally, we extend the author's 2012 selection example from exponent one to every $p>0$ and to every proper symmetric Banach sequence ideal. The good subsequences are exactly those whose index sets have uniformly bounded runs of consecutive integers; in the good case the detected quotient is isomorphic to $c_0$ and the whole selected sequence is weak-star Schauder basic.

papers.title: Characterization of sets in metric spaces where the big Lipschitz derivative is infinite
papers.authors: Jes\'us Llorente, Oleksandr Maslyuchenko, Ziemowit W\'ojcicki
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a metric space without isolated points. In this paper we prove that $E$ is a $G_\delta$-set in $X$ if and only if there exists a continuous function $f:X\to\mathbb{R}$ whose big Lipschitz derivative is infinite precisely on $E$. To this end, we introduce a new generalization of the classical Takagi function to the setting of metric spaces.

papers.title: A Retrospective-Approximation Interior-Point Method
papers.authors: Frank E. Curtis, Zahra Khatti, Daniel P. Robinson
papers.abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for solving nonlinearly constrained continuous optimization problem instances wherein the objective function is defined by an expectation over a random variable argument and the constraints include inequalities (and perhaps equalities) involving functions that may be nonconvex. The algorithm combines a retrospective-approximation strategy for handling the objective and an interior-point approach for handling the constraints. In each iteration of an outer loop, the objective is approximated by an empirical average over a set of realizations of the random variable argument and the resulting sampled problem is solved with an interior-point method that allows inexact search-direction computations for computational flexibility. Termination conditions for the interior-point method are tailored for those needed for convergence guarantees by the outer loop. Over the outer loop, the sample set is updated adaptively in such a manner that convergence guarantees for solving the original optimization problem can be assured. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the proposed algorithm can outperform competing methods that have comparable theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: On strongly FP-injective accessibility and weakly FP-projective periodicity
papers.abstract: Accessibility results are established for (Cartan-Eilenberg) strongly FP-injective complexes, by first proving the accessibility of Strongly FP-injective modules and then utilizing the pseudopullback theorem. We also prove that every acyclic complex of weakly FP-projective modules has weakly FP-projective cycles over left $<\aleph_m$-coherent rings for a non-negative integer $m$. This is achieved by introducing the cotorsion pairs $\bigl(\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj,\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}inj\bigr)$, cogenerated by all $\aleph_m$-presentable weakly FP-projective modules, and proving that acyclic complexes of modules from the class $\mathcal{C}\aleph_mP\text{-}proj$ have weakly FP-projective cycles for every non-negative integer $m$.

papers.title: Improved LCL Equivalences and Curve Decoding Alphabet Sizes
papers.authors: Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami, Yihang Sun, Mary Wootters
papers.abstract:
Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) properties, introduced by Levi, Mosheiff, and Shagrithaya (2025), capture coding-theoretic properties such as list decoding and list recovery. They showed that every LCL property has the same rate threshold for random linear codes (RLC) and random Reed--Solomon codes (RRS). Brakensiek, Chen, Dhar, and Zhang (2025) extended this to random additive codes. Thus any property of all subspace design codes holds for RLCs and RRS at the same rate.
  In this work, we improve the probabilistic guarantees in the RRS local equivalence theorem and extend the equivalence to all known subspace design constructions individually. Each such construction, including folded Reed--Solomon codes, has the same LCL threshold as RLC and RRS codes. We apply these results to alphabet-size bounds for curve decoding.
  Curve decoding, introduced by Goyal and Guruswami (2025) and Carmon et al. (2026), is a row-span-constrained LCL property implying proximity gaps (PG), correlated agreement (CA), and mutual correlated agreement (MCA), relevant to IOPs and SNARKs. Informally, a rate-$R$ code $C \subset \mathbb{F}^n$ is $(\ell,\delta,a,b)$-curve decodable if any degree-$\ell$ curve $u:\mathbb{F}\to\mathbb{F}^n$ that is $\delta$-close to $C$ on at least $a$ points has at least $b\leq a$ nearby codewords lying on a degree-$\ell$ curve in $C$.
  Goyal and Guruswami (2025) and Goyal, Guruswami, Sun, and Wootters (2026) established curve decodability for RLC and RRS codes at radius $\delta$ approaching $1-R$, but with large alphabets in $\ell$ and $\eta:=1-R-\delta$. Using our improved LCL equivalence and rank-sensitive counting inspired by Goyal and Guruswami (2026), we exponentially improve alphabet requirements while matching the best known values of $(a,b)$. For $\ell=O(1)$, our alphabet-size bounds match the best known for list decoding, and improves results for PG, CA, and MCA.

papers.title: Early warning of critical transitions: Distinguishing supercritical and subcritical bifurcations from noisy observations
papers.authors: Paul A. Sanders, Christian Kuehn, Bastian Hilder, Robbin Bastiaansen
papers.abstract: Early-warning methods can indicate that a system is approaching a loss of stability, but they do not usually reveal whether the approaching bifurcation is supercritical or subcritical. We investigate whether this distinction can be made from noisy pre-transition observations. For this investigation, we extend a regression-based stability method by including the leading cubic nonlinear term, whose sign is used to predict the bifurcation type. We test the method on a stochastic pitchfork model and a spatial stochastic Swift-Hohenberg equation. In both models, classification improves with longer observation horizons, closer proximity to the bifurcation, stronger noise, and larger nonlinear effects. However, these conditions are also linked to a higher risk of noise-induced tipping in the subcritical case. The useful early-warning window is therefore determined by a balance between obtaining enough information to identify the bifurcation type and doing so before noise-induced tipping becomes too likely. In spatially extended systems, we find that observing the full spatial field allows classification over shorter observation horizons, and performance improves when a broader range of spatial modes contributes to the observed dynamics. Altogether, we identify the conditions under which the method can reliably distinguish between supercritical and subcritical bifurcations.

papers.title: An asymptotic Jensen-Polya criterion for GRH
papers.abstract: The Jensen--P\'olya criterion expresses the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for Dedekind zeta-functions as a real-rootedness condition on their Jensen polynomials. Previous asymptotic results require large shifts, while computations establish real-rootedness in the Riemann case through a finite range of degrees. Here we study the unshifted family as the degree tends to infinity. For every number field $K$, we prove unconditionally that $J_{K,d}(X)$ is nonzero and has at least $d-C_K\sqrt{d\log d}$ distinct negative real zeros for all sufficiently large $d$, where $C_K>0$ depends only on $K$. Therefore, the proportion of real zeros tends to one with error $O_K(\sqrt{\log d/d})$. The main theorems have been autoformalized in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.

papers.title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
papers.authors: Sutanay Bhattacharya, Sylvie Corteel, Yuhan Jiang, John Lentfer, Brendon Rhoades
papers.abstract:
We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$.
  We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.

papers.title: Homogeneous polynomial approximation on symmetric convex bodies: A proof of Kro\'o's conjecture
papers.abstract: We resolve Kro\'o's 2004 conjecture on homogeneous polynomial approximation in every dimension, without smoothness or curvature assumptions. For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ with nonempty interior, every continuous real function on $\partial K$ is uniformly approximated by sums of homogeneous polynomials of degrees $n$ and $n+1$ as $n\to\infty$. Moreover, approximation of the constant function by homogeneous polynomials of degree $2n$ is uniform over all such bodies in each fixed dimension. Via homogenization, we also resolve Kro\'o's 2019 weighted approximation conjecture for every convex admissible weight on Euclidean space. The key construction produces homogeneous polynomials with a common Gaussian boundary profile and localization errors controlled by arbitrary polynomial weights. Its analytic core is a weighted Gaussian approximation theorem: for \(d\ge2\), sufficiently broad Gaussians on $\mathbb R^{d-1}$ can be approximated by $e^{-f}F$, where $f$ is nonnegative, convex and Lipschitz with $f(0)=0$, and $F$ is a Schwartz function with Fourier support in an arbitrarily small ball about the origin. Small Fourier support allows Taylor truncation to a lower degree, while the remainder enforces decay through homogenization. We then use positive spherical quadrature and degree raising to yield the full approximation theorem.

papers.title: Continuous Envy-Free Allocation via Reciprocal Preference Matrices: An Alternative to Sperner-Based Discretization
papers.authors: Luis \'Angel Calvo Pascual, Susana Merch\'an Rubira, Diego de Pereda Sebasti\'an, Javier Rodrigo Hitos
papers.abstract: Fair allocation problems on a continuous simplex are often approached through Sperner-type discretizations: agents label mesh vertices according to their preferences and a fully labelled elementary triangle gives a discrete localization of a fair outcome. We develop a continuous alternative for three agents and three alternatives by representing preferences with multiplicatively consistent reciprocal pairwise-comparison matrices. Two independent ratios per agent induce exact linear indifference boundaries and turn envy-free allocation into a finite-dimensional feasibility problem. For the six possible assignments, we introduce an assignment score $\Phi$ built from the agents' consistent priority vectors and prove that an incentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique minimizer of $\Phi$, whereas a disincentive solution component is nonempty if and only if its assignment is the unique maximizer. Consequently, the strict solution region is either empty or a unique convex preference region whose closure lies in the interior of the simplex. The weak solution set is never empty and degenerates exactly when $\Phi$ has ties. We also compare the exact continuous formulation with Sperner-based discretization, including the boundary convention required in the disincentive model. Under exact consistency, the model uses six independent pairwise thresholds, whereas a regular triangular mesh with resolution $m$ contains $(m+1)(m+2)/2$ vertices. The method therefore exchanges a stronger parametric preference assumption for an exact continuous solution set and a resolution-independent elicitation stage.

papers.title: The vanishing viscosity limit for the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations around a small obstacle
papers.abstract: We investigate the interaction between a vanishing obstacle and the vanishing viscosity limit in the setting of the inhomogeneous incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. We work in the space exterior to a small obstacle in three dimensions. We prove quantitative convergence rates, assuming that the obstacle is sufficiently small, namely smaller than a constant times the viscosity. The convergence holds as long as the solution to the limit problem is known to exist and stays sufficiently smooth. This extends the results of Iftimie, Lopes Filho and Nussenzveig Lopes to the inhomogeneous Navier-Stokes equations. Moreover, we can show improved convergence rates and convergence of the gradient in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

papers.title: Serre's conjectures for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$
papers.abstract: The present article proves (assuming GRH and a minor technical result) the veracity of Serre's conjectures for the field $\Q(\sqrt{13})$. In doing so, we prove a ``reduction to level 1'' result that holds for any real quadratic field with narrow class number one. However we can only establish the needed base cases for $\Q(\sqrt{13})$.

papers.title: Exh subspaces of bounded variation spaces generated by submeasures
papers.authors: Jacek Gulgowski, Adam Kwela, Pawe{\l} Sawicki, Jacek Tryba
papers.abstract: In the present paper we are building one more bridge between the theory of ideals on the set of natural numbers and the theory of spaces of functions of bounded variation. It is already known that $F_\sigma$ ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Fin}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a nice generalization of different concepts from the theory of functions of bounded variation (Waterman variation and Chanturya classes). In this paper we show that analytic P-ideals (that is, ideals of the form $\text{Exh}(\phi)$, where $\phi$ is a lower semicontinuous submeasure on $\mathbb{N}$) lead to a generalization of spaces of functions continuous in $\Lambda$-variation. The properties of this generalization are investigated.

papers.title: Anisotropic error estimates for the $L^{2}$-projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces
papers.authors: Joaqu\'in Valenzuela D\'iaz, Yuan Wang, Sander Rhebergen
papers.abstract: Anisotropic error estimates are determined for the $L^2$-orthogonal projection onto discontinuous finite element spaces in two and three dimensions. These estimates are determined in $W^{m,p}$-seminorms, in which $p \in [1,\infty]$ and $0 \le m \le k+1$, where $k \ge 0$ is the polynomial degree. The analysis relies on a geometric condition that is equivalent to the maximum angle condition. As an application, an apriori error analysis is presented for a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin discretization of the Poisson problem on two and three dimensional anisotropic meshes.

papers.title: Universality in randomly connected neural networks: old and new on a conjecture of Geman and Hwang
papers.abstract: Randomly connected networks are ubiquitous in computer science, physics or biology. A central question is whether, and how, their collective dynamics depend on the choice of the distribution of the random couplings. Forty years ago, Geman and Hwang formulated a precise version of this \emph{universality} question for randomly connected neural networks. We come back to these conjectures, review what was proven since, provide a few new extensions and propose new conjectures in this paper. For $n$ neuron networks with couplings with a mean scaling as $1/n$ and light enough tails, two classes of limits are expected. For \emph{weakly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance $o(1/n)$, the network is predicted to converge to a McKean--Vlasov equation, and a broad literature has established this under general assumptions. For \emph{strongly heterogeneous} couplings, with variance of order $1/n$, the limit is a non-Markovian equation driven by a self-consistent Gaussian process. After landmark results for Gaussian couplings, universality was only recently established for linear interactions, while the continuous-time nonlinear case relevant to neuroscience remained open. Here, in the weakly heterogeneous regime, we prove quenched convergence on every time interval under a fourth-moment assumption only, and convergence in probability under an assumption slightly stronger than a second moment. In the strongly heterogeneous regime, we prove convergence for nonlinear interactions in continuous time, averaged over sub-Gaussian couplings and on every time interval, by a relative-entropy comparison with Gaussian couplings. We then extend the conjecture to heavy-tailed couplings, and propose a limit driven by a self-consistent $\alpha$-stable process, for which we prove existence for every $\alpha\in(0,2)$ and uniqueness for $\alpha\in[1,2)$, and provide extensive numerical evidence in all three cases.

papers.title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
papers.abstract: We give an analytic proof of the comparison conjectured by Das, \L{}ochowski, Matsuda and Perkowski for the fractional Brownian level-crossing constant: for standard fractional Brownian motion, $c_H>\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $0<H<1/2$ and $c_H<\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $1/2<H<1$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$. At $H=1/2$, both constants equal one. The main tool is Gaussian comparison under ordering of increment variances. It applies because truncated variation is translation invariant and lattice-submodular, as follows from its minimum-total-variation characterization. A tangent variogram produces Brownian motion with an independent Gaussian drift on the upper side, and a periodic Brownian bridge on the lower side. The former has an explicit stationary reflection rate. For the latter we calculate an integrated cyclic crossing count by first-passage Laplace transforms. Elementary hyperbolic, theta-series, and Gamma inequalities then give strict comparisons on both full parameter ranges. No numerical integration, simulation, interval certificate, or quantitative local expansion at $H=1/2$ is used.

papers.title: Sharp dimension bounds for right-angled hyperbolic polytopes
papers.abstract: We determine the largest dimensions in which right-angled hyperbolic polytopes of finite volume can exist. The dimension is at most eight in general, and at most four when all vertices lie at infinity. Both bounds are attained, improving the previously known upper bounds of twelve and six. Our proofs use elementary properties of hyperbolic polytopes together with bounds for configurations of points on spheres.

papers.title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
papers.abstract: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_\mu$ and the mass element $q_\sigma$. We show that $p_\mu-q_\sigma=wp_\mu$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.

papers.title: A Note on the Smoluchowski Coagulation-Fragmentation Equation with Fractional Laplacian
papers.abstract: In this work, we assess the well-posedness of the Smoluchowski coagulation-fragmentation equation with fractional Laplacian. In particular, we consider a truncated set of discrete Smoluchowski-type equations modeling the formation of clusters, with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, where the diffusive term describes a non-standard behavior in the movement of particles ('anomalous' diffusion).

papers.title: Uncertainty principles as forcing mechanisms
papers.abstract:
In this note we first consider the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. We show that it acts as a {\bf forcing mechanism} in the following sense. Real functions that approach its limit are close to Gaussian distributions, with proximity both in the sense of total variation distance and Wasserstein-1 distance.
  We next consider the uncertainty principle for functions defined on finite Abelian groups, and show that it acts as a forcing mechanism in the following sense. Functions that approach its limit are close (after translation and modulation by a complex exponential) to indicator functions of some subgroup, with proximity measured in ${\mathbb {L}}^1$-norm.

papers.title: Finite-size ignition laws near a vanishing branching deficit on near-regular simple graphs
papers.abstract: We study heterogeneous bootstrap percolation on uniform simple graphs with prescribed degrees of mean $d\to\infty$ and deviations at most $C\sqrt d$. Thresholds are independently one with probability $(1-c/d)/d$ and two otherwise; seeds form an independent uniform set of prescribed size $a$. Let $T_a$ be the terminal number of active vertices and $b$ be one minus the mean number of threshold-one descendants of a reached vertex. Let $K\sim d^2$ be the quadratic response coefficient. If $b>0$ and $nb^3/K\to\infty$, we prove, uniformly over seed counts $a$, $ \mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)=\Phi(\frac{a-n\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}}{w})+o(1)$ with $w=\sqrt{nb/K}$, where $\alpha_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the exact empirical response-barrier center and $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. Put $a_0=(n/K)^{1/3}$. If $d^4/n\to0$, $a/a_0\to x>0$ and $\lambda=ba_0\to\ell\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\mathbb{P}(T_a\ge n/2)\to p(x,\ell)$, the one-sided Brownian parabolic survival probability. A sequential absolute-error law joins these regimes. A graphical counterexample shows that replacing the exact center by its leading term can cause limiting probability error $1/2$. The proof balances adaptive early-exploration transfer against late concentration at a tunable physical horizon, despite exponentially rare simplicity. We also prove quantitative and mesoscopic-seed refinements in explicitly narrower regimes. The only external graph-enumeration input is a stated reduction of McKay--Wormald's estimate; the probabilistic estimates for the cascade argument are proved in the text and appendices.

papers.title: A Gasch\"utz Lemma for linear algebraic groups with applications to the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
papers.abstract: The classical Gasch\"utz Lemma states that for a surjective morphism $G\to H$ of finite groups, generators $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of $H$ can be lifted to generators $g_1,\ldots,g_d$ of $G$, provided that $G$ can be generated by $d$ elements. We prove an analog of this statement for linear algebraic groups. This has applications to the algebraic-geometric theory of linear differential equations: We show that every regular singular differential embedding problem over the rational function field has a regular singular solution. We also establish a purely algebraic variant of the Riemann-Hilbert correspondence on the punctured projective line that works over any countable algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.

papers.title: $L$-Space Knots in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n}$-like Knot Floer Homology
papers.abstract: It has been of particular interest in recent years to relate categorifications of quantum knot invariants like the Jones polynomial to Floer-theoretic invariants like knot Floer homology using spectral sequences. In pursuit of Rasmussen's conjecture, Dowlin constructed a family of invariants with properties like those of Khovanov and Rozansky's $\mathfrak{sl}_n$-homology theories. In this paper, we explore these invariants for $L$-space knots and thin knots. In particular, for $n\geq 2$ the invariants of thin knots can be computed from a change of coefficients from the minus flavor of knot Floer homology, and the same holds for an $L$-space knot exactly when an explicit condition relating $n$ to its Alexander polynomial is satisfied.

papers.title: Mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group
papers.authors: Gaia Bombardieri, Mattia Fogagnolo, Valentina Franceschi
papers.abstract: We study the arrival time equation of the mean-convex horizontal mean curvature flow in the Heisenberg group. We prove existence of viscosity solutions when the initial set is horizontally mean-convex and either non-characteristic, or axisymmetric and with horizontal mean curvature extending continuously across the characteristic set. A key ingredient is an approximation scheme by sets with prescribed Riemannian mean curvature, which preserves the mean-curvature bounds up to an arbitrarily small error. We further show that, when the evolving level sets form a generalized \(C^2\)-foliation, the horizontal mean curvature blows up around characteristic points. This provides an obstruction to self-similar evolution in the axisymmetric class considered above and, in particular, shows that the Pansu sphere cannot evolve self-similarly.

papers.title: Controllability of Nonlocal Partial Differential Equations
papers.authors: D. Cardona, S. E. Chorfi, F. Et-tahri, L. Maniar
papers.abstract: This chapter provides a short survey of recent developments in the controllability of nonlocal partial differential equations. We first review controllability results for evolution equations involving nonlocal spatial operators. Particular attention is devoted to unique continuation properties, observability inequalities, and Carleman estimates in establishing controllability properties. We then discuss controllability issues for partial differential equations with memory terms, highlighting how memory effects influence reachable states, null controllability, and exact controllability. We review and compare various analytical techniques developed to overcome the difficulties arising from the nonlocal structure. We also provide a critical assessment of some of these methods. Throughout the chapter, we emphasize the interplay between controllability and observability, the adaptation of classical control methods to nonlocal settings, and the distinctive phenomena that arise in comparison with local equations. We then discuss geometric inequalities and their role in the controllability of diffusion models. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current challenges and several open problems, aiming to provide directions for future research.

papers.title: Variable Metric Three Operator Splitting
papers.abstract:
To minimize the sum $f + g + h$ of three convex functions when $f$ is differentiable with a Lipschitz-continuous gradient,
  we present a proximal algorithm, variable-metric three operator splitting (VMTOS), a generalization of the three operator splitting (TOS) scheme of Davis and Yin.
  We establish convergence guarantees by controlling changes in the metric.
  The smallest saddle-point residual among the first $k$ primal-dual iterates is $\tilde{O}(k^{-1/2})$.
  When $f$ and the convex conjugate $h^*$ are strongly convex and the accepted metrics and their inverses are uniformly bounded, the rate improves to $\tilde{O}(\beta^k)$ for some $\beta \in (0,1)$.
  We develop a practical Barzilai--Borwein update for diagonal metrics that satisfies our bound on metric changes.
  Under the same strong convexity assumptions, this update guarantees the required uniform metric bounds, yielding R-linear convergence.
  Numerical experiments on benchmark optimization problems show that VMTOS is competitive with other proximal algorithms.

papers.title: Optimization-based lane-changing trajectory planning in mixed traffic with embedded input convex neural networks
papers.authors: Yuanxiang Yang, Yu Liu, Fabricio Oliveira, Yu Han, Claudio Roncoli
papers.abstract: Lane-changing (LC) maneuvers are highly challenging vehicle interactions, with substantial implications for traffic safety and efficiency. Developing effective LC strategies for connected and automated vehicles in mixed traffic is complicated by the uncertainty associated with surrounding-vehicle behavior and the computational burden of embedding realistic prediction models within optimization schemes. To capture these complex interactions while retaining tractability, this study proposes a data-driven optimization framework that embeds neural network (NN) surrogates for safety and lateral comfort within a B\'ezier-curve-based trajectory planner. Specifically, the safety cost during the LC process is quantified via a surrogate composed of an input convex recurrent neural network (ICRNN) encoding the planned trajectory, a fully input convex neural network (FICNN) embedding the LC duration, and a partially input convex neural network (PICNN) decoder fusing them with historical traffic states; separately, another FICNN surrogate approximates the optimal lateral comfort cost as a function of the LC duration. Both surrogates are embedded via linear programming (LP) formulations, avoiding the binary variables required by conventional mixed-integer programming (MIP) approaches for NN-embedded optimization. We further theoretically establish their exactness at optimality and extend the framework to problems with additional analytical objective terms and multiple surrogates. Experiments on a hybrid dataset combining real-world and simulated trajectories demonstrate that the proposed method achieves surrogate accuracy competitive with unconstrained baselines while substantially improving optimization efficiency over conventional MIPs. Closed-loop simulations further show that the proposed planners markedly reduce the weighted planning cost and consistently outperform baseline methods.

papers.title: Regularity theory for non-local almost minimal surfaces via Euler-Lagrange inequalities at small scales
papers.authors: Serena Dipierro, Ovidiu Savin, Enrico Valdinoci, Riccardo Villa
papers.abstract:
We extend the notion of non-local almost minimal sets introduced in [Dipierro, Valdinoci, and Villa, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2026)] by admitting lower-order powers for the remainder term.
  We combine classical techniques and a new, weaker version of the Euler-Lagrange inequalities (at a microscopic scale) to obtain $\mathcal{C}^{1,\alpha}$-regularity for non-local almost minimal sets, up to Hausdorff dimension $n-3$.
  In turn, this formulation is well-suited for the non-local counterpart of the so-called Massari's problem for sets with prescribed mean curvature. In particular, such a generalization allows us to consider sets with $L^p$ non-local mean curvature (with $p\geq n/s$), which do not satisfy any curvature equation (neither in the classical nor in the viscosity sense).
  The results presented here lie beyond the reach of previously established methodologies. Indeed, the approach developed herein is based on a conceptual shift relative to the existing literature, which relied on a strong form of the Euler-Lagrange equation that is not available for general non-local almost minimal sets.

papers.title: Anchored isoperimetry in percolation
papers.authors: Sahar Diskin, Lyuben Lichev, Ritvik Ramanan Radhakrishnan, Benny Sudakov, Laury Verhoeven
papers.abstract: We show that, for any infinite transitive graph $G$, the infinite cluster after supercritical percolation almost surely inherits the anchored isoperimetry of $G$. Moreover, the probability of violating the corresponding isoperimetric inequality decays exponentially in the isoperimetric profile of the host graph. This was previously known only for nonamenable transitive graphs, $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and very recently for transitive graphs of polynomial growth. Our proof combines the thinning-and-sprinkling technique with a novel counting algorithm.

papers.title: Invariant means, coset correct means and the Hahn-Banach Theorem
papers.abstract: We show that, in ZF set theory, the existence of "coset correct means" on all groups is equivalent to the Hahn-Banach Theorem, as well as to the existence of invariant means on abelian groups.

papers.title: Stationary Limits of the Point Spectrum
papers.abstract: We give an example of a directed set whose Tukey spectrum is not closed under stationary limits. This is a counterexample to a theorem due to Isbell from the 60's. We isolate a combinatorial principle arising from our example, between stationary reflection and weak compactness.

papers.title: The Oriented Freudenthal Suspension Theorem
papers.abstract: The Freudenthal Suspension Theorem states that the connectivity of the unit map $X\rightarrow\Omega\Sigma X$ of the suspension-loop adjunction for a pointed space $X$ is twice the connectivity of $X$ itself. We extend this theorem to $X$ being a pointed $(\infty,\infty)$-category, i.e. an oriented space in the sense of Gepner--Heine.

papers.title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
papers.abstract: We prove a Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one. The proof identifies the classical presentation through Steinberg Lie superalgebras and establishes injectivity using evaluation homomorphisms, iterated coproducts in degreewise completions, and coefficientwise tensor separation.

papers.title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $\phi$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $\rho$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_\rho$, $\overline{\Delta}_\rho$, $IC_\rho$, and $\delta_\rho$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp!}\pi$, and $i_{b!*}\pi$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $\pi$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $\phi$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.

papers.title: Compactification of parabolic Hermitian--Einstein moduli spaces on complex surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{X}$ be a compact complex surface with a Gauduchon metric, and let $D\subset\overline{X}$ be a smooth connected divisor. We construct an Uhlenbeck compactification of the moduli space of rank-two parabolic Hermitian--Einstein connections with prescribed holomorphic determinant.

papers.title: A First-Order Phase Transition in Spin-Imbalanced BCS Theory of Superconductivity
papers.abstract: We study a translation-invariant BCS functional of superconductivity for a system of spin-$1/2$ fermions with spin-dependent chemical potentials, $\mu_+\neq\mu_-$. Numerical work of Caldas and Mota and analytical work of Freiji, Hainzl, and Seiringer has suggested an unusual first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS models, in which the normal state becomes globally unstable while remaining locally stable. Here, we prove that a first-order phase transition occurs in such spin-imbalanced BCS functionals. For each sufficiently small fixed spin imbalance and sufficiently low temperature, there is a coexistence coupling $\lambda_{\mathrm{fo}}$ strictly below the linear-stability threshold $\lambda_{\mathrm{lin}}$ of the normal state at which the Cooper pair density exhibits a nonzero jump and the minimized energy has a kink. The methodological insight is a coercivity estimate obtained by decomposing the BCS energy minimization into two parts, where the ``inner'' problem minimizes over the one-particle density matrices at fixed pairing and can be exactly solved by a Legendre--Fenchel transform.

papers.title: Topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition
papers.abstract: We study the topology and regularity of small sub-Riemannian balls under an index condition on length-minimizing curves in the metric tangent space. We prove that sufficiently small spheres are Lipschitz hypersurfaces homeomorphic to Euclidean spheres, while closed balls are homeomorphic to Euclidean closed balls, and open balls are diffeomorphic to Euclidean open balls. These results improve the known ones and extend them beyond two-step distributions. The proof relies on uniform Lipschitz estimates for the distance, of independent interest.

papers.title: Amitsur groups of Imprimitive Fano Threefolds
papers.abstract: We classify possible Amitsur groups of smooth imprimitive Fano threefolds defined over $\cc$ that admit a faithful action of a finite group.

papers.title: Dice enterprises and polynomial approximation: uniform query tails
papers.abstract: A binary-output dice enterprise uses independent rolls of a die with unknown face probabilities $\mathbf p$ (along with fair coin flips) to simulate a coin with bias $f(\mathbf p)$. We determine which power-law tails, uniform over the closed probability simplex, are attainable for the number $N$ of rolls. For continuous $f$ with values in $(0,1)$ and $q>0$, some enterprise for $f$ satisfies $\sup_{\mathbf p}\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf p}(N>n)=O(n^{-q})$ if and only if $f$ can be approximated uniformly by polynomials of degree $k$ with error $O(k^{-2q})$. When this holds, the same tail bound is attained by an oblivious enterprise, which chooses its number of rolls before rolling. The characterization extends to multiple dice, with total degree on a product of simplices; it then suffices to roll the dice in a fixed cyclic order. For $q>1$, these enterprises have a uniformly bounded expected number of rolls.

papers.title: Regular closedness off the real axis for root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
papers.abstract: For each integer $h\ge1$, let $Z_h$ be the closure in the complex plane of the roots of nonzero integer polynomials whose coefficients have absolute value at most $h$, with no degree restriction. We prove that $Z_h$ is regular closed off the real axis: every non-real point of $Z_h$ is a limit of interior points. The root-closure identification of Espigul\'e and Juher, for which we include a self-contained proof, shows that the same closure arises from monic polynomials and that outside the closed unit disc it is the connectedness locus of $h+1$ equally spaced collinear similarities. The main step proves that this locus is regular closed off the real axis; this was known for $h=1$ by Calegari, Koch and Walker, for $h\ge19$, and inside an explicit lens. The symmetry $z\mapsto1/z$ then gives the full-plane statement. The proof adapts the method of traps of Calegari, Koch and Walker, using a neighboring-piece criterion, short chains through consecutive digits, and Rouch\'e's theorem. We also classify the convex attractors.

papers.title: Spectral Structures on Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: We develop an intrinsic theory of spectral structures on holomorphic vector bundles over compact Riemann surfaces, generalising eigenspace decompositions without eigenvalues. Their geometric realisations are presentations of vector bundles as pushforwards of line bundles along finite branched covers. We construct their analytic moduli stack locally of finite presentation and identify it with the relative Picard stack of the universal family of finite covers. We prove that the forgetful morphism to the stack of vector bundles is representable by analytic spaces and is smooth and surjective on a distinguished smooth open substack. Consequently, every holomorphic family of vector bundles locally admits spectral presentations along smooth connected simply branched covers, and these presentations can be deformed alongside the underlying bundles. The relative Picard description yields explicit local dimension formulas and recovers the stack of regular Higgs bundles as base change along the Hitchin base. We also characterise the additional data supplied to a spectral structure by a regular Higgs field as a global twisted generator, and give examples of smooth connected spectral structures which cannot arise from any Higgs field.

papers.title: Non-concordant 2-links in simply-connected 4-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct an infinite family of smooth 2-component links of 2-spheres $\Sigma_k\subset S^2\times S^2$ whose respective components are smoothly concordant but which are pairwise not topologically concordant in any topological $\mathbb{Z}$-homology cobordism. In particular, the $\Sigma_k$ are pairwise non-concordant in $(S^2\times S^2)\times[0,1]$.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic and Dynamical Phi^4 Limits of Ising-Kac Models with Diffusion-Based Interactions on the Sierpi\'nski Gasket
papers.abstract: We introduce a general form of Ising--Kac interactions through heat-kernel averaging, with the heat-time parameter replacing the role of the interaction range. From the viewpoint of Dirichlet forms theory, this construction provides an intrinsic analogue of the mesoscopic averaging in classical Kac models when translation invariance is unavailable. We then investigate limits of this model on graph approximations of the Sierpi\'nski gasket. For the associated Glauber dynamics, we establish a hierarchy of scaling limits for the magnetization field. First, at fixed interaction heat time and inverse temperature, we derive a nonlocal hydrodynamic equation on the continuum gasket. Second, as the heat time vanishes and the inverse temperature approaches its mean-field critical value, suitably rescaled hydrodynamic solutions converge to the solution of the deterministic Allen--Cahn equation. Finally, under a joint scaling of graph refinement, interaction heat time, and inverse temperature near criticality, we prove convergence of critical magnetization fluctuations to the solution of the dynamical $\Phi^4$ equation. These results provide a concrete realization of the Ising-$\Phi^4$ correspondence in a geometric setting with non-integer spectral dimension.
