In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. Numerical experiments for a semiconductor inverse problem confirm that the proposed Bayesian all-at-once approach yields a speedup of approximately a factor of two, while having a comparable reconstruction quality as the conventional reduced-based setting.

papers.title: A Combinatorial Formula and a Hilbert Scheme Realization of a Rank-One Virasoro Irregular Conformal Block
papers.abstract: For general central charge, we give a combinatorial formula and a geometric realization of the formal expansion of the rank-one Virasoro irregular conformal block of type $(0,0,1)$ at its irregular singular point. We realize the normalized block as a coefficientwise matrix element on the localized equivariant Hilbert--Fock space associated with Hilbert schemes of points on $\mathbb C^2$. At $c=1$, we prove the author's conjecture and express the parameter-independent coefficients in terms of skew-tableau numbers and Littlewood--Richardson coefficients, establishing their nonnegativity and integrality. The proof combines sectorial asymptotics of screening integrals with Laguerre--Jack evaluations. We express the screening kernel using the flow of a degree-raising differential operator and compute the Jack coefficients of its exponential from the one-box Pieri rule and the shifted Jack coefficient formula of Okounkov and Olshanski.

papers.title: Arbitrary Dirichlet Eigenvalue Multiplicities on Smooth Star-Shaped Euclidean Domains
papers.authors: Zhijie Chen, Chen-Gang Long, Shihong Zhang
papers.abstract: In every fixed dimension \(N\ge3\), for any finite list of positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\), we construct smooth strictly star-shaped Euclidean domains whose first \(\ell+1\) distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues can have multiplicities \(1,m_1,\ldots,m_\ell\) respectively. The condition "star-shaped" is almost optimal in the sense that this statement can not hold for bounded convex domains. In fact, we show that the second Dirichlet eigenvalue of any bounded convex domain has multiplicity at most $N$, and this bound is sharp.

papers.title: Solid Arithmetic D-modules
papers.abstract: We introduce a solid ring of arithmetic differential operators analogue to Berthelot's D-dagger, and its derived infinity-category of solid quasi-coherent modules. We show that there is a fully faithful functor from Berthelot's derived category of bounded complexes of D-dagger-modules with coherent cohomology into our new category.

papers.title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
papers.abstract: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schr\"oer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.

papers.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the H\"oegh-Krohn model.

papers.title: An introduction to the strategy of transcendence proofs
papers.abstract: The proof by Ch. Hermite of the transcendence of the number e in 1873 is the model on which most transcendence proofs for constants of analysis are based. The Schneider-Lang Theorem gives an opportunity to understand the strategy behind the proof. We only outline the main ideas, without providing technical details, for which we refer to the bibliography.

papers.title: A complete theory of local minimizers for periodic variational problems
papers.abstract: We study the periodic problem in the Calculus of Variations and give a complete characterization of the positive definiteness of the second variation, extending the Reid Roundabout Theorem to periodic boundary conditions. Two formulations are established: one in terms of conjugate and semi-coupled points, and one in terms of the existence of a symmetric solution of the associated Riccati equation satisfying a boundary inequality. We show by an explicit example that the latter condition, while sufficient, is not necessary except in dimension one. As applications, we obtain sufficient conditions for weak and strong local minimizers of periodic solutions of the Euler-Lagrange equation.

papers.title: On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (I): weighted analysis
papers.authors: Yu Li, Longhuan Yan, Wenjia Zhang
papers.abstract: We develop the weighted Sobolev and H\"older analysis needed to study perturbations of complete asymptotically conical (AC) Ricci shrinkers. Weighted elliptic estimates yield a global weighted divergence-free slice in spaces that retain the asymptotic data at infinity. As a geometric application, we prove pointed Gromov-Hausdorff rigidity of nontrivial AC shrinkers with vanishing infinitesimal solitonic deformation space.

papers.title: On short averages of the Fibonacci partition function
papers.abstract: We show that short averages of the Fibonacci partition function over $(H, H + H^\alpha]$ can be significantly smaller than long averages over $(0,H]$, for any constant $\alpha \in (0,1)$. This provides a negative answer to a question that we asked in our previous work on this topic (Journal of Number Theory, 2024).

papers.title: Euler--Lagrange Flow Monotonicity for the Radon Transform
papers.abstract: We present a new gradient-like flow that targets critical points of the inequality for the planar Radon transform $\mathcal{R}$ proven by Oberlin and Stein, partially answering a question of Christ, who gave a complete characterisation of the extremisers of the inequality via rearrangement methods. We show that for non-negative radial initial data near the extremiser manifold, solutions to the flow exist globally and there exists a rescaled subsequence of the flow that converges to a critical point of the Radon functional $\|\mathcal{R} f\|_3/\|f\|_{3/2}$ locally in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We also obtain a quantitative result for the rate of decay of critical points, which complements a result of Christ arXiv:1106.0719 in the special case of radial functions. We prove a novel localised smoothing estimate for the operator $\mathcal{R}^*[(\mathcal{R}\cdot)^2]$ restricted to radial functions. This approach is complementary to that of Christ and provides a robust framework for studying extremal problems associated to Radon-like operators.

papers.title: Rational points of exact period three for the quadratic family
papers.abstract: For the quadratic family $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$ over $\Q$, we isolate a general $S$-unit and ABC template for rational periodic cycles: under the ABC conjecture, any rational quantity built from the consecutive-point sums of a rational period-$n$ cycle whose value and shift-by-$1$ are both $S$-units (with $S$ the support of the denominator of $c$) has logarithmic height at most $(1+\eps)\sum_{p \in S} \log p + O_\eps(1)$. Specializing to period $3$ in the change of coordinates $u = x_0 + x_1$ and $v = x_0 + x_2$, the period-$3$ condition reduces to $v = -1/(1+u)$, forcing the parameter $t = u$ to satisfy $t, t+1 \in \Z[S^{-1}]^\times$; the template then yields, under ABC, $\max\{|a|,|b|,|a+b|\} \le C_\eps \rad(d)^{1+\eps}$ for $t = a/b$ in lowest terms. We also characterize the period-$3$ locus on the $(u,v)$-plane intrinsically, isolating the ghost curve. Extending the height bound to higher periods remains an open structural question.

papers.title: Distributionally robust chance-constrained standard quadratic optimization with Wasserstein ambiguity
papers.authors: Immanuel M. Bomze, Daniel De Vicente, Simge K\"u\c{c}\"ukyavuz
papers.abstract: The standard quadratic optimization problem consists of minimizing a quadratic form over the standard simplex. It has highly relevant applications ranging from portfolio optimization to machine learning. However, if the quadratic form is neither convex nor concave, this problem is NP-hard. We study a distributionally robust chance-constrained variant whose ambiguity set is a Wasserstein ball around the sampled distribution and make four contributions. First, although the problem is nonconvex in the decision variable, we exploit its linear dependence on the uncertain matrix to reduce the problem to a mixed-integer quadratic optimization problem. Second, we show that a judicious choice of matrix norm---the entrywise maximum norm---makes this reformulation both exact and tractable, and we describe the induced worst-case distribution. Third, our formulation is, by construction, the minimization of the worst-case Value-at-Risk of the random quadratic form; this unifies it with existing frameworks for uncertain standard quadratic optimization problems, in particular under chance constraints, and we identify natural settings in which it collapses to a single deterministic instance. Finally, we report numerical experiments on positive-definite and indefinite instances which quantify how the model parameters drive the optimal value and solution time, and expose the computational cost of indefiniteness.

papers.title: On convex envelopes of bilinear terms over polygonal domains
papers.authors: Adrian G\"o{\ss}, Jan Krause, Martina Kuchlbauer, Tobias Kuen
papers.abstract: We develop an algorithm for computing the convex envelope of the bilinear function $f(x,y)=xy$ over possibly nonconvex polygonal domains. Building on existing methods for convex polytopes, our approach uses the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions and an analysis of the contact points between affine underestimators and the graph of $f$. Nonconvex domains admit additional contact configurations that prevent several simplifications available in the convex case. We resolve these configurations explicitly and show that the envelope admits a finite polyhedral subdivision with affine, quadratic, or rational expressions on its cells. For orthogonal polygons, whose edges are horizontal or vertical, we establish substantial reductions in the generator sets needed to compute the envelope. We also present methods for constructing such domains as relaxations of two-dimensional projections of nonlinear optimization problems. An illustrative example quantifies the loss in relaxation strength caused by convexifying the domain before computing the envelope. Computational experiments on MINLPLib instances show that cuts derived from orthogonal polygons strengthen root relaxations and reduce branch-and-bound nodes in aggregate.

papers.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Blind Passive Beamforming in RIS-Assisted MIMO Systems
papers.authors: Ouma\"ima Bounhar, Thomas Ch\^ene, Ghaya Rekaya-Ben Othman, Oussama Damen
papers.abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) are a promising solution for improving millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications by controlling signal propagation. Yet, selecting the optimal RIS configuration remains challenging due to the high-dimensional search space and signaling overhead. We propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework for blind passive beamforming, where a Deep Q-Learning (DQL) agent learns an adaptive policy to select near-optimal RIS configurations while sounding only few codewords, without channel state information. Results show that our approach outperforms Q-Learning (QL) and conventional baselines in convergence, performance, and overhead reduction.

papers.title: Klein-Gordon-Born-Infeld equations driven by mixed local-nonlocal operators
papers.authors: Nicol\`o Cangiotti, Maicol Caponi, Alberto Maione, Enzo Vitillaro
papers.abstract: In this paper we study a class of Klein-Gordon-Born-Infeld systems in which the classical Laplacian appearing in the matter equation is replaced by a mixed local-nonlocal operator, whose nonlocal part is allowed to be nonpositive definite according to a real parameter. Both the approximate and the exact Born-Infeld field equations are considered in parallel. After making the functional framework explicit, we identify a range of real parameters for which infinitely many radially symmetric standing waves exist, obtained as Mountain Pass critical points of the associated reduced energy functionals. The mixed local-nonlocal operator reduces to the classical Laplacian as the nonlocal weight vanishes, and is motivated, in the spirit of effective field theories, by nonlocal corrections to the matter dispersion relation.

papers.title: Instability theory of stationary solutions for nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract: We study the orbital instability of algebraically decaying stationary solutions of nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations in dimensions $d\ge2$, taking competing double-power nonlinearities as a canonical model. At zero frequency, the essential spectrum of the linearized operator touches zero, and the usual $H^1$ coercivity is lost. We construct the zero-frequency limit $\eta_0$ of the frequency derivatives $\partial_\omega\phi_\omega$ of standing-wave profiles and determine its sharp asymptotic behavior. For a stationary ground state $\phi_0\in H^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, we prove instability if $\langle x\rangle\,\phi_0\notin L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ or, when $\langle x\rangle\,\phi_0\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, if the duality pairing $\langle\eta_0,\phi_0\rangle$ is negative. This criterion is a zero-frequency counterpart of the negative slope condition in the Grillakis--Shatah--Strauss theory. The proof combines variation of parameters for the linearized ODE with a shooting analysis that determines the global behavior of the homogeneous solution regular at the origin. We then localize $\eta_0$ to construct an unstable direction and establish instability through a Lyapunov functional argument based on the variational characterization of ground states. The results extend with essentially the same proofs to a class of multiple-power nonlinearities.

papers.title: The Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in dimensions three and four
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, confirming the Kawatani--Okawa conjecture in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.

papers.title: A note on the ideal lattice of a weighted Leavitt path algebra
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $L_K(E,w)$ the Leavitt path algebra of a row-finite weighted graph $(E,w)$. Suppose that $L_K(E,w)$ is not isomorphic to an ordinary Leavitt path algebra. We prove that the ideal lattice of every countably generated unital $K$-algebra embeds as a closed interval into the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$. The embedding preserves multiplication of ideals modulo the lower endpoint of the interval. It follows that the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$ is not distributive and that ideal multiplication in $L_K(E,w)$ is not commutative. Moreover, we show that if $(E,w)$ is countable, then $L_K(E,w)$ has exactly $|K|^{\aleph_0}$ ideals, prime ideals, left primitive ideals, and right primitive ideals.

papers.title: A Semigroup-Aware Kernel Neural Operator with Latent Exponential Integration for Forced PDEs
papers.authors: Naseem Abbas, Vittorio Colao, Davide Macr\`i, Matthieu Barreau, William Spataro
papers.abstract: We propose a semigroup-aware structured kernel neural operator for source-driven evolution PDEs. Unlike generic time-conditioned kernel models, the proposed formulation represents temporal dependence through a latent exponential propagator \(e^{tA_\theta}\), where \(A_\theta\) is a learned latent generator. This provides a structured transition from a non-ODE kernel representation to an ODE-inspired kernel operator whose latent temporal evolution satisfies the composition principle of evolution semigroups. For time-dependent forcing terms, a direct kernel-based evaluation requires repeated quadrature over delayed kernel evaluations. To address this computational bottleneck, we derive a latent-first reformulation of the source term: the forcing field is projected onto the kernel-induced latent space, where its accumulated effect is represented as the solution of a forced linear latent dynamical system. For a fixed learned kernel, this reformulation is exact. The resulting system can then be integrated using a \(\phi_1\)-based exponential integrator, yielding a source-evaluation path that is structurally aligned with the learned latent propagator. The resulting framework combines geometry- and physics-conditioned low-rank kernel factorization with alternative source-evaluation paths based on either explicit Duhamel quadrature or latent exponential integration. Dissipativity constraints on the latent generator and identity-preserving corrections near the initial time are optional architectural components. Numerical experiments on advection-iffusion-reaction (ADR) problems compare the non-ODE and semigroup-aware formulations, evaluate the quadrature and \(\phi_1\) source paths, and assess predictive accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: The information geometry of the Sinkhorn divergence on a Hilbert manifold
papers.abstract: The Sinkhorn divergence, the debiased entropic optimal transport cost, determines a metric tensor on probability measures defined along curves, due to Lavenant et al. We construct a real-analytic Hilbert manifold of measures, the smooth stratum, on which this tensor is a weak Riemannian metric, and we continue Eguchi's construction of a geometry from a divergence to the third order. The stratum consists of the measures with a positive Sobolev density on a closed Riemannian manifold, and the strata form a scale whose intersection is the Fr\'echet manifold of smooth positive densities of Ay. Following it, we characterize the metric through the gradients of mean values: its cotangent form is a spectral reweighting of the Dirichlet form of a Markov chain, so the metric is of the same kind as the Fisher-Rao and the Otto metric, and on the stratum it is bounded by a multiple of the Fisher-Rao metric (but not conversely). At third order, the Sinkhorn divergence is self-dual: both connection forms of Eguchi's construction coincide with the Levi-Civita form of the metric, and the cubic tensor vanishes, as a consequence of the transposition symmetry of the transport problem. On every stratum, the Levi-Civita form is represented, so the stratum has a real-analytic Levi-Civita connection, which on the Fr\'echet manifold is the connection of Ay and Schwachh\"ofer.

papers.title: Moments of characteristic polynomials at random matrix Gram points
papers.abstract: We evaluate the characteristic polynomial of a random unitary matrix at the points on the unit circle where the polynomial takes real values. In analogy to the Riemann zeta function we call these the ``random matrix Gram points''. On the random matrix side we answer in the affirmative a question of Richard Hall, who expected that zeta on the Gram points should be larger than typical. We prove that for any fixed positive $k$, the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the random matrix Gram points is larger than the $2k$th moment of the characteristic polynomial averaged over the whole unit circle. For large $N$ the leading-order asymptotic term is the same size, but all lower-order terms are larger. In an appendix we show how to adapt the heuristic recipe of Conrey--Farmer--Keating--Rubinstein--Snaith to conjecture moments of zeta at Gram points, and show by example that the second and fourth moments calculated by following the recipe agree with previously proven results.

papers.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
papers.abstract: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.

papers.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vign\'eras
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vign\'eras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.

papers.title: Planarity estimates and codimension reduction for ancient flows at the Andrews-Baker threshold
papers.abstract: We derive an interior planarity estimate for space-time proper mean curvature flows of $n$-dimensional submanifolds of $\mathbb R^{n+p}$, $n\geq5$, that are uniformly quadratically pinched up to the Andrews-Baker threshold $\frac{4}{3n}$. The estimate is parabolically scale-invariant and it requires neither curvature nor entropy bounds. The proof combines Naff's gradient estimates with a localization argument in the spirit of Ecker and Huisken. In dimensions five and six, Naff's estimates alone do not give the gradient terms a sign. We bound these terms from below with an argument we developed in a previous work. As a consequence, for $n\geq5$, and by known results for $2\leq n\leq4$, every space-time proper ancient solution that is uniformly $\frac{4}{3n}$-pinched is either a static affine $n$-plane or lies in a fixed affine $(n+1)$-dimensional subspace. This replaces the finite entropy and polynomial curvature growth assumptions of Lee, Naff and Zhu by space-time properness, and improves their pinching constant in dimensions two, five and six. For closed flows, we extend Lynch's planarity estimate to a larger range of exponents.

papers.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
papers.abstract: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.

papers.title: Three-dimensional stress-gradient non-locality problem: Displacement field for an arbitrary and a conservative force
papers.abstract: In order to obtain the displacement field, both generally in the case of an arbitrary body force and specifically in the case of a conservative body force, the mechanical problem of statics of three-dimensional stress-gradient non-local medium is analytically solved on unbounded domain by considering a system of equations consisting of an equilibrium equation, infinitesimal strain, and both scalar- and tensor-type stress-gradient Eringen three-dimensional models. Since the system of equations is linear, for each model the solution is obtained in the form of a superposition of the local-type displacement field, common to each model, and the non-local-type displacement field, specific to the non-locality operator of the model. Among the three scalar-type and five tensor-type considered models, six distinct analytical displacement field expressions are obtained for an arbitrary body force: one expression specific to a scalar-type model, three specific to individual tensor-type models, while each of the remaining two expressions are common to one scalar- and one tensor-type model. The displacement vector fields are graphically represented in the case of gravitational body force, yielding five different models, since two tensor-type models become the same when the force is conservative.

papers.title: Randomized Symplectic Model Reduction: One-Pass Basis Construction and Sketched Hamiltonian Assembly
papers.authors: Robin Herkert, Bernard Haasdonk, J\"org Fehr
papers.abstract: Symplectic model order reduction of Hamiltonian systems yields reduced dynamics that conserve the reduced Hamiltonian along exact trajectories, avoiding the artificial energy drift that can arise from conventional projection methods. For large-scale spatial discretizations, however, basis construction and reduced-operator assembly can involve substantial offline costs. Randomized numerical linear algebra can reduce these costs through low-dimensional sketches while supporting streaming and parallel implementations. We develop randomized techniques for two parts of the offline stage while preserving the Hamiltonian structure of the reduced dynamics. First, we introduce the one-pass sketched randomized cSVD (Ops-rcSVD), a one-pass randomized variant of the complex-SVD algorithm. Combining randomized range finding with an independent left sketch, Ops-rcSVD constructs an ortho-symplectic reduced basis from a single pass over the snapshot ensemble. Second, for quadratic Hamiltonian systems, we introduce a randomized reduced-Hamiltonian assembly based on sketching the reduced basis and operator actions, yielding a reduced Hamiltonian system by construction. We derive bounds for the snapshot projection error, uniform-in-parameter perturbation bounds for the sketched reduced Hamiltonian, and an energy-norm estimate for the difference between reduced and sketched reduced trajectories. Experiments on large-scale systems show that Ops-rcSVD attains projection accuracy comparable to deterministic and two-pass randomized constructions while reducing basis-construction time. They further demonstrate accurate sketched reduced-Hamiltonian assembly when storing the complete snapshot ensemble is no longer feasible.

papers.title: Strong rate for one-dimensional driftless continuous strict local martingales
papers.abstract: For one-dimensional strict local martingales of the form $\mathrm{d} X_t=\sigma(X_t) \mathrm{d} W_t$ starting from $X_{0}=x_{0}>0$, we prove the strong rate $\mathbb{E}\left[|X^h_N-X_T|\right] \lesssim h^{\min\{\theta\alpha,\frac{1}{2}\}}$ for a discrete scheme~$X^h$ truncated at a level $h^{-\alpha}$, with time step~$h$, as $h\downarrow 0$, where~$\theta$ depends on the truncation property. For the CEV model $\sigma(x)\equiv x^{1+\gamma}$ in particular, the rate is~$\frac{1}{2}$ for any $\gamma \in (0,1)$ (up to a logarithmic pre-factor at $\gamma=\frac{1}{2}$).

papers.title: The asymptotic number of zonotopes
papers.abstract: We provide a sharp estimate for the asymptotic number of lattice zonotopes inscribed in [0, n] d as n tends to infinity. Our estimate refines the logarithmic equivalent established by B{\'a}r{\'a}ny, Bureaux, and Lund when the sum of the generators of the zonotope is prescribed. As we shall see, the exponential part of our estimate is a polynomial of degree d in n 1/(d+1) , plus a term involving the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Our analysis is based on a correspondence between power sums over primitive vectors (vectors with coprime coordinates) and Eulerian polynomials. We also analyse some combinatorial properties of lattice zonotopes. In particular, we compute the asymptotic mean and variance of the diameter of the graph of a random lattice zonotope inscribed in [0, n] d as n goes to infinity, and show that this diameter satisfies a central limit theorem.

papers.title: Efficient Low-Rank Approximation of Quaternion Matrices via Adaptive Cross Approximation
papers.abstract: The adaptive cross approximation (ACA) algorithm is a powerful tool for constructing low-rank matrix approximations using only a small subset of matrix entries. While extensively studied for real and complex matrices, its extension to quaternion algebras, remains largely unexplored. This paper presents the first comprehensive framework for adaptive cross approximation operating natively in the quaternion algebra H. Unlike approaches that rely on real embeddings or complexifications, our method preserves the algebraic structure of quaternions throughout the computation, avoiding information loss and maintaining the natural correlations between quaternion components. We develop a fully quaternionic ACA algorithm with rigorous theoretical foundations, including convergence analysis, error bounds, and complexity estimates. The algorithm achieves O(r(m+n)) complexity per iteration and demonstrates quasioptimal approximation properties comparable to the quaternion singular value decomposition (QSVD), but with significantly reduced computational cost. We provide a detailed MATLAB with numerical experiments on color image compression. Our results show that native quaternion ACA outperforms significantly the basic SVD algorithm in terms of computational efficiency, with very close approximation accuracy.

papers.title: Interacting particles in random irregular media
papers.authors: Luca Bondi (UNITO, OC), Elena Issoglio (UNITO), Francesco Russo (ENSTA Paris, OC)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first develop novel tools of independent interest in the field of stochastic calculus related to SDEs with distributional drift, namely the formulation of a quasi-Stroock-Varadhan martingale problem in the sense that the test functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ instead of solutions of Kolmogorov type PDE. This has several applications, among which, the time restriction and the notion of conditional rough martingale problem and related solution.

papers.title: Split Quaternion Toolbox: A MATLAB Implementation
papers.authors: Salman Ahmadi-Asl, Abbas Moradi, Yang Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper presents a MATLAB toolbox for working with split quaternions and split quaternion matrices. Split quaternions, also known as coquaternions, form a four-dimensional associative non-commutative algebra over the real numbers with a signature (+,+,-,-). The toolbox provides two main classes: SplitQuaternion for scalar-valued split quaternions and SplitQuaternionMatrix for matrix-valued split quaternions. The implementation includes arithmetic operations, algebraic functions, matrix operations, linear algebra utilities, and various conversion methods. The toolbox is designed to be intuitive for users familiar with MATLAB's standard matrix operations while providing the full power of split quaternion algebra. This paper details the implementation, provides numerous examples, and demonstrates the toolbox's capabilities through practical demonstrations. The MATLAB toolbox is accessible at https://github.com/SalmanAhmadi-Asl/Split_Quaternion.git.

papers.title: Cocycles on Tiling Spaces
papers.abstract: The space of tilings by rectangles form an interesting collection of multidimensional subshifts. Here, we study cocycles on such tiling spaces and provide an algorithmically decidable necessary and sufficient condition for the tiling space associated with a collection of rectangles to admit a nontrivial cocycle. Along the way, we also prove that the tiling spaces corresponding to a class of rectangular tile sets satisfy certain mixing properties.

papers.title: Low-rank matrices with three prescribed off-diagonal values over $\mathbb{F}_p$
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime such that $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$. We prove that, for every three-element set $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ and every integer $n\geq1$, there exists a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with zero diagonal, off-diagonal entries in $L$, and rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. This answers a question of Bukh for all such primes and, in particular, settles the case $L=\{1,4,6\}\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{19}$ singled out on his problem list. When $0\notin L$, a standard polynomial argument shows that the exponent $1/3$ is optimal. The proof combines a geometric construction in characteristic two with an incidence matrix factorization over $\mathbb{F}_p$. The same construction yields integer lifts $L'$ of the prescribed sets $L$ and symmetric $L'$-matrices of rational rank $O_{p,L}(n^{1/3})$. When $0\notin L'$, this improves Bukh's general quadratic lower bound, giving matrices of order $\Omega_{p,L}(r^3)$ and rational rank at most $r$.

papers.title: Least common multiples of polynomial values: averaging, ray classes, and Galois statistics
papers.abstract: We study analogues over number fields and the probabilistic congruence input that enters averaged versions of this problem. We prove an asymptotic formula for the least common multiple of ideals in a fixed ray class, record local equidistribution estimates for random $S_n$-polynomials, and give a conditional reduction of the averaged higher degree problem to explicit dispersion and large prime collision estimates. We also formulate an individual quadratic number field analogue and reduce it to a prime ideal quadratic root equidistribution statement together with a geometric pair counting estimate. The Galois group counting input is updated using Bhargava's theorem over $\mathbb Q$ and the determinant method estimates of https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35030 .

papers.title: Lie point symmetry analysis of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model with exponential claim sizes
papers.authors: Aminu Ma'aruf Nass, Kassimu Mpungu, Rahmatullah Ibrahim Nuruddeen, Yaqoob Al Rahbi
papers.abstract: We carry out a Lie point symmetry analysis of the coupled integro-differential system satisfied by the conditional Gerber--Shiu functions of a dependent jump-diffusion risk model. In the model, claim sizes are exponential, the intensity of the next claim arrival depends on whether the current claim exceeds a random threshold, and both the volatility and the premium rate may depend on the surplus. We write the system as the restriction to the half-line of a far-field operator with prescribed exterior data, derive the complete set of determining equations, including the condition imposed by the nonlocal convolution term, and solve them. The resulting group classification holds for every surplus-dependent volatility and premium of the form considered and for every absolutely continuous or constant threshold distribution. A non-trivial symmetry beyond scaling and superposition exists if and only if the volatility and the premium rate are constant, and it is then exactly the translation in the surplus variable. We construct the optimal system of one-dimensional subalgebras. We show that the invariant solutions of the combined translation--scaling generators exist precisely when a $2\times2$ generalized Lundberg determinant vanishes, and we give this determinant for an arbitrary threshold distribution, with explicit forms for the constant and exponential thresholds. We prove existence and sign properties of the adjustment coefficient, derive its sensitivities to all model parameters, and establish Cram\'er--Lundberg-type asymptotics for the Gerber--Shiu functions, including the limit of the ratio between the two regimes. A numerical study shows that claim-size-driven dependence lowers the adjustment coefficient markedly below that of an independent model with the same mean claim intensity.

papers.title: On record behaviours of returns for interval maps
papers.abstract: Given a dynamical system $(X,T)$ and an ergodic invariant measure $\mu$, a $\mu$-typical point $x\in X$ under $T$ visits arbitrarily small neighbourhood of $x$. We will use techniques based on extreme value theory and Laplace functional for point process to show that, for interval maps with suitable mixing and anti-clustering conditions, the limiting distributions of the record times and values of the return process $Y_j(x)=-\log d(T^jx,x)$, after possible normalisation, has Poisson-type laws.

papers.title: Iterative Methods for Solving New Generalized Absolute Value Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose two iterative methods, the modified Picard method (MPM) and the generalized Traub method (GTM), to solve a new generalized absolute value equation (NGAVE). We establish their convergence under appropriate assumptions. Additionally, numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the developed algorithms.

papers.title: A New Invariant for Doubly Periodic Solutions of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
papers.authors: Nicolas Hasse, Ross Ogilvie, Martin U. Schmidt
papers.abstract: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. These transcendental period conditions are studied through Whitham deformations, which deform the curve while preserving the periods. We extend Whitham deformations to all real hyperelliptic curves of this type, by holding fixed the plane spanned by the periods, or this plane together with its complex structure. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions the resulting isoperiodic sets are manifolds of dimensions three and one, respectively. Along the one-dimensional isoperiodic sets, a generalization of the Willmore energy is a local parameter away from its critical points, to which the spectral curves of tori belong. Finally, using homology bases adapted to the branch points, we find discrete invariants of the isoperiodic sets of doubly periodic curves: a triple of integers and a refined conformal type.

papers.title: Variational characterization of principal eigenvalues for a general class of linear weighted BVP's under mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type
papers.abstract:
The main goal of this paper is to characterize the existence of principal eigenvalues of $$
  \left \{ \begin{array}{ll}
  -\mathrm{div}\left(A\nabla u\right) +qu=\lambda m u \quad & \hbox{in} \;\; \Omega,\\[1ex]
  \mathscr{B} u = 0 \quad & \hbox{on} \;\; \partial \Omega, \end{array} \right. $$ where $m\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ satisfies some of the conditions (A1)-(A3) below, as well as to deliver their variational characterizations whenever they exist. As we are dealing with general boundary operators of mixed non-classical type, in the general setting of this paper our results are far more general than all existing results. The case when $m$ satisfies (A2) has not been previously explored in the literature.

papers.title: Compatibility of Perverse Truncation of Ng\^o Fibrations
papers.authors: Bin Wang, Shihao Wang, Chenglong Yu
papers.abstract: We study compatibility of perverse truncations for morphisms between Ng\^o fibrations with rationally smooth total spaces. We show that, under an effective rank inequality, equivariant pullbacks preserve the normalized perverse truncations. Applied to the diagonal, this gives multiplicativity of perverse truncations for Hitchin systems with rationally smooth total spaces.

papers.title: Sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplacian with Morrey data
papers.abstract: We obtain sharp regularity for the anisotropic fractional Laplace equation with a right-hand side belonging to a Morrey space. We derive local $C^{\sigma+\lambda-n}-$regularity of solutions when $\sigma+\lambda-n\neq1$, where $\sigma\in(0,2)$ is the order of the operator and $\lambda\in(n-\sigma,n)$ is the Morrey decay rate of the right-hand side. In the case $\sigma+\lambda-n=1$, we show that solutions are locally in the Zygmund class, and hence are Log-Lipschitz continuous. Explicit examples attest to the sharpness of the conditions.

papers.title: Level Crossing Rate Bounds for Products of Independent Nonstationary Fading Processes
papers.abstract: We develop a unified framework for the instantaneous total level crossing rate (LCR) of products of independent positive nonstationary fading processes. Universal upper and lower bounds are first derived from an exact decomposition of the product derivative and signed crossing imbalance, requiring only factor-wise crossing statistics. We then introduce the drifting Gaussian-derivative (DGD) class, in which each conditional derivative is Gaussian with possibly nonzero drift. For products of DGD factors, an exact Gaussian-mixture representation yields bounds that jointly capture aggregate drift and derivative fluctuations. The lower bound reduces under stationarity to a known $\ell_2$ bound, whereas, to the best of the author's knowledge, the upper bound is new even in the stationary case. Furthermore, the bounds are asymptotically exact in drift-dominated regimes. The framework is specialized to nonstationary Double-Rayleigh fading and to quasi-identically distributed DGD factors, with closed forms for products of $\alpha$-$\mu$ envelopes. Numerical results show that the DGD bounds closely bracket the exact LCR.

papers.title: On the variational characterization of a laminated core model in ferromagnetic materials
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of iron losses in transformers, electric motors, and generators at elevated frequencies requires accounting for eddy currents in laminated magnetic cores during field simulation. We study local material models for these lamination losses that resolve the inhomogeneous magnetic-field distribution across the thickness of the respective steel sheets via one-dimensional diffusion equations. This allows to incorporate skin-effect and eddy-current losses in the laminations at each material point of a two- or three-dimensional magnetic-field simulation. The macroscopic material response is described implicitly through a minimization problem involving a set of internal variables which encode the load history and current state of the material. The variational structure of these problems allows us to prove well-posedness, to include anisotropy and hysteresis, and to develop efficient globally convergent solvers for the evaluation of the macroscopic material response. The proposed framework thus allows to efficiently and reliably predict magnetic behaviour of laminated core material over a wide frequency range and is well-suited for integration into nonlinear magnetic field solvers.

papers.title: On self-similar random quotients of the line
papers.abstract: A surprisingly wide variety of important random fractal metric spaces in modern probability theory can be viewed as self-similar random quotients of the real line, including the continuum random tree, Liouville quantum gravity surfaces, the trace of Brownian motion in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and self-similar ($s=2d$) long-range percolation on $\mathbb{R}$. We prove that the metric and resistance growth dimensions are well-defined in a certain sense for every random metric space in a class containing all of the above examples. Our results are new for the trace of Brownian motion.

papers.title: Dense Minors from the Crux
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree $d>0$ and $C_\alpha(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph whose average degree is at least $\alpha d$ for any fixed $0<\alpha<1$. Then $G$ has a minor of average degree $\Omega(\sqrt{d\,C_\alpha(G)})$, which is asymptotically tight up to a constant factor. This reveals a unified mechanism underlying previous results on dense minors in locally sparse graphs.

papers.title: Vanishing near the virtual cohomological dimension of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$
papers.abstract:
We prove the Church--Farb--Putman conjecture that \[
  H^{N_n-i}(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z);\mathbb Q)=0,
  \qquad N_n=\binom n2,\quad n\ge2,\quad 0\le i<n-1. \] The proof relies on Franke's filtration of the weighted automorphic cochain complex, developed in his proof of Borel's conjecture. We treat trivial and nontrivial cuspidal support separately. For nontrivial support, we combine a degree calculation with the Chenevier--Lannes lower bound of $11$ for the motivic weight of level-one regular algebraic cuspidal representations of rank at least two. This reduces the contributing inducing data to a trivial factor and a Speh factor attached to such a representation. We construct primitives for closed lifts of cohomology classes in the filtration quotients by combining an Eisenstein residue identity with a cochain homotopy and finite distributions in the spectral parameters. A finite-filtration lifting argument then yields vanishing for nontrivial cuspidal support. The trivial-support case is treated using Franke's topological model.

papers.title: Mean-Square Convergence Analysis of a Three-Level MGRIT Method for Linear Stochastic Evolution Equations with Additive Noise
papers.abstract:
We investigate the mean-square convergence of a three-level multigrid reduction-in-time (MGRIT) method based on F-relaxation for linear stochastic evolution equations driven by additive Gaussian noise. The method combines exponential Euler time stepping on the finest grid with implicit Euler discretizations on the two coarser grids. The inexact solution of the intermediate-level full approximation scheme problem gives rise to coupled error recursions involving two interlevel propagator discrepancies. Under a common spectral decomposition of the drift and noise covariance operators, we establish a geometric contraction estimate in a modal mean-square norm, with a contraction factor uniform in the temporal grids and both coarsening factors. We further derive fixed-iteration temporal error bounds that are uniform in the first coarsening factor and explicitly quantify the dependence on the second.
  For a fixed iteration count $k$ and a fixed second coarsening factor, we prove an $O(\Delta T_1^r)$ error bound relative to the finest-grid reference solution for $0<r\le k+1$ provided that $\mathcal R_{r,B}<\infty$. 
  We also prove that the error-propagation operator is nilpotent on each fixed temporal grid, ensuring finite termination of the iteration. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence behavior and compare temporal critical-path work under a unit-cost model.

papers.title: On the maximum interval index of a graph
papers.abstract: For a connected graph P G on n vertices, the interval index is defined by Int(G) = {u,v} subset V(G) (|I(u, v)| - 1), where I(u, v) denotes the set of all vertices lying on a shortest u - v path. It was conjectured that, among all connected graphs on n vertices, the path Pn attains the maximum value of the interval index. In this paper we settle this conjecture, and we prove that the maximum is attained only for Pn, except for n = 4, when the cycle C4 attains the same value. We also prove that, for every n >= 31, the maximum interval index among graphs without pendant vertices equals (n^3 - n)/6 - 2(n - 4) and it is attained by a dumbbell graph, obtained by joining two 4-cycles by a path.

papers.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
papers.abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.

papers.title: Three-dimensional noncompact trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We classify connected, simply connected, noncompact three-dimensional trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds. In [1], we showed that, in the compact case, such a manifold is either of $\beta$-Kenmotsu type or homothetic to a Sasakian manifold. In this paper, in the noncompact case, we find families of trans-Sasakian $\eta$-Einstein manifolds that are neither $\beta$-Kenmotsu nor homothetic to Sasakian manifolds. These families have infinitely many degrees of freedom. We give these nontrivial metrics explicitly. We also give a structure theorem for the case in which the characteristic vector field is Palais-nonregular.

papers.title: The H\'enon equation beyond the critical Sobolev exponent
papers.abstract: We consider the Dirichlet problem $-\Delta u=|x|^\alpha u^p$, $u>0$ in $\Omega$, $u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$, where $\Omega\subset R^N$, $N\ge 3$, is a bounded domain containing the origin and $\alpha>0$. We prove that a solution exists for every exponent $1<p<p_\alpha=\frac{N+2+2\alpha}{N-2}$, in particular in the whole Sobolev-supercritical range $\frac{N+2}{N-2}\le p<p_\alpha$, provided $\Omega$ is invariant under $O(N-1)\times O(1)$ and satisfies an angular monotonicity condition. This class contains the balls, the oblate ellipsoids of revolution, lens-shaped domains, and non-convex, non-smooth and non star-shaped domains. The solution is obtained by minimizing the Rayleigh quotient on a suitable closed convex cone.

papers.title: Complexity of finding color-avoiding connected components
papers.authors: Panna T\'{i}mea Fekete, Roland Molontay, Kitti Varga
papers.abstract:
Two vertices of a (not necessarily properly) arc-colored digraph are called arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected if, after the removal of the arcs of any at most $\ell$ colors, they remain strongly $k$-arc-connected. The arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components are maximal sets of vertices such that any two of those vertices belonging to the set are arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected in the graph.
  We investigate the problems of finding the arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected components and the maximal arc-$\ell$-color-avoiding strongly $k$-arc-connected subgraphs of an arc-colored digraph. We also consider possible generalizations to $k$-vertex-connectivity and to vertex-colored digraphs. We show that despite the seemingly minor differences in definitions, the complexity of these problems varies significantly: some can be solved in polynomial time, while others are NP-hard. It also turns out that in some cases the problem is NP-hard when multiple colors can be assigned to each vertex, but the problem becomes polynomial-time solvable when each vertex is single-colored.

papers.title: Rigidity of K\"ahler-Finsler Metrics with Constant Radial Curvature
papers.authors: Jinling Li, Longjie Li, Chunhui Qiu
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we prove that a smooth strongly pseudoconvex K\"ahler--Finsler metric $F$ satisfying the constant radial curvature condition \[ \Omega(\chi,\bar\chi)\chi=cF^2\chi,
  c\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}, \] is induced by a Hermitian K\"ahler metric of holomorphic sectional curvature $2c$. Under the Abate--Patrizio curvature symmetry \[ \langle\Omega(\cdot,\bar\chi)\chi,\chi\rangle =\langle\Omega(\chi,\bar\chi)\cdot,\chi\rangle, \] this result gives Hermitian rigidity for nonzero constant holomorphic sectional curvature and the classification of complete simply connected metrics of negative curvature. As an application, we show that the Kobayashi metric of a bounded strongly convex domain with smooth boundary is K\"ahler--Finsler if and only if the domain is biholomorphic to the unit ball. We also prove that the universal cover of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain $D $ with smooth boundary is biholomorphic to the unit ball if and only if its Kobayashi metric is a smooth strongly pseudoconvex K\"ahler--Finsler metric. Furthermore, we give two explicit examples to illustrate the distinction between the weakly K\"ahler--Finsler and K\"ahler--Finsler conditions.

papers.title: Multi-split Multiple-sets Implicit Convex Feasibility Seeking As Split Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We introduce a new class of problems, termed multi-split multiple-sets implicit convex feasibility problems (MSMS-ICFPs), define a proximity function for it and analyze its properties under certain assumptions on the involved general point-to-set operators. Additionally, we discuss its properties for a special class of point-to-set operators. For these kinds of point-to-set operators, we deploy a new iterative algorithm to solve the associated MSMS-ICFP and show that any sequence generated by it converges in norm to a solution of the MSMS-ICFP whenever a solution exists (i.e., in the consistent case). We also define a generalized proximity function for the MSMS-ICFP using the Bregman distance. Based on this function, we present a generalized simultaneous projection gradient algorithm for the split feasibility problem with multiple output sets, by examining various related results. We conclude by discussing several further special cases of the MSMS-ICFP.

papers.title: A Yau-Tian-Donaldson correspondence for degenerations
papers.abstract:
We prove an equivalence between the existence of a unique K\"ahler-Einstein metric on a degeneration of Fano varieties and uniform CM minimization. This proves a discretely valued analogue of the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture, in the sense of non-Archimedean geometry.
  As a main tool, we prove that Ding stability of a degeneration implies uniform Ding minimization, proving a converse to work of Blum-Xu. We also prove an analogous result in geometric invariant theory (GIT), stating that uniform GIT height minimization of a family of points is equivalent to GIT stability, proving a converse to work of Wang, Wang-Xu and the author.

papers.title: A Liouville theorem for plurisubharmonic functions with periodic complex Monge-Amp\`ere measure
papers.abstract: We study entire continuous plurisubharmonic solutions of the complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation $(i\partial\bar\partial u)^n=2^n n!\mu$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$, in the Bedford-Taylor sense, where $\mu\not\equiv 0$ is a nonnegative locally finite Borel measure periodic with respect to a lattice of full real rank. We assume that $\mu$ is locally dominated by complex Monge-Amp\`ere measures of H\"older continuous plurisubharmonic functions, a condition under which the existence theorem of Demailly et al. yields H\"older continuous periodic correctors. Under this assumption, we prove that every such solution with positive two-sided quadratic growth can be written uniquely, up to an additive constant, as the sum of a real quadratic polynomial and a H\"older continuous periodic function.

papers.title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups
papers.abstract: We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.

papers.title: Hilbertian Fields and Profinite Iterated Monodromy Groups Over Transcendental Elements with Specializations of Infinite Index
papers.abstract: Given a field $L$ and polynomial $f(x)/L$, one can consider the indices of the profinite iterated monodromy groups formed over the ground field within the profinite iterated monodromy groups over elements transcendental over $L$. For any countable Hilbertian field $k$, we show random Galois fixed field extensions almost surely make the indices infinite over all ground field elements, with certain conditions on $f(x)$. This is a generalization of a result in arXiv:2012.03076 by Dittmann and Kadets.

papers.title: A nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth
papers.authors: Barbara Niethammer, Lorena Pohl, Juan J. L. Vel\'azquez
papers.abstract: We study a nonlocal transport problem describing pore growth in a biological membrane exposed to a periodic electric potential, where the growth term is modified through the first moment of the solution $n_1(t)$. We show that for initial data $f_0$ with noncompact support it holds $n_1(t) \rightarrow \infty$ , whereas for $f_0$ with compact support the limit of $n_1$ depends sensitively on the data. For a broad class of initial data we additionally obtain $n_1 \sim t^{\frac{1}{2}}$. In the case of a constant external potential we further prove that solutions converge to the self-similar solution having the same tail behaviour as $f_0$.

papers.title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_\mu$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.

papers.title: On Terao's conjecture for at most nine planes
papers.abstract: In this note we show that Terao's freeness conjecture holds for arrangements of at most nine planes in the complex projective $3$-space. Moreover, we show that every essential and irreducible free arrangement of at most nine planes in $\mathbb{P}^{3}_{\mathbb{C}}$ is divisionally free, and we list all intersection lattices of such arrangements. Our approach is based on Ziegler's restriction theorem and a simple count involving the numbers of multiple lines. As a by-product, we show that Cynk--Szemberg octic arrangements are never free. Finally, motivated by a recent work of Dimca and Pokora, we present examples of weak Ziegler pairs of plane arrangements, including pairs of octic arrangements leading to rigid double octic Calabi--Yau threefolds.

papers.title: Submodular decompositions: a bounded-variation counterexample and an exact planar cut formula
papers.authors: Guoqing Wang, Linlin Wang, Jun Yue
papers.abstract: B\'erczi, Geh\'er, Imolay, Lov\'asz, and Schwarcz (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 40(2026), 308--335) asked whether every set function of bounded variation is a difference of two bounded submodular functions, and how to determine the optimum in a monotonic sum-decomposition of a planar graph cut function. In this paper, we answer both questions and obtain quantitative extensions. For the first question, we characterize the continuous profiles $f:[0,1]\to\R$ for which $A\mapsto f(m(A))$ is a bounded submodular difference on an atomless probability space. More precisely, we express the minimum oscillation of the subtracted component through the positive part of the distributional second derivative. We also characterize admissible discontinuous profiles and give an exact summability criterion for countable block functions. In particular, the first question has a negative answer even for increasing functions of variation one whose scalar profiles have log-Lipschitz derivatives and belong to every $C^{1,\alpha}$, $0<\alpha<1$. Turning to graph cuts, we prove that the optimum equals the total edge weight minus the maximum fractional triangle-packing weight for every nonnegative weighting if and only if the graph is $K_5$-free. Moreover, maximum packings parametrize the symmetrized optimal components, while on $K_4$-free graphs we describe all optimal components and characterize uniqueness. Consequently, the formula applies to weighted planar graphs and implies edge-weight monotonicity on $K_5$-free graphs. For rational weights, it also yields polynomial-time constructions.

papers.title: The S-function at arbitrary order: hyperplanes of symmetries and the realisability condition
papers.authors: L. G. S. Duarte, L. A. C. P. da Mota
papers.abstract: For a scalar equation $y^{(n)}=\varphi(x,y,\dots,y^{(n-1)})$ the $S$-function of the extended Prelle--Singer method is a vector $S=(S_0,\dots,S_{n-2})$, the null-form vector of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Lakshmanan and collaborators, and the jet gradient of a first integral solves the adjoint of the variational equation. We describe the solutions of the system satisfied by $S$ intrinsically, and determine which of them come from first integrals. Over the field $C$ of first integrals the solutions are exactly the hyperplanes of the $n$-dimensional space $VV$ of symmetry characteristics, recovered from $n-1$ independent characteristics by a Pl\"ucker formula; in flow-box coordinates they are the hyperplane fields on the local space of leaves. A solution is the $S$-vector of a first integral if and only if the corresponding hyperplane field is integrable. This Frobenius condition splits into the $S$-system itself plus $\binom n3$ further differential conditions, so it is vacuous for $n=2$ and a genuine restriction for every $n\ge3$, for which we give an explicit non-realisable solution. The same picture explains why $\lambda$-symmetries and $S$-functions coincide only when $n=2$: line fields and hyperplane fields agree only on surfaces. For the computation of $S$ we record that the system is equivalent to one scalar equation for the last component, which is the Riccati form of the adjoint variational equation, and we spell out what this does and does not imply for a rational search.

papers.title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
papers.authors: Antun Milas, Jan-Willem M. van Ittersum
papers.abstract: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.

papers.title: Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions
papers.abstract: Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$. On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$. We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$. Along the way, we introduce a criterion for producing boundary points of $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is an arbitrary $k$-linear triangulated category. As a byproduct, we deduce the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on certain quotients of the derived categories of K3 and Enriques surfaces.

papers.title: The Torelli Group and Euler Class Zero $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Representations
papers.authors: Marit Bobb, James Farre, Peter Smillie
papers.abstract: We prove that every representation of a closed surface group of genus at least $3$ into $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ that is sufficiently close (but not equal to) a representation that has non-compact solvable image has a simple closed separating curve that is mapped to a non-trivial elliptic element in $\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. This can be seen as evidence for an affirmative answer to a question of Bowditch and a conjecture of Goldman.

papers.title: G-equivariant Alterfold TQFT in any dimension
papers.abstract: For a discrete group $G$, we construct an $(n+1)$-dimensional $G$-equivariant Alterfold topological quantum field theory from a $G$-equivariant $S^n$-algebra satisfying strong semisimplicity, complete finiteness, and Morita invariance. We use state sum on triangulation to define a partition function and prove that it is invariant under local surgery relations and is invariant under gauge transformations relative to the boundary. If the input is given a reflection-positive structure, the theory is unitary. For $n=2$ and input reconstructed from a strict faithful spherical $G$-fusion category, the restriction to ordinary $G$-cobordisms is naturally isomorphic to the Turaev--Virelizier state-sum HQFT \cite{turaev20123}. A Tambara-Yamagami example recovers the Quon language \cite{liu2017quon} as a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-equivariant Alterfold TQFT.

papers.title: $\gamma$-Valued Stein--Tomas Restriction for Schatten Classes
papers.abstract: Let $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact $C^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent Schatten-valued Stein--Tomas range \[ R_\Sigma:L^p(\mathbb R^3;S^a)\longrightarrow\gamma(L^2(\Sigma),S^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] The core endpoint is $E_\Sigma:\gamma(L^2(\Sigma),S^4)\to L^4(\mathbb R^3;S^4)$. After squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the Hilbert--Schmidt class. A local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. We also show that Gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary Banach spaces. Applications include matrix Herglotz waves, a two-dimensional Schr\"odinger $L^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.

papers.title: Data-driven Regularization for Inverse Problems
papers.abstract:
In many applications, we are interested in studying an object of interest $x$. However, its properties are often not directly measurable. Instead, we only observe $y = F(x)$, where the (known) function $F$ is referred to as the forward mapping. To infer about $x$ from the observation $y$, we seek an (approximate) inverse mapping $x \approx F^{-1}(y)$. This process is known as solving the inverse problem.
  In practice, the inverse mapping $F^{-1}$ may be ill-defined or discontinuous, which forces us to choose a certain solution from many possible ones based on prior assumptions on $x$. Such assumptions about $x$ are typically incorporated into the inversion process through regularization. Therefore, the first part of this course focuses on the classical regularization theory of inverse problems.
  In the second part, we transition to algorithmic approaches for solving inverse problems. The foundation for this lies in the variational formulation of inverse problems, where reconstructions are obtained by minimizing specific functionals. Here, we will explore key optimization principles, discuss their practical implementation, and examine how they contribute to robust reconstructions.
  Today, classical methods are often modified to incorporate data-driven machine learning techniques, which improve the empirical performance. However, this often comes at the cost of explainability or convergence guarantees. Such properties are critical, for example, in medical applications, where one wants to be confident that reconstructed abnormalities are of physical nature and not phantoms resulting from the method.
  For these reasons, we discuss a number of machine learning methods for inverse problems, such as unrolling techniques, learned regularizers and plug-and-play methods, and explore their performance guarantees.

papers.title: Model Theory of Johnson Graphs
papers.authors: Bjarki Geir Benediktsson, Dugald Macpherson, Isolde Adler
papers.abstract:
A \emph{Johnson graph} $J(n,k)$ is a graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of an underlying set of size $n$ where two vertices are adjacent if they intersect in a subset of size $k-1$. We extend the definition to allow infinite parameters and we study a natural limit theory $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ of Johnson graphs. We show that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is complete and we give an axiomatisation of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, from which we obtain a complete description of the models of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$.
  We use this to show tameness properties of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, namely that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is $\omega$-stable of Morley rank $\omega$, but not monadically dependent. In particular it follows that the class of all finite Johnson graphs is stable, and therefore dependent but not monadically dependent.

papers.title: Invariant probability measures on holomorphic functions on the unit disk
papers.abstract: We study probability measures on the space of holomorphic functions on the unit disk that are invariant under pre-composition by conformal automorphisms and give no mass to constant functions. We determine the slowest possible growth of functions supported by such measures. Let $M_f(R)$ denote the maximum modulus of $f$ on the hyperbolic ball of radius $R$ centered at the origin. We show that given a non-decreasing function $G:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$, there exists an $\textrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$-invariant probability measure $\mu$ on $\textrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}, \mathbb{C}) \setminus \{\textrm{constant functions} \}$ such that $\log^+ M_f(R)=O_f(G(R))$ for $\mu$ almost every $f$ if and only if $\int_1^\infty (R/G(R)) \, dR <\infty$. For the lower bound, we use a mass transport argument to show that almost every trajectory of the gradient flow of $\log |f|$ has finite energy. To establish sharpness, we construct holomorphic functions of slow growth on infinite Riemann surfaces.

papers.title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
papers.abstract: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.

papers.title: Higher-order jet and its application to the Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the deffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher order $\mu$-discreteness for subgroup $\Gamma < {\rm Diff}(M)$.
  As applications, we show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher order $\mu$-discreteness.

papers.title: Singularity of harmonic measure on Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the harmonic measure of simple random walk on the Poisson--Voronoi tessellation in $\mathbb{H}^d$ is almost surely singular with respect to Lebesgue measure on the boundary. This answers a question of Benjamini, Paquette, and Pfeffer in the hyperbolic plane and establishes the analogous result in higher dimensions. Our proof is based on ergodic theory of rerooting relations and their boundary extensions.

papers.title: Harmonically lifting linear series from curves to K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We investigate the question of which Brill--Noether special linear series on a curve on a K3 surface lift to the surface. Work of Reid, Donagi--Morrison, Green--Lazarsfeld, Lelli-Chiesa, and others shows that Brill--Noether special linear series admits lifts in many cases, in particular when the linear series computes the Clifford index of the curve. Using the recently defined notion of harmonic filtrations of Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, we show the same is true for a linear series computing the Brill--Noether special Clifford index, an analogue of the classical Clifford index considering only Brill--Noether special linear series, and show that the Brill--Noether special Clifford index is constant in linear series on K3 surfaces.

papers.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$
papers.abstract: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.

papers.title: The bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three
papers.authors: Shane Chern, Trieu Nguyen, Chanh Tran, Tanay Wakhare
papers.abstract: Using a rational analogue of an $\mathrm{A}_2^{(1)}$ Rogers--Ramanujan type identity discovered by Warnaar, we establish sum-like expressions for a bivariate generating function for cylindric partitions of rank three. These expressions provide the finishing touch towards conjectures of Warnaar and Kanade--Russell.

papers.title: An HDG-type discretization of 1D embedded blood flow in complex networks with Riemann-coupled junctions
papers.authors: Raksha Devi, Luca Heltai, Lucas O. M\"uller
papers.abstract: We present a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for one-dimensional blood flow in arterial networks with Windkessel boundary conditions. The scheme uses a Harten--Lax--van Leer (HLL) numerical flux and implicit time integration.
