After spatial discretization, the complete network---including cell states, hybrid traces, junction conditions, and dynamic $\mathrm{RCR}$ terminal pressures---is written as a residual index-one differential--algebraic equation (DAE) and integrated with variable-step, variable-order backward differentiation formulas. The implicit formulation removes the CFL stability restriction of explicit schemes and allows variable-order, variable-step solvers. The resulting single global residual and Jacobian for the network and its terminal dynamics also provide a natural interface for monolithic coupling with external nonlinear models. We establish local solvability and a semi-discrete energy balance, and show numerically optimal convergence rates for both solution variables in the $L^2$ norm and the broken $H^1$ seminorm. The solver is validated against established benchmarks, including an aortic bifurcation and a $37$-artery network, and is further applied to a cerebral arterial network. Mass conservation is observed in a synthetically generated anatomical liver network of $8\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels, and strong-scaling studies are performed on synthetic networks of $50\,\mathrm{k}$ and $100\,\mathrm{k}$ vessels.

papers.title: A total variation threshold for the first coordinates of uniform parking functions via Lorentzian polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $\pi_n$ be a uniform parking function of size $n$. We determine the scale at which its first $k$ coordinates cease to be close in total variation to $k$ independent uniform variables on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The distance is comparable to $1\wedge \sqrt{k\log(k+1)/n}$, uniformly for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and tends to one above the scale $n/\log n$. At the critical scale $k\sim\lambda n/\log n$, it converges to $2\Phi(\sqrt{\lambda/\pi})-1$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. A key ingredient is the Lorentzian property of the occupation generating polynomial of parking functions. Together with a strengthened Han inequality, this yields a relative entropy estimate for approximation by the product of the one-coordinate marginals.

papers.title: Multi-excited random walks on general trees
papers.abstract: We study multi-excited random walks on infinite locally finite trees. The model is described by placing a stack of ``cookies'' at each vertex, with one cookie consumed on each successive visit. As long as cookies remain, the walk is in an excited regime and makes nearest-neighbour steps according to a prescribed sequence of biases. Once the stack is exhausted, the walk is in a non-excited regime and moves uniformly among the neighbouring vertices. The model is closely connected to foraging ecology, where repeated visits to a location can deplete local resources and thereby influence the attractiveness of that location for future visits. We prove that the process exhibits a sharp phase transition between recurrence and transience. The critical threshold is determined by the branching-ruin number of the tree, which is equal to the Hausdorff dimension of the tree's boundary under a suitable metric. Our result substantially extends Zerner's recurrence-transience criterion for multi-excited random walks on $\mathbb Z$ [Probab. Theory Related Fields 133 (2005)] to general trees.

papers.title: Ergodicity for the Two-Dimensional Stochastic Navier-Stokes Equations with Shear-Thickening Viscosity
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional stochastic Navier-Stokes equations with a shear-thickening viscosity driven by multiplicative noise are studied. After the problem is formulated as an abstract stochastic evolution equation on suitable function spaces, the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions are established through local monotonicity methods. Moment estimates are then obtained and used to prove the existence of an ergodic invariant probability measure via the Krylov-Bogolyubov technique. The uniqueness of the ergodic invariant measure is subsequently established by constructing a generalized coupling through a controlled auxiliary equation. Finally, the results are extended to other types of viscosities as well as to different stochastic hydrodynamical models.

papers.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
papers.abstract: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

papers.title: Rota universality of shifts on trees
papers.abstract: We consider shift operators on infinite directed trees. We prove that under very mild assumptions on the structure of the tree, the resulting operator is universal (in the sense of Rota). We show connections between the spectrum of the operator and the frequency of branching in the tree.

papers.title: On the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv Problem for $\mathbb{Z}_n^r$
papers.abstract: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv problem is a classical extremal problem in discrete geometry. We prove that, for all positive integers $n$ and $r$, every sequence of $4^r n$ lattice points in $\mathbb{Z}^r$ contains $n$ points whose centroid is again a lattice point.

papers.title: Holomorphic 1-forms without zeros on K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: Assuming the existence of good minimal models, we give a bimeromorphic classification of compact connected K\"ahler manifolds admitting a holomorphic 1-form without zeros.

papers.title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $\chi$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$.
  To the character $\chi$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_\chi=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $\chi$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition
  of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_\chi$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.

papers.title: Failure of the $H^1\times H^1\longrightarrow L^{1/2,\infty}$ estimate for the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal function and applications
papers.authors: Sanghyuk Lee, Ji Li, Chaojie Wen, Liangchuan Wu
papers.abstract:
In contrast to Christ's theorem that the lacunary spherical maximal operator is bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ ($d\geq2$), we show that the lacunary bilinear spherical maximal operator $$
  \mathcal B_{\mathrm{lac}}(f,g)(x)
  =\sup_{\ell\in\mathbb Z}
  \Bigl|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-2^\ell y)\,g(x-2^\ell z)\,d\sigma(y,z)\Bigr| $$ is not bounded from $H^1(\mathbb R^d)\times H^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$ for any $d\geq1$. In particular, it is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^1(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. More precisely, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, we construct two finite linear combinations of smooth, compactly supported, mean-zero $H^1(\mathbb R^d)$-atoms for which the ratio of the weak $L^{1/2}$ quasinorm to the product of the two Hardy norms is at least $c_d\log(N+1)$. This lower bound holds already for the supremum over a suitable set of $N$ dyadic radii. For $d=1$ this answers the case $p=q=1$ of a question in Borges's survey. For every $k\ge3$ and $d\ge1$, a modification of the construction proves that the lacunary $k$-linear spherical maximal operator does not map $(H^1(\mathbb R^d))^k$ into $L^{1/k,\infty}(\mathbb R^d)$. We also indicate extensions to certain hypersurfaces and to horizontal spherical averages on the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.

papers.title: Characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the annulus
papers.abstract: We establish algebraic characterizations of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space on the annulus. As an application, we characterize compact perturbations of Toeplitz operators.

papers.title: Asymptotically Compatible Variational Energy Dissipation Laws and Structure-Preserving Variable-Step Linear Relaxation Schemes for a Subdiffusive Tumor-Nutrient Model
papers.authors: Hui Yu, Zhaoyang Wang, Ping Lin
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a mass-conservative subdiffusive tumor-nutrient model coupled through chemotaxis and memory-dependent reaction exchange, together with structure-preserving variable-step linear relaxation schemes. A weighted Riemann-Liouville identity is proved and used to construct a variational energy and the associated energy dissipation law for the proposed model. Both the model and the associated variational energy dissipation law are asymptotically compatible with their integer-order counterparts as the fractional order approaches one. For numerical approximation, we discretize the Riemann-Liouville fractional derivatives using the L1R formula on nonuniform time meshes and derive the associated discrete weighted inequality. We first construct a variable-step linear relaxation scheme for the subdiffusive model. Then, to mitigate alternating perturbations induced by the auxiliary-variable error and amplified by the L1R convolution at small fractional orders, we construct a temporally damped linear relaxation scheme. Since temporal damping leaves the auxiliary-variable recurrence unchanged, we further introduce an a posteriori relaxation correction to reduce alternating errors in the auxiliary variable. All three schemes preserve total mass, are proven to satisfy discrete variational energy dissipation laws using the discrete weighted inequality, and remain consistent with the integer-order limit. Several numerical examples are presented to validate the accuracy and stability of the proposed schemes.

papers.title: Graphical Models Induced by Irreversible Event Accumulation on Trees
papers.abstract:
Decomposable graphical models are usually adopted for their computational convenience rather than derived from a data-generating mechanism. We show that a special class of them arises naturally from the irreversible accumulation of events along a branching history. Each event is attached to an edge of a latent rooted tree and is inherited by everything below that edge; an observation records which events have occurred at a randomly chosen node, not necessarily a leaf. When the tree is a path, this is the cumulative coding of an ordinal variable, whose indicators form a Markov chain; in the general tree case the Markov chain is replaced by a junction tree.
  The conditional independence graph of the event indicators is always decomposable and, in fact, is the line graph of the tree (maximal cliques correspond to nodes where two or more edges meet and separators are the single events on the edges joining two such nodes). The graph determines the tree up to the choice of root. A connected graph arises in this way if, and only if, it is chordal, any two of its maximal cliques share at most one vertex, no vertex is in three maximal cliques, and the graph is such that any two maximal cliques share at most one vertex. This provides a simple graphical test for compatibility with the mechanism (necessary but not sufficient, as irreversibility also constrains the distribution's support).
  The structure breaks down if we look at just the leaves, and measurement error destroys the exact screening and leads to a denser graph rather than simply a weaker dependence. We discuss inference, provide diagnostics for departures such as recurrent events, illustrate them on some simulated data and discuss their application in the context of mutation accumulation and lineage tracing where both ancestral and descendant types are sampled together.

papers.title: Hypersurface and Foliation Isoparametric Transfer for Generalized $(\alpha,\beta)$-Metrics
papers.abstract: Let $F=\alpha\Phi(q,s)$ be a regular generalized $(\alpha,\beta)$-metric, where $q=\|\beta\|_\alpha^2$ and $s=\beta/\alpha$, endowed with the Busemann--Hausdorff or Holmes--Thompson volume. We derive explicit comparison formulas for the induced hypersurface volume and the associated volume mean curvature and use them to study two transfer problems suggested by the Randers case. The first asks whether the same hypersurface is isoparametric for $\alpha$ and $F$; the second asks whether the same regular foliation is isoparametric for both metrics. Exact local and global criteria are obtained. Their Randers specializations recover the corresponding hypersurface transfer and the condition $df(W)=\varphi(f)$. We also prove an all-normal induced-volume rigidity theorem and construct a complete non-Randers example realizing both transfer mechanisms.

papers.title: Full immersions in Eulerian group-labeled graphs
papers.authors: Ioannis Eleftheriadis, Rose McCarty, Caleb McFarland, Evangelos Protopapas, Paul Wollan
papers.abstract: An immersion of a graph H in a graph G is full if the immersion uses every edge of G. We give a structure theorem for group-labeled Eulerian graphs excluding a fixed group-labeled graph as a full immersion.

papers.title: Integer-Quantized Hierarchical Matrices with Adaptive Bit Allocation
papers.authors: Erin Carson, Xinye Chen, Ritesh Khan
papers.abstract: We present an adaptive bitwidth allocation method for quantizing low-rank factors in hierarchical matrices in order to decrease storage while meeting a given constraint on their reconstruction error. For the bitwidth allocation we formulate a discrete storage minimization problem and show that an optimal assignment can give larger singular values at least as many bits as smaller ones. We further develop a greedy algorithm that meets the specified max-norm quantization error budget. We investigate a hierarchical block partition in which all of the non-diagonal blocks are represented by quantized low-rank factors and only dense blocks remain dense; in this way a global reconstruction bound related to $\eta_k$ and $R_k$ is obtained, with the former and latter being bounds on the truncation and reconstruction arithmetic errors, respectively. Extensive simulations, carried out with kernel and BEM matrices under block-relative budgets, indicate that the proposed method achieves a reduction in storage of up to $44.3\times$ when compared to storing the complete matrix densely in FP64, and a reduction of up to $5.70\times$ when compared to the FP64 low-rank factors within the same partition, together with measured reconstruction errors that remained below the maximum norm bounds in all the hierarchical tests.

papers.title: Local $Tb$ theorems in non-homogeneous metric spaces, and applications to caloric measure
papers.authors: Andrea Merlo, Mihalis Mourgoglou, Carmelo Puliatti
papers.abstract:
We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel. Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators.
  As an application in the parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(\sigma)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $\sigma$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.

papers.title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
papers.abstract: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.

papers.title: Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits for the total edge-length of random directional nearest-neighbour graphs
papers.authors: Nicholas Georgiou, Qasem M. Tawhari, Andrew Wade
papers.abstract: We study planar random spatial graphs defined by inserting an edge between every point of a homogeneous Poisson process on the unit square and a nearest-neighbour within a fixed cone of directions (if there is such a point). We prove large-sample distributional limit theorems for the total Euclidean edge length of the graph, where the limit distribution is either Gaussian (due to contributions from the bulk) or, when one or both of the boundaries of the cone of directions align with the edges of the square, a convolution of Gaussian with a non-Gaussian law arising from boundary effects due to long edges near a boundary. This work extends previously known cases, including the ordinary nearest-neighbour graph (full cone of directions), where the Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Bickel & Breiman and Avram & Bertsimas, and Bhatt & Roy's minimal directed spanning forest (with 'south-west' directions), where the non-Gaussian limit theorem was obtained by Penrose & Wade.

papers.title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications
papers.abstract: We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csisz\'ar, K\"orner, Lov\'asz, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lov\'asz theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tun\c{c}el on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.

papers.title: Dynamical relations on $\mathbb{P}^1$, higher bifurcations, and arithmetic bigness
papers.abstract: In this article, we study algebraic relations among rational maps on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and among their preperiodic points. Working over $\mathbb{C}$, we characterize algebraic families of positive-dimensional varieties in $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ and tuples of maps $(f_1, \ldots, f_N)$ for which the subvariety is dynamically special for a Zariski-dense set of parameters. Moreover, outside of well-understood elliptic phenomena, we show that all families of maps and subvarieties that bifurcate are maximally bifurcating. Working over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we characterize arithmetic and geometric potential bigness for the canonical line bundle associated to families of endomorphisms of $(\mathbb{P}^1)^N$ when restricted to the subvarieties. As consequences, we obtain uniform bounds for the periods and preperiods of relations among non-exceptional maps, and we show uniform bounds on the geometry of preperiodic points satisfying these relations. Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, our results yield corresponding uniform bounds for points and subvarieties satisfying a height gap.

papers.title: Compact and Hilbert-Schmidt composition operators on weighted Hardy spaces
papers.authors: Francisco J. Cruz-Zamorano, Eugenio Dellepiane, Daniel Seco
papers.abstract: Lef\`evre, Li, Queff\'elec, and Rodr\'iguez-Piazza [12] recently characterized the sequences $\beta$ for which the weighted Hardy space $H^2(\beta)$ has the same bounded composition operators as the Hardy space $H^2$. We investigate the analogous questions for the compactness and the $p$-Schatten classes: for which sequences $\beta$ does the space $H^2(\beta)$ have the same compact or $p$-Schatten class composition operators as $H^2$?

papers.title: Packing and covering random trees
papers.authors: Caelan Atamanchuk, Simon Briend, Serte Donderwinkel, Elaine Herrera
papers.abstract:
We study the sizes of optimal packings and coverings of conditioned branching processes by balls with growing radii. We find a universal limiting constant, and thereby establish universality of packing and covering numbers across different scales and different offspring distributions.
  To be precise, for $\mu$ an offspring distribution with mean $1$ and finite variance $\sigma^2$ we let $T_n$ be a Bienaym\'e tree with offspring distribution $\mu$ conditioned to have size $n$. We prove that the packing number (resp. covering number) of $T_n$ with balls of radii $1\ll \gamma_n \ll n^{1/2}$ is asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C} n /(\sigma^2 \gamma_n^2)$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C} n /(4\sigma^2 \gamma_n^2)$), for a universal constant $\mathfrak{C}$.
  We also show that the order of limits can be exchanged and that the same limit occurs when we first consider the limiting covering number of $T_n$ by balls of fixed radius $R$, and thereafter let $R$ tend to $\infty$.
  We then extend these results to the Brownian continuum random tree conditioned to have mass $1$. For this model, we prove that the packing (resp. covering) number with balls of radii $\varepsilon$ are asymptotically equivalent to $\mathfrak{C}/\varepsilon^2$ (resp. $\mathfrak{C}/(4\varepsilon^2)$), for the same constant $\mathfrak{C}$, in contrast with a conjecture by Aldous.
  Finally, our results answer a question by Devroye, Eide and Pralat on the asymptotic burning number of mean $1$ finite variance Bienaym\'e trees of size $n$, by showing that it lies between $(c+o(1)) n^{1/3}$ and $(2c+o(1))n^{1/3}$ with high probability, for a constant $c$ that only depends on the offspring variance.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $\Phi = \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(\Phi\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture. Our approach combines a degeneration argument via ultrafilters with a new non-archimedean rigidity theorem, along with the quantitative dynamical Zhang's inequality by Mavraki and the second author.

papers.title: Model-assisted estimation of the finite population mean via local linear regression with associated kernels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a general regression-assisted estimator of the population mean based on local regression with associated kernels, a broad class that encompasses both classical (symmetric) kernels, such as the Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels, and asymmetric kernels, such as the gamma kernel. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator, including explicit expressions for the bias, mean squared error, and asymptotic normality, under a unified framework that applies to any kernel in this class. Through simulation studies on nonnegative data and one real-data application, we compare the finite-sample performance of the estimator based on the gamma kernel with those relying on the Gaussian and Epanechnikov kernels. When the data are supported on the positive real line, symmetric kernels suffer from boundary bias near zero due to mass assignment outside the support, whereas the gamma kernel, naturally adapted to $[0,\infty)$, alleviates this effect. The results confirm that the choice of kernel within the associated matters in practice, and that asymmetric kernels provide a reliable and efficient alternative when the underlying regression function is supported on the positive real line or exhibits marked asymmetry.

papers.title: Optimal subtrees of finite metric graphs
papers.authors: Levi Haunschmid-Sibitz, Fredrik Viklund, David Witt Nystr\"om
papers.abstract: We consider a metric graph analog of a classical extremal problem for Riemann surfaces studied by Teichm\"uller, Jenkins, Strebel, and others. In particular, we prove that on any finite metric graph with a marked point, there is a unique open subtree which maximizes a metric graph analog of the reduced modulus, and we also give an equivalent characterization of this optimal subtree in terms of balanced harmonic measures.

papers.title: Multivariate Lebesgue bounds for R-Leja lower grids
papers.abstract: We establish an algebraic upper bound for the Lebesgue constant of multivariate polynomial interpolation on $\mathfrak R$-Leja lower grids. For each fixed dimension $d\geq2$ and every nonempty finite lower set $A\subset\mathbb N_0^d$, let $P_A$ denote the corresponding grid with $N=|A|$ nodes. We prove $\Lambda(P_A)\leq C_dN^{\beta_d}$, where $q_d=d/(d-1)$ and $\beta_d=1+q_d^{-1}\log_2(1+2^{q_d})$. The exponent satisfies $\beta_2=2.160964\ldots$ and increases to $\log_2 6=2.584962\ldots$ as $d\to\infty$, improving both the cubic estimate and the exponent $3-1/d$ obtained from quadratic prefix bounds. Our proof exploits the binary structure of known univariate estimates to control sums of powers of Lebesgue constants over interpolation prefixes. A weighted H\"older inequality and a disjoint-box packing argument then transfer these prefix-moment bounds to arbitrary lower sets. The resulting estimate is uniform over all lower-set shapes and choices of disk Leja maximizers, with constants depending only on $d$.

papers.title: Polarimetric Low-Rank Imaging of Anisotropic Maxwell Media
papers.authors: Xianbo Chen, Jingzhi Li, Ping Liu
papers.abstract: We consider three-dimensional imaging of compactly supported anisotropic electric media from fixed-frequency polarimetric Maxwell far-field data. Maxwell transversality creates an obstruction absent from scalar Born inversion: each measurement determines only a projected action of the tensor-valued Fourier transform. We first resolve this obstruction by a finite-dimensional polarimetric inversion. For a general complex $3\times3$ contrast, three incidence--observation configurations are necessary, and we give an explicit three-configuration design that is sufficient at every nonzero interior Fourier point. Its Gram determinant yields quantitative conditioning information and exhibits the loss of recoverability at the boundary of the accessible Fourier ball. After tensor demixing, the inverse problem reduces componentwise to restricted Fourier inversion on the unit ball, which we regularize by spectral cutoff in three-dimensional ball generalized prolate spheroidal wave functions. For discrete acquisition, a combined reconstruction error estimate separates the effects of measurement noise, polarimetric amplification, off-grid Fourier mismatch, quadrature error, Born modeling error, and spectral truncation. Numerical tests examine polarimetric conditioning and use analytically generated Born data to compare three- and six-configuration recovery and assess off-grid sensitivity. Reconstructions from full-Maxwell volume-integral data assess the effects of noise, wavenumber, and basis choice, as well as the recovery of different tensor components.

papers.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
papers.abstract: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth M\"obius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.

papers.title: Von Neumann regular and semisimple rings realized as principal quotients of domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that every commutative von Neumann regular ring is a quotient of a characteristic-zero B\'ezout domain by its principal Jacobson radical. We then characterize the commutative semisimple rings that occur as quotients of Dedekind domains. For a finite product of fields $R=\prod_{i=1}^n k_i$, such a presentation exists exactly when the cardinals $|k_i|^{\aleph_0}$ are all equal. When this condition holds, the source may be taken to be a characteristic-zero semilocal principal ideal domain, and the quotient ideal may again be its Jacobson radical.

papers.title: New hierarchical matrices for fast kernel matrix-vector products with Applications to Gaussian processes and kernel ridge regression
papers.abstract: This article presents two new multilevel hierarchical matrices to perform fast kernel matrix-vector products in $d$ dimensions $(d>1)$, namely $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime}$, $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime \prime}$. We introduce a novel hybrid weak admissibility condition to construct these hierarchical matrices. More precisely, at coarser levels of the tree (i.e., larger blocks), we use a weak admissibility condition, wherein \textbf{far-field} and \textbf{vertex-sharing} clusters are considered admissible, while at the finer levels (i.e., smaller blocks), the \textbf{adjacent} clusters are treated as admissible. The admissible blocks at coarser levels of $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime}$ and $\mathcal{H}_{hw}^{\prime \prime}$ are represented using semi-nested and fully nested bases, respectively. In both hierarchical matrices, the finer levels at which adjacent clusters are treated as admissible are constructed in a non-nested fashion. Thus, they can be viewed as a hybrid of $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{H}^2$ matrices. We use adaptive cross approximation (ACA) and nested cross approximation (NCA) to construct non-nested and nested bases, respectively. The fast matrix-vector products are performed using the proposed hierarchical matrix formats. To evaluate the performance and usefulness of the proposed hierarchical matrices, we conduct some numerical experiments. The numerical results show that they outperform their uniform admissibility counterparts in terms of storage and matrix-vector product cost, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid formats. We also show that the proposed formats are competitive with the standard (or strong) admissibility-based $\mathcal{H}^2$-matrices. Furthermore, we showcase some interesting applications of the proposed hierarchical matrices.

papers.title: Whitham Deformations of Nodal Spectral Curves of the Sinh-Gordon Equation
papers.abstract: Spectral curves of constant mean curvature tori in Euclidean three-space are real hyperelliptic curves carrying two meromorphic differentials with integral periods. Deformations that preserve the periods, called Whitham deformations, are well understood for nonsingular curves, where the isoperiodic sets are manifolds. We extend Whitham deformations to curves with ordinary double points that are fixed by the real involution. At such curves the isoperiodic sets remain manifolds and are transverse to the curves with double points, so Whitham deformations can change the genus of the spectral curve. We describe how the double points open, and when the derivative of the normalized Willmore energy vanishes at a nodal curve. By inserting double points, we show that every value of a discrete invariant of the isoperiodic sets found in previous work occurs.

papers.title: Inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-Selfless Groups
papers.authors: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Mario Klisse, Matteo Pagliero
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless groups and study their structural properties. We prove a Fourier coefficient extraction theorem for invariant subalgebras of crossed products by such groups under a compatibility assumption on the action. Consequently, every inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selfless group has the relative $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property, and every finite product of such groups has the $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-invariant subalgebra rigidity property. We also introduce another group-theoretic notion, which we call cyclic Powers property. This implies inner $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, complete $\mathrm{C}^{\ast}$-selflessness, and the Powers property, among others. We establish it for groups admitting a topologically free extreme boundary action on a compact Hausdorff space with more than two points, and for Zariski-dense discrete subgroups of $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb K)$ containing a biproximal element, where $\mathbb K$ is a local field and $d\geq2$. In particular, we obtain the Powers property for $\mathrm{PSL}(d,\mathbb Z)$, $d\geq3$, answering a question posed more than twenty years ago by Bridson-de la Harpe. Finally, we show that every non-trivial mixed identity-free discrete group has the relative invariant subalgebra rigidity property for its group von Neumann algebra. This shows that the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ with $|m|,|n|\geq2$ and $|m|\ne|n|$ have the relative ISR property, thereby answering a question of Dudko-Jiang.

papers.title: The $6\frac{1}{2}$-functor formalism of Cartier modules
papers.abstract:
Let $p$ be a prime. We construct a coherent formalism of geometric operations on Cartier modules with coefficients in ind-coherent sheaves on noetherian derived $\mathbb F_p$-schemes. For such a scheme $X$, we consider the stable presentable category $\mathrm{Cart}(X)$ of ind-coherent sheaves $M$ equipped with a structural morphism $F_{*,X}M \to M$, where $F_X$ denotes the Frobenius endomorphism.
  We construct pushforward functors for arbitrary morphisms and exceptional pullback functors for separated morphisms almost of finite type, together with coherent composition and base-change equivalences. We single out conditions under which these functors admit further adjoints.
  On derived schemes separated and almost of finite type over $\mathbb F_p$, we construct compatible closed symmetric monoidal structures given by shriek tensor products, and establish which functors are symmetric monoidal.
  The constructions arise from a general procedure for forming functor formalisms of Cartier objects, using their description as lax limits and the universal properties of span $2$-categories developed by Cnossen--Lenz--Linskens [arXiv:2505.19192].

papers.title: An Adaptive Transferable Neural Network for Partial Differential Equations with Anisotropic or Sharp Solutions
papers.abstract: Transferable neural network (TransNet) has demonstrated great potential for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with high accuracy and efficiency. However, it struggles significantly when dealing with PDEs featuring anisotropy or sharp solutions. In this work, we propose an adaptive transferable neural network (A-TransNet), a novel machine learning framework that adaptively expands neurons in regions with large solution gradients to effectively capture complex solution behaviors. Instead of relying on training or random sampling, the location parameters of newly added neurons are determined by integrating the active subspaces method and local gradient analysis based on posterior gradient information. This adaptive strategy enables neurons to be allocated where they are most needed, thereby improving the resolution of anisotropic and sharp features without additional computational costs. Moreover, the shape parameters of new neurons are automatically determined from the neuron density induced by their locations, further enhancing the network representation capability. An iterative neuron expansion strategy is developed, together with rigorous analysis of stability, a posteriori error estimation, and convergence of the proposed A-TransNet method. Extensive numerical experiments on challenging PDE problems with anisotropic and sharp solutions demonstrate that A-TransNet achieves superior accuracy, efficiency, and robustness compared with existing methods.

papers.title: On a class of meromorphic functions with three singular values
papers.abstract: We give a parametrization of the class of real meromorphic functions in the plane for which the preimage of $\{0,1,\infty\}$ is contained in the real line, and all singular values belong to $\{0,1,\infty\}$. As corollaries, we obtain a new parabolic type criterion and prove that all such functions are limits of rational functions of the same class.

papers.title: The Segal conjecture for large objects and semiadditive lifts
papers.abstract:
We prove a projection formula for homotopy fixed points of trivial actions of finite $p$-groups. More precisely, for every bounded-below, $p$-complete spectrum $X$ whose mod-$p$ homology is $I$-complete, the canonical map \[ (\mathbb S_p)^{BG}\otimes X \overset{\simeq}{\rightarrow} X^{BG} \] is an equivalence for every finite $p$-group $G$, where $I$ is the augmentation ideal of the Steenrod algebra.
  Building on earlier joint work with Burklund, our proof combines the Adams--Gunawardena--Miller calculation with an adaptation of Carlsson's induction. As an application, using the work of Yuan, we construct height-one semiadditive lifts of such spectra and show that their cohomology of $p$-finite spaces depends only on the $1$-type.

papers.title: Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons I
papers.abstract: We define mathematically the Point-Splitting Perturbative Chern-Simons Theory. The framing anomaly arise directly from the dependence of the configuration space of points on the frame.

papers.title: Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons II
papers.abstract: We extend the formalism of Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons to include Wilson Loops.

papers.title: Berezin--Li--Yau inequalities for Aharonov--Bohm operators
papers.authors: Michael Levitin, Iosif Polterovich, Romain Speciel
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp Berezin--Li--Yau inequality for Riesz means of order at least one for Aharonov--Bohm operators on bounded planar domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions. This confirms a conjecture posed by Frank and Hansson in 2008. We also obtain an improved lower bound for individual eigenvalues and extend it to the case of magnetic potentials with bounded magnetic field. These results are then applied to deduce estimates for Riesz means of orders between zero and one, and for Aharonov--Bohm eigenvalues on product domains.

papers.title: Discrete hermitian groups are FC-hypercentral
papers.abstract: We show that a discrete group is hermitian if and only if it is FC-hypercentral, that is, if and only if it does not have any nontrivial ICC quotients. In particular, a finitely generated group is hermitian if and only if it is virtually nilpotent. The main step is an elementary, self-contained proof that every hermitian ICC group is trivial, based on a finite-set separation property of nontrivial ICC groups.

papers.title: On stable twist 2-groups of quasi-Hopf algebras
papers.abstract:
For any finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebra $A$, we define the notion of a stable twist of $A$. We show that stable twists form a strict 2-group $\2ust(A)$, which is equivalent to $\OAut(\C{A})^{\rev}$. Given a group homomorphism $\rho: G \to \ost(A)$, we determine the obstruction in $H^3(G,Z_G(A))$ to lift $\rho$ to a $G$-action on $\C{A}$. We also establish a bijection between such liftings and cocentral cleft extensions of $\k[G]$ by $A$.
  The main application of $\2ust(A)$ is the computation of $\OAut(\C{A})$, together with an explicit description of the corresponding tensor autoequivalences. We apply this framework to pointed Hopf algebras $A$ that arise as central extensions of Taft algebras by cyclic groups, and we explicitly determine all of their tensor autoequivalences. The equivariantizations of $\C{A}$ by $\ost(A)$ produce a new family of Hopf algebras $\N(n,\xi)$ of dimension $2nm$, where $\xi$ is a scalar of order $m\mid n$ such that neither $\N(n,\xi)$ nor its dual has the Chevalley property.
  In dimension 24, we prove that $\N(6,-1)$ and its dual are precisely the Hopf algebras $H$ for which neither $H$ nor $H^*$ has the Chevalley property. This completes the classification of nonsemisimple Hopf algebras of dimension 24.

papers.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problems for Sturm--Liouville Operators with Potentials in $L^p(0,1)$
papers.abstract:
We study an optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for a one-dimensional Sturm--Liouville operator on a finite interval. The problem is to find a potential $V \in L^p(0,1)$ that realizes a prescribed finite set $\lambda_1^* < \lambda_2^* < \dots < \lambda_m^*$ and has the smallest $L^p(0,1)$-distance from an a priori given potential $V_0 \in L^p(0,1)$.
  We formulate and prove results on the regularity of the isospectral manifold, the existence of an OISP solution, and an explicit analytic representation of the optimal potential by means of a power map applied to a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions.
  Using a unified differential-algebraic approach to squared eigenfunctions, we show that whenever these squares are linearly dependent, the corresponding potential can be expressed in terms of them and is an analytic function.
  For $p=2$, we prove that nondegenerate stationary points are isolated and that the number of global minima is finite provided that each of them is nondegenerate. For every $1<p<\infty$, we establish uniqueness for the first eigenvalue when $\lambda_1^*\ge\lambda_1(V_0)$ and generic global uniqueness in the sense of Baire category in $L^p(0,1)$.
  A separate section provides examples with at least two global minima for $m=1,2$ in the presence of a sufficiently high finite symmetric barrier. We describe an iteration with frozen eigenfunctions and a local Newton--KKT method with continuation in the spectral data, and state explicitly the limits of their guarantees.
  The final part discusses applications of OISP theory to nonlinear boundary value problems and to applied problems of diagnostics and optimal spectral design of acoustic and electromagnetic resonators.

papers.title: The fractional Faber--Krahn inequality in sharp quantitative form
papers.authors: Michael Goldman, Matteo Novaga, Berardo Ruffini
papers.abstract: We prove that the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the fractional Laplacian satisfies the sharp quantitative Faber--Krahn inequality. This was conjectured by Brasco, Cinti and Vita, who proved the inequality with a sub-optimal exponent. The proof adapts to the non-local setting the level-set argument recently introduced by Guerra, Machado and Ramos for the Laplacian. It is carried out on the horizontal level sets of the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of the torsion function, where the asymmetry appears only as a boundary value at the corner of the extension variables.

papers.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
papers.abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

papers.title: Positive Toeplitz Operators Between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Fock Spaces
papers.authors: Deepak K. Dileep, Xiang Fang, Pham Trong Tien
papers.abstract:
We study positive measure-symbol Toeplitz operators between Gaussian radial--angular mixed-norm Fock spaces throughout the full range of exponents, including infinity. We obtain a complete characterization of boundedness in terms of weighted local masses of the symbol measure, or equivalently in terms of its Gaussian Berezin profile. The criterion separates the transfer of angular integrability from that of radial summability and remains valid in the quasi-Banach and endpoint regimes.
  We further characterize compactness and obtain the corresponding essential-norm estimates through the asymptotic behavior of the same local-mass and Berezin profiles, and determine the mappings involving the large and little outer-endpoint spaces. We also prove an independent characterization of bounded positive Toeplitz sesquilinear forms. The proofs combine atomic recovery, localized Gaussian matrix estimates, and Rademacher extraction.

papers.title: Ergodic treeable equivalence relations are richly ergodic
papers.abstract: We study the density of ergodic subrelations in the canonical Polish space of subequivalence relations of a probability-measure-preserving countable Borel equivalence relation. Our main result establishes rich ergodicity for ergodic treeable equivalence relations. The proof combines a strongly increasing exhaustion with relative ergodic hyperfinite decomposition. As an application, for every $2\leq r<\infty$, we show that the product of the dyadic odometer action of $\mathbb{Z}$ with the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_r$ has a richly ergodic orbit relation, whereas the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{F}_r$ does not. Thus rich ergodicity of a free ergodic action is not determined by the acting group.

papers.title: Second variation of the fractional torsion energy and linear stability of the ball
papers.authors: Michael Goldman, Matteo Novaga, Berardo Ruffini
papers.abstract:
We compute the second shape derivative of the fractional torsion. It is an explicit quadratic form on the boundary, which involves a Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator for half-harmonic functions blowing up at the boundary. We deduce an explicit formula for volume preserving variations on the ball and show
  that as in the local case, the shape Hessian is negative and coercive in \(H^{1/2}\) modulo translations.

papers.title: Skein reduction and stabilization for the odd Khovanov spectra of $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$
papers.abstract: For split links the even Khovanov spectrum is a smash product of the spectra of the pieces; the odd one is not. For $T(2,m)\sqcup T(2,n)$ we show that the odd spectrum is, in each quantum grading, a wedge of spheres and copies of a suspension of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$. Using the skein cofiber sequence at the level of spectra, we prove that for fixed $q-m-n$ the number of these copies is determined by finitely many small links and stabilizes for large $m$ and $n$. The $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ summand of $T(2,3)\sqcup T(2,3)$, due to Sch\"utz and Rajapakse, persists in quantum grading $m+n+8$ for all $m,n\ge3$. We conjecture that the number of copies of $\mathbb{CP}^{2}$ equals the number of copies of $\mathbb{RP}^{2}\wedge\mathbb{RP}^{2}$ in the even spectrum.

papers.title: An Arithmetic Property of Intertwining Operators for Real Reductive Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of complex points of a connected split reductive group defined over ${\mathbb Q}$. We study the standard intertwining operator between representations parabolically induced from essentially tempered cohomological representations of Levi subgroups of maximal parabolic subgroups. Under certain algebraicity, purity, and criticality hypotheses, the operator is holomorphic and invertible at a particular point of evaluation. The relative Lie algebra cohomology of these induced representations is one-dimensional in the lowest nonzero degree. Under prescribed rational generators of these one-dimensional spaces, we show that the intertwining operator is a nonzero rational multiple of a certain product of ratios of local $L$-factors. This is a cohomological version of Langlands's calculation of the Gindikin-Karplevic formula. The main theorem provides a local input for the arithmetic study of special values of Langlands--Shahidi $L$-functions.

papers.title: Division and noetherianity in quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes
papers.authors: Andr\'e Belotto da Silva, Avner Kiro
papers.abstract:
We show that the local rings of quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes need not be Noetherian. More precisely, we construct quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes $C^M$ whose local rings $C^M(\mathbb{R}^d,0)$ are not Noetherian for any $d\geq 2$. Conversely, we exhibit quasianalytic classes whose local rings in dimension two are regular and Noetherian.
  Our approach is based on the problem of exact division: if $f=\varphi g$, where $f\in C^M$, $\varphi$ is real-analytic, and $g\in C^\infty$, under which conditions does it follow that $g\in C^M$? We introduce a quantitative scale-growth condition on the defining weight sequence $M$ and prove that exact division holds in two variables whenever this condition is sufficiently strong relative to the rate at which the nonreal branches of the complex zero set of $\varphi$ approach the real plane. We also construct quasianalytic weight sequences with prescribed growth thresholds and establish corresponding counterexamples to exact division. These yield nonclosed principal ideals and, consequently, non-Noetherian local rings.

papers.title: Extreme values of Artin $L$-functions at $s=1$
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Galois extension of number fields with Galois group $G$. Let $\chi$ be any character on $G$ and $\kappa(\chi)$ be the leading coefficient of the Laurent series of the Artin $L$-function $L(s,\chi)$ at $s=1$. Cho, Lemke Oliver, and Zaman (2026) recently established a conditional bound for $\kappa(\chi)$ assuming GRH for the Dedekind zeta function of $K$. Up to implied constants, we show that the extremal values of these bounds are attained for an infinite family of extensions $K/\mathbb{Q}$ and all irreducible faithful characters $\chi$, provided $G$ is a regular Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$. All characters $\chi$ are permitted without restriction when $G$ is abelian, $A_n, S_n$, or any sporadic group. Our method removes the assumptions of GRH and Artin's holomorphy conjecture from an argument of Duke (2003) by following the strategy of Lemke Oliver, Thorner, and Zaman (2024) on the existence of extremal class numbers for number fields of arbitrary degree. Key ingredients include progress by D\'{e}bes (2017) towards Malle's conjecture, and an Artin $L$-function large sieve by Lemke Oliver and Smith (2024).

papers.title: On separators in $K_t$-minor-free graphs
papers.abstract: This manuscript presents a proof of the Alon--Seymour--Thomas conjecture developed under the author's guidance using ChatGPT 6pro. The author has checked every formula and theorem by hand and used Codex to assist with writing. GPT 6.1 Sol (Max) was also used to check the proof repeatedly and to generate numerous examples for verification. More precisely, for every integer $h\geq3$, every $n$-vertex $K_h$-minor-free graph has a vertex set of size at most $\min{n,21h\sqrt n}$ whose deletion leaves every component with at most $2n/3$ vertices.

papers.title: The Borodin--Kostochka Conjecture for Two Classes of Diamond-Free Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the Borodin--Kostochka conjecture for $(\mathrm{diamond},L_4)$-free graphs and $(\mathrm{diamond},K_5^+)$-free graphs, where $L_4$ is obtained from $K_4$ by attaching a path of length two to one clique vertex, and $K_5^+$ is obtained from $K_5$ by adding a vertex adjacent to exactly one clique vertex. The proof uses structural properties of maximum cliques in diamond-free vertex-critical graphs with $\chi=\Delta$.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff versus Hausdorff distances for Euclidean submanifolds with positive reach
papers.abstract: This paper is about comparing the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between a pair of sets to the Hausdorff distance between the pair. Recent work on this problem has focused on two settings, Riemannian manifolds and metric graphs. Here, we focus on embedded submanifolds of Euclidean space endowed with the Euclidean metric. We prove that when $\mathcal{M}\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact connected embedded submanifold without boundary, with positive reach, and $\mathrm{A}\subset\mathcal{M}$ is a subset that is sufficiently dense in $\mathcal{M}$ with respect to the reach, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathcal{M}$ is bounded below by $1/2$ of the Hausdorff distance between them. We extend this result in two ways. First, we show that the factor $1/2$ can be improved using Jung's theorem. Second, we prove bounds on the Gromov-Hausdorff distance for pairs of subsets of $\mathcal{M}$. When $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ is equipped with the two-dimensional Euclidean metric, the Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ and any sufficiently dense subset of $\mathbb{S}^{1}$ can be expressed explicitly as a function of the Hausdorff distance between the two. We use interleavings between geometric simplicial complexes, nerve lemmas, properties of reach and the nearest-point projection map, and the fundamental class to produce the inequalities for general $\mathcal{M}$. We use the Borsuk-Ulam theorem for $\mathcal{M}=\mathbb{S}^1\subset \mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: Levi-Civita's type theorem for projectively equivalent sub-Riemannian metrics on step 2 distributions
papers.abstract: This paper extends the classical results of Eisenhart (1923) and Levi-Civita (1896) on the classification of pairs of germs of Riemannian metrics with the same geodesics, either as parametrized curves (affine equivalence) or as unparametrized curves (projective equivalence), to sub-Riemannian metrics on arbitrary step 2 distributions: at every stable point in the projective case and at every point in the affine case. This extends the results of Zelenko (2004) for contact and even-contact distributions and the affine result of Lin and Zelenko (2024) for step 2 distributions with ad-surjective Tanaka symbols; our projective result covers the ad-surjective case as well. In the affine case, we prove that if a sub-Riemannian metric admits an affinely equivalent metric that is not constantly proportional to it, then locally it is a product of two sub-Riemannian metrics. In the projective case, we prove the 2019 conjecture of Jean, Maslovskaya, and Zelenko on generalized Levi-Civita pairs; in particular, the distribution admits a product structure, the squares of its components are involutive, and the restrictions of the two metrics to each leaf of the corresponding foliation are conformal to each other under the appropriate pullback. The proof is based on a new graph-theoretic formalism, in which compatible moving frames are represented by the vertices and edges of certain graphs. As a byproduct, we introduce a new discrete invariant of step 2 nilpotent graded Lie algebras, the characteristic tuple. The compatible graphs are used on the open dense set where this tuple is locally constant; the resulting bracket relations are identities between smooth tensors, so they extend by continuity across the points where the tuple jumps. Consequently, our classification holds without any assumption of local constancy of the characteristic tuple.

papers.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $\lambda$-convex bodies
papers.abstract: For a given $\lambda > 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $\lambda$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/\lambda$. We show that among all $\lambda$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $\lambda$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/\lambda$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $\lambda > 0$.

papers.title: Drift-diffusion equations with saturation on $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: We study a class of nonlinear drift--diffusion equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with saturation-type mobilities, not necessarily concave. Under structural assumptions on the mobility and potentials, bounded-domain approximations and local Caccioppoli estimates yield weak solutions for all positive times and an $L^1$-contraction estimate. The same estimates provide local space--time compactness of time translates, whose subsequential limits are weak solutions. Under additional confinement assumptions, uniform mass-tail estimates yield a mass-preserving, free-energy dissipating $C_0$-semigroup of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$-contractions. In this confining setting, every trajectory converges strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to a stationary state with the same mass, and the resulting time-limit operator is an $L^1$-contraction. Under the same assumptions, we also identify the unique global and $L^1$-local minimiser of the free energy at each fixed mass and prove that it is stationary under the semigroup.

papers.title: Perturbations of Truncated Toeplitz operators
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of kernels of finite-rank perturbations of truncated Toeplitz operators. By realizing a perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator on a model space as a suitable matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operator on an enlarged model space, we identify its kernel with a coordinate projection of the kernel of an associated block Toeplitz operator. This realization enables us to transfer the nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of Toeplitz kernels to the perturbed truncated setting. More precisely, for a perturbation of rank at most $n$, we show that the kernel of the perturbed truncated Toeplitz operator is nearly $S^*$-invariant with defect at most $2n+1$. We then extend the method to truncated Toeplitz operators on multiband spaces. In this setting, a perturbation of rank at most $n$ again preserves the finite-defect nearly $S^*$-invariant structure of the kernel, with the explicit upper bound $2n+2$ for the defect.

papers.title: Bulk gap stability and spectral flow for fermions with weak long-range interactions
papers.abstract:
We prove that weak long-range many-body interactions preserve the bulk gap of a free fermion system and that a quasi-local spectral flow transports the free ground state to ground states of the interacting system. Let $\Phi_h$ be a free fermionic interaction, possibly including pairing terms, whose infinite-volume Majorana coefficient operator $h$ has no spectrum in $(-g,g)$, and let $\mathcal V$ be an even self-adjoint many-body interaction. For sufficiently small $|\lambda|$, we construct pure ground states $\omega_{\lambda}$ of the interacting bulk system $\Phi_{\lambda}=\Phi_h+\lambda\mathcal V$ and quasi-local automorphisms $\beta_{0,\lambda}$ such that $\omega_{\lambda}=\omega_0\circ\beta_{0,\lambda}$, where $\omega_0$ is the free ground state of $\Phi_h$. Each $\omega_\lambda$ has a GNS Hamiltonian with gap at least $g-C_*|\lambda| \|\mathcal V\|_*$, where $\|\cdot\|_*$ is the relevant interaction norm.
  Our result allows polynomial decay of both the free coefficients and the many-body interaction. For two-site interactions on a uniformly discrete point set $\Gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a sufficient condition is decay as $(1+|x-y|)^{-\varpi}$ with $\varpi>2d$, for both the hopping and pairing coefficients and the interaction terms. The spectral-flow generator preserves the spatial exponent of the polynomial interaction norm, and its automorphisms satisfy locality bounds at that exponent. If $h$ and $\mathcal V$ have stretched-exponential decay, so does the spectral-flow generator.
  The proof constructs the spectral flow and establishes the gap through an excitation-number comparison, using polynomial propagation bounds for evolved interactions proved in a companion paper.

papers.title: Ricci curvature of semigroup walks on graphs and generator representations
papers.abstract: We present an operator-theoretic framework for the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of (one-parameter families of) random walks generated by positive semigroups on graphs. On a metrically complete graph $(G,d)$ that is $d$-locally finite, we introduce a class of admissible semigroup random walks whose infinitesimal first-order approximation is itself a random walk. We prove that the Ollivier--Ricci curvature of an admissible semigroup random walk is well-defined and completely determined by its first-order approximation. We then establish a variational representation of the curvature of random walks in terms of a notion of the initial-time generator. This representation applies in particular to admissible semigroup random walks. Finally, we use this representation to define an operator-theoretic Ollivier--Ricci curvature for operators acting on spaces of functions over general metric spaces and establish sufficient conditions for well-definedness. This framework contains, in particular, Markovian random walks associated with discrete Laplacians.

papers.title: Characterization of the Tau Spectrum for Eigenvalue Problems
papers.authors: Keaton J. Burns, Ilaria Fontana, Daniel Lecoanet, Geoffrey M. Vasil
papers.abstract: We consider tau approximations of a general eigenvalue problem for a $K$-th-order linear differential operator in one dimension, and we show that the approximate spectrum satisfies a resolvent-based spectral determinant property, which we use to investigate it. More specifically, we analyze the spectral determinant property for a second-order Sturm-Liouville eigenvalue problem approximated using Gegenbauer tau methods. Notably, a quantitative error analysis identifies two values of the Gegenbauer parameter $\gamma$ leading to better approximation properties. These values correspond to Legendre polynomials and their derivatives. Moreover, we discuss the behavior of the largest eigenvalue of the tau approximation. The results are validated with a numerical implementation.

papers.title: Enhanced convergence guarantees of score-based generative models in $\mathcal{W}_2$-distance beyond log-concavity
papers.authors: Xiaoyan Zhang, Chenxu Pang, Xiaojie Wang
papers.abstract: Although score-based generative models (SGMs) have achieved remarkable success in real-world sample generation tasks, it is still far from sufficient to understand them from a mathematical perspective. In this paper, we aim to provide enhanced convergence guarantees for two existing SGMs in $\mathcal{W}_2$-distance beyond log-concavity. More precisely, we develop a novel framework of {\color{black}discretization} error analysis for Euler-Maruyama (EM) and Poisson midpoint (PM) time discretization schemes for SGMs. Under a non-log-concavity condition, we show that $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{d}/\epsilon)$ iterations suffice to approximate the target distributions in $\epsilon$-accuracy for the classical EM-based SGM, considerably improving upon the existing iteration complexity $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d/\epsilon^2)$. Notably, the novel framework of error analysis also enables us to establish an $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{d}/\epsilon^{2/3})$ iteration complexity for the PM-based SGM in $\epsilon$-accuracy, significantly outperforming current state-of-the-art Wasserstein convergence guarantees for SDE-based diffusion samplers.

papers.title: Tangential center problem for planar Hamiltonian differential equations
papers.authors: M. J. Alvarez, J. L. Bravo, L. A. Calderon, S. Rebollo-Perdomo
papers.abstract: Consider a planar Hamiltonian differential equation with a nondegenerate center at the origin. The Tangential Center Problem asks for a characterization of polynomial perturbations for which the center persists at first order. This problem plays a fundamental role in the study of the center-focus problem. We propose an effective algorithmic approach to the Tangential Center Problem for planar polynomial Hamiltonian differential equations. Using this approach, we obtain a complete solution of the quadratic Tangential Center Problem. We further apply it to a non-generic family of cubic Hamiltonian differential equations containing the planar Hamiltonian Lotka--Volterra equation. For a general cubic polynomial perturbation, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the vanishing of the corresponding first Poincar\'e--Pontryagin--Melnikov function and characterize all tangential centers.

papers.title: Matrix Nearness Problems Revisited
papers.abstract: Given a nonempty set of matrices $\mathcal{E} \subseteq \mathbb{C}^{m \times n}$ and a matrix $A \not\in\mathcal{E}$, a matrix nearness problem (or matrix distance problem) consists in finding a matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ that is closest to $A$, in some norm, as well as the corresponding distance. This article is a survey of matrix nearness problems and of numerical algorithms for their solution. We pay special attention to modern related topics, such as Riemannian optimization and pseudospectra, that were not discussed in depth in previous reviews about this topic. Besides collecting known facts, we also prove some foundational results that, at least in the present form, we could not locate in the literature.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness and failure of positivity preservation for doubly critical semilinear heat equations
papers.abstract:
At the Fujita exponent $p=1+2/N$ we construct a strictly positive mild solution of $u_t-\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$ in $\mathbb R^N$ whose initial trace in $L^1$ is zero. In similarity variables the solution approaches a Gaussian profile, and $$\|U(t)\|_1\sim C_N(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},\qquad
  \|U(t)\|_\infty\sim c_Nt^{-N/2}(\log(1/t))^{-N/2},$$ with explicit constants $C_N$ and $c_N$. In particular, uniqueness fails at the borderline logarithmic rate, and the solution lies outside every stronger logarithmic uniqueness class; this answers two questions raised by Miyamoto [J. Evol. Equ. 21 (2021), 151--166, Remark~1.6]. We also prove that, up to time translation, this is the only ancient solution of fixed sign of the rescaled equation that decays in a Gaussian weighted supremum norm. On a bounded smooth domain the whole-space solution can be localized at finitely many interior points, with independently chosen signs, on top of an arbitrary bounded initial datum. The resulting solutions are classical for $t>0$ and continuous at $t=0$ in $L^1$. Consequently, uniqueness fails for every bounded datum, and positivity is lost for every bounded nonnegative datum, $u_0\equiv1$ included. These results provide affirmative answers to Open Problems~3 and~4 posed by Brezis and Cazenave in [J. Anal. Math. 68 (1996), 277--304].

papers.title: Symmetries and exact solutions of stochastic differential equations: the CIR model
papers.abstract: It is well known that in the celebrated Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process for interest rates there exists a critical relation among the model parameters. In the present work, we explain this critical relation by studying the symmetries of the stochastic differential equation and compute the solution of the model using this symmetry. In this way we also recover results of a recent paper where this property has been studied within a broader context by analyzing the relationships among the symmetries of stochastic differential equations and their corresponding forward Kolmogorov equations.

papers.title: Computer-Assisted Results for \(n\)-Sided Non-Transitive Dice Taking Face Values in \([n]\)
papers.abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with \(n\) sides restricted to taking face values in the set \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). We give a computer-assisted proof that \(n=6\) is the smallest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage. For \(n=6\), we identify the two unique non-transitive cycles of length \(6\). We present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that \(n=6\) is the largest \(n\ge3\) which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length \(n\) with uniform and minimal winning advantage.

papers.title: Relativistic collision geometry and global near-vacuum solutions at critical transverse regularity
papers.authors: Xinfeng Hu, Shuangqian Liu, Haoran Peng, Yi Zhou
papers.abstract: We establish global well-posedness near vacuum for the relativistic Boltzmann equation with soft and hard potentials in the range $\gamma\in(-2,1]$. The initial data have critical Besov regularity of order $2/r$ in the transverse spatial variables for an admissible range of $r$ depending on $\gamma$, together with weighted integrability in the longitudinal and momentum variables. The proof combines a fixed-direction div--curl lemma with bilinear collision estimates. In particular, to control the gain term, we combine localization to spherical caps with energy-weighted angular estimates. The key relativistic estimate controls the singularity associated with the first component of the post-collisional relative velocity. These bounds yield the required time decay.

papers.title: Optimal Neural Estimation for High-Dimensional Nonparametric Regression under Multisource Covariate Shift
papers.authors: Chenghao Xu, Haotian Xu, Shivam Kumar, Daren Wang
papers.abstract: We study high-dimensional nonparametric regression under multisource covariate shift, where $\mathrm J$ sources of training data share a common regression function but differ in their covariate distributions, sample sizes, and noise variances. Our goal is to combine these sources to estimate the regression function accurately under a target covariate distribution. We propose an oracle weighted neural estimator and establish its minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors through matching upper and lower bounds. The resulting rate is $\mathsf n_{\rm eff}^{-2p/(2p+K)}$, where $p$ and $K$ denote the effective smoothness and dimension of the regression function, and the effective sample size is \begin{align} \mathsf n_{\rm eff} =\sum_{j=1}^{\mathrm J} \frac{n_j}{(1+\sigma_{\rho,j})\sigma_{\epsilon,j}^{2}}. \nonumber \end{align} Here, $n_j$ is the sample size of source $j$, $\sigma_{\epsilon,j}^{2}$ is its noise variance, and $\sigma_{\rho,j}$ controls the deviation between the covariate distribution of source $j$ and the target covariate distribution. We also develop an adaptive procedure that requires no knowledge of source noise variances or covariate-shift parameters. Under suitable conditions, this procedure attains the oracle minimax rate up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Stationary Structures of the Boussinesq equations
papers.authors: Marc Nualart, Jaemin Park, Javier Pe\~nafiel-Tom\'as
papers.abstract: We investigate the steady configurations supported by the inviscid two-dimensional Boussinesq equations in the periodic channel. We show steady laminar velocity fields (closed non-contractible fluid trajectories) coupled to non-decreasing density stratifications are necessarily stratified shear flows. The direction of density monotonicity along level sets is in fact fundamental: in striking contrast with the Euler equations, we exhibit laminar non-stagnant non-shear stationary solutions in the periodic channel. We also provide distinct flexibility and rigidity results (laminar persistence or appearance of islands for nearby non-shear solutions) close to stratified shear flows according to their stagnation points. As a by-product of our analysis, we establish a uniform Crandall-Rabinowitz bifurcation theorem that might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups. In the two cases of Deligne--Lusztig surfaces of type $A_2$ and ${}^{2}A_2$, we give explicit formulas for the Lefschetz numbers for a generator of the stabilizer of an irreducible component. It follows that the equivariant Euler characteristic of the compactification $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$ is not virtually free as a virtual module over the covering group.

papers.title: Degeneration of (-1)-shifted symplectic stacks and categorification of Donaldson-Thomas invariants
papers.abstract: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. The generic fiber of degeneration family is a $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack. Over the special fiber, the derived restriction to $S$ is derived Lagrangian, and its homotopy fiber product is also $(-1)$-shifted symplectic. Our goal is to relate the categorical DT invariants of the generic fiber moduli, induced by periodic cyclic homology of matrix factorization category of 0-shifted potential functions over such moduli, to that of the special fiber obtained via derived Lagrangian intersection and geometric quantization. This is achieved via construction of a flat Gauss-Manin connection that relates the generic fiber cohomological DT invariants to that of the special fiber. The geometric framework, universal trace diagrams, and fourfold foliation were developed jointly with Jacob Kryczka in arXiv:2510.20325. Here we construct ordinary critical realizations, oriented cyclic-to-bar comparisons, and Gauss-Manin operators, and verify finite specialization in explicit moduli problems. We workout our construction via several explicit examples such as Grassmannians, Relative Hilbert Schemes and moduli space of pure 2 dimensional sheaves with support moving in a fixed linear system of divisors in the ambient threefold.

papers.title: Local determination of low-energy states in gapped fermion systems with weak long-range interactions
papers.abstract:
We consider bulk-gapped fermion systems whose infinite-volume bulk is obtained by adding sufficiently weak even many-body interactions to a free Hamiltonian with spectral gap $g>0$, allowing polynomial spatial decay of both parts. We prove quantitative local determination of low-energy states: whenever another interaction agrees with the bulk interaction inside a finite or infinite region $U$, with bulk terms crossing its boundary unchanged or removed, all its states with excitation energies in $[0,3g/4]$ have local expectations close to those of the bulk ground state deep inside $U$. The error decays with the distance to the complement of $U$, independently of the interaction terms supported outside $U$ and of the chosen low-energy state.
  Quantitative local determination has strong consequences. (i) The bulk interaction has a unique algebraic ground state. (ii) A strong "local perturbations perturb locally" (LPPL) principle holds: arbitrary distant defects change local ground-state expectations only by a spatially decaying error. (iii) Low-energy excitations in finite samples remain localized near the boundary for all times, up to spatially decaying tails, uniformly over arbitrary even boundary terms. (iv) Correlations from deep inside $U$ to outside $U$ are small, with quantitative bounds in terms of spatial separation and distance to $U^c$.
  To prove local determination of low-energy states, we combine quasi-adiabatic transport of the free ground state to the interacting bulk ground state with a new condition, local excitation detectability (LED). A companion paper establishes gap stability and constructs the transport for weak interactions, while we prove LED at sufficiently weak coupling. The abstract theorem is nonperturbative and applies whenever the transport and LED hypotheses hold.

papers.title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
