Using a $C^{++}$ computer program, the authors obtained families of Type-2 isomorphic $C_{n}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = 2,3,5,7 for $n\in\mathbb{N}$ as well as $C_{np^3}(R)$ w.r.t. $m$ = $p$ where $p$ is a prime and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. In this paper, we present the $C^{++}$ program and also a VB program POLY415.EXE which is used to show how Type-1 and Type-2 isomorphisms of a circulant graph take place as well as for checking and finding Type-1 and Type-2 circulant graphs of a given order. This article is the $9^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}.

papers.title: A Study on Type-2 Isomorphic Circulant Graphs: Part 7: $C_{432}(R)$, $C_{6750}(S)$ - each has 2 types of Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs
papers.abstract: In this study, we obtain two families of circulant graphs, (i) family of circulant graphs $C_{432}(R)$, each has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2 as well as $m$ = 3; and (ii) family of circulant graphs $C_{6750}(S)$, each has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 3 as well as $m$ = 5. This article is the $7^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}.

papers.title: Noether symmetries and conservation laws of a class of time-dependent multidimensional nonlinear wave equations
papers.abstract: Conservation laws of a class of time-dependent damped nonlinear multidimensional wave equations are derived by Noether's theorem. For arbitrary nonzero damping coefficient and nonlinear interaction term, its infinitesimal variational symmetries span a Euclidean algebra $\euclid(n)$ of space translations and rotations. They produce conservation of linear and angular momentums. For some specific forms of these two terms symmetry algebra is enlarged to a subalgebra of the conformal algebra $\conf(1,n)$ and in this case more interesting conservation laws are found.

papers.title: Reachability-Augmented Dual Dynamic Programming for Optimal Path Parameterization
papers.authors: Yunan Wang, Jizhou Yan, Chuxiong Hu, Zeyang Li
papers.abstract: Optimal path parameterization (OPP) is a fundamental problem for planning trajectories along a prescribed geometric path under kinodynamic constraints and task-dependent objectives. Among existing OPP works, it remains challenging to simultaneously achieve feasibility guarantees, general-objective optimality certificates, and online-compatible computation in a unified framework, especially for third-order OPP (OPP3) with non-convex constraints. This paper proposes reachability-augmented dual dynamic programming (RDDP), a state-grid-free and objective-aware dynamic programming (DP) framework for OPP. The key idea is to replace the relatively complete recourse assumption used in classical dual DP (DDP) with OPP-specific backward reachable sets, and then generate both value-function cuts and trial trajectories only inside these reachable sets. For convex and non-convex OPP, we prove global optimality and Karush-Kuhn-Tucker convergence of RDDP under OPP-specific conditions, respectively. Efficient instantiations are developed for second-order OPP (OPP2) and OPP3. Experiments show that RDDP achieves objective values comparable to convex-optimization baselines with speedups of approximately 15.3 and 4.9 times over the fastest of 4 tested solvers for OPP2 and OPP3, respectively. RDDP also achieves faster convergence than grid-based DP. Compared with reachability-analysis methods, RDDP retains the reachability mechanism while replacing local maximum-control propagation with value-function-guided control selection, thereby enabling objectives beyond traversal time. In summary, RDDP addresses a key capability gap in OPP by unifying certifiable general-objective optimization, reachability-based feasibility preservation, and online-compatible low-dimensional DP computation in a single framework.

papers.title: Hubbard--Heisenberg Thermodynamic Comparison at Half Filling in a Fixed Staggered Field
papers.abstract:
We study the repulsive Hubbard model at half filling in the canonical ensemble and compare its thermodynamics with the spin-$\frac12$ antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model at superexchange coupling $J_0(U)=4t^2/U$. For fixed hopping $t\ne0$, bounded staggered fields $|h|\le h_0$, and inverse temperatures $\beta J_0(U)\ge\ell_0>0$, we establish a volume-uniform pressure comparison with error $O(U^{-3}+|h|U^{-2})$. On the Heisenberg field scale $h=J_0(U)x$, the error improves to $O(U^{-3})$ for bounded $x$.
  Using the quantum Lee--Yang theorem of Suzuki and Fisher, we obtain a volume-uniform $O(U^{-1})$ comparison of staggered magnetizations on compact positive intervals of the scaled field $x$. By combining a recent fermionic Lee--Yang theorem with analytic interpolation, we improve this estimate to $O(U^{-2}\log U)$ in the thermodynamic limit. The latter analysis also establishes analyticity of the limiting Hubbard pressure at nonzero real fields. The improved comparison extends to vanishing positive fields satisfying $U^{-3}\ll h(U)\ll U^{-1}$, with error $O((1+\log(U^3h(U)))/(U^3h(U)))$. Consequently, sufficiently low-temperature Heisenberg N\'eel order yields a quantitative positive lower bound on the Hubbard staggered magnetization in this regime.
  Furthermore, we prove $O(U^{-2})$ bounds on the double-occupancy and charge-defect densities and the normalized charge-density-wave second moment. At zero staggered field, this decay rate is optimal for both densities, even in the thermodynamic limit. Our approach uses finite-order Schrieffer--Wolff transformations and does not establish spontaneous N\'eel order at fixed finite $U$.

papers.title: Mixed-Precision GPU Acceleration for Large-Scale Minimum Enclosing Ball Problems
papers.abstract: A mixed-precision GPU-oriented optimization framework is developed for computing the minimum enclosing ball of a collection of balls. The approach is built on an equivalent second-order cone programming reformulation and a relative-type inexact proximal augmented Lagrangian method (ripALM), which provides a high-accuracy optimization backbone while solving the inner subproblems only to a progress-dependent relative accuracy. The proximal augmented Lagrangian inherits a constraint-wise separable structure: its objective, gradient, generalized Hessian, and multiplier updates can be efficiently evaluated on GPUs as parallel maps over the input balls followed by reductions. To further improve efficiency, a mixed-precision reduction strategy is introduced. A low-precision ripALM run identifies balls near the approximate boundary, a high-precision ripALM run refines the reduced problem, and a full a posteriori feasibility check detects and reintroduces any violated discarded balls. Thus, low precision is used only for screening and warm starting, while the final feasibility is enforced against the original problem. Experiments on synthetic and real-data instances show that the proposed methods can compute accurate solutions, with GPU execution providing substantial speedups and mixed-precision reduction further reducing running times on most tested instances.

papers.title: Perverse filtration on the cohomology of affine Springer fibers
papers.abstract: We show that the top cohomology of any affine Springer fiber, as a Weyl group representation, contains a large part of the total cohomology of certain Springer fibers. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of a ``perverse filtration'' on the pure part of the cohomology of affine Springer fibers.

papers.title: Long Time Well-posedness for the Benjamin-Ono Equation with Quasi-Periodic Initial Data
papers.abstract:
This paper investigates the long time well-posedness of the Benjamin-Ono (BO) equation with quasi-periodic initial data in analytic space. We demonstrate that the Lax operator of the BO equation exhibits a trivial spectrum, and elucidate the fundamental mathematical obstacles to establishing global well-posedness.
  Furthermore, by employing Tao's gauge transformation in conjunction with the Birkhoff Normal Form method, we extend the lifespan of the solutions to $O(\epsilon^{-3})$.

papers.title: UCP Maps on Finite Toeplitz Systems
papers.abstract: We study unital completely positive (UCP) maps on the finite Toeplitz operator system $\mathcal T_d$ of $d \times d$ Toeplitz matrices. We give an explicit characterization of pure UCP maps on $\mathcal T_d$ taking values in $M_n$ in terms of positive $n\times n$ matrix-valued trigonometric polynomials of degree at most $d-1$. This characterization yields a checkable criterion for deciding whether a given UCP map is pure. As an application, we prove that every pure UCP map on $\mathcal T_d$ has a unique completely positive extension to the generated $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: The symmetric hit problem in four variables: Relative cohits and stabilizer-fixed preimages
papers.authors: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the symmetric hit problem in four variables by analyzing the relative cohit space, defined as the kernel of the inclusion-induced map from symmetric to ordinary cohits. We establish that this relative space is isomorphic to a kernel in the first group cohomology of the permutation group and, equivalently, to an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel for the general linear group, equipped with a canonical action of the normalizer quotient. We use explicit Lucas--Cartan identities to construct unconditional fixed Steenrod preimages for nontrivial stabilizers, resolving infinite families of monomials strictly above the minimal-spike weight. Using the ordinary and symmetric Kameko isomorphisms, we reduce the determination of complete bases in two generic degree families to exact calculations in degrees one, three, six, ten, and sixteen. The relative space first becomes nonzero in degree fifteen, where it is one-dimensional, and it is an indecomposable two-dimensional normalizer module in degree eighteen. In the family $5\cdot2^t-4$, the symmetric cohit dimension stabilizes at six and the relative dimension at one for $t\geq2$; in the family $7\cdot2^t-4$, they are four and zero for $t\geq1$. We give complete bases by explicit exponent formulas and prove Janfada's monomial implication [7, Conjecture 1] in every degree of both families. We extend the known optimal bound for ordinary Kameko isomorphisms to every permutation-invariant cohit space, prove its optimality there, and transport the entire symmetric hit basis by a direct-sum formula.

papers.title: A novel class of high-order uniformly accurate exponential integrators with local linear extension for the charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic field
papers.authors: Lina Wang, Bin Wang, Beibei Zhu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel class of high-order uniformly accurate exponential integrators for charged-particle dynamics under strong magnetic field. The small parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll 1$ induces rapid temporal oscillations, rendering traditional numerical methods prohibitively expensive due to severe step-size restrictions. To address this issue, a linearization technology that introduces auxiliary polynomial variables is employed to recast the original charged-particle dynamics as a higher-dimensional system. Classical exponential integrators are subsequently applied to this augmented formulation, which inherently carries richer structural information, thereby yielding a family of uniformly accurate exponential integrators that can reach arbitrarily high order without requiring any order conditions. For strong magnetic fields under the maximal-ordering scaling, we rigorously establish through algebraic techniques that the schemes with auxiliary polynomial variables of degree $k\geq2$ achieve an improved position error bound of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+1}h,\varepsilon h^{k+1}\})$ and a uniform velocity error bound of $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k}h,h^{k+1}\})$, where $h$ denotes the time-step size. Under the additional condition that the magnetic field gradient vanishes at the origin, these bounds sharpen to $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+2},\varepsilon h^{k+1}\})$ and $\mathcal{O}(\min\{\varepsilon^{k+1},h^{k+1}\})$ for the position and velocity, respectively, for $k\geq1$. The same sharper bounds hold for constant strong magnetic fields. Numerical experiments confirm the advantages of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Branch and Price for Railway Crew Scheduling: Benchmark Instances and Computational Study
papers.abstract: Railway crew scheduling consists of assigning a set of tasks to crew members in the form of feasible duties so as to minimise costs, and is one of the key planning problems faced by railway operators. While column generation is the dominant solution method, literature on exact branch-and-price approaches is scarce. Moreover, few publicly available benchmark instances exist. We conduct a systematic computational study of branch and price for railway crew scheduling, evaluating the contribution of branching rules, primal heuristics, and reduced cost fixing. To this end, we introduce a novel library of 100 benchmark instances, ranging in size from 90 to 3,016 tasks, each provided in a single-depot and a multi-depot variant. The instances are generated by mimicking the railway planning process, validated against data from Netherlands Railways, and publicly available with best known solutions and a solution checker. We report average optimality gaps below 1% across all instance sizes, driven primarily by the strong performance of primal heuristics, whereas branching and reduced cost fixing contribute little to closing the gap. Branch and price also outperforms a multi-commodity flow formulation, which fails to find a feasible solution on many of the smallest instances. Our findings provide support for the popularity of column generation-based primal heuristics, and show that improving the dual bound remains the main challenge for exact methods in railway crew scheduling.

papers.title: Domination in Johnson graphs J(n, 3) for odd n
papers.abstract: In 2025 Cornet, Dravec, and Torres determined the domination number $\gamma(J(n,3))$ of the Johnson graph for every even $n \ge 6$, expressing it as a closed form $\phi_n$ in terms of Fort-Hedlund covering numbers, and conjectured the same value for odd $n$. We prove this conjecture: $\gamma(J(n,3)) = \phi_n$ for every odd $n \ge 7$. A dominating set of $J(n,3)$ is the same as a lotto design $\mathrm{LD}(n,3,3,2)$, and the lotto numbers $L(n,3,3,2)$, and hence $\gamma(J(n,3))$, were already determined for every $n$ by Bate (1978) and by Brouwer (1981). The contribution of this paper is therefore a new proof of the odd case, carried out within the bijective framework of Cornet, Dravec, and Torres.

papers.title: Dual Gauss--Legendre polynomials
papers.abstract: We define and investigate two families of dual polynomials associated with the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, which have recently found interesting applications in computer graphics. Using the presented results, one can derive representations of the Gauss--Legendre polynomials, construct the dual bases for Lagrange bases and solve certain approximation problems arising, for example, in CAGD.

papers.title: Continuous stochastic flows driven by white noise and their duals
papers.abstract: We study a class of continuous stochastic flows driven by a space-time white noise and characterize their dual flows by explicit stochastic differential equations. A key ingredient of the proof is the convergence of solutions under coefficient approximations. As an application, we derive the dual flows in two illustrative examples, the squared Bessel flow and the Jacobi flow. We also introduce a new model of polynomially self-repelling (PSR) flow and show that it enjoys a self-duality property.

papers.title: The Ornstein$-$Uhlenbeck process on $\mathscr P_2$ with a volatility operator
papers.abstract: We analyze diffusion processes ${(\mu_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ on the $2$-Wasserstein space $\mathscr P_2$ over $\mathbb R^d$, which can be classified as Ornstein--Uhlenbeck processes by means of their Fukushima decomposition. Characteristically for this class, $ | \mu_t|_2^2-|\mu_0|_2^2-2ct+2\int_0 ^t|\mu_s|_2^2\,d s,\, t\geq 0,$ is a martingale, where $c\in(0,\infty)$ is a constant and $|\mu_t|_2:=(\int_{\mathbb R^d}x^{\text{T}} x\mu_t(d x ))^{1/2}$ denotes the second moment. Making a particular choice from this class, we obtain a process ${(\mu_t)}_{t\geq 0}$ such that all moments exist and ${\mu_t(\theta)}-{\mu_0(\theta)}-\int_0 ^t\mu_s\big(\Delta \theta-\langle \text{id}_{\mathbb R^d},\nabla \theta\rangle\big)d s$, $t\geq 0$, is a martingale for each multivariate polynomial $\theta:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$.

papers.title: Anti-Zariski pairs
papers.abstract: In 1929, O. Zariski found a pair of complex plane algebraic curves of the same degree and with the same collection of singularities, but embedded into the plane in a topologically different way. Accordingly, such curves belong to different components of the equisingular family. This phenomenon has been intensively studied till now. In this note, we propose a different insight on this subject: Two curves $C',C''\subset\PP^2$ form an {\it anti-Zariski pair}, if $(\PP^2,C')$ and $(\PP^2,C'')$ are homeomorhic, but $C'$ and $C''$ belong to different components of the equisingular family. We exhibit examples of anti-Zariski pairs and discuss related issues.

papers.title: A study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs. Part 8: Isomorphism series, digraph and graph of $C_n(R)$
papers.abstract: This article is the $8^{th}$ part of a detailed study on Type-2 isomorphic circulant graphs having ten parts \cite{v2-1}-\cite{v2-10}. In this study, we define {\em isomorphic set}, {\em isomorphism series}, {\em isomorphism digraph} or {\em isomorphism diagram} $\mathcal{D}$ and {\em isomorphism graph} $\mathcal{G}$ of circulant graphs and obtain these corresponding to $C_{16}(R)$, $C_{27}(S)$ and $C_{54}(1,3,17,19)$ and present the isomorphism digraph and the isomorphism graph of $C_{432}(T)$ which has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 2,3 and of $C_{6750}(U)$ which has isomorphic circulant graphs of Type-2 w.r.t. $m$ = 3,5 where $T$ = $\{16, 27, 48, 54, 128, 160, 189\}$ and $U$ = $\{135, 243, 250, 750, 1107, 1593, 2000, 2457, 2500, 2943\}$. We also define {\em diameter of isomorphic set} of $C_n(R)$ and {\em isomorphic distance} between any two circulant graphs. We find that the order of isomorphic sets of $C_{432}(T)$ and $C_{6750}(U)$ are 36 and 450 and their diameters are 3 and 3, respectively.

papers.title: Singular stationary Navier-Stokes flows: examples and stability
papers.abstract: Landau solutions, when oriented along the vertical axis, represent a one parameter family of exact, self-similar, axisymmetric, swirl-free solutions to the 3D stationary Navier-Stokes equations forced by an upward facing point-source of momentum at the origin. They have an isolated singularity at the origin. Other singular steady state solutions can be derived from a similar framework. Some of these variants have been proposed as models for physical scenarios. For example, a solution first found by Squire has been proposed as a model of a fluid entrained to a radially discharging surface layer of oil. Another, Serrin's swirling vortex, exhibits qualitative features shared with some tornadoes, like a two-cell structure consisting of a central downdraft and peripheral updraft as well as swirl. The first objective of this paper is to provide a detailed analysis of these and other examples, especially when boundaries are present. In this direction we find several new, physically motivated classes of solutions and identify new connections between the physics literature and the mathematics literature. Many of these examples are formulated on the half-space, but much of the mathematical literature on singular steady-state solutions is for $\mathbb{R}^3$. The second objective of this paper is to establish asymptotic stability for many of these solutions by formulating the problem in domains with boundaries. Our most general result in this direction uses a new approach to asymptotic stability that is based on eventual regularity. In a different direction, we prove that a class of singular steady-state solutions motivated by Serrin's swirling vortex are stable under certain axisymmetric perturbations. This requires a novel observation because these ``Type III'' solutions are too singular to be directly amenable to existing approaches.

papers.title: Rank-Two Drinfeld Modules over Elliptic Coordinate Rings
papers.authors: Chuangqiang Hu, Ze-Dong Huang, Chang-An Zhao
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathbf A}$ be the affine coordinate ring of $E\setminus\{\infty\}$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\infty$ is rational. We solve the rank-two case of the open problem of explicitly classifying sign-normalized Drinfeld ${\mathbf A}$-modules in generic characteristic with a fixed determinant motive; the classification for rank greater than two remains open. Outside an explicit exceptional locus, the rank-two Drinfeld modules are parametrized by the open modular curve $Y^{q+1}=\pi(X)$ with $Y\neq0$. The polynomial $\pi$ is squarefree, and the smooth projective completion of this curve has genus $q^2$. The roots of $\pi$ split into two types. Above roots of the first type, all coefficient functions extend regularly, and their extensions yield exactly the exceptional modules. Roots of the second type correspond to cusps of the modular curve; above these roots, the coefficient family has poles.

papers.title: Equilibria in Motion: Stability, Tracking, and Convergence
papers.abstract: {We study nonautonomous systems whose equilibrium sets are nonisolated and move with time. Their motion is measured on each ball by a localized Attouch--Wets distance, which yields an equilibrium speed that may depend on the radius. The distance from a trajectory to the current equilibrium set is estimated in two ways: through a composite Lyapunov function compared with a power of this distance, and, without any Lyapunov function, through a decay condition on the frozen vector fields. In the first setting, we prove practical stability, and Lyapunov stability when the dissipation has no residual, a case that forces the equilibrium sets to be nested. In the second, we obtain, in the region where the decay condition holds, an explicit tracking estimate driven by the equilibrium speed and the inputs, and we prove asymptotic tracking whenever their averages over unit time intervals vanish, a condition that cannot be weakened among conditions on the speed alone. We also derive input-to-state stability bounds and explicit convergence rates. When the equilibrium speeds are integrable, the equilibrium sets converge in the Attouch--Wets sense to a limiting set at an explicit rate. If, moreover, the velocity is bounded by a multiple of the distance to the current equilibrium set, every trajectory remaining in the region considered has finite length and converges to a point of the limiting set; for a fixed equilibrium set, this yields semistability. The results are illustrated on a scalar example and on resource-allocation models with time-varying demand and with rotating weights.

papers.title: Hypocoercivity-preserving space-time Galerkin methods for kinetic Fokker-Planck equations
papers.abstract: We design and analyse a family of hypocoercivity-preserving fully discrete Galerkin methods for the kinetic Fokker--Planck (kFP) equations, a class of evolution partial differential equations (PDE) with \emph{degenerate} diffusion. The key idea in the method design is to mimic the framework of enhanced quadratic forms of Villani \cite{villani} to obtain a coercive bilinear form in a sufficiently strong exponentially weighted norm admitting a spectral gap/Poincar\'{e} inequality, despite the degeneracy. The problem is posed as a fourth-order evolution PDE on the whole space $\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^d$. The spatial discretization employs continuous piecewise polynomial approximation spaces on simplicial and/or box-type meshes comprising finite and infinite elements. Nonconformity is treated by constructing appropriate numerical fluxes in the spirit of $C^0$-interior penalty ($C^0$-IP) methods for fourth-order elliptic problems. The proof of coercivity requires new trace inverse inequalities for exponentially weighted norms on $d$-dimensional simplicial and box-type domains, and prismatic domains with infinite length. We prove these inequalities for a variety of exponential weights. Once coercivity is established, exponential convergence to equilibrium follows from an exponentially weighted Poincar\'{e} inequality. A fully discrete extension is obtained by coupling the spatial discretization with an $hp$-version discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping scheme. Exponential convergence to equilibrium is also proven for the fully discrete scheme. The proposed methods preserve total mass and exhibit \emph{provably} exponential convergence to equilibrium, a manifestation of `numerical hypocoercivity,' making them well suited for long-time kFP simulations. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical results and investigate the convergence behaviour of the proposed method.

papers.title: Montel's theorem and tautness in calibrated geometry
papers.authors: Anton Iliashenko, Spiro Karigiannis, Jesse Madnick
papers.abstract: We relate the hyperbolicity of a calibrated manifold $(X, \phi)$ to the analytic properties of the space of Smith immersions $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ from the Poincare $k$-ball into $X$. In particular, we establish the following calibrated analogue of a theorem of Royden: if $X$ is $\phi$-saturated, then $R_\phi$- and $K_\phi$-hyperbolicity coincide, and either implies the equicontinuity of $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ with respect to the $\phi$-distance. This yields a Montel theorem for compact $\phi$-saturated calibrated manifolds as an immediate corollary. Our primary technical tool is a new Schwarz lemma for Smith immersions from $B^k$ into $X$, which is of independent interest. In a similar spirit, we also prove a calibrated analogue of Kiernan's theorem to the effect that the $K_\phi$-hyperbolicity of $X$ is almost equivalent to $\mathrm{SmIm}(B^k, X)$ being a normal family. Finally, we prove that bounded domains in flat euclidean space are $R_\phi$-hyperbolic for any calibration $\phi$, and we investigate the hyperbolicity of products and discrete quotients.

papers.title: Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces
papers.authors: Shin-ichi Ohta, Marco Rehmeier, Kohei Suzuki
papers.abstract:
A Minkowski normed space is the Euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of Finsler manifolds.
  We construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear Finsler heat equation in Minkowski normed spaces.
  This process is constructed as a solution to a singular McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear Markov process in the sense of McKean.
  We show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime.
  Since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard Brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{Brownian motion in Minkowski normed spaces.}
  Furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever Minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard Bessel process.
  To the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in Finslerian spaces.

papers.title: Spectrum of Complete K\"ahler Metrics on Bounded Hyperconvex Domains
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^{n}$ be a bounded domain, and let $\rho:\Omega\to[-1,0)$ be a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion function. We consider the logarithmic potential $g=-\log(-\rho)$ and the associated complete K\"ahler metric $\omega=dd^{c} g$. We prove that if $\rho$ satisfies the finite weighted Monge-Amp\`ere mass condition with weight $(-\rho)^{\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, then the spectrum and the essential spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator of $(\Omega,\omega)$ both coincide with $[n^{2},\infty)$. In particular, the bottom of the spectrum satisfies $\lambda_{0}(\Delta_{\omega},\Omega)=n^{2}$, and $n^{2}$ is not an $L^{2}$-eigenvalue. For each $\alpha > \frac{n}{2}$, we set $f=(-\rho)^{\alpha}$ and prove that $f$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(\Omega,\omega)$ if and only if the Monge-Amp\`ere mass of $\rho$ weighted by $(-\rho)^{2\alpha-n}$ is finite. The integral identities underlying this equivalence, applied to the complex powers $(-\rho)^{\alpha+it}$, give, after normalization, a singular Weyl sequence at every $n^{2}+4t^{2}$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$, as $\alpha\downarrow\frac{n}{2}$. Combining our theorem with Cegrell's finite-mass exhaustion theorem, we obtain a complete K\"ahler metric with spectrum and essential spectrum equal to $[n^{2},\infty)$ on every bounded hyperconvex domain.

papers.title: Coloring t-perfect graphs with fewer colors
papers.abstract:
Recently, Chudnovsky, Cook, Davies, Oum, and Tan obtained the first finite bound on the chromatic number of t-perfect graphs, showing that they are 199053-colorable. We improve this bound to 130 by refining their proof.
  The original proof establishes that every graph with large odd girth and large chromatic number contains a certain structure called an r-arithmetic rope, and that its existence in a certain leveling of a graph with large odd girth would imply an odd wheel as a t-minor, a known obstruction to t-perfectness. While their technique requires a lower bound on the chromatic number that is exponential in r, we show that the existence of an r-arithmetic rope can already be guaranteed under a linear bound. Using a slightly weakened notion of arithmetic ropes allows us to reduce the bound even further.

papers.title: Strictly stable solutions in uniformly convex planar domains may have nonconvex superlevel sets
papers.abstract: We construct smooth, uniformly convex planar domains that admit minimal, strictly stable solutions of a semilinear Dirichlet problem whose superlevel sets are nonetheless nonconvex. The class of admissible nonlinearities includes, in particular, two prototypical cases: the Gelfand-type nonlinearity $e^u$ and the family of shifted power-type nonlinearities $(a+u)^p$, where $a>0$ and $p>1$. By applying the elementary scaling properties of the Dirichlet problem, we also show that the same lack of convexity of superlevel sets holds for the corresponding parameter-dependent equations. These results provide a negative answer to a question posed by Brezis, who inquired whether the stability of a solution necessarily entails quasiconcavity for these prototypical stable configurations.

papers.title: Equation-Free Screening of Mittag-Leffler-Compatible Dynamics from Scalar Time Series via kNN Multi-Horizon Profiles
papers.authors: N'Gbo N'Gbo, Andrei Velichko, Bruno Carpentieri
papers.abstract: We study an equation-free screen for finite-window Mittag-Leffler compatibility, in which multihorizon relaxation profiles are constructed out of sample by k-nearest-neighbor prediction from ensembles of scalar trajectories and compared with candidate temporal laws. The screen assesses compatibility, not the generating mechanism. In a matched, noise-free calibration, it reproduces the generating Mittag-Leffler behavior to numerical precision, while relaxation-rate heterogeneity shifts the fitted Mittag-Leffler order toward lower values. For noise-free classical distributed-rate ensembles, a Mittag-Leffler preference over a single exponential disappears when a biexponential alternative is included. Under observational noise, this recovery is incomplete: with three candidate families, the Mittag-Leffler law is still selected in 60% of runs for a classical ensemble, against 72% for a fractional reference. In the tested noise-free settings, simpler profile constructions reproduce the screening decisions, whereas kNN predicts individual trajectories far more accurately than a constant predictor. The screening interpretation of a single-record example, initially investigated as a chaotic test case, is withdrawn as evidence about the continuous system after numerical verification revealed a nonrobust simulated regime. Mittag-Leffler compatibility is therefore a comparative, condition-dependent screening outcome, not identification of fractional origin.

papers.title: The point-cross dimension
papers.abstract: Two transverse segments have local Hausdorff and upper box dimension one at their crossing, although they carry two independent tangent directions. We define the Point-Cross Dimension by assigning each tangent line the largest local upper box dimension captured by intersection with a regular \(C^1\) curve in that direction, then taking the supremum of their sums over finite independent families of tangent lines. Every Bouligand direction admits such a recurrent curve. The resulting profile is invariant under closure and covariant under local \(C^1\)-diffeomorphisms. Each directional weight is attained, and the profile is upper semicontinuous. An integral representation by ranks of weight superlevel sets gives submodularity and, together with projection bounds, exact Cartesian-product additivity. Germs with the same projective tangent support, local upper box dimension, and rank of segment directions can have different Point-Cross Dimensions. Further computations give exact directional profiles for chirps and the Point-Cross Dimension of a self-affine carpet. Finally, approximation of a ray with error \(O(t^d)\), for \(d>1\), forces directional weight at least \(1-1/d\), and this bound is sharp.

papers.title: On two counterexamples in the geometry of numbers
papers.abstract:
We give counterexamples to two optimization problems in dimensions eight and nine.
  1. The Cartesian-product problem posed by Cassels for critical determinants and later formulated by Zong for lattice packings and for packings allowing translations but not rotations: whether the corresponding product inequalities are always equalities. The counterexample also disproves the natural product formula for unrestricted congruent packings.
  2. A question raised by Sarnak and formulated as a conjecture in Chiu: whether, among unit-volume flat tori, height is minimized by a lattice maximizing the length of its shortest nonzero vector.

papers.title: Real and complex stability radii for a class of transport networks
papers.authors: Anthony Hastir, Birgit Jacob, Hannes Wagener
papers.abstract: We characterize stability and its robustness for a class of boundary controlled, boundary observed hyperbolic partial differential equations. In particular, we show that asymptotic and exponential stability coincide for this class. Furthermore, we introduce the real and complex stability radii for which we give explicit formulas. In addition, we consider the dual system and its application to controllability and observability. Our main results are illustrated with two examples.

papers.title: The exact region determined by Blomqvist's beta, Spearman's footrule and Kendall's tau
papers.authors: Liljana Ferbar Tratar, Damjana Kokol Bukov\v{s}ek, Bla\v{z} Moj\v{s}kerc, Jacob Israel Orenday Lares, Marcus Rockel, Nik Stopar
papers.abstract: We determine the exact region $\Omega_{\beta,\phi,\tau}= \{(\beta(C),\phi(C),\tau(C))\mid C\in\mathcal{C}\}$ of possible joint values of Blomqvist's beta, Spearman's footrule and Kendall's tau over the class $\mathcal{C}$ of all bivariate copulas. The region consists precisely of all triples $(\beta,\phi,\tau)$ satisfying $-1\le \beta\le 1$, $\frac{3}{16}(1+\beta)^2-\frac12\le \phi\le 1-\frac38(1-\beta)^2$ and $\frac43 \phi-\frac13\le \tau\le \frac23 \phi+\frac13$. In other words, the known exact $(\beta,\phi)$- and $(\phi,\tau)$-regions already characterize the joint region, so that, once the value of Spearman's footrule is fixed, Blomqvist's beta imposes no additional restriction on the possible values of Kendall's tau. The proof is constructive: two $2$-parameter families of shuffles of $M$ realize all the points in $\Omega_{\beta,\phi,\tau}$ with $\phi = \frac{3}{16}(1+\beta)^2-\frac12$, and ordinal sums spread realizations of these two families over the whole region $\Omega_{\beta,\phi,\tau}$.

papers.title: Right $q$-Radial Calculus at Integral Superdimension
papers.authors: Juan Bory-Reyes, Baruch Schneider, Diana Barseghyan Schneiderov\'a, Yifan Zhang
papers.abstract: We study the intrinsic right $q$-radial derivative at integral superdimension $M=m-2n$, using an independent formal parameter $Q$ before the specialisation $Q=q^M$. The exterior-blade action carries the parity factor $(-1)^{|I|}$, and the corresponding Fischer theory uses right multiplication. We establish finite-support compatibility, faithful coordinate realisations in a sufficient finite-block range, and localised Green and determinant-localised Fischer decompositions. For one vector, we determine the kernel and cokernel explicitly, including the additional singular monomial and missing image exactly when $M\in-2\mathbb N_0$. In degree zero the right Fischer operator is diagonal on auxiliary exterior blades, with eigenvalue $[M-p]_q+p$ at nonempty support rank $p$. For positive integral $M$, resonances in $0<q<1$ occur exactly at ranks $p>M$: each rank has one simple resonance, these values increase strictly with $p$, and the corresponding kernels and singular right-monogenic elements are explicit. The two-vector Fischer determinant is nonzero for positive $M$ and $0<q<1$.

papers.title: Quantum XYZ Stabilizer Codes
papers.authors: Alessio Baldelli, Davide Orsucci, Francisco L\'azaro, Massimo Battaglioni
papers.abstract: Stabilizer codes are often constructed within the Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) framework, where two mutually orthogonal binary classical codes define $X$ and $Z$-type stabilizer generators. While this structure is algebraically convenient, additional non-CSS constraints may help suppress low-weight logical operators and improve decoding performance in the finite-length regime. We thus introduce quantum XYZ stabilizer codes, whose parity-check matrix (PCM) is built from three pairwise orthogonal binary PCMs associated with $X$-, $Y$-, and $Z$-type stabilizer generators. A nontrivial point is that an XYZ code instance is not automatically genuinely non-CSS: the same stabilizer group may admit a CSS generating set. We characterize this collapse, obtaining algebraic and rank conditions for deciding when the $Y$-type checks are redundant and when they define genuinely non-CSS stabilizer constraints. We also derive upper and lower bounds on the quantum minimum distance, including bounds for mixed Pauli logical operators. The novel framework includes a known non-CSS topological code, namely the XYZ$^2$ hexagonal code, and yields also sparse finite-length quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) constructions from intersecting-subset and quasi-dyadic code families. Simulations under depolarizing code-capacity noise and quaternary belief propagation decoding show that the proposed XYZ qLDPC instances can outperform representative CSS qLDPC instances with similar finite-length parameters.

papers.title: On the Role of Normalization in Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding for 1-bit Compressed Sensing
papers.abstract: Binary Iterative Hard Thresholding (BIHT) is a simple, yet effective, greedy method for recovering a sparse vector from one-bit sign measurements. In its original form, BIHT performs a ``gradient-descent'' step, followed by hard thresholding. A convergence analysis of this algorithm was left open in the introductory work of Jacques, Laska, Boufounos, and Baraniuk [IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory (2013)] and has remained unresolved for over a decade, with subsequent sharp analyses studying a normalized variant instead, that additionally projects every iterate onto the unit sphere. This paper resolves that gap and characterizes when per-iterate normalization is algorithmically necessary. In the noiseless setting, we prove a universal, sample-optimal convergence theorem for the original BIHT algorithm. Specifically, with $\widetilde O(s/\epsilon)$ measurements, a deterministic, computable finite-time iterate has directional error at most $\epsilon$, simultaneously for every $s$-sparse unit vector. This matches the optimal sample dependence achieved by normalized BIHT in prior work. Under sign corruptions, we prove a sharp separation. If at most a $\tau$ fraction of signs are flipped adversarially, then BIHT, without per-iterate normalization, still reaches the robust error floor at an early iterate with a matching $\widetilde O(s/\epsilon)$ sample complexity rate as its normalized variant. This recovery, however, is not stable. We prove a scalar lower bound showing that any nontrivial corruption pattern, even one that involves only one flipped sign together with one clean sign, forces the iterates to oscillate indefinitely. Consequently, no general last-iterate convergence theorem can hold for BIHT under sign corruptions, while its normalized surrogate provably escapes this instance.

papers.title: A family of mixed-mixed strongly conservative finite element methods for Biot's model of consolidation
papers.authors: Qingguo Hong, Johannes Kraus, Maria Lymbery
papers.abstract: We consider a four-field formulation of Biot's quasi-static model of consolidation with the (effective) elastic stress, the solid displacement, the fluid flux and the fluid pressure as unknown physical quantities of interest. The weak form of this system composed of the momentum and mass balance equations complemented by the stress-strain relation and Darcy's law yields a two-fold perturbed saddle-point problem. Its well-posedness is proven for a natural choice of inifinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, where the displacement-flux pair is sought in a novel Hilbert space. Next, based on recent works on $H(\rm div \, \rm div)$-conforming finite elements, we propose a family of mixed-mixed finite element methods that preserve the angular momentum as well as the fluid mass balance pointwise, i.e., in a strong sense. We prove the well-posedness of the arising discrete problem and establish optimal a priori error estimates for the related family of fully conservative mixed-mixed finite element methods.

papers.title: On dualizability and invertibility in the higher Morita category
papers.authors: Claudia Scheimbauer, Pelle Steffens, William Stewart
papers.abstract:
We prove a conjecture of Lurie characterizing $(n+1)$-dualizability in higher Morita categories of $\mathbb{E}_n$-algebras in terms of dualizability over certain factorization homologies. A key ingredient is a higher Morita category based on the recently developed framework of pointless factorization algebras of Karlsson and the first author. We also verify an invertibility conjecture of Brochier--Jordan--Safranov--Snyder as an immediate corollary of our main result.
  Moreover, we prove a relative version of the dualizability conjecture, yielding a new criterion for relative/twisted field theories. We give some examples, including Dirichlet and Neumann relative theories.

papers.title: Obstructions to embedding singular curves in toric varieties
papers.authors: Maya Banks, Izzet Coskun, Kevin Tucker
papers.abstract: For every integer $d \geq 2$, we show that there exists an irreducible, reduced curve which embeds in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but in no projective normal toric variety of dimension less than $d$. In particular, there exist reduced irreducible curves that embed in $\mathbb{P}^d$ but do not embed in any weighted projective space of dimension less than $d$.

papers.title: Free energy and spectral edge of the SYK model
papers.abstract: Consider the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model with $N$ Majorana fermions and interaction order $q$. For even $4\leq q\ll \sqrt{N}$, we present a microscopic framework that determines the free energy limit at every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$. In particular, this gives the first rigorous derivation of the Schwinger-Dyson thermodynamics of the model. For all even $q\in \{4,6,...,N-4\}$, we further determine the asymptotic location of the largest eigenvalue, which answers a question posed by Feng-Tian-Wei \cite{FengTianWei1}. Consequently, we obtained the free energy limit along every sequence $\beta\equiv \beta_N\to\infty$.

papers.title: Archimedean Modular Symbols for Rankin-Selberg Convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$
papers.abstract: We explicit calculate the archimedean modular symbol for Rankin-Selberg convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$, for all generic cohomological representations.

papers.title: A note on application of mean-field limit to non-exchangeable non-conservative systems
papers.abstract: In this paper we apply the newly developed theory of extended graphons to a certain class of non-exchangeable, non-conservative problems. We establish the mean-field limit by proving the convergence of the associated generalized weighted empirical measures.

papers.title: Affine Extension of the Free-Particle--Oscillator--Inverted-Oscillator Triangle
papers.abstract: We study the one-dimensional linear-potential system as an affine extension of the conformal triangle formed by the free particle, harmonic oscillator (HO) and inverted harmonic oscillator (IHO). Unlike these homogeneous quadratic Hamiltonians in the $sl(2,\mathbb R)$ sector, the linear-potential Hamiltonian involves the Heisenberg ideal of the Schr\"odinger algebra. Its direct relation to the free particle is a regular accelerated-frame transformation, developed here at the levels of the classical action, canonical transformation, wave-function intertwiner and propagator; its HO and IHO realizations instead arise through singular displaced-oscillator limits. The Airy energy eigenstates follow from a cubic-phase transform of free-particle momentum eigenstates, from condensation of highly excited harmonic-oscillator levels, and from the limit of a subdominant parabolic-cylinder scattering branch of the inverted oscillator. We also develop a planar extension in homogeneous crossed electric and magnetic fields, where uniform acceleration generates the electric interaction, while uniform rotation produces the Landau coupling and the centrifugal inverted-oscillator term; the guiding-center dynamics yields the Hall drift.

papers.title: Multiplier obstructions for Legendre pairs of length 333
papers.authors: Arthur F. Ramos, David B. Hulak, Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz
papers.abstract: A Legendre pair of length 333 would yield a Hadamard matrix of order 668, the smallest order presently unresolved by the Hadamard conjecture. We study the structured case in which both sequences are fixed by a common subgroup $H\leq(\mathbb Z/333\mathbb Z)^\times$ acting by coordinate multiplication. We prove that such a pair can exist only when $|H|\leq 6$. After a mod-3 compression reduces the problem to an order-108 kernel, there are exactly 30 subgroups. We exclude 21 of them, including all 19 subgroups of order at least 9. The final order-9 subgroup is eliminated analytically: its orbit structure restricts the 9-compressed entries to $\{\pm1,\pm17,\pm19,\pm35,\pm37\}$; the Legendre equations force a $+17,-17$ pair in one compressed sequence, and a single-shift autocorrelation bound then contradicts the required compressed correlation. The remaining exclusions use full-image compression, a row-sum congruence, exact meet-in-the-middle enumeration, and proof-carrying pseudo-Boolean encodings. The solver-assisted cases are accompanied by independently checked DRAT proofs or direct arithmetic certificates. The result constrains fixed common-multiplier symmetry only; the unrestricted existence problems remain open.

papers.title: The mean-field limit of non-exchangeable particle systems with non-conservative dynamics and adaptive weights
papers.abstract: In the paper we introduce vector-valued dynamic extended graphons in order to obtain the mean-filed limit for certain class of problems with adaptive weights. We impose fairly general assumptions on the matrix of initial connections, which allows us to cover the case of sparse graphs.

papers.title: Analysis and structure-preserving discretization of the Heat-GLM system
papers.authors: Firas Dhaouadi, Laura R\'io-Mart\'in, Michael Dumbser
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a prototype hyperbolic system arising from the coupling of Generalized-Lagrangian-Multiplier (GLM) curl-cleaning with linear acoustics. We first show that, in the absence of dissipation, the equations can be rigorously derived from an underlying variational principle and that the resulting system is symmetric-hyperbolic. Further analysis shows that it not only conserves the total energy but also admits a set of invariants consisting of quadratic combinations of differential operators applied to the state variables. The addition of a stiff relaxation source term allows the system to be extended to dissipative dynamics, describing, for example, Cattaneo-type heat transfer processes that are asymptotically compatible with the Fourier law in the stiff relaxation limit; in this case, the total energy and invariants are dissipated accordingly. A new semi-implicit compatible numerical scheme on staggered grids is developed to solve this system while exactly preserving its key properties at the discrete level. In particular, we prove that the scheme is asymptotic-preserving in the Fourier limit, with a convergence rate depending on the initial data. We also show that the scheme conserves exactly the total energy as well as all the invariants in the absence of relaxation, and dissipates them consistently in its presence. These findings are demonstrated on a set of representative test cases.

papers.title: Characterization of the boundedness of the segment multiplier on rearrangement-invariant spaces
papers.authors: Miguel F. Barea-Fern\'andez, Ron Kerman, Jan Lang, Javier Soria
papers.abstract: Given rearrangement-invariant (r.i.) spaces $X$ and $Y$, we show that the segment multiplier, the truncated Hilbert transform, and the discrete Hilbert transform (on the associated discretized space) are bounded from $X$ to $Y$ simultaneously. Moreover, when $X = Y$ this boundedness is characterized by a condition on a pair of Boyd-type indices. We also exhibit an r.i. space on which the segment multiplier is bounded while the (non-truncated) Hilbert transform fails to be bounded.

papers.title: A Hopf algebra on permutations with a coupling product
papers.authors: Huilan Li, Yishuo Yang, Nantel Bergeron
papers.abstract:
We define a coupling product and a draw coproduct on permutations and show that they define a graded, connected, cocommutative, free Hopf algebra $\mathbb{KS}$. In characteristic zero,
  this implies that $\mathbb{KS}$ is isomorphic to a certain cocommutative Hopf algebra associated with the dual of the coradical filtration of the Malvenuto--Reutenauer Hopf algebra on permutations.
  The coupling product and draw coproduct are permutation analogues of the product and coproduct on the monomial basis of symmetric functions;
  therefore, we can say that our presentation is a monomial basis for $\mathbb{KS}$.

papers.title: Explicit and logarithmically improved chromatic bounds for $(P_2\cup P_3)$-free graphs
papers.abstract:
We prove that every $(P_2\cup P_3)$-free graph $G$, with $k=\omega(G)$, satisfies \[
  \chi(G)=O\!\left(k^3\frac{\ln\ln k}{\ln k}\right). \] Thus the class admits an $o(k^3)$ binding function. We also prove the explicit bound \[
  \chi(G)\le \frac{k^3}{8}+\frac{5k^2}{4}-4k+8
  \qquad(k\ge8), \] with a sharper formula for odd $k$. A further refinement gives an explicit cubic bound with leading coefficient $104/837<1/8$.

papers.title: Blow up and Concentration without Quantization: sharp Harnack type inequalities
papers.authors: Daniele Bartolucci, Paolo Cosentino, Lina Wu
papers.abstract: Motivated by the Onsager statistical mechanics description of turbulent Euler flows with point singularities, we refine the blow up analysis for sequences of solutions of a class of perturbed singular Liouville equations which share the phenomenon of ``blow up and concentration without quantization". The problem is delicate because we are dealing with the exact threshold value above which one meets the well known ``concentration without quantization" phenomenon, as recently pushed forward in [C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris} (2016)] and in [Y. Lee, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, W. Yang, {\em Comm. PDE.} (2017)]. We overcome these difficulties by developing different strategies for ``fast" and ``slow" blow up, combining refined Pohozaev identities, elliptic estimates and ``Sup+CInf" inequalities in the same spirit of [C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, {\em Comm. An. Geom.} (1998)]. In the process, we also derive a new sharp Harnack type inequality by using a moving-plane method, following the ideas in [D. Bartolucci, C.C. Chen, C.S. Lin, G. Tarantello, {\em Comm. P.D.E.} (2002)].

papers.title: Arithmetic Landscape Functions of a Discrete Cat Map
papers.abstract: For a permutation of a finite set, we define a landscape by summing a discounted weight over the times each point returns to itself. The landscape value is determined by the point's least period. We relate the trace of the associated resolvent to fixed-point and exact-period counts, and show that the associated determinant is the reciprocal of the Artin-Mazur dynamical zeta function. We apply this framework to the discrete cat map modulo $N$. For every prime $p\ne5$, all nonzero points have period equal to the order of the cat-map matrix modulo $p$, yielding explicit formulas for the landscape trace and determinant. We prove a period-lifting formula at odd primes $p\ne5$, derive exact fixed-point and period counts modulo $5^a$, and combine prime-power results for composite moduli using the Chinese remainder theorem.

papers.title: Hyperstructures as complete atomic Boolean algebras
papers.abstract: We show that several categories of hyperstructures, including the mosaics of Nakamura and Reyes and the hypergroups of Marty, are realizable as categories of objects with extra structure within the category of complete atomic Boolean algebras (CABAs) and atom-preserving morphisms.

papers.title: Notes on the Kuznetsov component of cubic sevenfolds
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a cubic 7-fold. When $Y$ is smooth, its Kuznetsov component is a Calabi-Yau category of dimension 3, and we construct an embedding of the Kuznetsov component into the derived category of Clifford modules over $\mathbb{P}^4$. When $Y$ is a general cubic 7-fold singular along a line, we construct an explicit weakly crepant categorical resolution of its Kuznetsov component by the derived category of a smooth Calabi-Yau 3-fold, recovering a result of Favero-Kelly. In this construction, we express the resolution functor explicitly as a composition of geometric functors and mutations, and identify its kernel with a category equivalent to a pull-back of the derived category of a stacky curve.

papers.title: Infinite and finite series involving central binomial coefficients and closed forms of generalized hypergeometric functions
papers.authors: Ganesh Bahadur Basnet, Narayan Prasad Pahari, Feng Qi, Arjun Kumar Rathie
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{Z}^-=\{-1,-2,\dotsc\}$ and $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,\dotsc\}$. In 2023, Qi and Lim gave two claims for summing the infinite series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\binom{2k}{k}\frac{1}{\alpha+k}\bigl(\frac{\pm1}{4}\bigr)^k$ for $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{Z}^-$. In this paper, we confirm these claims by expressing the infinite series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\binom{2k}{k}\frac{1}{\alpha+k}\bigl(\frac{z}{4}\bigr)^k$ and the finite series $\sum_{k=1}^{n}\binom{2k}{k}\frac{1}{\alpha+k}\bigl(\frac{z}{4}\bigr)^k$ in terms of the Gauss hypergeometric function ${}_2F_1\bigl[\tfrac12,\alpha;1+\alpha;z\bigr]$ and a generalized hypergeometric function ${}_3F_2$, for $|z|\le1$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Using the Euler integral representation, we derive closed forms, in terms of finite sums of sines and cosines of $\arcsin\sqrt{z}\,$, for ${}_2F_1\bigl[\tfrac12,\tfrac12+n;\tfrac32+n;z\bigr]$, ${}_2F_1\bigl[\tfrac12,1+n;2+n;z\bigr]$, two related ${}_3F_2$ functions, and the incomplete beta functions $B_z\bigl(\frac12+n,\frac12\bigr)$ and $B_z\bigl(1+n,\frac12\bigr)$. By the Pfaff transformation, we obtain closed forms of several further Gauss hypergeometric functions with parameters shifted by $n$. We also give a closed form of $\bigl[(1-z)\frac{\operatorname{d}}{\operatorname{d}z}(1-z)\bigr]^n\frac{\arcsin\sqrt{z}\,}{\sqrt{z(1-z)}\,}$ and a combinatorial identity.

papers.title: On colorful Helly numbers and the growth of Tverberg numbers
papers.authors: Chaya Keller, Skand Parvatikar, Tuan Tran
papers.abstract: We establish new bounds on colorful Helly and Tverberg numbers in abstract convexity spaces with Radon number $r$. We show that the colorful Helly number is at most $(r-1)2^r$, improving Holmsen--Lee's bound $r^{r^{O(\log r)}}$ and matching the known lower bound $2^{r-1}-1$ up to a factor $O(r)$. Furthermore, we prove that the Tverberg number is $r_k=O(r^{\lceil \log_2 r\rceil }k)$, reducing P\'alv\"olgyi's coefficient $r^{r^{r^{O(\log r)}}}$ to a quasipolynomial function of $r$. For $S_4$-separable spaces, we prove $r_k=O(r^2k)$. In the other direction, we construct a sequence of $S_4$-separable spaces with Tverberg number $r_k=\Omega(r^2k)$. This shows that the weak Eckhoff conjecture, asserting that $r_k=O(rk)$ in any abstract convexity space, fails already in separable spaces. The same construction refutes the analogue of Reay's conjecture in separable spaces.

papers.title: $L^p$ approximation results for infinite dimensional Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Leveraging the neural architectures which we introduced in arXiv:2109.13512v4, we show a global universal approximation theorem in the topology of $L^p(\mu)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $\mu$ is a Radon probability measure on a suitable infinite dimensional topological space $\mathfrak X$. Namely, any function $f:\mathfrak X\to \mathbb R$ in $L^p(\mu)$ can be approximated to any degree of accuracy by suitable infinite dimensional architectures. These architectures can be in turn approximated by almost classical neural networks which are specified by a finite number of parameters only. The vectorial case (where $f=f(x)\in E$ and $E$ is a Banach space) is also considered and analogous results are obtained.

papers.title: Essential $p$-dimension and Chern numbers
papers.abstract:
Let $X$ be a smooth, projective, connected variety over a field $k$ containing a root of unity of order $p$. If $X$ has a Chern number prime to $p$, we show that every finite $p$-group acting on $X$ acts through a subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_n(k)$, where $n=\dim X$. This allows one to transfer properties of representations of finite $p$-groups to their actions on $X$. We deduce a fixed-point theorem which, unlike earlier results of this kind, is sensitive to the arithmetic of the base field, and whose dimensional bound is sharp for each individual group (apart from one low-dimensional case when $p=2$). We also obtain restrictions on finite $p$-groups of birational automorphisms of rationally connected varieties; for instance the Cremona group $\operatorname{Cr}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ contains no element of order $p^2$ when $p \ge n+2$.
  More generally, we prove variants of these results in the presence of a Chern number not divisible by a given power of $p$.
  The method is based on the following observation about the essential $p$-dimension $\operatorname{ed}_p(G)$ of an affine algebraic group $G$: over a field of characteristic zero, the number $\operatorname{ed}_p(G) + \dim G$ is the least dimension of a smooth projective variety $Y$ with a generically free $G$-action such that the degree map $\operatorname{CH}_G(Y) \to \mathbb{F}_p$ from the equivariant Chow group is nonzero. The Chern numbers modulo $p$ of $Y$ lie in the image of this map; combined with Karpenko and Merkurjev's computation of the essential $p$-dimension of finite $p$-groups, this yields our results.

papers.title: A further study of quandles and quandle rings
papers.authors: Gregory Churchill, Indu Rasika Churchill, Neranga Fernando, Bhitali Kousik
papers.abstract: We investigate core quandles and idempotents in quandle rings of core quandles. We answer several questions on the rank of core quandles and nontrivial idempotents in quandle rings. We also present solutions to two questions raised in a recent paper about non-trivial idempotents in quandle rings $\mathbb{Z}[R_5]$ and $\mathbb{Z}[C_5]$, where $\mathbb{Z}$, $R_5$ and $C_5$ are the ring of integers, the dihedral quandle of order 5, and the commutative quandle of order 5, respectively. We then study units in extended quandle rings of a trivial quandle and the Joyce quandle, and nilpotent elements in extended quandles rings of a trivial quandle, where the ground ring is an integral domain. As a consequence, we show that the quandle ring and the extended quandle ring of a trivial quandle are not nil clean rings. We also explore prime rings and semi-prime rings among quandle rings. We introduce zero-divisor graphs of quandle rings and find an intriguing mirror symmetry among the in-degree and out-degree of the vertices. Moreover, we find a bivariate polynomial in the ring $(\mathbb{Z}_{2n+1}[Q])[X,Y]$ that determines the commutative quandle of order $2n+1$, where $2n+1$ is prime.

papers.title: Classification of anomalous actions of finite groups with the Rokhlin property
papers.abstract: Given a finite group G, we develop a generalization of the fundamental classification of Rokhlin G-actions on C*-algebras to the setting of anomalous G-actions with the Rokhlin property. For Rokhlin G-kernels on C*-algebras covered by the classification program, this implies that the induced G-action on some known invariants determines the conjugacy class. Extending a result of Izumi, we show that G-kernels with the Rokhlin property on Kirchberg algebras are classified by their anomaly and the induced module structure on the K-theory groups. We explore K-theoretic obstructions for the existence of Rokhlin G-kernels on general separable C*-algebras and use these to characterise which G-module structures arise as K-groups of Kirchberg algebras admitting a Rokhlin G-kernel with a given lifting obstruction.

papers.title: The determinant of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a surface with boundary and periods of holomorphic differentials on its double
papers.abstract:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth orientable $2d$ Riemannian manifold of genus $\mathfrak{g}$ with Riemannian metric $g$ and connected boundary $\Gamma$. Let $\Lambda$ be the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on $\Gamma$ and let ${\rm det}_\zeta(\Lambda)$ be its (modified, i. e. with zero mode excluded) $\zeta$-regularized determinant. It is well-known that the quantity ${\rm det}_\zeta(\Lambda)/|\Gamma|$ (where $|\Gamma|$ is the length of $\Gamma$) is a conformal invariant. It was shown by Edward and Wu (\cite{EV}) that this invariant equals one for $\mathfrak{g}=0$; in the case $\mathfrak{g}>0$ Guillarmou and Guillop\'e \cite{Guillarmou} found two explicit expressions for this invariant through the Rouelle and (respectively) the Selberg zeta-functions of the two surfaces of negative constant curvature from the conformal class of $(M,g)$: one is of infinite volume and complete whereas another has geodesic boundary.
  We present an elementary counterpart of the formulae of Guillarmou and Guillop\'e using the periods of holomorphic differentials on the double $2M$ of $M$ only. Our approach is based on the properties of the Hilbert transform of $M$ \cite{B,HilbKor} and the Kontsevich-Vishik-Friedlander-Guillemin regularization of the determinants of pseudodifferenial operators \cite{KV,Ww,F}. In particular, a connection between the length spectra of (uniformized) $M$, $2M$ and the periods of holomorphic differentials on $2M$ is established.

papers.title: Caged subsequences in permutations
papers.authors: Niranjan Balachandran, Omkar Ramdas, Umesh Shankar
papers.abstract: Given a sequence $\mathfrak{a}:=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ of reals, a subsequence $\mathfrak{b}=(a_{i_1},\ldots,a_{i_k})$ is said to be "caged" if the largest and smallest among the members of $\mathfrak{b}$ are $a_{i_1}$ and $a_{i_k}$, though not necessarily in that order. In this paper, we consider the problem of maximal caged sequences in permutations $\pi\in S_n$. We also consider the same problem for a random permutation, both when the permutation is chosen uniformly at random and also when it is picked uniformly at random from among the permutations of rectangular shape, via the RSK correspondence. We also give a $O(n\log n)$ time algorithm to obtain these maximal caged sequences. In addition, we propose a randomized linear time algorithm that gives the length of the maximal caged sequence up to the factor of $(1-o(1))$.

papers.title: A simple acylindrical recipe for non-split characteristic $2$ sharply $k$-transitive actions and their generalizations
papers.abstract: We provide a fairly simple list of conditions on a group $G$ acting acylindrically on a $\delta$-hyperbolic metric space sufficient for the group to admit an action on a set that is $k$-sharp, transitive on $k$-sets and has the property that for any $k$-set $A$ the setwise stabilizer of $A$ acts on $A$ as prescribed by some fixed subgroup of the group of permutations of $k$ elements. In particular, this yields a large class of non-split sharply $2$ and $3$-transitive actions containing many finitely presented groups, and allows us to characterize sharp $2$-transitivity within the class of hyperbolic groups that do not contain a copy of $C_{2}\times C_{2}$.

papers.title: Generic Spectral Determination of Semiclassical Schr\"odinger Operators with $\mathbb Z_2$-Symmetry
papers.abstract: Consider the two-dimensional semiclassical Schr\"odinger operator $P_\hbar=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2}\Delta+V$ on $\mathbb R^2$, where $V$ has a nondegenerate well at the origin, its harmonic frequencies are rationally independent, and $V$ is $\mathbb Z_2$-symmetric. We prove that, generically, the first three layers of the quantum Birkhoff normal form (QBNF) determine the full Taylor series of $V$ at the origin, up to the unavoidable spatial inversion $V(x)\mapsto V(-x)$. The generic condition depends only on the jet of $V$ through order ten. Consequently, for real analytic potentials with a unique isolated global well at the origin, the low-lying semiclassical spectrum generically determines $V$ up to spatial inversion.

papers.title: Lie methods for countably categorical Engel groups: the Wilson conjecture for 4-Engel 5-groups
papers.abstract: We are interested in the following conjecture of Wilson from 1981: every locally nilpotent countably categorical group is nilpotent. Following our previous work on the Lie algebra analogue of the conjecture, we use Lie methods to deduce the first nontrivial cases of the Wilson conjecture for n-Engel groups: countably categorical 3-Engel groups and 4-Engel 5-groups are nilpotent, from which we also conclude that countably categorical 4-Engel groups of odd exponent are nilpotent. This is implemented via an exceptional case of the Lazard correspondence, checked using computer algebra systems. We also study the transfer of nilpotency results between the three categories: groups, Lie algebras, associative algebras. Among other things, we prove that the Wilson conjecture implies the analogous nilpotency statement for associative algebras (modulo the commutative case).

papers.title: Equilateral Completion in Floretion Triangular Coordinates: Locality, Product Points, and Reflection Symmetry
papers.abstract:
We study nondegenerate equilateral triangles whose vertices are centroids of the $4^n$ order-$n$ floretion tiles. Scaled integer triangular coordinates give exact equilateral completions and, by an obstruction modulo $3$, show that all three vertices have the same tile orientation. In particular, the complete triangle family and its synchronized local cyclic subfamily have respective sizes $|E_n|=\frac{4^n(4^n-1)}{12},\quad |L_n|=\frac{7^n-4^n}{3},$ so the local proportion tends to zero.
  Our principal new result answers the radial-homogeneity question left open in the preceding revision: for every order, the number of triangles containing a given tile is given by an exact affine formula in its squared scaled centroid radius. Although the two tile orientations have different formulas, their attainable squared radii belong to disjoint residue classes modulo $3$, yielding a single radial-incidence law on the full centroid set. We also determine local and nonlocal vertex incidences and obtain circular-shell and squared-radius moment identities.
  The unsigned vertex product defines an algebraic product point. By a rigidity theorem of Ma and Zhang, the multiplication-generated triangles are precisely the nontrivial global cyclic orbits; combining this with our geometric shell classification, we show that the product point is the origin exactly when the Euclidean triangle center is the origin. Further results enumerate central-vertex, no-$e$, and main-axis families, derive Fibonacci and finite-state recurrences for product-centered and reflection-restricted classes, and characterize pairwise anticommutation.

papers.title: Gradient H\"older regularity for singular fractional $p$-Laplace equations
papers.abstract: We prove interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity for globally bounded weak solutions to the fractional $p$-Laplace equation $(-\Delta_p)^s u=0$ under the assumptions $n\ge2$, $1<p<2$, $0<s<1$, and $sp>p-1$, where $\alpha=\alpha(n,p,s)>0$. This resolves the open problem of gradient H\"{o}lder continuity for globally bounded solutions in the singular range $sp>p-1$. The proof is based on affine approximation and estimates independent of the normalized affine slope. When these slopes tend to infinity, we prove convergence to a solution of a linear nonlocal equation of order $sp-p+2$, together with convergence of the normalized energies to the corresponding quadratic energy. The regularity of the limiting equation yields an improved affine approximation. For bounded slopes, we prove that every globally Lipschitz weak solution of $(-\Delta_p)^s u=0$ in $\mathbb R^n$ is affine and use this result in a compactness argument. The two estimates are combined in an iteration that preserves the required energy and tail bounds and gives H\"older continuity of the gradient.

papers.title: A Sharp Joint Bias-Energy Envelope for Radial Clipping
papers.abstract: Radial clipping does two things at once: it cuts off the part of a vector outside a ball and leaves a bounded vector inside the ball. The part cut off defines the residual. For a random vector, we study the magnitude of the bias in the mean and the energy, defined as the centered second moment of the clipped vector. Controlling these effects is important in stochastic optimization with heavy tails, where the choice of the clipping threshold affects convergence bounds for algorithms. In the deterministic problem, for a fixed threshold $\tau>0$, $1\le p\le2$, and nonnegative coefficients $\alpha,\beta$, we find the smallest constant that simultaneously bounds the residual and energy in terms of $\lVert x\rVert^p$. This same constant remains sharp in the stochastic counterpart for random vectors in a Hilbert space. We also find the exact supremum of the corresponding linear combination of normalized bias and energy for arbitrary $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R$. We then give a geometric picture in the energy-bias plane. Varying the weights, we describe the smallest closed convex region containing all normalized pairs and the attainable set itself, identifying unattainable boundary values. Every attainable pair at a fixed threshold can be realized by a real-valued random variable taking at most two values. We also consider all thresholds simultaneously. For any integrable random vector in a Hilbert space, we construct a single $\mathbb R^3$-valued random vector preserving its norm distribution, bias magnitude, and energy simultaneously at every threshold $\tau>0$. Finally, we apply the joint bound to risk-adjusted reinsurance costs for a prescribed retention threshold and to the logarithmic shortfall of a clipped portfolio strategy relative to any constant-fraction strategy. AI was used in preparing this paper (see Section 8).

papers.title: Degeneracies of Lagrange functions and geometric interpretations of Lagrange multipliers
papers.abstract: We introduce Lagrange functions associated with height and distance-squared functions on implicit plane curves. We show that degeneracies of these functions characterize geometric properties of the curves, such as inflections and vertices, and give geometric interpretations of the corresponding Lagrange multipliers in terms of contact with lines and circles.

papers.title: Categorification in Representation Theory
papers.abstract: In this survey article, we give an introduction to the relatively young subject of $2$-representation theory, which studies categorifications of important players in classical representation theory. In particular, we provide a streamlined exposition of the main results leading to the classification of simple $2$-representations for Soergel bimodules associated to finite Weyl groups in characteristic $0$, obtained in [M. Mackaay, V. Mazorchuk, V. Miemietz, D. Tubbenhauer and X. Zhang, Simple transitive $2$-representations of Soergel bimodules for finite Coxeter types. Proc. London Math. Soc. 126 (2023)].

papers.title: Interior curvature estimates for convex solutions of a prescribed curvature quotient equation
papers.abstract: In this note, we prove a priori interior curvature bounds for convex solutions to an elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equation. The proof avoids integral estimates, doubling inequalities and compactness arguments. It relies on a concavity inequality for the equation operator and a novel choice of the auxiliary function to carry out an elementary maximum-principle argument. As an application, we obtain interior curvature bounds for convex solutions of a prescribed special Lagrangian curvature equation in dimensions three and four.

papers.title: Three omitted values and non-Blaschke point divisors in half-planes
papers.authors: Quanyu Tang, Bokai Cui, Wei He, Tao Hu, Yanyang Li, Ke Wang, Zijun Yu
papers.abstract: We construct a real meromorphic function $F$ on $\mathbb C$ such that $F^{-1}(\{0,1,\infty\})\subset\mathbb R$, while $F$ is not of bounded type in either half-plane. More strongly, for every $a\in\widehat{\mathbb C}\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, the $a$-point divisor in either half-plane fails the Blaschke condition. Thus the construction gives a negative answer to the half-plane bounded-type question arising from Nevanlinna's 1925 work. Postcomposition gives the analogous counterexample for any prescribed triple of distinct values in the Riemann sphere. The core construction and proof were generated during an autonomous run of GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra.

papers.title: The Multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for Plane Curves
papers.abstract: We prove the multivariable Strong Monodromy Conjecture for the local topological zeta function of arbitrary tuples of nonzero nonunit plane curve germs. The entries may be nonreduced and may have common irreducible factors. We also prove that the non-equivariant local motivic and topological zeta functions have the same polar locus and generic pole orders, using a multivariable extension of the Nicaise--Xu definition of motivic pole order. Our arguments combine twisted Poincar\'e residues with resolution formulas and specialization to one variable. In arbitrary dimension, we prove that a nonzero iterated residue class on a stratum of a log resolution implies the vanishing of the Bernstein--Sato ideal at the corresponding parameter. In particular, every topological polar hyperplane whose order equals the ambient dimension is contained in this zero locus. For algebraic germs, the topological pole order is at most the motivic pole order, and the two attain maximal order simultaneously.

papers.title: Two-point correlations of multiplicative functions with dense orbits
papers.abstract: Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{T}$ be completely multiplicative functions with dense images in the complex unit circle $\mathbb{T}$. We prove that, for every non-empty open set $U \subset \mathbb{T}^2$, the set of integers $n$ such that $(f(n),g(n+1)) \in U$ has positive upper logarithmic density, unless the pair $(f,g)$ is of a special form. This result strengthens earlier theorems of Klurman and Mangerel, as well as of Charamaras, Mountakis, and Tsinas, and yields simpler proofs.

papers.title: An approximate zero bias transformation for random sums: Applications to sampling with outliers, auto insurance, and generative AI
papers.abstract: We develop $L^1$ bounds for the difference between a test function of a random sum and a standard normal random variable, where the summands are assumed to be independent but not necessarily identically distributed. The bounds are obtained through a new version of the approximate zero bias transformation specifically developed for random sums. Although the identical distribution assumption is relaxed, the bounds are of order $1/\sqrt{n}$, matching the order of existing bounds in the literature under the same distributional assumption on the number of summands. The main results are then applied to three real-world settings: random sums obtained from simple random sampling with outliers, total insurance claims, and generative AI response times.

papers.title: Generalized Fermat equation over number fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and $A,B,C\in\mathcal{O}_K\setminus\{0\}$. Put $S_K=\{\mathfrak{P}:\mathfrak{P}\mid2\}$ and $S_K'=\{\mathfrak{q}:\mathfrak{q}\mid2ABC\}$. We establish two criteria for the non-existence of non-trivial solutions of $Ax^p+By^p=Cz^p$ over $K$ for sufficiently large prime exponents $p$. Both criteria use a valuation bound on the $S_K'$-unit equation at a fixed $\mathfrak{P}\in S_K$. The first excludes all non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ when $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(A)=v_{\mathfrak{P}}(B)=m$ and $v_{\mathfrak{P}}(C)=m+k$, with $k>4v_{\mathfrak{P}}(2)$. The second, under an explicit nonvanishing condition on the coefficient valuations, excludes solutions $(a,b,c)\in(K^\times)^3$ whose $\mathfrak{P}$-valuations are not all equal. In particular, it excludes non-trivial primitive integral solutions with $\mathfrak{P}\mid abc$. Neither criterion restricts the residue degree of $\mathfrak{P}$.
