Both criteria hold unconditionally over every totally real field; over general number fields, we assume residual modularity and Eichler--Shimura-type conjectures. The first criterion covers a new coefficient range. In particular, under the corresponding $S_K$-unit bound, $x^p+y^p=2^rz^p$ has no non-trivial solutions in $K^3$ for each fixed $r\geq5$ and sufficiently large prime $p$. This bound holds for a set of real quadratic fields of relative density $1$. For a family of imaginary quadratic fields of relative density $5/6$, we explicitly determine the $S_K$-unit solutions and verify the valuation bound for both criteria when $A,B,C\in\{\pm2^r:r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}\}$, including the same $r\geq5$ conclusion.

papers.title: A GPU-Accelerated Blocked Adaptive Randomized Range Finder Based on an Implicit Householder QR Decomposition
papers.abstract: Low-rank methods can reduce the memory and computational requirements of deep neural network training in approaches such as GaLore. Randomized range finders offer an attractive alternative to singular value decompositions, particularly when the required rank is determined adaptively from a prescribed approximation tolerance. We introduce a blocked adaptive randomized range finder based on a Householder QR decomposition and an optimized hybrid CPU--GPU implementation. Numerical experiments show that it preserves orthogonality and approximation accuracy in regimes where block Gram--Schmidt without reorthogonalization becomes unstable. The blocked formulation exposes matrix--matrix operations and enables overlap of CPU panel factorization with GPU updates. On an NVIDIA GH200, the overlapped implementation reduces the runtime for the largest tested matrix from 9.91 s on the CPU to 0.407 s. The method provides a stable and efficient building block for low-rank approximation on heterogeneous systems with applications in computational science and engineering.

papers.title: Higher-order Approximate Symmetries
papers.abstract: The Fushchych--Shtelen (FS) construction of approximate symmetries, based on a triangular system for the coefficients of a solution expansion, is extended to arbitrary order. A coefficient-map formulation establishes, under explicit hypotheses, a correspondence with the Baikov--Gazizov--Ibragimov (BGI) method. The two approaches are compared for a perturbed cubic wave equation. Nonlinearities admitting an FS point symmetry with prescribed projection onto the unperturbed dilation are classified through second order, up to equivalences. They comprise a power family and logarithmic families at exceptional exponents. Nonlinearities admitting second-order BGI point symmetries that continue this dilation are also classified. Among perturbations nontrivial at first order, these form a proper subfamily of one FS family; another family is admitted by both methods when the perturbation first enters at second order. Joint reduction by the Lorentz algebra and the inherited FS dilation yields explicit invariant solutions for all FS normal forms and recovers the first-order solutions of Fushchych and Shtelen. For the common family with a nontrivial first-order perturbation, the logarithmic corrections arise from expanding a power law with a perturbation-dependent exponent. Periodic traveling waves illustrate the long-scale validity of the FS expansion. The first correction is obtained by quadrature, second-order secular terms are identified, and phase renormalization yields bounded approximations. For integer-power members of the power family, the amplitude dependence of the corrected wavenumber agrees with the symmetry scaling weights.

papers.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
papers.abstract: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.

papers.title: A class of port-Hamiltonian systems with general time delays
papers.authors: Rogelio Arancibia Bustos, B\'alint Farkas, Birgit Jacob, Merlin Schmitz
papers.abstract: We define a class of infinite dimensional linear port-Hamiltonian delay systems, give a characterization for such systems, and provide an easily verifiable sufficient condition to belong to this class, thereby extending the study by Breiten, Hinsen and Unger in [IEEE Trans. Autom. Control vol. 69, no. 12 (2024), pp. 8924-8930, doi: 10.1109/TAC.2024.3464332]. The results rely on the operator semigroup theoretic treatment of linear delay PDEs.

papers.title: Transformation of Adaptive Multistage Sampling for Solving Finite-Horizon Markov Decision Processes with Unknown Model
papers.abstract: This work provides a learning approach to solving finite-horizon Markov decision processes (MDPs) when the underlying model of a given finite MDP is unknown to the decision maker. We transform the adaptive multistage sampling (AMS) algorithm into a sampling-free algorithm, called "adaptive multistage rollout (AMR)," for estimating the optimal value at an initial state when only the state set and the action set are known. AMR emulates the backward induction as in AMS but in a reinforcement learning (RL) setting. At each iteration, AMR generates a non-stationary policy to be used for exploration and rolls out the policy in order to obtain a single trajectory of experiences and traces it backwards in a non-recursive way while doing relevant updates only at visited states and for actions taken at the visited states. We show that AMR is asymptotically optimal such that the sequence of the expected absolute errors approaches zero and its convergence rate depends on the number of visits to each reachable state at each stage from the initial state, essentially transforming the result of AMS into the RL setting.

papers.title: On the real-rootedness of Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of $(132,213)$-avoiding permutahedra
papers.abstract: Let $P_d$ be the convex hull of the permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ that avoid the patterns $132$ and $213$, and let $H_d(t)$ be its Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. We prove that all zeros of $H_d(t)$ are real and negative for $3\le d\le1000$ and for every $d\ge2^{62}$; for $d\le2$ the polynomial is constant. Expanding $H_d(t)$ in refined Eulerian polynomials does not suffice, since a coordinate is already negative at $d=7$. Let $A_{d,i}(t)$ enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ with first entry $i$ by number of descents. For $c\ge0$, we prove that every nonnegative linear combination of $A_{d,1},\ldots,A_{d,d}$ and the adjacent differences $A_{d,r+1}-cA_{d,r}$, $2\le r\le d-2$, is real-rooted for all $d\ge4$ simultaneously if and only if $c\le2-\sqrt3$. This reduces real-rootedness to the positivity of explicit weighted tails of the coordinates. An exact certificate checks these inequalities for $d\le1000$, and coefficient estimates based on Darroch's theorem on the mode of a sum of Bernoulli variables prove them for $d\ge2^{62}$; the range $1001\le d<2^{62}$ remains open. Along the way we identify $P_d$, up to lattice equivalence, with twice a chain-poset permutahedron and with the Newton polytope of a discriminant, which transfers the known cube structure and volume of these models to $P_d$. We also show that the coefficient of $t^{d-1}$ in $H_d(t)$ counts strong tournament score sequences for $d\ge3$, confirming a conjecture of Rehberg in this range.

papers.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
papers.abstract: We show that for every prime power $q$ and $\rho\in(0,1-\frac1q)$ there exists $\varepsilon_0(q, \rho) > 0$ such that for all positive $\varepsilon < \varepsilon_0(q, \rho)$, a random linear code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of rate $1-h_q(\rho)-\varepsilon$ has list size $\lfloor h_q(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_q(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$ with probability $1-o(1)$. Before this work, the list size was known only up to a constant factor for $q\ge3$, and for $q=2$ it was known to be either $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor-1$, $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$. We also show that the same two-point concentration holds for the list size of random LDPC codes. This follows from a general theorem establishing that random LDPC codes and random linear codes have the same threshold rate for distance, list decoding, list recovery from errors and any other \emph{convex} property, which answers a question of Mosheiff, Resch, Ron-Zewi, Silas and Wootters.

papers.title: On a Brunn-Minkowski principle for first-order information functionals
papers.authors: Lidia Gordo Malag\'on, Eugenia Saor\'in G\'omez, Jes\'us Yepes Nicol\'as
papers.abstract:
In this work we present the following general principle: every positive homogeneous functional on an abstract convex cone satisfying a suitable Brunn-Minkowski inequality gives rise to an information functional -defined as the quotient of the functional by its relative surface area- that satisfies a linear Brunn-Minkowski inequality. We also establish the dual counterpart of this principle for functionals satisfying an analogous convexity property, yielding reverse linear Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for the associated information functionals.
  Furthermore, we show that homogeneity is necessary within this principle by providing a counterexample to the expected result for the information functional associated to the standard Gaussian measure.
  As applications, we recover, via an alternative first-order argument, a classical result by Giannopoulos, Hartzoulaki and Paouris (2002) for the ratio of two consecutive quermassintegrals, together with a characterization of the equality case. The same argument extends to the setting of mixed discriminants of symmetric positive definite matrices.
  Finally, our approach yields new extensions of the Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Dembo, Cover and Thomas, for the classical information functional, both to the $L_p$ setting ($p \geq 1$), where the relative surface area is expressed in terms of Lutwak's first $L_p$ quermassintegral, and to the measure-theoretic framework, for measures with homogeneous densities satisfying some concavity. Moreover, we prove that our principle applies also in the context of the Blaschke addition, both in the volume and in the (mixed) affine surface area cases, obtaining new inequalities as an application of it.

papers.title: The derived length of subgroups of the Cremona group
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal derived length of a solvable subgroup of the plane Cremona group over $\mathbb C$ is equal to $5$. The main difficulty is the case of subgroups containing loxodromic elements. To treat this case, we prove that the maximal derived length of a finite solvable subgroup is $4$ and establish a centraliser theorem: the centraliser of a finite solvable subgroup of derived length $4$ contains no loxodromic element. The proof of the centraliser theorem relies on Blanc's classification of maximal algebraic subgroups and then uses equivariant Sarkisov theory, orbit estimates, superrigidity, and fixed curves of genus at least two.

papers.title: Existence of regular sets in circulant quartic graphs: a complete characterization
papers.authors: A. Abdollahi, J. Bagherian, F. Jafari, M. Khatami, Z. Shokoohi, R. Sobhani
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma=(V,E)$ be a graph and let $a,b$ be nonnegative integers. A nonempty proper subset $C\subset V$ is an \emph{$(a,b)$-regular set} if each vertex of $C$ has exactly $a$ neighbors in $C$ and each vertex outside $C$ has exactly $b$ neighbors in $C$. Perfect codes and total perfect codes are the $(0,1)$- and $(1,1)$-regular sets. For every connected circulant quartic graph $\operatorname{Cay}(\mathbb{Z}_n,\{x^{\pm k},x^{\pm\ell}\})$ and every pair $(a,b)$ we decide, in terms of $n$, $k$ and $\ell$, whether an $(a,b)$-regular set exists. Existence is proved by exhibiting unions of residue classes; non-existence comes from a Fourier-analytic obstruction combined with the fact that certain sums of roots of unity cannot vanish.

papers.title: Collision-Free Schedule Acquisition through Slotted ALOHA: Scaling Laws and Fluctuations
papers.abstract: Decentralized networks can learn collision-free periodic transmission schedules, but acquisition can consume much of a finite operating horizon. We characterize acquisition in a reservation protocol for a fixed population of $n$ nodes and a period of $\Gamma_n\ge n$ slots. Initially, each node attempts independently in each slot with probability proportional to $1/n$. A success reserves a slot that the node reuses every $\Gamma_n$ slots, retaining it after collisions. Nodes use only their own acknowledgments and small local memory. An exact finite-population Markov reduction, independent of the arrangement of reserved slots, characterizes the time until every node has a distinct reservation. As $n\to\infty$, mean acquisition takes $O(n^2)$ slots when $\Gamma_n=n$ and $O(n\log n)$ slots when $\Gamma_n\sim(1+\theta)n$, for fixed $\theta>0$. With a fixed number $\Gamma_n-n$ of spare slots, the standard deviation of acquisition time has the same asymptotic order as its mean. If that number diverges while $\Gamma_n/n$ remains bounded, the ratio of standard deviation to mean tends to zero. A diverging sublinear number of spare slots yields $o(n^2)$ mean acquisition while long-run utilization, the fraction $n/\Gamma_n$ of slots with successful transmissions, tends to one. Simulations validate these laws and compare acquisition and delivered packets per slot with existing access protocols.

papers.title: Links and singularities of stable maps from $3$-manifolds to surfaces
papers.abstract: For any two links in the $3$-sphere, we provide a visual construction of a stable map $f$ from the $3$-sphere to the Euclidean plane such that $f$ has no cusp points, the set of definite (resp. indefinite) fold points of $f$ is isotopic to the first (resp. second) given link, and $f$ does not have a certain type of singular fibers. Moreover, we obtain a similar result for any $3$-manifold by setting the target space to the $2$-sphere.

papers.title: Unimodality shenanigans in Ehrhart theory
papers.abstract: We construct counterexamples to a four-decade-old conjecture attributed to Stanley concerning the unimodality of $h^*$-polynomials of IDP polytopes. As additional applications of our main constructions, we also disprove a conjecture by Brenti on the log-concavity of $h^*$-polynomials of Gorenstein IDP polytopes, and a conjecture by Ferroni and Higashitani concerning the log-concavity of the Ehrhart series of IDP polytopes. We also answer their question about the existence of very ample polytopes with non-log-concave interior Ehrhart series. Our class of examples arises by taking Cayley sums of rectangular prisms, and hence they possess regular unimodular flag triangulations by a result of Haase, Paffenholz, Piechnik and Santos. Remarkably, for the unimodality conjecture we can even find smooth counterexamples.

papers.title: Convexity of a ratio function involving polygamma functions and monotonicity of the sectional curvature of the Fisher--Rao manifold
papers.abstract: This paper proves that the sectional curvature of the Fisher--Rao manifold of beta distributions, restricted to the diagonal, is strictly decreasing. The proof is based on a general convexity lemma for ratios involving positive decreasing functions and is applied to a quotient of polygamma functions.

papers.title: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2$ is invertible requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm for multiplication in this algebra costing $O(N \log N)$ arithmetic operations in $R$ and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage when the doubling parameters of $A_n$ are units whose square roots lie in a fixed commutative coefficient algebra $S$ finitely generated as an $R$-module and admitting an $R$-linear map $\pi\colon S \to R$ with $\pi(1) = 1$. In particular, over $\mathbb{R}$ and every finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ of odd characteristic, a quadratic field extension contains a square root of every possible doubling parameter, so the algorithm applies to every Cayley-Dickson tower over these fields, and the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ over them is at most $(9n-21)2^n+28$ when $n\ge2$. When the top doubling parameter is a non-square, as in the standard real tower, the bound is $(9n-15)2^{n-1}+10$. To the author's knowledge, the algorithm presented in this paper is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. When $R=\mathbb{R}$ with every doubling parameter equal to $-1$, the real quasilinear schedule uses fewer total arithmetic operations than both direct multiplication and a uniform algorithm of Cariow-Cariowa for $n\ge4$. An implementation for the standard real tower is available in the MIT-licensed C11 library fastCD, with a NumPy-backed Python interface. In single-core benchmarks against direct multiplication and the uniform Cariow-Cariowa method, the quasilinear implementation had the lowest mean time of the three at every tested dimension $N\ge32$, for both single and batched products, and was over $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

papers.title: Verified Linear Programming via Tolerance-Aware Precision Boosting
papers.authors: Ernesto Casablanca, Martin Sidaway, Sadegh Soudjani, Paolo Zuliani
papers.abstract: Linear programming plays a fundamental role in computer science, with applications in optimization, formal verification, SMT solving, and numerous other domains. When exactness guarantees are required, numerical inaccuracies arising from floating-point arithmetic can compromise soundness, whereas exact rational arithmetic often incurs significant computational overhead. In this paper, we investigate the numerical stability of the simplex algorithm and establish conditions under which a precision-boosting floating-point implementation provably produces the same pivot decisions and final basis as an exact rational implementation, from which the final result is reconstructed and certified exactly. Our analysis shows that correctness depends on both arithmetic precision and a careful handling of numerical tolerances. Based on these results, we develop a tolerance-aware, precision-boosting simplex algorithm with formal correctness guarantees. Finally, we introduce a delta-complete termination criterion that allows the algorithm to terminate once certified upper and lower bounds on the optimal objective differ by at most a user-specified threshold delta, providing a certified, user-controlled optimality gap.

papers.title: MOE-DGSCND: Multi-Objective Enterprise Green Supply Chain Network Design
papers.abstract: This paper introduces and studies the Multi-Objective Enterprise Doubly-Green Supply Chain Network Design (MOE-DGSCND) problem, an extension of Multi-Objective Supply Chain Network Design. The problem studied here is a three-objective combinatorial optimization problem that simultaneously minimizes total cost f1, carbon dioxide emissions f2 and customer dissatisfaction f3 over binary decisions regarding which distribution centers to open and how to assign customer zones to open facilities. The problem generalizes the capacitated facility location problem (CFLP) and is known to be NP-hard (Garey and Johnson, 1979). This paper formally specifies the decision variables, objective functions and constraints and investigates three solution approaches using a single numerical instance: (A) an exact weighted-sum integer linear programming (ILP) formulation solved with Python combinatorially and via PuLP, (B) three Fully Polynomial-Time Approximation Schemes (FPTAS) providing (1 + $\epsilon$)-approximate solutions for $\epsilon$ := 0.15 and (C) two baseline heuristics for comparison. On an instance with eight customers and five candidate distribution centers, the exact solver certifies the optimal (sampled) supported solutions across eight weight combinations, while the FPTAS-based approaches complete within milliseconds, compared to centiseconds for the exact ILP on this tiny non-stochastic instance.

papers.title: First-Derivative Chromatic Symmetric Reconstruction For Proper Trees
papers.abstract: Richard Stanley asked whether every tree $T$ is determined up to isomorphism by its chromatic symmetric function $X_T$. We approach this open problem by regarding $X_T$ as a polynomial in the power-sum symmetric functions $p_1, p_2, \dots$ and studying the invariant $\Phi_T = \left.\frac{\partial {X_T}}{\partial p_1}\right\rvert_{p_1 = 0}$. We prove that $\Phi_T$ distinguishes, among proper trees, every proper tree in which any non-leaf vertex with two or more non-leaf neighbors has a number of leaf neighbors occurring at no other non-leaf vertex. We give an equivalent formulation of Stanley's question in terms of $\Phi_T$. Finally, we show that counts of spanning forests with at most $t$ edges cannot distinguish all $k$-vertex trees when $t<\left\lfloor k/2\right\rfloor$, for every $k\ge4$.

papers.title: Duality and Baire like properties in topological abelian groups
papers.authors: Mar\'ia V. Ferrer, Salvador Hern\'andez, Isabel Sep\'ulveda
papers.abstract:
This article investigates the duality of abelian topological groups by delving into the interplay between the algebraic and topological properties of a group $G$ and those of its dual group. In particular, extending the notion of a $g$-barrelled group, we introduce and study the classes of $\kappa$-barrelled and $\omega$-barrelled groups. Our first main result establishes that every $\omega$-barrelled group is $\aleph_0$-barrelled (i.e., if every weakly convergent sequence in the dual group is equicontinuous, then every metrizable weakly compact subset of the dual group is also equicontinuous). From this, we deduce that the free topological abelian group $A(K)$ over a metrizable compact space $K$ is determined by the subgroup generated by any of its dense subsets.
  Furthermore, we prove that if $G$ is a $\sigma$-compact, $\omega$-barrelled group, then its dual group $\widehat{G}_\kappa$ equipped with the compact-open topology is sequentially complete (complete if $G$ is hemicompact). We also solve an open question posed by Trigos-Arrieta by constructing an explicit example of an $\omega$-barrelled metrizable group that fails to be $g$-barrelled. Finally, we investigate the dualization of groups lacking infinite compact subsets, proving that for a totally bounded abelian group $G$, every compact subset of $G$ is finite if and only if its dual group $\widehat{G}$, endowed with the finite-open topology, is unordered Baire-like.

papers.title: A positive version of Miljutin's Theorem
papers.authors: Javier Laguna-Ricart, Gonzalo Mart\'inez-Cervantes, Jakub Rondo\v{s}, Alberto Salguero-Alarc\'on
papers.abstract: In this paper we provide a positive version of Miljutin's theorem. Namely, we show that for any uncountable compact metric spaces $K$ and $L$ there exists a positive isomorphism $T:C(K)\longrightarrow C(L)$. Moreover, the inverse of $T$ is a regular operator, and $T$ may be chosen so that $\|T\|_\mathrm{r} \cdot \|T^{-1}\|_\mathrm{r} \leq 9+6\sqrt3$. The method also gives positive versions of classical nonmetrizable results for Miljutin and Dugundji compacta. In particular, if $G$ and $H$ are infinite compact groups of the same weight, then $C(G)$ and $C(H)$ are positively and regularly isomorphic with the same uniform quantitative estimate.

papers.title: Generalized Bratteli diagrams without probability tail invariant measures
papers.abstract:
The paper focuses on the following problem: given a generalized Bratteli diagram $B$, determine conditions under which the tail equivalence relation $\mathcal R$ does not admit a tail invariant probability measure on the path space $X_B$. We give several sufficient conditions, formulated in terms of the incidence matrices, that guarantee the nonexistence of such a measure.
  We also discuss a new spectral method for finding tail invariant measures for a class of stationary generalized Bratteli diagrams. This method allowed us to answer affirmatively an open problem formulated in arXiv:2212.13803.

papers.title: On the largest prime factors less than $y$ of consecutive shifted primes
Algebraic and measurable embeddings between square-free right-angled Artin groups
papers.authors: Adrien Abgrall, Alexandra Gurieva, Camille Horbez
papers.abstract:
Let $\Gamma,\Delta$ be finite simplicial graphs, and assume that $\Gamma$ has no induced squares. We prove that the right-angled Artin group $A(\Delta)$ measurably embeds into $A(\Gamma)$ if and only if $A(\Delta)$ embeds as a subgroup in a graph product of free abelian groups over $\Gamma$. This in turn has a graph-theoretical characterisation which can be checked algorithmically.
  If additionally $A(\Gamma)$ and $A(\Delta)$ have cohomological dimension equal to two and $A(\Gamma)$ is not isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}\times F_n$, we get that $A(\Delta)$ measurably embeds into $A(\Gamma)$ if and only if it embeds as a subgroup in $A(\Gamma)$.
  Our proof relies on the following algebraic statement. Let $K_1,\dots,K_n$ be a family of pairwise disjoint cliques in the square-free graph $\Gamma$, and let $g_1,\dots,g_n$ be elements of $A(\Gamma)$ with respective parabolic supports $A(K_1),\dots,A(K_n)$. Then the subgroup of $A(\Gamma)$ generated by $g_1,\dots,g_n$ is a right-angled Artin group, where the only relations impose that $g_i$ and $g_j$ commute if $K_i\cup K_j$ is contained in a clique of $\Gamma$. The same holds true more generally for pairwise disjoint cliques $K_1,\dots,K_n$ in the extension graph $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ext}}$, up to possibly replacing the elements $g_i$ by powers.

papers.title: A proof of the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture for small volumes under a Ricci curvature lower bound
papers.authors: Marcos Agnoletto, M\'arcio Fabiano Da Silva, Stefano Nardulli, Reinaldo Resende
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture, also known as the Aubin conjecture, in the small volume regime under a lower Ricci curvature bound, for any dimension $n\geq 2$. More precisely, we show that if $(M^n,g)$ is a Cartan-Hadamard manifold satisfying $\mathrm{Sec}_g\leq\bar k\leq 0$ and $\mathrm{Ric}_g\geq (n-1)\underline k$, then its isoperimetric profile is at least that of the model space of curvature $\bar k$ for small enough volumes. We also reduce the proof of the generalized Cartan-Hadamard conjecture to establishing rigidity in the equality case.

papers.title: Prediction with Five Experts and Geometric Stopping: A Probabilistic Construction and Analytic Verification
papers.authors: Erhan Bayraktar, Ibrahim Ekren, Nikolaos Kolliopoulos
papers.abstract: We present a solution of the limiting five-expert prediction problem with geometric stopping, based on stochastic calculus and partial differential equations. If $\delta$ is the stopping probability, the minimax expected regret from tied initial scores is $45\pi^2/(512\sqrt{2\delta})+o(\delta^{-1/2})$ as $\delta\downarrow0$. The adversarial rank control selecting the best and third-best experts maximizes the limiting Hamiltonian at every state. Following the four-expert construction of Bayraktar, Ekren, and Zhang (2020), we represent the value correction as a discounted boundary-local-time expectation for a degenerate obliquely reflected Brownian motion. The hyperbolic systems governing its boundary traces are derived and solved explicitly. To verify the nonlinear Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation, we combine heat-equation minimum principles in equality directions, ODE minimum principles applied to convex combinations of multiple controls, and comparisons across controls. These arguments reduce the 48 regional control inequalities to a few lower-dimensional boundary problems, with the remaining signs established by explicit monotonicity arguments and by factorization of multivariate integral kernels that are positive polynomials in some of their variables. We prove global $C^2$ regularity across both regional interfaces and changes in rank ordering. We also show that the alternating COMB control only attains the limiting Hamiltonian maximum exactly when the two highest scores coincide and the third- and fourth-highest scores coincide.

papers.title: Existence and Regularity of Stable Resonant Spectral Submanifolds and Linearization Maps
papers.authors: Florian Kogelbauer, Rafael de la Llave
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of $C^{r_{*},\alpha}$-regular sub-stable invariant manifolds and conjugacies for analytic maps near a fixed point in the presence of resonances, assuming an invertible semisimple linearization. The regularity order $r$ and the admissible H\"older exponents $\alpha$ depend on the resonant indices and the relative rates of contraction. Our approach uses functional expansions based on logarithmic polynomials, which allow the invariance equation to be solved explicitly and algorithmically to arbitrary order. The existence results are obtained via a fixed-point argument in a suitable Banach space. We further present several analytic examples that illustrate the theorem and demonstrate the loss of regularity caused by resonances.

papers.title: A Note on a Result of Chen Li: the Thinning Problem via the Kernel Method
papers.abstract: Recently, C. Li posted a preprint that resolves the fractional version of Talagrand's discrete convexity problem. In this note, we use the method of C. Li to answer another problem of Talagrand.

papers.title: Sharp Strichartz estimates on the one-dimensional torus
papers.authors: Yangkendi Deng, Chenjie Fan, Shaoming Guo, Zihua Guo, Yongming Luo
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the sharp Strichartz estimates for the Schr\"odinger equation on the one-dimensional torus. More precisely, via obtaining a sharp weak $L^{6}$ estimate with no derivative loss, we obtain sharp $L^{6}$ Strichartz estimate, and sharp no loss $L^{p}$ Strichartz estimate for any $2<p<6$. The latter answers a question by Bourgain \cite{Bourgain93}.

papers.title: Limit shape, avalanches, and stabilisation of abelian sandpiles on comb lattices
papers.abstract: We study two aspects of the abelian sandpile model on comb lattices. First, we prove that the infinite-volume limit of the stationary measures is supported on the saturated configuration. We then investigate the shape of avalanches induced by adding a particle at the origin in finite boxes of size $(2n+1)\times(2n+1)$ around the origin. In the stationary distribution on these finite boxes, we show that avalanches reach the boundary along the vertical teeth with probability tending to $1$, while the horizontal spread is of order $\sqrt{n}$. Finally, we establish that the single-source limit shape for abelian sandpiles on the comb lattice agrees with the corresponding limit shapes for the divisible sandpile, internal diffusion-limited aggregation (IDLA), and rotor-router aggregation models. This establishes limit shape universality on the comb lattice.

papers.title: Bad Reduction of Genus Two Curves with complex multiplication
papers.authors: Jan Hendrik Bruinier, Tonghai Yang, Peng Yu
papers.abstract: We study genus two curves whose Jacobians have complex multiplication by a biquadratic CM field. In this setting the Jacobian decomposes as a product of two elliptic curves with complex multiplication by orders in the same imaginary quadratic field. We derive upper bounds for the primes of stable bad reduction of such curves in terms of the discriminants of the CM orders. To do so, we give an explicit description of principally polarized abelian surfaces with CM by a biquadratic field via small CM cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety of signature (3,2). We use it to prove an arithmetic intersection formula between such CM cycles with Humbert surfaces in terms of coefficients of incoherent Eisenstein series and representation numbers of ternary positive definite quadratic forms. Finally, employing the arithmetic properties of higher Green functions, we show that primes of stable bad reduction always exist.

papers.title: Regularity of the Value Function in Multi-Asset Portfolio Selection with Proportional Transaction Costs
papers.abstract:
This paper concerns the variational inequality arising from a specific singular control problem: portfolio selection under proportional transaction costs. This variational inequality is a gradient-constrained partial differential equation (PDE). Generally, the literature only guarantees the W^{2, \infty} regularity of the solution to such a PDE, and counterexamples exist for higher regularity.
  In this paper, by exploiting the concavity of the value function, we connect this gradient-constrained problem to an obstacle problem, and finally show that the solution is C^{2,\alpha} except at the corner points where multiple gradient constraints bind. Especially, if there are two assets, then a global C^{2,\alpha} solution can be guaranteed.

papers.title: Two-disjoint-cycle-cover edge bipancyclicity in Cartesian products
papers.authors: Ke Lu, Ruichao Niu, Min Xu
papers.abstract: For two even integers $r_1\leq r_2$, a graph $G$ of even order is \emph{2-DCC edge $[r_1,r_2]$-bipancyclic} if for every ordered pair $(e,f)$ of independent edges and every even integer $\ell\in[r_1,r_2]$, there exist two vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1$ and $C_2$ with $V(C_1)\cup V(C_2)=V(G)$, $|C_1|=\ell$, $|C_2|=|V(G)|-\ell$, $e\in E(C_1)$, and $f\in E(C_2)$. We study this property for Cartesian products $G=H_1\square\cdots\square H_d$ with $d\geq2$, where each factor is $K_2$ or an even-order bipartite edge-Hamiltonian graph. We prove that $G$ is 2-DCC edge $[4,|V(G)|/2]$-bipancyclic whenever $d\geq4$, and also for $d\in\{2,3\}$ under explicit Hamiltonian-cycle conditions on $H_i$. Here $1\leq i\leq d$. As applications, we give sharp characterizations for undirected toroidal meshes, star-cube networks, and hyperstar networks.

papers.title: The Hibi-Li Face-Number Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the face-number conjecture of Hibi and Li: for every finite poset, the order polytope has no more faces of any given dimension than the chain polytope. More generally, the face numbers increase weakly along the admissible family of chain--order polytopes when one order coordinate is replaced by a chain coordinate. We also prove that, unless the order and chain polytopes are unimodularly equivalent, all face-number inequalities in dimensions $2,\ldots,|P|-1$ are strict.

papers.title: Constraints on admissible behavior of GMRES applied to tridiagonal Toeplitz systems
papers.abstract: The result of Greenbaum, Pt\'ak, and Strako\v{s} that for a given set of eigenvalues, any convergence curve is possible [SIMAX 1996] and the subsequent parameterization of such matrix-right-hand side pairs $(A,\mathbf{b})$ of Arioli, Pt\'ak, and Strako\v{s} [BIT 1998] demonstrated that the behavior of the GMRES could not be completely characterized by the eigenvalues of $A$ alone. In this paper, we consider how to use this theory to understand the admissible and attainable \gmres behavior for matrices with constrained structure, focussing on non-Hermitian (non-symmetric) tridiagonal Toeplitz matrices. We show that Toeptliz structure necessarily constrains the how the theory from these papers can manifest but that a continuum of admissible behaviors is still attainable.

papers.title: The Smoothability of Embedded Surfaces in 4-Manifolds Under Stabilizations
papers.abstract: We study the smooth stabilization number of a locally flat embedded surface in a smooth $4$-manifold, defined as the minimum number of connected sums with $S^2\times S^2$ needed to make the surface topologically isotopic to a smooth embedding. We prove that a nonsmoothable locally flat surface in a closed, simply connected smooth $4$-manifold becomes smoothable after a single stabilization if its homology class is primitive and noncharacteristic and its complement has abelian fundamental group. This yields infinitely many examples of nonsmoothable surfaces with smooth stabilization number one. We also exhibit examples for which a single stabilization produces infinitely many pairwise smoothly nonisotopic representatives in the same topological isotopy class. In contrast, we construct a locally flat genus-eight surface representing $6h$ in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ whose smooth stabilization number is exactly two. More generally, we show that smooth stabilization numbers of locally flat embedded surfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ are unbounded.

papers.title: Minimal Products via Weighted Spheres
papers.abstract:
We establish an exact composition principle for spherical immersions coupled through coefficient profiles and norm-preserving bilinear maps. Under explicit mixed orthogonality, the spherical mean curvature vector splits into orthogonal input and profile contributions. The composition is minimal if and only if every input is minimal and the profile is $W$-minimal for the induced monomial weight. Tensor iteration allows weighted profiles to serve as inputs in further compositions.
  At fixed weights, Hsiang--Lawson reduction and Kapouleas--McGrath doubling yield closed embedded $W$-minimal profiles. When the effective exponents tend to infinity in positive limiting proportions, Gaussian transfer produces interior coefficient profiles from closed embedded self-shrinkers that are nondegenerate modulo rotations. The number of distinct corresponding profiles is bounded below by the Lusternik--Schnirelmann category of the rotation orbit.

papers.title: A gluing construction of $Z$-extremal K\"ahler metrics and new examples of Bismut Hermitian-Einstein $3$-folds
papers.authors: Vestislav Apostolov, Abdellah Lahdili, Kuan-Hui Lee, Fr\'ed\'eric Rochon
papers.abstract: We present a gluing construction for a class of 6th order geometric non-linear PDE's on a K\"ahler manifold or orbifold, arising in the study of Bismut Hermitian Einstein complex $3$-folds, the supersymmetric supergravity models in physics, and in Dervan's Z-critical K\"ahler metrics. As applications, we obtain a desingularization theorem for orbifolds with crepant singularities admitting a solution of the PDE, as well as a blowing-up of points theorem for smooth complex $3$-folds admitting such solutions. These results yield new examples of regular Bismut Hermitian Einstein structures on the smooth manifolds $3(S^2\times S^4)\sharp 4(S^3\times S^3)$, $5(S^2\times S^4)\sharp 6(S^3\times S^3)$ and $S^1\times 9(S^2\times S^3)$, as well as infinite topological types of smooth compact $7$-dimensional manifolds $Y_7$, providing new solutions to the supersymmetric ${\rm AdS}_3 \times Y_7$ type IIB and ${\rm AdS}_2 \times T^2 \times Y^7$ type $D=11$ supergravity models.

papers.title: A Functional Central Limit Theorem for Locally Stationary Time Series in Banach Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish a functional central limit theorem for locally stationary time series in a separable Banach space $B$. The result requires no type-2 or cotype assumptions and thus covers spaces central to functional data analysis, such as $C([0,1])$ and $L^p([0,1])$. Under moment conditions, summable physical dependence coefficients and a bracketing entropy condition controlling the infinite-dimensional tails, the centered partial sum process converges weakly in $D([0,1],B)$ to a centered Gaussian process, whose covariance is the integrated local long-run covariance, an element of the projective tensor product. We also obtain a stochastic integral representation with respect to a cylindrical Brownian motion. As the limit depends on the unknown long-run covariance, we prove consistency of a block multiplier bootstrap for the partial sum process. This yields CUSUM tests for a constant mean of the full process, based on arbitrary continuous seminorms and valid under a time-varying long-run covariance. For linear projections, we derive a self-normalized test with a pivotal limit. In simulations, the supremum norm test detects localized changes that its $L^2$ counterpart largely misses, and applications to EEG and temperature data illustrate the methodology. Examples in $C([0,1])$ and $W^{1,p}_0([0,1])$ show how the entropy condition can be verified.

papers.title: Smallest quotients and profinite rigidity of irreducible spherical type Artin groups
papers.authors: Federica Gavazzi, Igor Haladjian, Luis Paris
papers.abstract: We prove that irreducible spherical type Artin groups are profinitely rigid within the class of all spherical type Artin groups. As part of the proof, building on ideas of Kolay for the $n$-strand braid group, we compute the smallest non-abelian quotient of every spherical type Artin group. In particular, given an irreducible spherical type Artin group, its smallest non-abelian quotient is always that of the corresponding Coxeter group, except for dihedral Artin groups of weight divisible by $4$, which all have $\mathfrak S_3$ as a non-abelian quotient. Parts of the proof also rely on the computation of the cohomological dimension of the profinite completion of certain Artin groups.

papers.title: Poincar\'e's Inequality on Sliding-Window Occupation Count Kernels and the Optimal Normalized Spectral-Gap Constant
papers.abstract:
Let $P$ be an irreducible reversible Markov kernel on an $m$-state space $\Omega$, and denote its right spectral gap by $\Gap(P) =1-\lambda_2(P)$. For a stationary trajectory, let $K_t$ be the occupation-count vector of the length-$n$ window beginning at time $t$. The stationary pair $(K_0,K_1)$ defines a reversible projected count kernel $\widetilde P_n$. For each fixed $m\ge2$, define \[
  c_m^\star=
  \inf_{\substack{|\Omega|=m,\ P\ \mathrm{irreducible\ and\ reversible}
  n\ge2}}
  \frac{n\Gap(\widetilde P_n)}{\Gap(P)}. \] We prove \[
  \frac1{1080m}\le c_m^\star\le q_{m-2},
  \qquad
  q_0=\frac14,\quad q_{r+1}=q_r(1-q_r). \] We also show $q_{m-2}=(m+\log m+O(1))^{-1}$, which implies that $c_m^\star=\Theta(m^{-1})$. Thus, the reciprocal optimal comparison coefficient $C_m^{\mathrm{opt}}=(c_m^\star)^{-1}$ is of the order $m$. In the two-state case, we determine the exact values $c_2^\star=1/4$ and $C_2^{\mathrm{opt}}=4$. %the exact constants for $m\ge3$ remain open. The lower bound also holds for $n=1$ and is uniform in $P$, including sparse and periodic kernels. The proof combines short-window decorrelation with an averaged anchor-excursion decomposition, a Green-kernel hitting estimate, and a stopped Carleson--Hardy inequality. A nested rare-state construction produces finite $m$-state witnesses whose normalized Rayleigh quotients approach $q_{m-2}$ through an ordered sequence of limits. For every fixed finite irreducible reversible aperiodic kernel on at least two states, $\Gap(\widetilde P_n)=\Theta_P(n^{-1})$.

papers.title: Exact Traces for Vector-Valued Morrey Spaces
papers.abstract: We establish an exact trace theorem for vector-valued time-Morrey spaces and complementary continuity theorems for time-BMO evolution classes. For a Banach couple $X_1\hookrightarrow X_0$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<\lambda<1$, we prove that the trace of the class $u\in\mathcal M^{p,\lambda}(X_1)$, $u_t\in\mathcal M^{p,\lambda}(X_0)$ is exactly $(X_0,X_1)_{\theta,\infty}$, where $\theta=1-(1-\lambda)/p$. A constructive extension realizes every admissible trace, and counterexamples establish optimality of both the smoothness exponent and the weak fine index. Time-BMO control yields continuous finite-index interpolation traces and, under a mixed boundedness hypothesis, a logarithmic time modulus whose base-space logarithm is necessary. For the quadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation on the torus, we characterize the bounded initial data generating Morrey-regular solutions by the exact Besov condition $u_0\in B_{2,\infty}^{2\theta}$. The proof uses Hopf--Cole linearization and a direct composition argument, and requires no smallness assumption. Lacunary nonlinear solutions realize the sharp trace threshold. A forced Hamilton--Jacobi example exhibits genuinely logarithmic time regularity, and a forward--backward mean-field-game system illustrates initial and terminal trace compatibility. \par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} Morrey spaces; trace spaces; real interpolation; Hamilton--Jacobi equations; bounded mean oscillation.

papers.title: The geometry of solutions to the general sextic
papers.abstract: We study the geometry of the three simplest known formulas for roots of a general sextic polynomial. In contrast with work of Green on the quintic, we show that no "simultaneous uniformization" of the normal forms associated to the solutions exists. This demonstrates an intrinsic qualitative complexity of sextic equations that is not present in quintic equations. Additionally, we give a formula for the roots of a general sextic in terms of Hilbert modular cusp forms and the uniformizing differential equation of the associated Hilbert modular surface.

papers.title: 3GPP-Compatible Long-Range Sensing for LEO-ISAC: A Window-Grid Processing Framework
papers.authors: Yi Geng, Xun Fan, Chenfeng Xu, Yu Zhao
papers.abstract: This paper addresses long-range sensing in bistatic low-Earth-orbit integrated sensing and communication (LEO-ISAC). Conventional OFDM sensing fails in LEO-ISAC because millisecond-scale propagation delays destroy the transmitter--receiver symbol alignment and, with multiple targets, make the receive window longer than the transmitted block. We propose a window-grid (WG) processing framework that exploits the known beam-intersection swath to resolve both problems purely at the receiver, leaving the 3GPP symbol structure unmodified: the swath delay span is folded into cyclic-prefix-sized slices, each handled by one WG. With 103.2 MHz bandwidth at bistatic ranges beyond 640 km, simulations demonstrate meter-level ranging of two targets, and 1000 Monte-Carlo trials over random target--satellite geometries show that, with an ephemeris-based satellite-selection rule, every target is detected with a 90th-percentile range error of 2.4 m.

papers.title: Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conjecture
papers.authors: Max Aires, Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak, Greta Panova
papers.abstract: The balance constant is a poset parameter measuring how well random linear extensions can be split according to their relative order on two elements. We give an $\varepsilon$-improvement for the balance constant over the bound by Brightwell, Felsner and Trotter (1995), for some small $\varepsilon>0$. This is the first general result towards the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ conjecture in over 30 years.

papers.title: Bounds for Unions of Several Parts in Balanced Graph Partitions
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge3$ and $1\le \ell\le k-1$. We study balanced $k$-partitions of a graph for which the union of any $\ell$ parts induces few edges. We show that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges admits a balanced partition $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ such that \begin{equation*} \max_{\substack{A\in\binom{[k]}{\ell}}}e_G\left(\bigcup_{i\in A}V_i\right)\le\frac{\ell^2}{k^2}m+\frac{\ell^2(k-\ell)}{k^2}(n-1)+\frac{\ell(k-\ell)}{k(k-1)}\sqrt{\left(\binom{k}{\ell}-1\right)m}. \end{equation*} In the case $\ell=2$, our result confirms a conjecture of Bollob\'as and Scott in a stronger form.

papers.title: Discrete Mixed Quantization for Cat Maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a mixed quantization technique for graph vector bundles that combines semiclassical analysis and quantum cat maps. We apply it to study the Kesten--McKay law and quantum ergodicity.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Localised Moments of Automorphic $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In this article, we describe a method to obtain lower bounds for the $2k$-th moment of values of $L$-functions localised at the central point for all real $k > 0$. In particular, for the families of quadratic twists of self-dual irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representations of $\operatorname{GL}_D(\mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}})$ with $D\in\{2,3,4\}$, our results are new in the range $0<k<\tfrac12$ when $D\in\{2,3\}$, and new for all $k>0$ when $D=4$.

papers.title: A short proof of Bernstein's theorem via the Omori--Yau maximum principle
papers.authors: Luis J. Alias, Miguel A. Mero\~no
papers.abstract: We give a short, self-contained proof of Bernstein's theorem: every entire minimal graph in $R^3$ is a plane. The only global tool is the Omori-Yau maximum principle, which holds on entire minimal graphs with their induced metric. We apply it exactly once to a single explicit function $F$ built from the surface's angle function and principal curvatures. A pointwise differential inequality for $F$, combined with the Omori-Yau principle, forces it to attain its minimum value everywhere, which yields the planarity of the surface and hence Bernstein's theorem. As a by-product of our approach, we show that the same method, with a different function and with some extra work, also proves in a simple and self-contained way the generalization of Bernstein's theorem given by Osserman that a complete minimal surface in $R^3$ whose normals omit a neighbourhood of some direction must be a plane.

papers.title: Omega bounds for the Piltz divisor problem
papers.abstract: We improve our earlier omega bounds for the error term in the Piltz divisor problem over number fields. Our proof uses a weighted extension of a counting theorem of Balasubramanian and Ramachandra and an extension of Lamzouri's kernel to apply the long resonance method. We also discuss applications of our results to lattice points in norm-form regions, invariant sublattices, abelian covers of curves, spectral counting, and representation growth of Heisenberg groups.

papers.title: Uniqueness of four-body convex central configurations for all masses
papers.abstract: We prove that for every choice of four positive masses and every cyclic ordering of the bodies there is exactly one strictly convex planar central configuration with that ordering, up to similarity. This proves a conjecture of Albouy, Fu and Sun, also called the Sim\'o-Yoccoz conjecture, and answers Problem 10 in the list of Albouy, Cabral and Santos. Uniqueness follows by a covering argument from the nondegeneracy of these configurations. We prove nondegeneracy by hand: Dziobek's relations reduce it to an eigenvalue bound for a $2\times2$ matrix that depends only on the shape of the configuration. As consequences, every degenerate planar four-body central configuration is concave, and the known symmetry theorems for kites, isosceles trapezoids and rhombi follow in a few lines.

papers.title: A new proof of characteristic-free Kn\"orrer periodicity
papers.abstract: Let $R = S/(f)$ be a complete local hypersurface ring and let $A = S[\![u,v]\!]/(f+uv)$. Pfister and Popescu showed that the stable categories of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules over $R$ and over $A$ are equivalent, with no assumption on the characteristic. We give a short proof. If $(\Phi,\Psi)$ is a matrix factorization of $h$ and $\partial$ is a derivation, then $(\partial\Psi,\partial\Phi)$ is a null-homotopy for multiplication by $\partial h$. Since $u$ and $v$ are partial derivatives of $f+uv$, they act as zero on the stable category of $A$, so the Koszul complex on $u$ and $v$ splits in the singularity category, and this gives density. For the double branched cover $S[\![z]\!]/(f+z^2)$ the same argument yields $2z$: it recovers Kn\"orrer's lemma up to free summands on the double branched cover when $2$ is a unit, and we show by an example that this lemma, and periodicity for the iterated double branched cover $S[\![z,w]\!]/(f+z^2+w^2)$, fail in characteristic two. We also compute the second syzygy over $A$ of a maximal Cohen-Macaulay $R$-module by an explicit resolution, and show that the change of basis used there cannot be given by a universal matrix formula.

papers.title: Coded Computing for Dynamic System via Cartesian Products
papers.authors: Chenglin Li, Minquan Cheng, Youlong Wu
papers.abstract: Coded distributed computing (CDC) mitigates the Shuffle communication bottleneck through coded multicast, but existing schemes with predetermined worker populations do not directly adapt to worker arrivals and disconnections. To address these dynamics, we propose a dynamic CDC scheme that preserves surviving workers' caches and Reduce assignments while exploiting the storage brought by arriving clusters. The model accommodates general MapReduce tasks under a placement that is partly fixed and partly new. The scheme uses Cartesian products of cluster-wise placement delivery arrays (PDAs) for file placement. A delivery-aware greedy algorithm reassigns abandoned Reduce functions, and a Communication Array allows workers with no Reduce function to serve as coded transmitters. For arbitrary feasible disconnections, the scheme's exact communication load is derived. A converse bound under one-shot communication shows that, in the absence of disconnections, the scheme lies within a factor of 2 of the lower bound under these assumptions when new clusters arrive, and within a factor of 4 otherwise.

papers.title: Optimal Universal Coding of Integers
papers.authors: Wei Yan, Yunghsiang S. Han, Leqian Zheng
papers.abstract: Universal coding of integers (UCI) provides prefix codes for positive integers such that, for every nonincreasing source distribution $P$, the average codeword length under $P$ stays within $K$ times $\max\{1,H(P)\}$. For a given UCI $\mathcal{C}$, the smallest such constant $K$ is called the minimum expansion factor of $\mathcal{C}$, denoted $C_{\mathcal{C}}^{*}$. Let $C^{*}\triangleq \inf \{C_{\mathcal{C}}^{*}\}$ over all UCIs. A UCI attaining $C^{*}$, or a family of UCIs attaining $C^{*}$ in the limit, is called optimal. It is currently known that $2\le C^{*}\le 2.0386$. In this paper, we construct a family of one-point plus uniform-tail distributions and prove that, for every UCI, a distribution in this family attains the worst-case ratio; thus, the family is least favorable for the UCI problem. We further establish an inequality, called the \emph{UCI inequality}, which plays the same role for UCI as the Kraft inequality does for prefix codes: for any real number $B\ge 1$, it decides whether $B$ lies below or above $C^*$. The UCI inequality gives an equivalent definition of $C^*$. By numerical computation, we determine $C^* = 2.00012475703610197861701176297579886254\cdots$, the first $38$ decimal digits being certified. Once $C^*$ is known, we can theoretically construct the optimal UCI.

papers.title: Sections, pseudosections, and multisections of Lefschetz fibrations
papers.abstract: We show that not every symplectic Lefschetz fibration over the $2$--sphere admits a smooth section, settling a long-standing open problem. To prove this, we develop a method for studying sections via lifts of monodromy factorizations with point-pushing maps and the induced handle decomposition of the total space, and apply it to an infinite family of Lefschetz fibrations. In contrast, we show that every Lefschetz fibration over $S^2$ admits positive multisections. Some of these examples admit no multisections with spherical components. We also construct signature-zero Lefschetz fibrations of every odd genus $g\geq 7$, which in turn give symplectic Lefschetz fibrations of any prescribed signature in each of these genera.

papers.title: Flow Matching for Fast Posterior Sampling in Bayesian Inverse Problems
papers.authors: Jan Blechschmidt, Oliver G. Ernst, Moritz Poguntke, Bj\"orn Sprungk
papers.abstract: Sampling from the posterior is the central task of computational Bayesian inverse problems. The standard workhorse in Bayesian inference---Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)---is sequential, yields correlated samples, and must be rerun for each new observation. Conditional flow matching offers an amortized alternative: a transport map, trained once on joint samples of parameter and data, that yields independent approximate posterior samples for any observation at negligible online cost, without new likelihood evaluations. We give a careful, MCMC-literate assessment of flow matching for PDE-based inverse problems with function-valued parameters. Exploiting the flow's tractable density, we derive computable accuracy estimates for the learned posterior in total variation distance and Kullback--Leibler divergence and, moreover, propose a hybrid sampler that is made asymptotically exact by Metropolization. We validate the accuracy estimates and demonstrate amortization in several numerical examples, including electrical impedance tomography and a likelihood-free Lotka--Volterra model. Flow matching reproduces posterior means and credible bands closely at a fraction of the forward solves required by MCMC, but its accuracy degrades for concentrated posteriors and for observations that are atypical under the prior.

papers.title: Classification of commutation relation for multi-chordal SLE
papers.authors: Mo Chen, Chongzhi Huang, Hao Wu
papers.abstract:
We classify the linear solution spaces of the chordal Belavin--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (BPZ) equations, which arise in Dub\'edat's commutation relations for multiple Schramm--Loewner evolutions (SLE). Without imposing growth conditions, we determine the subspaces selected by successive conformal Ward identities and their exact dimensions. For every $\kappa>0$ and BPZ spectral parameter $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$, we determine the spectrum and Jordan structure of the translation operator. When $\lambda=0$ and $\kappa\in(0,8)$, we further determine all admissible scaling exponents and the dimensions of the corresponding translation-invariant solution spaces. A triangular change of derivative coordinates yields a first-order system of rational Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov type, allowing us to represent the Ward operators explicitly and reduce the classification to finite-dimensional linear algebra.
  For $2N$ boundary points and $\kappa\in(0,8)$, translation-invariant BPZ solutions with $\lambda=0$ and the homogeneity required by M\"obius covariance automatically satisfy the third Ward identity and the usual power-law bound. This recovers, under weaker assumptions, the Catalan dimension formula previously established by Flores and Kleban. At $\kappa=8$, the third Ward identity imposes an additional constraint when $N\ge2$, but the full M\"obius-covariant solution space still has Catalan dimension, establishing completeness of the partition functions constructed from uniform spanning trees. Finally, at $\kappa=4$ and $\lambda>0$, we construct an explicit basis of positive BPZ solutions and identify its elements as partition functions for level lines of a Gaussian free field with suitable harmonic means.

papers.title: GPU-Accelerated Bregman Douglas-Rachford Splitting for Discrete Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: We present GPU-accelerated Bregman Douglas--Rachford splitting algorithm (BDRS) for discrete optimal transport problem in three input formats: an explicit cost matrix, a point cloud with a ground cost between them, and a separable cost on a regular grid. For each input format, we propose hardware-aware designs of mathematically equivalent representations for the BDRS iterations to enhance numerical stability and empirical runtime. We benchmark the three proposed implementations against eight GPU baseline solvers from the literature on the same device. We demonstrate that our implementations of BDRS achieve state-of-the-art performance on their respective input formats. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first cross-solver study of GPU DOT solvers with a unified measure of optimality.

papers.title: Scalar curvature bounds and tangent cones for K\"ahler--Ricci shrinkers
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform scalar curvature bound, depending only on the dimension, for K\"ahler--Ricci shrinkers. We also prove that every noncompact K\"ahler--Ricci shrinker has a unique tangent cone at infinity, naturally homeomorphic to the base of its polarized Fano fibration. For shrinkers with maximal volume growth, this cone is isometric to the metric completion of the regular part equipped with the intrinsic distance induced by the limiting K\"ahler metric.

papers.title: Radii of Starlikeness of Spirallike Functions
papers.abstract: A normalized analytic function $f$ defined on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ is called $\alpha$-spirallike if $f(\mathbb{D})$ is an $\alpha$-spirallike domain, that is, for every $z\in f(\mathbb{D})$, the $\alpha$-spiral $ze^{-e^{i\alpha}t}$, $t\ge0$, is contained in $f(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(e^{i\alpha} {zf'(z)}/{f(z)}\right)>0$ for all $z\in \mathbb{D}$. The 0-spirallike functions are the usual starlike functions. The function $f$ is parabolic starlike, if $\operatorname{Re}\!\left(\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}\right)>\left|\frac{zf'(z)}{f(z)}-1\right|$, and lemniscate starlike if $|(zf'(z)/f(z))^2-1|<1$ respectively. In this paper, we determine the radii of parabolic starlikeness and lemniscate starlikeness of $\alpha$-spirallike functions. Our approach combines geometric characterizations of the underlying regions with the resultant method for eliminating auxiliary variables, leading to explicit equations for the sharp radii. Some known radius results are recovered as special cases.

papers.title: Refinements on the Restriction and Kakeya problems range in $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: We obtain improved Fourier restriction and Kakeya maximal estimates in $\mathbb R^4$. More precisely, by proving the two-ends incidence estimates $\mathbf{TE}\left(\frac{269}{89},\frac{179}{89},\frac{493}{534}\right)$ and $\mathbf{TE}(3.06\ldots,3.06\ldots,0.94\ldots)$, we extend the restriction range to $p>2+ \frac{356}{447}$ and the Kakeya maximal estimate up to dimension $3.06056$. The implications to the known lower-bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and the Bochner--Riesz conjecture are also studied.

papers.title: A Converse to the Archimedes Sphere Theorem
papers.authors: Mohammad Ghomi, Ralph Howard, Mijia Lai
papers.abstract: We show that a convex surface in Euclidean 3-space is a sphere if the area cut off from it by a slab of some fixed width depends only on the direction of the slab. This result generalizes theorems of Blaschke and Stamm, which assumed the slab-area property for every width. It holds also for any smooth closed embedded surface, and we obtain analogous results in higher dimensions. The proof is based on an averaging identity, which relates slab areas to the Newtonian potential of the surface, the electrostatic characterization of spheres by Mendez and Reichel, and analytic microlocal properties of the Radon transform, which are used to show that the slab-area property forces real analyticity, via theorems of Kashiwara and Boman.

papers.title: Webs and finite dimensional representation theory for quantum symmetric pairs
papers.abstract: We develop a highest weight framework and construct explicit finite dimensional irreducible modules for the type AIII (quasi split) quantum symmetric pair subalgebras $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$. In Part 1, we provide a uniform construction of Cartan subalgebras and Verma modules for both subfamilies. Our construction recovers Letzter's Cartan subalgebra in one subfamily and gives a new Cartan subalgebra in the other. We construct a weak triangular decomposition of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$ via the Letzter map. Then we define Verma modules as induced modules and prove that finite dimensional simple $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$-modules are quotients of our Verma modules. In Part 2, we define a diagrammatic category $Web^B$ that controls polynomial representations of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$. We prove a multiplicity-free decomposition of the quantum exterior powers $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$ as a $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$-module, using a explicit eigenspace decomposition of certain dot morphisms in $Web^B$. As applications, we deduce the multiplicity-freeness of the involved anti-spherical Hecke module. For $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$, we explicitly determine the highest weight vectors and their weights, thereby determining the isomorphism classes of their irreducible summands. Finally, we determine the kernel of the $Web^B$-action on certain finite dimensional representation category of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$.

papers.title: Coanalytic subfields and bases of prescribed dimension
papers.abstract: Assume $V=L$. We prove two uniform theorems producing coanalytic sets of prescribed Hausdorff dimension in Euclidean space. The first concerns countable families of partial operations of finite arity on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose evaluation is hyperarithmetic and which are tame in each vector variable separately. For such families a single lightface $\Pi^1_1$ relation yields strictly increasing, left-continuous chains of proper sets closed under the operations, one of each Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$, uniformly in the family and in $n$; no exchange property of the closure is needed. As an application, there are coanalytic proper subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,1]$. The second theorem constructs coanalytic bases of every possible Hausdorff dimension for effectively coded pregeometries. As an application, there are coanalytic Hamel bases of $\mathbb{R}^n$ and transcendence bases of $\mathbb{C}$ of every Hausdorff dimension in $[0,n]$ and $[0,2]$, respectively.

papers.title: Long intervals of consecutive composite values of polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $f\in\mathbb Q[t]$ be an irreducible integer-valued polynomial of positive degree with positive leading coefficient. We show that there is a constant $c_f>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large real $X$, the interval $(X/2,X]$ contains a block of at least $c_f\log X\log\log X$ consecutive integers $n$ for which $f(n)$ is composite. The exponent of $\log\log X$ does not depend on the degree of $f$. This improves a result of Ford and Gabdullin, replacing a small fixed power of $\log\log X$ by $\log\log X$. The result includes the case $f(t)=t^2+1$.

papers.title: A shape theorem for a radially excited random walk in dimensions $d \ge 2$
papers.abstract:
NOTE (October 2026): This paper has been superseded by the joint paper "Limit shapes for centrally excited walks", by Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Tuan-Minh Nguyen, Yuval Peres and Arvind Singh (arXiv:2610.10162), which brings together the results and ideas of three independent drafts.
  We consider a once-excited random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d \ge 2$, where the walk on its first visit has a bias of constant strength $\beta>0$ toward the origin and moves like a simple symmetric random walk on subsequent visits to that site. We show that the walk is recurrent and prove an almost sure spherical shape theorem: the trace after $n$ steps is asymptotically a Euclidean ball centered at the origin, with radius proportional to $n^{1/(d+1)}$, and the local times have an asymptotically conical profile. This result confirms a conjecture of Kozma (2007) on the shape of the trace for this model.

papers.title: Measure Theory in Convergence Spaces Part I: Sion-Carath\'eodory Extension in Net Convergence Groups
papers.abstract: We study extension of additive measures when the range carries a prescribed separated Abelian net convergence. On a $\sigma$-complete, lattice-$\sigma$-continuous pseudo-D-lattice, we prove an uncontrolled modular extension theorem using finite-response reflection, closed countable summation and uniform closure. Completeness is imposed only on the limit-stable hull of the source values. No topology, lattice order or positive control is required in its range. Modular interval identities, an order-null separation argument and two uniform transfer arguments construct the extension before establishing its normality. A separate relative lifting theorem combines this modular construction with a nonmodular Sasaki argument. Its cone conditions are verified for positive lattice-group values, lattice-normed groups, products and limit-stable subgroups. These verifications give explicit positive, dominated lattice-normed and topological corollaries. Uniqueness holds among all sigma-additive extensions to the generated domain. Sion's inner and outer nets exist in the original convergence and recover the extension there. For Boolean domains we retain the stronger identification with the full regulated splitting class and the finite-variation and finite-semivariation results.

papers.title: Gaussian inequalities with different covariance matrices - the Heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality
papers.authors: Emanuel Milman, Shohei Nakamura, Hiroshi Tsuji
papers.abstract:
We establish the following novel heterovariant Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality (involving general covariance matrices $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2,\Gamma$) for origin-symmetric convex sets $K,L \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ and $p,\lambda \in (0,1)$: \[
  \gamma_{\Sigma_1}(K)^{1-p} \gamma_{\Sigma_2}(L)^p
  \le
  \left( \left( \frac{1-p}{1-\lambda} \right)^{1-p} \left( \frac{p}{\lambda} \right)^p \right)^{n}
  \gamma_{\Gamma}((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L) , \] whenever $\Gamma \leq \Sigma_1 \sharp_p \Sigma_2$, the $p$-geometric mean of $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$. This immediately implies both the dimensional Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality of Eskenazis-Moschidis (by using $\Sigma_1 = \Sigma_2 = \Gamma$ and optimizing over $p$) and the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem of Cordero-Erausquin-Fradelizi-Maurey (by using $K=L$, $p=\lambda$ and diagonal covariances), fusing them into a single unified statement. In fact, the inequality applies to convex sets whose appropriate Gaussian barycenter is at the origin. Furthermore, it reveals a new *bilinear* version of the strong Gaussian (B)-theorem (involving *two* convex sets); in particular, for all $a,b > 0$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$: \[ \gamma(a K)^{1-\lambda} \gamma(b L)^{\lambda} \leq \gamma \left ( a^{1-\lambda} b^\lambda \left ((1-\lambda) K + \lambda L \right) \right ) . \] A more general heterovariant version of the (bilinear) (B)-theorem replaces dilation by general linear transformations. A different version yields a heterovariant form of the recently established Gaussian conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequality. By averaging these Gaussian inequalities with respect to the covariance matrices, we obtain dimensional Brunn-Minkowski and conjugate Rogers-Shephard inequalities for Gaussian mixtures. The proofs are based on the Gaussian Forward-Reverse Brascamp-Lieb inequality established in our previous work.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of radial bound states with prescribed number of nodes for nonlinear dispersive equations on spherically symmetric manifolds
papers.abstract: Standing waves $e^{i\omega t}u(x)$ of nonlinear dispersive equations, such as the nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations, have a profile $u$ that solves the semilinear elliptic equation $\Delta u+f(u)=0$. We prove the existence of radial bound states with a prescribed number of nodal surfaces for this equation on a large class of spherically symmetric manifolds and for a broad class of nonlinearities $f$. Under further assumptions on the metric, we prove uniqueness of such bound states for the model nonlinearity $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u-u$. Both existence and uniqueness results apply to the hyperbolic spaces $\mathbb{H}^n_\lambda$ of any curvature $-\lambda^2$ and dimension $n\geq 3$, and to some manifolds with a singularity at the origin.

papers.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
papers.abstract: Let $\Lambda_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteq\Lambda_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $\Lambda_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $\Lambda_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partial\Lambda_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question was left open in the previous versions; it has since been settled, $\Lambda_4=S_4$, by a computer-assisted proof of L. Marshall, after an earlier claim by D.Z. Liu, who also proved that $\Lambda_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{\pi^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $\Lambda_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

papers.title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
papers.abstract: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.

papers.title: Global solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations in the half-space and exterior domains
papers.authors: Hairong Liu, Jinlong Wu, Hua Zhong
papers.abstract: We study the initial boundary value problem for the compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson equations without damping in the three-dimensional half-space and in smooth exterior domains. The velocity satisfies the no-slip boundary condition, and the electric potential satisfies the homogeneous Neumann boundary condition. For small perturbations of a constant state in $H^3$, with a small initial electric field in $L^2$, we establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The uniform estimates combine density dissipation, tangential and normal derivative estimates, and a modified energy expressed through the Helmholtz projection. In exterior domains, boundary normal coordinates and localized elliptic estimates control the geometric terms. We also obtain algebraic decay in the full energy norm. In the half-space, finite tangential negative Sobolev norms of order $-s$, with $\frac12\leq s<1$, yield the rate $(1+t)^{-s/2}$. In exterior domains, integrable initial density and velocity perturbations yield the same form of estimate for $0<s<\frac14$. The exterior decay proof uses whole-space negative-order estimates for localized variables and the time integrability of the dissipation.

papers.title: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture after OpenAI
papers.abstract: We provide a simplified and more human-friendly version of the proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture recently given by OpenAI.

papers.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
papers.abstract: Combining local boundary analysis, algebraic curves and the computational statements specified in the appendix, we prove that the planar Newtonian five-body problem has finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling for every choice of positive masses. This gives the five-body statement of Smale's sixth problem. We use the singular-sequence classification of Albouy and Kaloshin and resolve the corresponding boundary equations through weighted blow-up charts, rank calculations and local compatibility conditions. For the two remaining diagrams, we prove that the product $\Delta$ of all squared mutual distances vanishes. On a hypothetical solution curve containing a positive arc, a pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $\Delta$. A pole of $\Delta$ elsewhere on the completed curve, together with $\Delta^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$, then contradicts the same local vanishing result. The computational statements for Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 involve exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.

papers.title: Log Density Spectrum Based Decoding of Polar Codes for Channels with Strong Phase Noise
papers.abstract: A decoding method is proposed for polar codes under channels with strong phase noise. In contrast to traditional SC decoding, where recursions are performed on scalar soft information such as probabilities, the proposed decoding recurses over probability density functions defined on the phase-noise variable. To make the density-level recursion computationally tractable, we represent each log-density by its spectrum, and derive approximate formulas for the spectrum recursion, therefore, the proposed method is termed log-density spectrum recursion (LDSR). Numerical results are given under strong phase noise and AWGN, showing that a prominent superiority of error performance is achieved by LDSR in comparison with traditional SC and Kalman-based methods.

papers.title: A Feasible Direction Method with Active-Set Identification for Derivative-Free Optimization
papers.authors: Jeffrey Larson, Matt Menickelly, Lara Zebiane
papers.abstract: We propose a model-based trust region method for derivative-free optimization with simulation-based inequality constraints. We are motivated by settings of simulation optimization in which both function evaluations at infeasible points may be unreliable and constraint evaluations are expensive. Our method maintains feasible incumbents and computes steps from a subproblem suitable for a feasible-direction method in order to encourage generation of feasible trial points. To reduce the computational cost of modeling the constraints, we describe an active-set estimation scheme that permits modeling with only a subset of constraints in each subproblem, as opposed to maintaining models of all constraints. We show that every limit point of the incumbents generated by our method is a Fritz-John point, and is additionally a KKT point under the Mangasarian-Fromovitz constraint qualification. Under standard nondegeneracy conditions, the active-set estimate identifies, within finite time, all constraints active at the limit point of the incumbents. Experiments on CUTEst problems show that our method generates feasible trial points more often than a comparable SQP-based approach and is competitive with an appropriate comparator in budgeted settings.

papers.title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
papers.authors: Bryan Bu, Fayzan Khan, Hyunjun Yi, Atharv Jha, Ishaan Chandupatla, Madhav Nagpal
papers.abstract: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers.
