While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) <= (1 + o(1))sqrt(n)/2, we construct sets achieving a leading constant of 1/2: lambda(n) <= (1/2)sqrt(n) + O(n^(1/4)sqrt(log n)), establishing limsup_{n->infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) <= 1/2. This construction combines a two-sided Sidon square identity, a Singer difference set, a Fejer-kernel majorant, a parity-biased deletion, and an exact-cardinality probabilistic selection. We also provide an L^4 criterion and a multiplicity bound constraining any construction with a smaller leading constant. In the opposite direction, we incorporate the L^1 norm into Bedert's boundary estimate with an explicit constant, yielding two lower bounds for f_A(x) = sum_{a in A} cos(ax): (1) -min f_A >= cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.

papers.title: Recovery of Rough Sources in the Inverse Monge-Amp\`ere Problem
papers.abstract:
We prove that every nonnegative $L^1$ source in the Monge-Amp\`ere equation \[
  \det D^2u=f\quad\text{in }\Omega, \] on a bounded uniformly convex $C^{1,1}$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, is uniquely determined by generalized boundary measurements of Alexandrov solutions. The measurement is the extremal boundary slope, which extends the classical outward normal derivative and may take the value $+\infty$. For each direction $\omega\in\mathbb S^{n-1}$, it suffices to know these slopes for cylindrical Dirichlet data $\frac{t_k^\omega}{2}|P_\omega x|^2$ along any sequence $t_k^\omega\to\infty$, where $P_\omega$ projects onto $\omega^\perp$. The boundary value and extremal slope determine the interior subgradient image up to a Lebesgue null set. An exact change of variables formula then converts equality of these images into integral identities for the source, and a large-amplitude limit recovers its Euclidean X-ray transform. This yields uniqueness without a positive lower bound on the source. For nonnegative $L^\infty$ sources, the extremal slopes are bounded and agree with the interior normal derivatives, giving a Dirichlet-to-interior-Neumann formulation. We also extend the inverse argument to the gradient-weighted equation \[
  \vartheta(\nabla u)\det D^2u=f, \] where the known weight $\vartheta$ is locally integrable, Borel measurable, and bounded below by a positive constant. We prove existence of the corresponding Alexandrov solutions and show that the same cylindrical boundary-slope data uniquely determine every nonnegative $L^1$ source.

papers.title: The Maximum Nonlinearity of 8-variable Balanced Boolean Functions is 116
papers.authors: Yueying Lou, Youle Xu, Qichun Wang
papers.abstract: Does there exist an 8-variable balanced Boolean function with nonlinearity 118? This is a famous and long-standing open problem in Boolean functions. In this paper, we give a negative answer to this open problem, and prove that the maximum nonlinearity of balanced Boolean functions in 8 variables is 116, establishing the 8-variable instance of Dobbertin's conjectured recursion for the minimum Walsh peak of balanced functions. Equivalently, the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,8) in 0-resilient Boolean functions is 116. We deduce the result by obtaining a quadratic form of polar rank 6, and reducing the problem to the existence of a 6-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity greater than 26 whose Hamming distance to a bent function is between 4 and 6.

papers.title: Modified support measures and Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities for nonsmooth h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
papers.abstract:
We establish the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and its modified version for arbitrary, possibly nonsmooth, horospherically convex bodies in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}, n\geq 2$, and prove that equality in each inequality holds if and only if the h-convex body is a geodesic ball. A key ingredient is a rigidity theorem characterizing geodesic balls via proportionality between modified support measures of adjacent orders. Its proof combines the $C^{1,\alpha}\cap W^{2,k+1}$ approximation of the outer parallel hypersurfaces by smooth strictly h-convex hypersurfaces with the estimates for the total variation norm of the signed measure associated with the proportionality relation along the shifted curvature flows independent of initial curvature bounds.
  For $0\leq k\leq n-1$, we construct weak flows preserving the $k$-th modified quermassintegral $\tilde{W}_k$ with arbitrary h-convex initial bodies as Hausdorff limits of the smooth flows. The rigidity theorem above characterizes the limit shape of the flow and gives a positive lower bound on the rate of decrease of $\tilde{W}_{k+1}$ for a short time whenever the initial h-convex body is not a geodesic ball, which characterizes the equality cases in the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.
  For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which characterizes the equality cases in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.

papers.title: Endpoint regularity of Radon transforms associated with real analytic phases in the plane
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the endpoint Sobolev regularity of Radon transforms associated with real-analytic functions in the plane. We establish all of the failure of endpoint regularity for real-analytic phases. On the one hand, the critical endpoint regularity $L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)\rightarrow L^p_s(\mathbb{R}^2)$, corresponding to extreme points of the reduced Newton polyhedron of phase function, is true if only and only if $p=2$. For generic extreme points, this failure of endpoint regularity generalizes a result of Christ \cite{christ}. On the other hand, we find that the endpoint Sobolev regularity also fails on a bounded segment of the reduced Newton polyhedron when the bisectrix $y=x$ intersects one of unbounded faces at a relative interior point. In particular, our results imply that the Radon transform is not bounded from $L^p$ into $L^p_{1/n}$ with $p=n/(n-1)$ or $p=n$, where the phase functions are real-valued homogeneous polynomials $S(x,y)=a_1x^{n-1}y+a_2x^{n-2}y^2+\cdots+a_{n-1}xy^{n-1}$ with $n\geq 3$ and $a_1a_{n-1}\neq0$. This answers a problem of Phong and Stein in 1994. Moreover, the main results of this paper also give examples which show failure of critical Sobolev regularity for degenerate Fourier integral operators satisfying finite type conditions formulated in \cite{Seeger93,seeger2}. Based on earlier results and our proof of several remaining cases, we conclude that all of other critical endpoint Sobolev estimates are true for Radon transforms associated with real-analytic phases in the plane. Therefore, all failures of endpoint regularity estimates are clearly determined.

papers.title: Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator on Lipschitz graphs
papers.authors: Joan Hern\'andez, Joan Mateu, Laura Prat
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calder\'on commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant.

papers.title: Semiclassical Band Splitting in the Infinite Chern Band Model
papers.abstract: We study the two lowest Bloch bands of the infinite Chern band model of Tan and Devakul in the semiclassical limit. When the Berry curvature parameter is an odd multiple of $\pi$, we show that the first two bands are exponentially close and meet at exactly one Dirac point. The proof combines Agmon estimates and WKB approximations for a matrix Schr\"odinger operator whose lowest potential eigenvalue has two wells. Geometric properties of the Agmon distance allow us to compute the leading tunneling coefficients by the method of stationary phase. We provide numerical computations to illustrate the asymptotic formula and support the conjecture that the two bands remain separated for other values of the Berry curvature parameter.

papers.title: Postnikov invariants for rational spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we construct a theory of Postnikov invariants for (complete) homotopy Lie algebras that is preserved by the integration functor of Robert-Nicoud and Vallette. This result is in the same vein as Berglund's theorem, which relates the homology groups underlying a nilpotent homotopy Lie algebra to the homotopy groups of the associated space. We then deduce an integration functor from filtered Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology groups to group cohomology groups.

papers.title: Observing minimal submanifolds with isolated singularities on open sets of metrics
papers.authors: Alessandro Carlotto, Yangyang Li, Zhihan Wang
papers.abstract: We develop a perturbative theory for minimal submanifolds with only (strongly) isolated singularities, with respect to varying background Riemannian metrics. As an application, we obtain a general "sporadic persistence" criterion, thus naturally complementing the non-persistence theorem by the authors. In particular, such a criterion is satisfied by the spherical suspension in $\mathbb{S}^{3m+2}$ of the Veronese embedding of $\mathbb{K}\mathbb{P}^2$ for $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}$ (the normed division algebras) in the round spheres of dimension $3m+1=4,7,13,25$ respectively, thereby providing families of continuously varying $(2m+1)$-dimensional stationary varifolds with isolated singularities that are observable on an open set of metrics. By our previous results, these phenomena cannot possibly occur in the codimension one scenario.

papers.title: Mahler Method and Vanishing Theorem
papers.authors: Kumiko Nishioka, Taka-aki Tanaka, Yusuke Tanuma
papers.abstract:
This paper is motivated by the recent work of Adamczewski and Faverjon [5], who established the algebraic independence of values of Mahler functions satisfying linear functional equations. While their work is a landmark result, some proofs are long and complex. The primary aim of this paper is to simplify those proofs and provide new applications.
  In their proofs, a vanishing theorem for polynomials, rather than power series, is sufficient. We give a proof of the vanishing theorem without using Szemer\'edi's theorem or Corvaja-Zannier's theorem. In the case of a single transformation, we present a refined vanishing theorem, which allows us to simplify the proof of algebraic independence. We also provide an elementary proof of a vanishing theorem for $q_i$-Mahler functions with various $q_i$.
  As an application, we prove the algebraic independence of certain continued fractions, extending previous results by Han\v{c}l, Adamczewski, and Bundschuh and V\"a\"an\"anen in which only linear independence and transcendence had been established.

papers.title: Sums of two dependent uniform random variables: a characterization by joint tail bounds
papers.abstract: Which laws can the sum of two uniform random variables have when nothing is known about how they depend on each other? For three or more uniform summands, convex order gives the answer; for two it does not, and the question has been open. We show that the attainable laws are exactly those that satisfy a family of explicit joint bounds on sums of tail probabilities, one bound for each finite set of thresholds. For laws with a density at most one, convex order alone decides. For densities at most two, convex order implies the simplest of the joint bounds, and the constant two cannot be raised for single-threshold bounds. The number of thresholds a law needs is set by the spacing of its atoms, not by how many atoms it has.

papers.title: Sharp Capacity Estimates and Volume Growth for Fractional Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract:
We obtain sharp two-sided estimates for the relative capacity of fat and thin annuli in the fractional Sobolev spaces $W^s_{p,q}$, where $s\in(0,1)$, $p\in(0,\infty)$, $q\in(0,\infty]$,
  in terms of an explicit volume growth quantity. The underlying space is a general metric measure space equipped with a doubling and reverse doubling measure. In particular, whenever the capacity is finite, the estimates are independent of the parameter $q$, and in the Ahlfors regular case with $p=q$ they recover Costea's logarithmic law at $sp=Q$. For $p<q$, we also introduce a sharp condition on the measure that is necessary for the existence of admissible functions in the space $W^s_{p,q}$. For thin annuli $(B_r,B_{r+\varepsilon r})$ under an $\eta$-annular decay property, we uncover a purely nonlocal phenomenon: for $sp <\eta$, the capacity remains bounded as $\varepsilon\to 0$, because the limiting competitor $\chi_{B_r}$ already has finite energy, while if $sp\geq\eta$ it blows up as $ \varepsilon\to0$.

papers.title: Bulk universality of scaling limits for the almost Hermitian Coulomb gas
papers.abstract: Inspired by the recent approach to edge universality of Cronvall and Wennman, we prove several local universality results for scaling limits in the bulk in the almost Hermitian regime, as well as associated results relating to reproducing kernel spaces of the Fock type.

papers.title: Energy Estimate and Convergence of Weak Solutions of a Class of Nonlinear PDEs with Robin Boundary Conditions
papers.authors: Adriana Neumann, Patr\'icia Gon\c{c}alves, Maria Chiara Ricciuti, Oslenne Ara\'ujo
papers.abstract: We establish strong convergence in $L^2([0,T]\times[0,1])$ of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear PDEs with Robin boundary conditions to weak solutions of the corresponding Neumann and Dirichlet problems as the boundary parameter $\kappa$ tends to $0$ and $\infty$, respectively. Our approach relies on a particle system whose hydrodynamic limits yield the Robin problem for each fixed $\kappa>0$. An energy estimate derived from the microscopic stochastic dynamics provides the key bounds for passing to the subsequent limits $\kappa\to0$ and $\kappa\to\infty$, thereby obtaining the Neumann and Dirichlet problems.

papers.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001, for Batyrev's mirror pairs of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and its orbifold generalization, without assuming that the lattice points in the defining reflexive polytope generate the ambient lattice. We then identify the pushforward of the extended hypersurface \(I\)-function with a generating series of normalized compact periods of the mirror, providing a period interpretation of the hypergeometric series governing ambient genus-zero orbifold Gromov--Witten theory. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.

papers.title: Zero-free half-planes for Hecke $L$-functions over number fields and Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: In [Liu26a], varying the length and moment parameters in the cubic-theta argument of [Ope26a] gave the zero-free half-plane $Re(s)>B_{\mathrm{new}}=0.874957019420098946\ldots$ for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and for Dirichlet $L$-functions, and its optimality in the specified exponent comparison system. In this paper, we extend the argument to finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $\mu_{12}$ and, by class-field descent, to every pair $(K,\eta)$ whose cyclic class field has metabelian normal closure over $\mathbb Q$, including every finite-order character over every abelian number field. Then, adapting the averaged numerator estimate developed by Xu and Sang [XS26] for Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and combining it with a limiting contradiction argument, we obtain the boundary $B_\flat=0.874886647039964\ldots$, the root near $0.8749$ of $133488B^4-376596B^3+384534B^2-167541B+26231$; it is the exact infimum of the refined comparison system, unattained by finite chains starting above it. Since the analytic argument uses only $\mu_{12}\subset F$, we run it over $F=K(\zeta_{12})$ for an arbitrary number field $K$ and descend: every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field is zero-free for $Re(s)>B_\flat$, giving a uniform Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis over number fields. The analytic argument uses the exceptional-theta constructions and local calculations of the preprint [Ope26b].

papers.title: Reverse Module Categories of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.authors: Chongying Dong, Binghui Li, Li Ren, Yilong Wang
papers.abstract: We study the realization of the reverse braided category of the module category of a rational vertex operator algebra V. Using holomorphic extensions and commutant constructions, we prove that this realization property is preserved under suitable cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds. As applications, we establish the property for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine vertex operator algebras of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, the corresponding principal W-algebras of type ADE, and related parafermion vertex operator algebras.

papers.title: Canard points in planar mass-action networks: a flux criterion, a duality, and a complete classification
papers.abstract: We determine which mass-action reaction networks on two species, one fast and one slow, admit a canard point: a singular Hopf bifurcation at a fold of the critical manifold, followed by a canard explosion. In flux coordinates, existence reduces to three linear equations, one linear inequation and a sign condition on the product of two linear forms, and the criticality of the explosion is the sign of an explicit cubic form. For four reactions with a balance matrix of full rank, both become integer polynomial conditions on the stoichiometry. A vacancy duality, which exchanges the activator--inhibitor and substrate-depletion mechanisms, preserves canard points together with their criticality. The central structural result is a mode criterion: a network has a canard point if and only if its elementary flux modes contain a sign-meeting pair and a mode carrying a fold. Hence every canard network contains a minimal one carried by at most three modes, and so by at most twelve reactions, whatever the molecularity. For complexes of molecularity at most three we enumerate all 138\,754 minimal canard networks and label each exactly by the criticalities it admits. None has more than six reactions; 32 have canard points of codimension zero and no explosion; and most six-reaction networks admit both criticalities, separated by degenerate canard points. All labels rest on certificates checked in exact rational arithmetic. Resolving the cubic steps into bimolecular ones through fast dimers keeps the canard points and changes the criticality only by an explicit term.

papers.title: Nonlocal Equations on Domains and Manifolds Without Symmetries
papers.abstract: In this work, we establish existence and regularity results for solutions to nonlinear nonlocal equations of the form $f(\Delta)u = U(x,u)$ and $f(\Delta_{g})u = U(x,u)$ in Euclidean and Riemannian settings, respectively. We prove existence results across three distinct geometric scenarios: bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, perturbed equations on compact Riemannian manifolds, and noncompact Cartan-Hadamard manifolds under suitable geometric curvature conditions.

papers.title: A New Modifications of the Milstein and Euler Methods and the Taylor-Ito Expansion for Ito Stochastic Differential Equations with Drift and Diffusion Coefficients Having Non-Differentiable or Singular Time-Dependent Multipliers
papers.abstract: The article presents a new modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods for systems of Ito stochastic differential equations with drift and diffusion coefficients having differentiable and non-differentiable or singular power-law time-dependent components (the latter depending only on the time variable). By iteratively applying Ito's formula to the mentioned differentiable components of the drift and diffusion coefficients, a new modification of the Milstein method is derived in the paper. A key feature of this modification of the Milstein method is the presence of time-dependent weight functions in the iterated Ito stochastic integrals of the second and first multiplicity (the specified weight functions are identically equal to unity in the classical Milstein method). To approximate the specified iterated Ito stochastic integrals (with respect to the components of a multidimensional Wiener process) that involve time-dependent weight functions, the paper proposes using the method of generalized multiple Fourier series, introduced by the author in 2006. The article also provides a modification of the Euler method and the Taylor-Ito expansion for Ito SDEs with non-differentiable or singular drift and diffusion coefficients. The convergence rates of the proposed modifications of the Milstein and Euler methods are established.

papers.title: Boundary-Driven Nonequilibrium for the Coulomb Landau Equation
papers.abstract: We establish a nonlinear theory of the Coulomb Landau equation in smooth bounded domains with non-isothermal diffuse reflection. We construct a stationary state, prove its perturbative uniqueness and global nonlinear stability, and establish exponential convergence when the wall temperature approaches its stationary profile exponentially. We also establish stationary and global nonlinear well-posedness for prescribed inflow, together with asymptotic stability. The analysis combines a critical kinetic integrability gain with finite-exponent velocity-gradient estimates near grazing, allowing the nonlinear Coulomb estimates to close without $L_x^\infty$ control of velocity gradients.

papers.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
papers.abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $\theta_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge \theta_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $\theta_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^\beta$, for any given $\beta\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $\theta_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.

papers.title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
papers.abstract:
This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\):
  \[
  \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad
  \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5).
  \]

papers.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
papers.abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).

papers.title: Finitely many solutions for the prescribed scalar curvature problem at the critical flatness order
papers.abstract:
We study the following prescribed scalar curvature problem $$
  -\Delta u=K(y)u^{2^*-1},\ \ u>0
  \,\ \ \text{in}\ \ \mathbb{R}^N, $$ where $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$. For $N\geq4$, we construct a positive $K(y)$ with maximum set $\{|y|=1\}$ and critical order of flatness $m=N-2$ at $|y|=1$, such that the equation admits only finitely many positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^N)$. To this end, we prove the compactness of the solution set for this equation by blow-up analysis and then apply Sard's theorem to choose $K$ for which each solution is non-degenerate and hence isolated, so that the solution set is finite. Our results also give a definite answer to Wei--Yan's conjecture in [J. Wei and S. Yan, JFA, 2010].

papers.title: A complete K\"ahler metric on $\mathbb{C}^n$ of nonnegative Ricci curvature with Euclidean volume growth and nonunique asymptotic cone
papers.abstract: We construct complete smooth K\"ahler metrics on $\mathbb{C}^n$ , $n\ge2$, with nonnegative Ricci curvature, Euclidean volume growth, and nonunique tangent cones at infinity. More generally, we prescribe the entire tangent cone set within a class of smooth Hopf cones, using a compact connected family of positive transverse Ricci forms on $\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. We identify all metric blow-downs and their Ricci currents, compute the exact asymptotic volume ratio, and classify isometries between the model cones. In particular, the K\"ahler condition does not ensure uniqueness at infinity under nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth, even in complex dimension two.

papers.title: Logarithmic Separation between LZ77 and LZ-End and Grammar Compression
papers.authors: Philip Bille, Inge Li G{\o}rtz, Rikke Jessen, Jingxun Li, Simon Rumle Tarnow, Renfei Zhou
papers.abstract: We show that there is a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and LZ-End, and between LZ77 and grammar compression.

papers.title: Sobolev inequalities for sections and projections of log-concave functions
papers.authors: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno
papers.abstract: Higher order sharp Sobolev and local Sobolev type inequalities for log-concave functions are established. The new inequalities directly imply the isoperimetric inequalities by Bollob\'as and Thomason in 1995, by Liakopoulos in 2019, and the recently discovered local isoperimetric inequalities from [1]. In order to do so, we make use of three ingredients. First, sets of functional inequalities proven by Alonso-Guti\'errez, Bernu\'es, Brazitikos and Carbery in 2021. Second, a multidimensional polynomial optimization result that originated in [1] and was initiated by Bollob\'as and Thomason. Third, a new integral formula for the projection of a log-concave function that links the geometric part with the more functional versions via some dependence on the Hessian matrix restricted to subspaces.

papers.title: $L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
papers.abstract:
We investigate the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
  $$
  u_{tttt}+\alpha u_{ttt}+\beta u_{tt}-\gamma \Delta u_{tt}-\delta \Delta u_{t}-\varrho \Delta u=(f(u))_{ttt}+(f(u))_{tt}
  $$
  under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a smooth bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\leq 3$, where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ and $\beta,\gamma,\delta,\varrho>0$. First, for any suitably regular initial data and assuming that $f\in C^4(\mathbb{R})$ with $f(0)=0$, we prove that the corresponding initial-boundary value problem admits a unique maximal strong solution $u$ on $(0, T_{max})$. Second, by combining three time-integrated formulations with a series of resolvent-regularized energy estimates, we show that gradient blow-up is ruled out in the sense that
  \begin{equation} \tag{*}
  T_{max}<\infty \quad\,\, \Rightarrow\quad\,\, \limsup_{t\nearrow T_{max}}\|u(\cdot,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}=\infty.
  \end{equation}
  Finally, assuming in addition that $f$ is convex and grows superlinearly in the sense that
  $$
  f''(\xi)\geq 0 \;\; \mbox{ for all}\;\;\xi \in\mathbb{R}, \qquad \frac{f(\xi)}{\xi}\rightarrow +\infty\;\;\mbox{ as}\;\; \xi\rightarrow +\infty , \qquad \int_{\xi_{0}}^{\infty}\frac{d\xi}{f(\xi)}<\infty \;\; \mbox{ for some}\;\; \xi_{0}>0,
  $$
  we employ the extensibility criterion (*) to prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, the solution blows up in finite time in the $L^\infty$-norm. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous description of finite-time blow-up for a genuinely nonlinear equation of fourth order in time.

papers.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
papers.authors: Silvia Bertoluzza, Gabriella Bretti, Micol Pennacchio, Christophe Prud'homme
papers.abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Extremals for Trudinger-Moser inequalities via polygonal profiles
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish the existence of extremal functions for the Trudinger-Moser inequality with logarithmic weights $(-\log |x|)^{\beta}$ in two dimensions throughout the full range $0\le \beta<1$. We also extend recent results on the existence of local maximizers for the Trudinger-Moser functional beyond the critical threshold. Our approach uses polygonal profiles to establish a lower bound uniform in the weight parameter. An explicit thirty-node profile gives the lower bound $\mathrm{TM}_{4\pi}>4.38421793217\,\pi$ for the classical critical supremum on the unit disk, improving on the value $4.3556\,\pi$ obtained in the computer experiments of Carleson and Chang. This lower bound has a purely analytic proof, which uses only elementary inequalities and exact rational arithmetic. Numerical experiments with polygonal profiles of up to $102400$ nodes suggest that this lower bound can be raised to $4.402732044\,\pi$, which improves the recent computational lower bound by Li and Sun.

papers.title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent under Relaxed Assumptions
papers.abstract: We study convergence rates of Nesterov's Accelerated Gradient Descent (NAG) method for convex optimization in both deterministic and stochastic settings. We focus on a more general smoothness condition raised from several machine learning problems empirically and theoretically. We show the accelerated convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}\left(1/T^2\right)$ in terms of the function value gap, given access to exact gradients of objective functions, matching the optimal rate for standard smooth convex optimization in \citep{nesterov1983method}. Under the relaxed affine-variance noise assumption for stochastic optimization, we establish the high-probability convergence rate of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{\log\left(1/\delta\right)/T}\right)$ and this rate could improve to $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\log\left(1/\delta\right)/T^2\right)$ when the noise parameters are sufficiently small. Here, $T$ denotes the total number of iterations and $\delta$ is the probability margin. Up to logarithm factors, our probabilistic convergence rate reaches the same order of the expected rate obtained in \citep{ghadimi2016accelerated} where the assumptions of bounded variance noise and Lipschitz smoothness are required. We additionally establish the convergence rates of the studied algorithms in the non-convex setting.

papers.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
papers.authors: Hao Guo, Chenxi Wang, Guoliang Yu
papers.abstract: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.

papers.title: Forcing square with small conditions
papers.abstract: We show that if $\kappa^{<\kappa} = \kappa$, then there is a $\kappa$-strategically closed, $\kappa^+$-c.c. partial order that forces $\square_\kappa$. We discuss consequences for generic large cardinals.

papers.title: The maximum spectral radius of connected graphs with prescribed order and size
papers.abstract: In 1986, Brualdi and Solheid asked which connected graph of prescribed order and size has maximum adjacency spectral radius. We complete the classification for every feasible pair of parameters. We prove that no graph outside the dense and star threshold families is extremal, including at ties, and settle the range $n\le e+1$, where the star candidate is not defined. The final comparison \emph{between} the dense and star candidates is supplied by Damnjanovi\'c's Propositions~4.1--4.2, not reproved here. We combine an exact Bellman recursion with dense-core domination, fractional complete-split bounds, and a virtual-star inequality. Three remaining comparison families (J), (K1), and (K2) are established analytically and by exact polynomial and Sturm certificates. The exact certificates are implemented in Python/SymPy and SageMath.

papers.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
papers.abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.

papers.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
papers.abstract:
Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. We study the quadratic response at uniform equilibrium, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings ($T=3$), we construct a nonzero smooth acceleration, whose first two final-state coefficients vanish. A planar curve reduces this cancellation to a scalar identity. At this reference acceleration, two integrations give an explicit control correction that preserves the linear return and produces any given leading change in the quadratic final state. The correction maps periodic $H^r$ targets with zero mean to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations only.
  Keywords: Controllability, control of partial differential equations, return method, Saint-Venant equations, Sylvester equations.

papers.title: An unconditionally convergent BDF2-type finite element integrator for the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
papers.authors: Michele Ald\'e, Hywel Normington, Dirk Praetorius, Michele Ruggeri
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme to approximate solutions to the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (iLLG) equation, a state-of-the-art model to describe the dynamics of the magnetization at subpicosecond time scales. The method employs first-order finite elements for the spatial discretization and the two-step backward differentiation formula (BDF2) for the time discretization, where the inertial term is treated by a convex combination of BDF2 and the backward Euler method. We prove well-posedness and unconditional stability of the scheme, and obtain explicit bounds for the error in the realization of the iLLG-inherent unit length constraint satisfied by the magnetization. Moreover, we derive the discrete energy law satisfied by the approximations, which resembles the inherent dissipative energy law of the model. Finally, with a constructive approach, we prove unconditional convergence of the approximations toward a weak solution of the problem. Numerical experiments assess the performance of the scheme and validate the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Influence of Anthropisation on a Mosquito Community in a Tropical Forest-Village Interface
papers.authors: Yves Dumont, Marc H\'etier, Valaire Yatat-Djeumen
papers.abstract: Tropical forests are undergoing deep changes caused by human activities, which have repercussions on the habitats of wild animal, particularly mammals. As mammals serve as a main source of blood meals for forest mosquitoes, their decline may affect the mosquitoes, as do changes in their habitats and abiotic conditions, such as rainfall, temperature, etc. Finally, along with humans come new species of mosquitoes-more generalist and more anthropophilic-that adapt to these new conditions and, moreover, serve as vectors for re-emerging diseases against which local populations have no more immunity. In this work, we derive a deterministic model which includes the effects of anthropisation, two species of mosquito that interact with one another (one is a generalist, whilst the other is sedentary and lives in the forest), and blood feeding preferences between multiple blood sources. We consider two socio-ecological areas, corresponding to a domestic area (for instance, a village), and a wild area (for instance, a tropical forest). A comprehensive analysis of the system is carried out using classical theory and monotone systems theory. We analyse the efficiency of individual protective measures, such as mosquito nets and repellents, against the domestic mosquito species. We investigate the risk of invasion of the wild area by a generalist mosquito species. We show that habitat anthropisation and high interspecific competition facilitate the invasion. When the mathematical system converges towards a periodic cycle, we provide numerical estimates for the periodic invasion threshold. Using a global sensitivity analysis, we show that the model is sensitive to the level of anthropisation, the adaptability of the invasive species to the forest area, and its fitness. The more efficient way to control the invasion is, therefore, to limit, as much as possible, the forest anthropisation.

papers.title: Uniform large-genus asymptotics of Weil-Petersson volumes
papers.abstract: Let $V_{g,n}$ be the Weil--Petersson volume of the moduli space of hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$ with $n$ cusps. The fixed-$n$ large-genus expansion of Mirzakhani and Zograf has correction terms polynomial in $n$ of degree $2i$ at order $g^{-i}$, and ceases to be uniform when $n$ is of order $\sqrt g$. We prove an asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/g$ that holds uniformly in all $n\ge0$, with coefficients analytic in a density parameter that ranges over a compact interval, including the limits $n/g\to0$ and $n/g\to\infty$. Its leading term is explicit, contains no undetermined constant and has relative error $O(1/g)$; truncation at an order proportional to $\sqrt g$ gives relative error $O(\exp(-a\sqrt g))$ for some $a>0$. For fixed $n$ this confirms Zograf's conjecture that the constant in the Mirzakhani--Zograf asymptotics is $1/\sqrt\pi$. We also determine, at every cusp density, the limits of the volume ratios $V_{g,n}/V_{g-1,n+2}$ and $V_{g,n+1}/(2gV_{g,n})$ and, in all degrees, the asymptotics of the ratios of adjacent coefficients of the one-boundary volume polynomial; this answers two questions of Mirzakhani. The proof deforms mixed $\kappa_1$--$\psi$ intersection numbers into pure $\psi$ intersection numbers along a family whose recursion has nonnegative coefficients, fixes the overall constant through Painlev\'e I without assuming resurgence, and recovers individual volumes by a local limit theorem in the number of cusps. As an application, the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random surface with $n\gg\sqrt g$ cusps tends to zero in probability; this removes the restriction $n/g\to0$ from a theorem of Shen and Wu.

papers.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
papers.abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.

papers.title: Positivity for a $t$-analogue of refined Littlewood-Richardson rules
papers.authors: Jiaming Du, Emma Yu Jin, Xiaowei Lin
papers.abstract:
In 2010, Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg proved that the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure atom $A_{\gamma}$ expands positively in terms of Demazure atoms, and interpreted the coefficients as the number of Littlewood-Richardson skew skyline tableaux of a given shape and a filling type. Extending this approach, they further established the positive expansion for the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a quasisymmetric Schur function $S_{\alpha}$, or of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure character $\kappa_{\gamma}$. In particular, the latter provides a refinement of the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule.
  We present a natural $t$-analogue of these positive expansions by deriving the expansion for a product of a Hall-Littlewood polynomial $P_{\lambda}(t)$ and a $t$-Demazure atom $E_{\gamma}(t)$ in terms of $t$-Demazure atoms. The corresponding coefficients are $\mathbb{N}\,[t,1-t]$-positive; that is, they are polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients in $t$ and $1-t$, and they are interpreted in terms of standard Young tableaux. We take the approach of connecting the multiplication coefficients with the LLT polynomials, which differs from the combinatorial insertion arguments of Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg.

papers.title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus. Thus, there are no unexpected toric positroid varieties.

papers.title: University Research and Leadership in the Age of AI: Mobilizing Intellectual Capacity and Building the Infrastructure for Discovery
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to disrupt research across academia, changing how knowledge is produced and how research is organized. Recent developments in mathematics provide an early example of strong AI research capabilities and the professional disruption accompanying them. Universities should respond by building the scientific, computational, and organizational capacity to develop AI and shape the research it enables. The relationship is reciprocal: AI can advance disciplinary research, while scientific questions, experimental evidence, and disciplinary expertise can guide AI development. This article proposes connecting shared computational resources with sustained technical teams, interdisciplinary research, experimental facilities, and knowledge infrastructure that makes findings traceable and reusable. It distinguishes three commitments with different resource requirements: operating existing models, developing AI for disciplinary research, and investigating the foundations of AI. Commercial services can support this agenda alongside institutional capabilities for independent investigation, evaluation, and preservation of the research record. Consortia and national facilities can broaden participation and support capabilities beyond individual campuses. Initial programs should assess scientific value, total costs, and contributions to AI development, with expansion guided by evidence. These changes require sustained funding, professional support, and recognition of the work that makes research reliable and cumulative. Building this capacity will enable universities to pursue new research directions, train future researchers, and exercise scientific leadership as AI transforms academic inquiry.

papers.title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
papers.abstract:
Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(\mu:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(\mu\), the symplectic quotient \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow N_a/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(N_a\) of \(\mu^{-1}(a)\). We define a formal Kirwan map \[\kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a).\]
  We prove that it is surjective under a local equivariant homotopy retraction condition on the slice level sets
  \[
  C_x=\mu_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x,
  \]
  which is satisfied.
  We also prove an equivariant tubular neighborhood theorem for singular level sets: under real analytic/proper or \(G\)-invariant Whitney stratified assumptions, there exists a \(G\)-invariant open neighborhood \(U\) of \(\mu^{-1}(a)\) and a \(G\)-equivariant strong deformation retraction \(U\to\mu^{-1}(a)\). When such a neighborhood exists, the formal cohomology is canonically isomorphic to the Borel equivariant cohomology of the level set, and the formal Kirwan map is the classical restriction map. The formal framework therefore yields a Kirwan-type map at the singular value with the surjectivity property.
  As an application we recover the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Power Iteration Algorithms: Convergence, Analysis and Application to Reactor Criticality Calculations
papers.authors: Alexander M. G. Cox, Tom Davis, Julian Hofstadler, Andreas E. Kyprianou
papers.abstract: We study Monte Carlo power iteration algorithms in the context of reactor criticality simulations. Under mild conditions on the underlying physical system and the algorithmic structure, we derive explicit error bounds, which are to the best of our knowledge the first rigorous results for such methods which are ubiquitous in nuclear engineering. This is done by exploiting connections to Sequential Monte Carlo algorithms, and extending recent developments about stochastic neutron transport. We demonstrate the applicability of our results by considering a concrete version of the Monte Carlo power iteration algorithm as well as variance reduction schemes.

papers.title: Periodic Solutions and Exponential Attractivity in Hopfield-Type Neural Networks with Generalized Piecewise Constant Arguments: Impulsive and Nonimpulsive Cases
papers.authors: Ricardo Torres Naranjo, Samuel Castillo Apolonio
papers.abstract: We investigate an impulsive Hopfield-type neural network with a generalized piecewise constant argument, including the nonimpulsive case in which all jump terms vanish. The piecewise constant argument is given by $\gamma(t)=\zeta_k$ on each interval $[t_k,t_{k+1})$, where $t_k\leq\zeta_k\leq t_{k+1}$, $k\in\mathbb{N}_0$. Depending on the position of $\zeta_k$, the argument may be advanced, retarded, or of mixed type. By representing periodic solutions through a Green function and applying a fixed-point argument, we obtain explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of an $\omega$-periodic solution. We then use a Gronwall-type estimate, together with period averages, to prove that this solution is globally exponentially attractive. These conditions can be checked directly from the system parameters, without requiring explicit knowledge of the periodic solution. In the course of the analysis, we also revisit and correct some estimates presented by Pinto et al. \cite{Pinto_ejqtde}. The case $\zeta_k=t_k$ reduces to their setting, whereas our results cover the more general choice of $\zeta_k$ within each interval. We also present examples illustrating different types of piecewise constant arguments.

papers.title: Energy equality and renormalization of Navier-Stokes-Vlasov equations
papers.abstract: We study weak solutions of the incompressible and the compressible Navier--Stokes--Vlasov systems on a bounded domain, where a viscous fluid is coupled to a dispersed particle phase through a drag force; the fluid obeys the no-slip boundary condition and the particles are subject to specular reflection. For solutions with Besov regularity, we show that the Vlasov equation is renormalizable in the sense of DiPerna--Lions, and we give regularity thresholds for the validity of the global energy equality. If the distribution function $f$ belongs to $B_p^{\alpha,\infty}$ in space and velocity with time integrability $p$, and the fluid velocity $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to $B_q^{\beta,\infty}$ jointly in space and time with integrability $q$, then the energy equality holds provided $\alpha+\beta>1$ and $\beta$ exceeds an explicit bound depending on $p$, $q$ and the dimension, under a natural integrability assumption on the pressure; an analogous criterion holds for the compressible system when the density is bounded from above and below. The condition $\alpha p>1$ imposed on $f$ is not merely technical: it is exactly the range in which the macroscopic momentum flux possesses a boundary trace, so that the specular reflection condition passes to the macroscopic energy balance. When the particle phase is absent, our thresholds coincide with the criteria $\beta>\frac12+\frac1q$ and $\beta>\frac3q$ obtained by Yu for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations alone. The proofs combine a boundary cutoff argument with commutator estimates based on a scale-localized Besov modulus, together with a boundary-strip analysis.

papers.title: Near-quadratic sum-product estimates in fixed number fields
papers.authors: Kaiqiang Zhang, Yuanguo Zeng, Yuyu Wang
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a fixed number field. We prove a quantitative expansion theorem for mixed sumsets $A+B$, assuming only that $A$ is covered by relatively few cosets of a multiplicative group of small finite valuation rank. The constants are independent of the generators, their heights, and their prime ideal supports. As a consequence, if $A\subset K^\times$, $|A|=N\ge 3$, and each element has nonzero valuation at at most $k$ finite places, then every $B\subset K$ with $|B|=N$ satisfies $$ \max\{|A+B|,|AA|\} \ge N^2\exp\left[-C_K\left((k+1)\log(\log N+2)+\sqrt{(k+1)\log N}\right)\right]. $$ This is $N^{2-o(1)}$ for $k=o(\log N/\log\log N)$. We also obtain a trade-off between the additive and multiplicative deficits, estimates for iterated linear sumsets, and a transfer theorem for product constructions $A=PG$ in terms of the multiplicative deficit of $P$. The proof recovers local scales from an exact sum and bounds the remaining conditional entropy by the overlap of entropy measures on fixed trees.

papers.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_{\alpha}^k$ on $A^2_\alpha(\mathbb{D})$
  if and only if $-1<\alpha\leq1$. We also show that, for every $\alpha>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.

papers.title: A sparse canonical Rado theorem
papers.authors: Zhenzhen Lou, Guangfu Wang, Man Wu, Zhifei Yan
papers.abstract:
Canonical Ramsey theory studies structured colour patterns in colourings with arbitrarily many colours. Lefmann's canonical Rado theorem extends the canonical van der Waerden theorem of Erd\H{o}s and Graham to partition-regular linear systems. Recently, Alvarado, Kohayakawa, Morris, Mota and Ortega proved a sparse canonical van der Waerden theorem for random set $[n]_p$.
  In this paper, we prove a sparse canonical Rado theorem. For every irredundant partition-regular matrix $A$ of positive rank with $k\ge3$ columns, and every prescribed partition witnessing the columns condition, if $p\ge Cn^{-1/m(A)}$, then with probability at least $1-e^{-cnp}$ every colouring of $[n]_p$ contains $$\Omega\big(p^k n^{k-\rank(A)}\big)$$ canonical solutions of $A\mathbf x=0$ with distinct coordinates. A matching 0-statement holds when the prescribed partition has one or at least three blocks; the Schur equation shows that it can fail for two-block patterns. For every prescribed partition, we also establish a robust threshold at the same scale under deletion of a fixed positive proportion of the random set.

papers.title: Stationary Coexistence in Stochastic Gause Systems with General Trophic Responses
papers.authors: Andr\'es S\'anchez, Leon A. Valencia, Jorge M. Ramirez Osorio
papers.abstract: We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment. For responses whose rare-predator limit is strictly increasing and whose value at positive predator density never exceeds that limit, we also establish necessity of positive predator invasion whenever the prey-only stationary law exists. If the prey per-capita growth attains its global maximum at zero, interior stationarity itself forces prey establishment, giving a necessary-and-sufficient criterion beyond logistic growth. Logistic and bounded saturating growth laws provide explicit Gamma and beta-prime resident distributions. Applications include Holling, Ivlev, Beddington-DeAngelis, and Crowley-Martin responses. Responses with the same rare-predator limit share the coexistence threshold, although predator interference changes the interior distribution. Reproducible quadrature and simulations illustrate this distinction. The analysis builds on existing stochastic persistence theory and identifies precisely the additional comparison argument needed for necessity, including exclusion of interior invariant measures at zero predator invasion.

papers.title: Regression Functions as Fields on Covariate Space: Evolution Equations, the Hessian, and Identification
papers.abstract: For each time $t$, the regression function $m_t(x)=E[Y_t\mid X_t=x]$ of an outcome on contemporaneous covariates can be regarded as a field on covariate space. When the covariates of units move as a diffusion and each unit's outcome has its own dynamics, we show that $m_t$ satisfies a second-order evolution equation whose diffusion term is $\frac12\mathrm{tr}(\Sigma\nabla^2 m_t)$, the Hessian of the regression function weighted by the covariance $\Sigma$ of covariate increments, whose transport term is the drift of the time-reversed covariate process, and whose source term is the conditional mean rate of change of the outcome; this yields a Feynman-Kac representation along reversed covariate paths. We relate this Hessian to quadratic regression (under Gaussian design the best quadratic approximation has Hessian $E[\nabla^2 m(X)]$) and to kernel smoothing bias. For bistable replicator dynamics on covariate space, travelling fronts are exactly logistic in $(x,t)$, so one logistic regression identifies the diffusion-reaction ratio and the invading strategy. We then ask whether spread in covariate space reflects fluctuating unit characteristics or imitation among similar units. Imitation acts through exactly the same operator as covariate fluctuation, so the two are observationally equivalent in the regression field; panel data separate them because they identify $\Sigma$ directly. The two cannot be separated on a travelling front, and we propose a split-sample instrumental-variables test that works on seeded, non-front profiles, with size and power evaluated in agent-based experiments.

papers.title: Negative Translations for Affine and Lukasiewicz Logic
papers.abstract: We investigate four well-known negative translations of classical logic into intuitionistic logic within a substructural setting. We find that in \emph{affine logic} the translation schemes due to Kolmogorov and G\"odel both satisfy Troelstra's criteria for a negative translation. On the other hand, the schemes of Glivenko and Gentzen both fail for affine logic, but for different reasons: one can extend affine logic to make Glivenko work and Gentzen fail and {\it vice versa}. By contrast, in the setting of \emph{{\L}ukasiewicz logic}, we can prove a general result asserting that a wide class of formula translations including those of Kolmogorov, G\"odel, Gentzen and Glivenko not only satisfy Troelstra's criteria with respect to a natural intuitionistic fragment of {\L}ukasiewicz logic but are all equivalent.

papers.title: Response time central-limit and failure rate estimation for stationary periodic rate monotonic real-time systems
papers.abstract: Real-time systems consist of a set of tasks, a scheduling policy, and a system architecture, all constrained by timing requirements. Many everyday embedded systems, within devices such as airplanes, cars, trains, and spatial probes, operate as real-time systems. To ensure safe failure rates, response times-the time required for the exection of a task-must be bounded. Rate Monotonic real-time systems prioritize tasks according to their arrival rate. This paper focuses on the use of the central limit of response times built in \cite{zagalo2022} and an approximation of their distribution with an inverse Gaussian mixture distribution. The distribution parameters and their associated failure rates are estimated through a suitable re-parameterization of the inverse Gaussian distribution and an adapted Expectation-Maximization algorithm. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the method is well-suited for the approximation of failure rates. We discuss the extension of such method to a chi-squared independence test adapted to real-time systems.

papers.title: A quantum central path algorithm for linear optimization
papers.authors: Brandon Augustino, Jiaqi Leng, Jialu Bao, Giacomo Nannicini, Tam\'as Terlaky, Xiaodi Wu
papers.abstract: We propose a novel quantum algorithm for solving linear optimization problems by quantum-mechanical simulation of the central path. While interior point methods follow the central path with an iterative algorithm that works with successive linearizations of the perturbed KKT conditions, we perform a simulation working directly with the nonlinear complementarity equations. Using a two-stage quantum eigenpath traversal schedule, this approach yields an algorithm for solving linear optimization problems involving $m$ constraints and $n$ variables to $\varepsilon$-optimality using $\widetilde{O}\!\left((m+n)^{3/2}\,\varepsilon^{-1}+(m+n)^{1/2}\,\varepsilon^{-3/2}\right)$ queries to an oracle that evaluates a potential function. In the standard gate model (i.e., without access to quantum RAM), our algorithm can obtain $\varepsilon$-precise solutions to LO problems using at most $$\widetilde{O}\!\left(\left[\frac{(m+n)^{3/2}}{\varepsilon} + \frac{(m+n)^{1/2}}{\varepsilon^{3/2}}\right] \cdot \mathrm{nnz}(A)\right)$$ elementary gates, where $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ is the total number of non-zero elements found in the constraint matrix.

papers.title: Boosting e-BH via conditional calibration
papers.abstract: The e-BH procedure is an e-value-based multiple testing procedure that provably controls the false discovery rate (FDR) under any dependence structure between the e-values. Despite this appealing theoretical FDR control guarantee, the e-BH procedure often suffers from low power in practice. In this paper, we propose a general framework that boosts the power of e-BH without sacrificing its FDR control under arbitrary dependence. This is achieved by the technique of conditional calibration, where we take as input the e-values and calibrate them to be a set of "boosted e-values" that are guaranteed to be no less -- and are often more -- powerful than the original ones. Our general framework is explicitly instantiated in three classes of multiple testing problems: (1) testing under parametric models, (2) conditional independence testing under the model-X setting, and (3) model-free conformalized selection. Extensive numerical experiments show that our proposed method significantly improves the power of e-BH while continuing to control the FDR. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through an application to an observational study dataset for identifying individuals whose counterfactuals satisfy certain properties.

papers.title: Amplituhedra and origami, I: tree level
papers.abstract: We establish a precise correspondence between points of the $m=4$ tree momentum amplituhedron and origami crease patterns. As an application, we prove that the BCFW (Britto-Cachazo-Feng-Witten) cells triangulate the $m=4$ tree amplituhedron both in momentum space and in momentum-twistor space. As another application, we show that every nondegenerate weighted planar bipartite graph $\Gamma$ admits a t-embedding, i.e., an embedding of the planar dual of $\Gamma$ such that the sum of angles of white (equivalently, black) faces around each vertex is equal to $\pi$.

papers.title: The Price of Failure Risk: Clipped Barrier Policy Gradients with Convex Regularization
papers.authors: Pekka Malo, Lauri Viitasaari, Antti Suominen, Eeva Vilkkumaa, Olli Tahvonen
papers.abstract: In many control problems, actions consume a resource budget, such as a wear allowance, and the probability of exhausting it within a given horizon must stay below a tolerance. A simple, widely used approach is to augment the state with the remaining budget, subtract an interior barrier from the utility and penalize exhaustion, so that policy-gradient methods can be applied unchanged. We clip the combined one-step reward from below at a level m to keep the returns of exploratory policies finite. The clip level is a price of failure risk, since the clipped value decomposes exactly into the utility before failure, the cost of the interior margin and m times a geometric failure risk. Consequently, an approximately optimal policy maximizes utility net of margin cost among policies with no greater risk. Its risk exceeds that of any comparison policy by at most order 1/m and can be certified from its value or from validation data. Our main result proves exponential convergence of the population policy-gradient flow for every parameter regularizer that is convex along generalized geodesics and sufficiently strong relative to the price. This extends the mean-field analysis from relative entropy to weight decay and to finite networks. Relative entropy adds parameter noise and a pull toward a prior, whereas weight decay provides only the pull. Action regularization bounds changes in failure risk by the relative entropy to a reference policy. The bounds are evaluated on an exact maintenance benchmark, a fuel-tank controller, a solvable flow and a benchmark-suite task.

papers.title: Long-range correlations in a locally constrained exclusion process
papers.authors: Stefan Gro{\ss}kinsky, Gunter Sch\"utz, Ali Zahra
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel exclusion process with a simple local kinetic constraint that leads to a remarkable transition between a homogeneous phase with short-range correlations and a clustered phase with long-range correlations and spontaneous breaking of translation invariance. The metastable dynamics of particle clusters lead to a coarsening cascade and glassy dynamics, as well as an intriguing faster-is-slower effect where an increasing asymmetry in the flow direction leads to a decrease of the stationary current.

papers.title: Classification of locality preserving symmetries on spin chains
papers.authors: Alex Bols, Wojciech De Roeck, Michiel De Wilde, Bruno de O. Carvalho
papers.abstract: We consider the action of a finite group $G$ by locality preserving automorphisms (quantum cellular automata) on quantum spin chains. We refer to such group actions as ``symmetries''. The natural notion of equivalence for such symmetries is \emph{stable equivalence}, which allows for stacking with factorized group actions. Stacking also endows the set of equivalence classes with a group structure. We prove that the anomaly of such symmetries provides an isomorphism between the group of stable equivalence classes of symmetries with the cohomology group $H^3(G,U(1))$, consistent with previous conjectures. This amounts to a complete classification of locality preserving symmetries on spin chains.

papers.title: On the minimax optimality of Flow Matching through the connection to kernel density estimation
papers.abstract: Flow Matching has recently gained attention in generative modeling as a simple and flexible alternative to diffusion models. While existing statistical guarantees adapt tools from the analysis of diffusion models, we take a different perspective by connecting Flow Matching to kernel density estimation. We first verify that the kernel density estimator matches the optimal rate of convergence in Wasserstein distance up to logarithmic factors, improving existing bounds for the Gaussian kernel. Based on this result, we prove that for sufficiently large networks, Flow Matching achieves the optimal rate up to logarithmic factors. If the target distribution lies on a lower-dimensional manifold, we show that the kernel density estimator profits from the smaller intrinsic dimension on a small tube around the manifold. The faster rate also applies to Flow Matching, providing a theoretical foundation for its empirical success in high-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Tight Generalization of Robertson-Type Uncertainty Relations
papers.authors: Gen Kimura, Aina Mayumi, Haruki Yamashita
papers.abstract: We establish the tightest possible Robertson-type preparation uncertainty relation, which explicitly depends on the eigenvalues of the quantum state. The conventional constant $ \tfrac{1}{4} $ is replaced by the state-dependent coefficient \[ \frac{(\lambda_{\max} + \lambda_{\min})^2}{4(\lambda_{\max} - \lambda_{\min})^2}, \] where $ \lambda_{\max} $ and $\lambda_{\min}$ denote the largest and smallest eigenvalues of the density operator $ \rho $, respectively. We prove that this coefficient is optimal among all Robertson-type generalizations and does not admit further improvement. We also obtain a complete characterization of all nontrivial equality cases. Our relation becomes more pronounced as the quantum state becomes more mixed, capturing a trade-off in quantum uncertainty that the conventional Robertson's relation fails to detect. In addition, our result also provides a strict generalization of the Schr\"odinger's uncertainty relation, showing that the uncertainty trade-off is governed by the sum of the covariance term and a state-dependent improvement over the Robertson bound. As applications, we also refine error-disturbance trade-offs by incorporating spectral information of both the system and the measuring apparatus, thereby generalizing the Arthurs-Goodman and Ozawa inequalities.

papers.title: Entanglement Scaling of Motzkin Chains under Spiral Hamiltonian-path Embeddings
papers.abstract: We investigate how a two-dimensional spatial embedding changes the entanglement observed across geometrically local bipartitions of a one-dimensional quantum spin chain. A $q$-deformed colored Motzkin chain is placed along a spiral-inspired Hamiltonian path that visits $N(L)=\Theta(L^2)$ sites of a square-lattice region while retaining a path interaction graph. Straight ambient-space cuts then correspond to unions of $\Theta(L)$ disconnected intervals in the chain ordering. We derive the scaling of a height-variation proxy for the leading color-pairing contribution and predict ambient-space entropy scaling proportional to $L^2$, $L$, and $O(1)$ for $q>1$, $q=1$, and $q<1$, respectively. We evaluate this proxy numerically using the matrix-product-state representation and verify its predicted finite-size scaling. The embedded and original Hamiltonians have exactly identical spectra and spectral gaps at fixed chain length. We also describe a sparse tensor-network representation and propose a two-chain junction extension. These results isolate the roles of interaction connectivity, spatial embedding, and subsystem geometry in entanglement scaling.

papers.title: On the Spherical Dirichlet Distribution: Corrections and Results
papers.abstract: This article revisits the spherical-Dirichlet distribution (SDD) introduced by Guardiola (2020) and clarifies the correction to its density presented in an earlier version of this preprint. The principal issue concerns Equation (3) of the original publication, which expresses the density in local Euclidean coordinates rather than with respect to spherical surface-area measure. We derive the corrected intrinsic density and revisit its moments, covariance matrix, mode, and limiting properties. We show that the two density representations describe the same probability distribution, preserving the moment formulas and likelihood-based parameter estimation. However, the mode and uniformity conditions depend on the reference measure and require corresponding clarification. Reported simulation and text mining estimates are revisited and updated. The resulting presentation reconciles the original construction with its intrinsic spherical properties.

papers.title: Invariant Reduction for Partial Differential Equations. III: Poisson Brackets
papers.abstract: We establish that local Hamiltonian operators admitted by systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) induce Poisson bivectors on suitable finite-dimensional subsystems describing invariant solutions. This correspondence is governed by the mechanism of invariant reduction, which applies uniformly to point, contact, and higher symmetries. We show that the induced Poisson bivectors relate constants of invariant motion to symmetries of such subsystems. Applying the same reduction mechanism to invariant conservation laws, we further deduce that the corresponding Poisson brackets on the reduced systems agree, up to a global sign, with those of the original systems. The results are illustrated by two examples in which the induced Poisson brackets and constants of invariant motion yield integrability of the reduced systems. The construction is independent of the choice of an $\ell$-normal inclusion of a PDE system into jet spaces, with the corresponding odd cotangent covering being $\ell$-normal.

papers.title: A nonparametric Bayesian analysis of independent and identically distributed observations of covariate-driven Poisson processes
papers.abstract: An important task in the statistical analysis of inhomogeneous point processes is to investigate the influence of a set of covariates on the point-generating mechanism. In this article, we consider the nonparametric Bayesian approach to this problem, assuming that $n$ independent and identically distributed realizations of the point pattern and the covariate random field are available. In many applications, different covariates are often vastly diverse in physical nature, resulting in anisotropic intensity functions whose variations along distinct directions occur at different smoothness levels. To model this scenario, we employ hierarchical prior distributions based on multi-bandwidth Gaussian processes. We prove that the resulting posterior distributions concentrate around the ground truth at optimal rate as $n\to\infty$, and achieve automatic adaptation to the anisotropic smoothness. Posterior inference is concretely implemented via a Metropolis-within-Gibbs Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that incorporates a dimension-robust sampling scheme to handle the functional component of the proposed nonparametric Bayesian model. Our theoretical results are supported by extensive numerical simulation studies. Further, we present an application to the analysis of a Canadian wildfire dataset.

papers.title: Fast subdivision of B\'{e}zier curves
papers.abstract:
It is well-known that a $d$-dimensional polynomial B\'{e}zier curve of degree $n$ can be subdivided into two segments using the famous de Casteljau algorithm in $O(dn^2)$ time. We show that it is possible to do this in $O(dn\log{n})$ time using the fast Fourier transform and its inverse. The direct application of the method is numerically unstable for larger values of $n$. Therefore, we also introduce a modified version based on parameter scaling, which retains the same asymptotic computational complexity. This scaling approach can improve numerical accuracy in some cases (for $n\lesssim 50$), as demonstrated by our experiments. Moreover, the new method has a nice property: if a B\'{e}zier curve is extended by an additional control point, the subdivision can be updated in $O(d)$ time. The method can be adapted to subdivide rational B\'{e}zier curves and rectangular B\'{e}zier surfaces, as well as to compute the derivatives of B\'{e}zier curves.
  Although motivated by applications in CAGD, the proposed methods may also be useful in other areas involving polynomial reparameterization.

papers.title: Commutative Algebra Modeling of Mutation and Disease Association
papers.authors: JunJie Wee, Mushal Zia, Faisal Suwayyid, Hongsong Feng, Yuta Hozumi, Guo-Wei Wei
papers.abstract: Genetic mutations can lead to disease by disrupting molecular interactions, altering protein stability, inducing misfolding, and promoting protein aggregation. Although existing predictive models have achieved promising performance, they often lack mechanistic interpretability and fail to fully incorporate the underlying physical and chemical principles governing mutation-induced effects. Moreover, current approaches typically address disease association, protein stability changes, and solubility alterations as separate prediction tasks rather than integrating them within a unified framework. In this study, we introduce a multiscale commutative algebra modeling framework for predicting disease-mutation association. Leveraging persistent Stanley-Reisner theory, we extract algebraic invariants to build two predictive models: Commutative Algebra Neural Network (CANet) and Commutative Algebra Gradient Boosting Tree (CATree). The proposed framework is applied to three biologically connected tasks: disease-associated mutation identification, mutation-induced protein stability change prediction, and mutation-induced protein solubility change classification. Across six benchmark tasks, CANet and CATree consistently achieve leading predictive performance, with up to 7.5% relative improvement over existing methods. These results demonstrate that commutative algebra provides a unified, interpretable, and generalizable modeling strategy for mutation-disease association prediction.

papers.title: Learning Survival Models with Right-Censored Reporting Delays
papers.abstract: Survival analysis provides statistical methods to model the time until an event occurs. Reporting delays arise when event times are not observed at their occurrence but are only revealed upon reporting. This issue is particularly critical for timely risk evaluation when the observation window is short due to administrative censoring. In this study, we incorporate right-censored reporting delays by jointly modeling parametric hazards for the event and reporting processes. We then construct a consistent estimator for the model parameters and develop a Monte Carlo expectation-maximization algorithm to compute it.
